The scope of the inspections carried out by the partnering administration includes both ships visiting ports in the area of inland waterways and ships in the shipping line Romania-Bulgaria, unfortunately at the present moment there is no information exchange between the two administrations on each side of Danube river, thus the result of each performed check remains unknown by the respective authority on the opposite side of the river. There is lack of communication also regarding the "Notices to skippers" related to the safety of navigation on waterways. At the present moment there is no mechanism allowing synchronizing the instructions related to the common area of the river. 

The present project is aiming at increase of the cooperation capacity and the efficiency of the two public institutions in a CBC context through development of Framework Agreement on the inspections performed under the river supervision regime and setting specific rules for navigation in the common Bulgarian - Romanian stretch of the Danube River. Indicated issues will be overcome with the supply of electronic database software package for the river supervision inspections and development of risk assessment methodology for river supervision inspections. As a result the R.N.A. and EAMA will possess an internal tool for exchange of extremely important information and at the same time improve their communication and coordinated activities in the CBC region in the name of more efficient and safe river navigability.

titleEn: Promoting Ecotourism and Organic Agriculture as Innovative Mechanisms for employment and local sustainable development in the Rural areas in the Romania-Bulgaria Cross-Border area
summaryEn:
This project is entirely relevant to the Programme area between the two municipalities – Lyaskovets and Videle - both face the same problems related to the unemployment and the lack of adequate skills and experience among the target group in the rural areas. The proposal is addressing the following problems such as the low level of information on employment opportunities in ecotourism and organic agriculture throughout the cross-border area, the lack of joint trainings and support as well as the exchanges of good EU practices for a better integration in the labour market.

The project objective strives to increase the employment opportunities and the mobility of the labour force through development of special competences and skills in the area of innovative ecotourism and organic agriculture and food production in the selected cross-border area.

The proposal consists of 10 activities – some of them are supporting to project implementation and the other ones are focused on obtaining necessary assets and services to deliver quality professional trainings, language courses, and joint cross-border markets. The development of web-based platform for green job opportunities in the cross-border region will be used by any interested person who is seeking or offering workforce, with or without a certain qualification, as well as by people interested to find service providers in the area. Besides using it very easy from any major web-browser installed on a device connected to internet, the platform will be installed on 4 info-kiosks placed in public places from Lyaskovets and Videle area.

A special attention is paid to the awareness campaign in order to inform more citizens regarding the green employment opportunities in the rural area in the cross-border region. The establishment of cross-border business incubators will activate the labour force and will offer services to employers thus strengthening the economic cooperation in the cross-border region.

The project outputs that are going to be achieved could be easily measured – 250 participants in 6 professional trainings in terms of green employment and labour mobility, 500 participants in special language courses, 160 participants in joint cross-border markets (job fairs), 100 participants in 5 editions of “Green Innovation Lab”. Also, the project will lead to increase the knowledge and skills of unemployed persons in the process of job seeking, will ensure face-to-face contact between potential “green” employers and “green” job seekers in the area of ecotourism and organic agriculture.

titleEn: Valorisation of authentic culture for cross-border tourism
summaryEn:
The main problem the project is addressing in the discovery of authentic culture and traditions in the small settlements and villages in the cross-border area of Vidin and Montana districts and Dolj county, their popularization and valorisation into a tourist product, raising public awareness for authentic cultural identity and popularization of the cross-border region as a culture destination.

The main project objective is to discover and promote the authentic culture in the cross-border area of Vidin and Montana districts and Dolj county and to create a new tourism product by using the cultural heritage of the target region.

The total budget of the operation is 421,713 euro.

The main activities of the project are: Field Study for discovering the local culture of people in the villages from Vidin, Montana and Dolj districts; Development of web site of authentic cross-border culture of real people; Promotion of voting campaign; Organization of 3 authentic culture festivals; 3 trainings for valorisation of culture into tourism products; Promotion of the created tourism products; Info-tour for journalists and tour operators; Presentation at 4 tourism fairs.

Expected project results corresponding to program output and results indicators:

Studied and described authentic traditions, crafts and culture in small settlements in the target region,

Filmed and promoted 210 authenticcultural events/crafts/skills/

Organized 3 festivals for authentic culture,

Valorisation of culture into cross-border tourist product.

titleEn: Balloon adventure - a new joint tourism product
summaryEn:
The cross-border area of Romania and Bulgaria is an extraordinary place, full of cultural and natural heritage, but tourism lacks genuine attractions targeted to the segment of richer tourists. Flying with hot-air balloons is a remarkable experience, a tourism attraction that could bring many well-paid tourists to visit the CBC area and also a possibility for many local cbc citizens to fulfill a dream. At the same time the balloons could bring added value to any event organized in the CBC area.

With this project we aim to create a new tourism product, which is still unknown for the cbc area and to involve all interested in tourism development stakeholders in the new touristic offer, eventually increasing the share of richer tourists in the area and promoting the image of the cbc area. Estimated project budget amounts at 488083,20euro.

The main objectives of the project are: project management, delivery of hot-air balloons and related equipment; balloon promotion of the CBC area; development of marketing strategy for the new product, workshops with local stakeholders for the creation of a joint CBC tourism offer; training of balloon ground crew; information and publicity; promotion at tourism fairs; balloon flights on ropes; balloon fiesta.

Project results will be:

the creation of a new functioning tourism product;

increased number of overnights – 1000;

created network with promoters of the new tourism product.

titleEn: Enhancing unemployed women’s potential to find a job within the CBC RO-BG region
Improving the workforce mobility and employment in cultural and creative industries from the RO-BG cross-border area
summaryEn:
The project “Improving the workforce mobility and employment in cultural and creative industries from the RO-BG cross-border area” aims to improve some of the situations identified as problems within the programming documents for INTERREG V-A RO-BG, namely the “deficits in creative industries”, the “brain drain of young and creative talents”, the “insufficiently explored and recognized potential of creative industries for the economy and the competitiveness of the region” and the „lack of cross border mobility for goods and persons”.

This will be achieved through a series of concrete and realistic objectives:

1. Improving the knowledge base on creative and cultural industries (CCIs), as well as labor mobility barriers in the CBC area through 2 comprehensive studies.

2. Developing the skills and knowledge of 220 people from the CBC area working in the CCIs in order to increase their chances for work mobility.

3. Supporting 120 professionals from CBC area, working in CCIs, to develop their cross-border experience.

4. Increase the level of awareness of 218 citizens on the employment and labor mobility opportunities in cross-border CCIs through job fairs and visits.

5. Encouraging the youth employment for 200 students in CCIs from the CBC area.

6. Increase the level of information of 22.000 citizens on the employment and labor mobility in cross-border CCIs through an intensive information campaign.

These objectives are going to be achieved through the following activities: elaboration of 2 studies; organizing trainings; organizing cross-border visits for exchange of experiences; organizing integrated joint cross-border job fairs; establishing 2 cross-border centers for supporting activities and employment; organizing educational caravans in universities; elaboration of audio-video promotion materials and website; information and publicity activities.

During the project implementation, 22.758 people will have access to joint employment initiatives, representing a contribution of 4,55 % to the result indicator, greater than the 4,12 % contribution to the financial indicator.

titleEn: United for a Common Labor Market
summaryEn:
The reduced integration of the Romania-Bulgaria cross-border area in terms of employment and labor mobility compared to the European context is determined by the small number of joint initiatives aiming to improve this situation in terms of: common statistics/information regarding the employment and labor mobility in the CBC area; actions in terms of activating mobility workforce in the CBC area; public-private partnerships to determine the regional problems of the labor market;  awareness campaigns on employment opportunities throughout the CBC area make the RO-BG cross-border area insufficiently integrated.

Given the above, the project objective consists in facilitating the employment and the labor mobility in the CBC area through a holistic approach that connects local public administration with private business and individual citizens from both countries. The proposed project will use a total budget of 575,676.00 Euro (VAT included) and will be executed by EMMA Foundation with the European Information Center. 

This objective will be achieved through: a CBC joint network of LPAs, recruitment companies and vocational schools; vocational training for youth in both regions; an awareness campaign for promoting employment opportunities throughout the CBC area; a CBC online job platform for economic interconnections between stakeholders.

Until the project end, joint methods and common tools will be created and more than 1.000 beneficiaries will be directly involved.

titleEn: A chance for development
summaryEn:
The project “A chance for development” aims to increase employability by developing professional skills and by ensuring a better communication between employer and the persons that are in search of a job in the counties of Dolj, Vidin and Veliko Tarnovo. Its priority is the inclusion in the labour market of students and university graduates of the region of implementation of the project. In this region, the unemployment rate is high enough (8.9% in Dolj and 23% in Bulgaria), the unemployment rate for young graduates tops 7% in Dolj and 18% in Bulgaria. 

The general objective of the project is to increase the degree of employability by developing the workers’ professional competences and by ensuring a contact between the employer and the unemployed. The value of the project is of 749 062,46 euros. Activities included: information and promotion, selection of the target group, professional training for the target group, the setting-up of a Romanian-Bulgarian centre for career and recruitment, Design of an interactive site and organisation of themed meetings between the employers and persons in search of a job, Working visits of students and professors to potential employers in Bulgaria and Romania. 

Expected results: 14 initiatives (12 initiation and training courses, 1 internet domain, 1 job fair), 400 participants in local joint and employment initiatives, 300 participants in joint education and training programmes.

titleEn: Development and promotion of a common natural heritage tourism product: Route “Protected natural heritage within the cross-border region Romania-Bulgaria”
summaryEn:
There are a number of protected natural sites within the CBC region - nature and special status parks and reserves. These areas are included in a network of Danube parks and they all have management plans, which integrate tourism management sections. A more targeted approach in the cross-border region is needed to attract tourists, to promote and enhance the common natural heritage and sustainable management of the ecosystems. The measures entail a common product development; networking and exchange of good practices of innovation in preserving the biodiversity and green infrastructure through tourism; and broad public consultations.

The Project’s objective is to enhance the sustainable use of the Romania-Bulgaria CBC area common natural resources through the development of a common natural heritage tourism product: Route “Protected natural heritage within the cross-border region Romania-Bulgaria” and campaign on the preservation, promotion and development of the common route. Total project budget: 807,493.92 Euro.

The main activities within the Project are 8 round tables, 1 conference, 1 common preliminary study on natural heritage, 2 common strategies: 1 on the development and 1 on marketing of the natural heritage tourism product, and 1 set of tourism product promotional materials.

The Project will attain the following results: 1 integrated tourism product, 2 common strategies, increase in expected number of visits with 40,000, and increase of overnight stays with 40,000.

titleEn: The Path of Clay
summaryEn:
Clay has had many different uses since it was found by the humans. Some of the oldest clay artifacts (5600 – 5300 B.C.) were found in the area of the Lower Danube. One of the newest and inspiring theories (theory of Harold Haarmann) is creating a new paradigm in historical science that the so cold Danube script wrote in clay is the oldest writings of an ancient civilization existing in the Balkans 8000 thousand years ago. Since then clay was used for occult objects, jewels, pottery, housing, decorations, art, etc. The entire clay historical heritage in the area of Lower Danube is rich and inspires great scientists, writers, researchers and history fans, but is still unknown to the wide tourist audience. The existing potential for development of boutique tourism based on clay and its promotion is not utilized and no integrated tourist offerings and itineraries are available on the tourist market for it. 

The project proposal aims to improve the sustainable use of this cultural heritage. The total budget of the project is approximately 381 344.09 euro. The project activities are: development of JCB tourist itinerary "The Path of Clay" and common strategy for boutique tourism, complete verbal interpretation for guides, promotion of the new tourist product; establishment of an Open Air Museum in Cherven Bryag; implementation of training in sculptural techniques, 4 clay workshops and 4 festivals; promotion of the new tourist product and services provided. The results contribute to the program indicators with: one integrated tourism product with 3 new tourist services, developed one common strategy, increase of the expected number of visits to supported sites of cultural heritage and attraction with 3000 people, raised tourists overnights in the CBC region with 1350.

titleEn: Cross Border Cooperation Audio Travel Guide
summaryEn:
The Romanian-Bulgarian cross-border region is extremely rich in cultural and natural heritage (which is the basis for numerous tourism activities, an important source of added value for any vacation) but suffers from a poor promotion of this heritage with negative effects on the number of tourist overnights in the area.

The CBC Audio Travel Guide offers the solution to the tourist retention problem, by improving the sustainable use of natural heritage and cultural heritage and by better promoting the tourism attractions and activities in the cross-border area.

The project objectives will be achieved through the design of 5 comprehensive tourism products specific to the RO - BG cross-border area and the provision of a new, integrated audio travel guide service.

With a total budget of 701,396.75 euro, CBC Audio Travel Guide will generate the following results: 

an inventory of the 1.500 main tourism attractions in the region, divided into 5 categories,

an integrated audio travel guide service, offering information about the tourism attractions. This service will be available by calling a dedicated phone number or, for those who have an Internet connection, by downloading a mobile devices application that integrates the GPS tracking function or by using the dedicated audio guide section on the project’s website.Through jointly valorizing and raising awareness on the natural and cultural heritage of the region, the project aims to a 32.400 overnights increase by 2018.

titleEn: Developing a Common Approach to Education in Entrepreneurship at School
Young Project Manager in CBC area
summaryEn:
The word project has become one of the most used statements together with the word management, projects of all kinds being found in any organization which develops processes aimed at achieving clear and realistic objectives with direct impact on its assertion.

The project aims to support youth employment in cross border area through promotion of mobility and vocational education of young people, building their capacities in the sector of project management. First initiative will provide 375 young people with the unique opportunity to acquire both professional skills and intercultural competences.

Target groups of the 15 project management training sessions (one in each administrative unit) are the students (last classes in high schools) who will soon have to decide what they will do in future. Therefore, by organizing the training sessions, the project will enhance the character of a professional counselling and will acquaint students with what has become the most popular “job”, the PM one, developing their personal skills, preparing them for a future adequate to the trends. The second initiative will create a platform providing young students with information and details about the institutions/organizations from the eligible area opened for organizing traineeships and/or summer internships.

About 745,000 euro will be used to prepare the students from cross border region for the challenges of tomorrow, anticipating long-term employment opportunities on both sides of the border.

titleEn: Networking for sustainable use of natural heritage and resources in the cross-border region
"Renaissance of architectural past of Vidin and Dolj district"
Network for smart cooperation of Black Sea communities in the cross- border region
summaryEn:
The local public authorities in the cross border area of Dobrich district and Constanta county are still suffering from weak administrative capacity. The communities, which are facing common challenges like Black sea Municipalities from both sides of the border, are developing separately without taking advantage of cooperation opportunities.   There a  too centralized public authorities structures with low cooperation capacity and low level of  public participation.

Project main objective is to contribute to increasing the cooperation capacity and effectiveness of public administrations of the cross border region of Black Sea Municipalities in Dobrich district and Constanta county and to enhance the participation of private stakeholders in public decision-making. The objective will be achieved through  involving at least 10 local communities, represented by public administrations and private stakeholders,  in  joint instruments for horizontal cross border cooperation and capacity improvement, such as Network  for smart cooperation of Black Sea communities in the cross- border region, Joint strategy for cooperation and evolved territorial development of the cross border Black Sea area, workshops, introducing of  e-government, fostering public participation in decision-making.

Budget amount: 541 665,55 EUR.


Expected results: Increased cooperation capacity and effectiveness of public administration of the target cross border region,  enhanced participation of private stakeholders in public decision-making.

The project will significantly contribute to program result indicator “Level of coordination of the public institutions in the eligible area”.

titleEn: Listen, Educate, Act and Read in a NETWORK
summaryEn:
The overall objective is to connect pupils to their communities, by broadening their understanding of the importance of building aspirations and vocation skills, in order to ensure career readiness.

The specific objectives are aiming to develop services of career guidance and counselling, for pupils from lower secondary school (VIII, IX and X grades), by identifying pupils` preferences and skills towards employment options, and, to encourage community Leads to help spread the word by serving as speakers and mentors as a way of strengthening school-labor market relationships and improving the transition.

Project`s value is 397.056,19 € and it`s main activities are:project management, information&publicity campaign,project identity campaign,Vocational Ateliers, Strategy development regarding the role of local public authorities in providing counselling and support for pupils as future  citizens of local communities, counseling programme,Vocation Quest local and county workshops and exploratory visits, creating a web-based resources network among the stakeholders,4 study visits.

The target group consists of pupils from lower secondary school (VIII, IX and X grades) from each partner location, local public administrations, employers,NGOs acting in the field of education and local, regional and national public authorities.

Project`s results namely a cross border Strategy, a common network between 5 partner locations and study visits address both output and result Programme indicators.

titleEn: “Collective” Education
summaryEn:
The project is a reply to the research developed by the beneficiaries’ representatives in the field of students’ education for life. The neediness for a CBC model regarding counselling and guidance classes in high school represents the main purpose of the project.

In this regard, the teachers from Ro and Bg, with the support of relevant institutions, and considering the aspects from the study developed will elaborate content for the models proposed to be discussed during the classes and interactive lessons for the students. Agreements with the most relevant intuitions from both countries will be concluded to ensure the sustainability and the viability of the modules. All the teachers from partners’ high schools (around 200) will be initiated in the new technology to create more attractive, accessible and valuable lessons. A pilot action will be organized to experience the new CBC model in the counselling and guidance classes. The learning platform will connect partners, teachers and students and will provide to all the actors a source of information and a digital collection of relevant documents in the educational field.

The project aim is to increase the cooperation of the relevant institutions/ organizations/key actors, making the educational system more efficient by involving them in the educational program. The budget about 1.5M euro will be invested in providing qualitative services and will open a new age in education, a more feasible one with benefit performance.

titleEn: “Danube Partnership for Mobility and Entrepreneurship”
summaryEn:
CCIA MH in partnership with CCIA Vidin propose the implementation of the project Danube Partnership for Mobility and Entrepreneurship, whose overall objective is to increase the potential of independent activities and entrepreneurship to create jobs in the cross-border area, by developing some joint training and information schemes and specific actions to increase mobility and employment across the entire RO-BG border.

Specific activities: Promotion and visibility, Development of a study entitled Opportunities and Challenges on Cross-border Entrepreneurship, Development of a study entitled Identification of training needs adapted to the economy of the cross-border region, Organisation of 16 training sessions, the Caravan of cross-border entrepreneurship, Creation of the network of entrepreneurs from the cross-border green economy, 2 experience exchanges at successful entrepreneurs in the cross-border area Giurgiu-Ruse, 1 cross-border job fair organised in Giurgiu.

Outputs: 2 studies, 16 training sessions: M1 dedicated to entrepreneurs, M2 dedicated to potential entrepreneurs, M3 dedicated to job seekers, the Caravan of cross-border entrepreneurship: 6 workshops, 4 job clubs, 20 entrepreneurial workshops, 5 awareness campaigns, Network of entrepreneurs in the cross-border green economy, Conference of funding and development opportunities - green entrepreneurship, 2 experience exchanges, 1 cross-border job fair, 1,300 beneficiaries.

titleEn: Cross Border Cooperation Mechanism in the Field of Social Assistance at multi-regional level Romania-Bulgaria
Increasing accessibility to the TEN-T in the border area Negru – Voda - General Toshevo
summaryEn:
Negru Vodă and General Toshevo are two tertiary nodes, according to the definition from the Applicant’s Guide, as both of them offer services (public and private) to their communities and beyond their administrative borders. For example, in Negru Vodă there are banks, social assistance facilities, a highschool, medical cabinets, an ambulance service anda post office.Negru Vodă is the only city on a radius of 32 km. In the same way, General Toshevo is the closest Bulgarian city to the Romanian border and its services are used by all the communities in the area.

The two cities are connected through the European Road E675 and the Negru Vodă-Kardam custom point.From the data provided by the Romanian General Inspectorate of the Border Police, 94% of the heavy traffic in the Constanța-Dobrich cross-border area is orientated through the Negru Vodă custom point, as it represents the best alternative to the more congested, especially during summer season, Kavarna-Constanța road, part of the comprehensive TEN-T network.

Still, some of the roads from Negru Vodă and General Toshevo, as highlighted by the feasibility studies, are in a poor and improper state for an efficient traffic. The project will improve the infrastructure of these roads, and therefore, the connection of cross-border tertiary nodes Negru Vodă and General Toshevo to the TEN-T infrastructure.

The activities that will be implemented by the two beneficiaries in order to achieve the objective are related to project management, works (core activity) and publicity measures for a proper information of the public regarding the EU contribution.

The estimated budget of the project is close to €8 mil, as specified in the detailed project budget below.

The output of the project will consist in 25,53 km of upgraded roads and one joint mechanism to facilitate the connection of tertiary nodes to TEN-T infrastructure, resulting in an increase of the border population served by modernized infrastructure leading to TEN-T.

titleEn: Danube Ecotourism
summaryEn:
There is a clear lack of administrative capacity to cooperate and network at cross-border level for drafting and implementing relevant projects for the diversification of local economies through eco-tourism, a key sector given the resources of the area.

The project aims at increasing the capacity of CBA public administration and civil society to identify measures for eco-tourism development, find EU financing sources, draft and implement successfully the resulting cross-border projects. To support this capacity building, the project aims at better integrating local administrations into EUSDR relevant networks of administrations and experts. Overall budget: 749423.85 EUR.

In order to achieve these objectives the project will organize 6 series of trainings as the core activities to train local human resources – the Danube Officers. Practical applications of the trainings will be done during familiarization trips and by creating 10 eco-tourism products, while an eco-tourism conference and landscape contest will bring the CBA and the best eco-tourism experts and landscape planners into closer contact. A series of communication and visibility actions will draw the attention of the general public and of other EUSDR areas to CBA eco-tourism potential and its new Danube Officers.

The result will be a new cross-border network of public administrators and civil society stakeholders – the Danube Officers – that has the tools to implement projects for eco-tourism development in the CBA.

titleEn: Entrepreneurship for Youth Labor Mobility
summaryEn:
The project addresses youth employability and labor mobility in the cross-border (CB) area as a result of 3 common territorial challenges: the insufficient linkage between vocational education (VE) and business sector, the language barrier and the gap in Entrepreneurship Education (EE) concerning the CB economic potential.

The 18-month proposal regards these issues as opportunities. It capitalizes on the EC Report on the Impact of EE in BG and RO and develops a Joint Educational Scheme on Entrepreneurship Education without Borders (JES on EEwB). Using the cooperation approach in education, the project empowers teachers from two secondary schools in Economics in Silistra and Calarasi (B2, B3) to jointly design 3 programs within the JES: Enterprise without Borders, Green Entrepreneurship, Linguistic training with CB exchanges. Then, during the school year, the project provides the pilot JES among 800 students from these two schools, supported by the local and business communities (LB, B4, B5). To enhance other young people’s employability, the proposal invests in 2 computer labs and a Learning management system for tertiary/life-long/distant learners. Also the partners build up a joint network, encourage mutual educational validation so that CB school communities include the JES on EEwB in school curricula. Thus 3500 people, mainly students, will access 10 joint employment initiatives, contributing to the integration of CB area in terms of youth employment and labour mobility.

titleEn: CROSS-BORDER ADVANCED TRAINING PROGRAMME FOR GIURGIU COUNTY AND RUSE DISTRICT ADMINISTRATIONS
summaryEn:
The implementation of CBA represents a priority for Giurgiu county (GC) and Ruse District (RD) because it will help support the improvement of structures and processes that contributes to organizational effectiveness and will provide higher quality public services to citizens. CBA will improve the performance of the human resources while developing the management skills necessary to take performance as close as possible to the level of local authorities’ representatives from EU countries.

The project’s objective is to increase the capacity of cooperation between GC and RD administrations through the professionalization of staff and creating a joint framework for cooperation in areas of common interest such as regional importance investments and green economy.

Through CBA, the staff of the 2 institutions will expand its knowledge and skills necessary to better put to use new technologies and absorb EU funds. Activities: preparation; PM, "Green economy" (strategy), trainings, information and publicity, exchanges of good practices, investment opportunities (action plan), with a budget of apx. 750.000 euro.

Results: increasing cooperation capacity and the efficiency of public institutions in a CBC context, which will lead to a higher level of co-ordination of the public institutions in the eligible area and a higher quality of administrative actions related to accessing EU Funds for the G-R CBC area, benefiting to approx. 515.000 inhabitants of GC and RD.

titleEn: MObility of Workers and unEmployed Upgrade
summaryEn:
The project objective is to elaborate and sustain bi-lingual multi device RO-BG web based platform, as tool for self assessment of knowledge, skills, abilities as well as for  information source about labour legislation, carrier opportunities and advice on job search or change, improvement of knowledge and skills, all prerequisites for mobility and employment.

It will tackle problems of employability, mobility and entrepreneurship. The labour market continues to face difficulties in creating employment opportunities while job seekers and business suffer of comprehensive data, tools, knowledge for optimizing the mobility on CB territory.

MOWEUP covers the whole eligible area.

Our objectives are to contribute to creating an integrated eligible area in terms of employment and labour mobility; to make the workforce seize cross-border jobs and entrepreneurship opportunities; to create measurable outcomes for enabling the area to be a region to live, study and work.

Budget: 466 086.03 EUR,

Through MOWEUP portal we will achieve our goals thus enabling and developing web based
- efficient information flows evolving technologies and data integration of successful CBC RO-BG outcomes
- services for personal and professional guidance and lifelong learning
- tools, based on predictive thinking and embracing analytical techniques.

We will promote outcomes of the project and INTERREG V A, involve CB stakeholders by establishing network of CB project beneficiaries.


By joint planning, management, financing and implementing expected results are:
- increased sources of data, tools and knowledge,

- improved access to joint employment initiatives,

- boosted development of innovative career services,

- promoted employment,

- supported labour mobility.

titleEn: Active employment measures in the Border Cooperation Region Drobeta Turnu Severin - Vidin
summaryEn:
The project “Active employment measures in the Border Cooperation Region Drobeta Turnu Severin - Vidin” will be realized in more phases.

In the first phase will be realized a study to identify measures for better correlation between the individual skills, education, employment potential and opportunities in the labor market from region Drobeta Turnu Severin - Vidin.

Through this study will be determined the amount of assistance needs and  indicators content (specifying the needs and priorities of information, advice and training, concrete methods of increasing the employment of the inactive population in the labor market, domains and sectors for suitable business development, strengths and weaknesses in the labor market).

After the study will be realized two Regional  Resource Centers for Employment (RRCE) will be established one in Drobeta Turnu Severin area and the second one in Vidin area;

In the second phase for 500 persons will be provided services in an integrated program to headquarter of RRCE. After the program will be provided, 250 persons out of 500 will enter into training courses in order to adapt qualifications to labor market needs. Moreover entrepreneurial, English and IT courses will be held.

In order to increase mobility rate two job fairs will be realized and an IT platform for labor mobility will be developed.

titleEn: Improved tertiary nodes Turnu Magurele - Nikopole for sustainable development of the region, for a better connection to TEN-T infrastructure
summaryEn:
I-TeN project is developed by Turnu Magurele and Nikopole municipalities addressing common problems: the poor connection with TENT core and comprehensive network because of under-developed road infrastructure, with a high risk of accidents, and have insufficient capacity. The problems are important at national level, national institutions in the field supporting I-TeN especially in the perspective of a new bridge. The general objective of I-TeN is to improve the development of cross-border transport system of the Turnu Magurele – Nikopole tertiary nodes in a better connection with TENT infrastructure for sustainable development of the area. 

One of the specific objectives is to improve the transport infrastructure of the both tertiary nodes: 10 streets along and/or at the intersection of several national roads (DN52, DN51A), which are taking over the national and international traffic and a municipal road PVN 3123. Two joint mechanism will be developed: joint traffic management and a common information system for public transport. The main activities includes elaboration of technical documentations, works contracts, traffic management plan and purchasing the equipment; a specific study, a conference and a workshops for public transport operators in order to generate a common system for passengers. 

The expected result is: 29,865 population served by modernized infrastructure leading to TENT and the output indicators are total length of 12,223 km modernized and 2 joint mechanisms. The total budget is 7,292,395.76 euro.

titleEn: Sommilabour
summaryEn:
The project is addressing one of the main common problems at the CB-region – low employment, poor developing economies and lack of social cohesion of the population. The project will create balance between the market needs for highly qualified specialists in sommelier, the wine producers and the potential employees.

Main objective of the project is to increase employment through provision of trainings in sommelier and investing in human capital, labour mobility and integrated initiatives in wine-selling, offering and promotion sphere. The main objective will be achieved through capitalization on results under previously implemented projects MIS ETC 742 and 199. The main project activities are:

1/ Project management,
2/ Establishment of Bulgarian-Romanian Sommelier Training Center and implementation of 8 trainings for 225 representatives of the target group (105 Romanian and 120 Bulgarian participants),
3/ Upgrade of educational materials, developed under MIS ETC 742,
4/ Communication project panel – promotional activities for popularization of the project ideas and results.

All the activities will be implemented jointly with clearly distributed responsibilities and costs between the partners.

The created networks under the project and the labour initiatives will support the improvement of regional wine and tourism businesses and will increase the job hiring opportunities and labour mobility, offering fully prepared and educated potential staff. 

Project budget 748 388.06 € will cover 2.5 % of the Programme indicators

titleEn: A CROSS BORDER UNION  IN THE SHADOW OF HISTORY
summaryEn:
The project is a joint solution identified by the 4 beneficiaries for problems related to the lack of concrete actions for the sustainable use of the specific natural and cultural resources. Harsova - Krushari area is characterized by a particular historical heritage, with great relevance in the identity and development of both peoples. Unfortunately, these cultural treasures are little known to the general public and both communities are shrouded in obscurity, although the hidden treasures can certainly generate development through tourism. Therefore, the main objective of the project is to create and promote an attractive tourism product, based on natural and cultural resources of the region, able to generate and maintain tourists’ interest in a consistent way. 

The objective will be achieved by creating a modern and attractive tourism infrastructure, as follows:  the renovation and restoration of Ensemble V. Cotovu - a historical heritage building -, which is currently in a state of decay and its transformation into a Multicultural Center Museum; the rehabilitation of the access road and the connection between Carsium Fortress and Ensemble V. Cotovu; tourism facilities in Zaldapa Fortress and Dry Valley and setting up an innovative outdoor museum in Krushari. This infrastructure will join the two cross-border communities, establish and promote a tourist route between them. It will boost and maintain tourism in the region. Thus, the impact on program’s indicators is obvious: the project generates an attractive tourism product that will be supported by a joint marketing strategy for attracting tourists, thereby increasing the number of overnight stays in the cross-border region.

titleEn: Short supply-chain platform for local artisan products in the CBC area
summaryEn:
FairDeal addresses the need for a more inclusive and efficient labour market in the CB area by enabling new economic opportunities and improved employment perspectives.

The CB area has a reputation for its community of artisans and craftspeople famous for their talent and hard work. This creative potential is insufficiently exploited as a driver of employment, entrepreneurship, economic growth and social inclusion.

The project brings together CB communities in a joint development of an innovative solution for online marketing of local artisan products. Based on e-commerce potential for shortening the supply chain path, it ensures a fairer deal for both suppliers and end-customers.

The FairDeal e-commerce platform is conceived as a cybermediary application, providing for virtual storefronts, where interested SMEs, tradespersons and craftspeople of the CB area will freely host and market artisan products and services. Integrating tradition with innovation, it will alter conventional patterns of trade, increase commercial efficiency, create new employment opportunities and improve community welfare. 

To overcome innate resistance to innovation promoters will provide trainings to craftspeople. Community support network will be formed to ensure the platform’s sustainable operation.

Utilizing a budget of EUR 714 580 the project will contribute to the Programme’s objectives by fostering innovation as a driver of entrepreneurship, qualitative and sustainable employment in the region.

titleEn: Improvement of the conditions for employment of youth in the tourism sector
CROSSBORDER PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN BOLINTIN VALE MUNICIPALITY AND STRAZHITSA MUNICIPALITY IN ORDER  TO IMPROVE DECISION-MAKING SYSTEM - ROWS OF BRIDGES AND GATES
summaryEn:
Bolintin Vale Municipality and Strazhitsa Municipality signed a cooperation partnership in order to develop the relations between the 2 municipalities. The project CROSSBORDER PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN BOLINTIN VALE MUNICIPALITY AND STRAZHITSA MUNICIPALITY IN ORDER  TO IMPROVE DECISION-MAKING SYSTEM - ROWS OF BRIDGES AND GATES (ROBG) represents the first step in this initiative. 

The project objective is sustainable improvement and streamlining of local government capacity and cooperation in the Danube area through an online platform which will be functioning as a communication and cooperation mechanism. 

The main activities of the project will be centred on creating the online platform, training the personnel of the 2 municipalities in fields related to future cooperation, providing the 2 municipalities the necessary equipment for a proper functioning and  communication and information of the communities and not only about this intitiative and the project results. 

The budget of the project is 317.434,17 euro. The project is an opportune initiative, in a context where transnational cooperation is just an objective on some strategies, and the actual context is lacking efficient and actively cooperation  mechanisms. It is important for a municipality to share iti experiences, its difficulties and succeses with other similar entities, which also can contribute in return. 

The results of the projects will contribute, since the begining of the project, to the programe indicator, by the partnership already signed and started, and will continue as the implementation of the project will go on to increase the level of coordination between the neighboring municipalities. The mutual workshops and the platform will have an important impact on the relations between the 2 partners, and the effect will continue after the completion of the project as well.

titleEn: New skills for job quality
summaryEn:
New skills for job quality project to implement an integrated program of measures to facilitate border inclusion of the Vidin-Dolj region, to support employment and labor mobility in the region above in order to develop a labor market. Thus, 6 educational programs will be implemented, activities of individual and group career counseling, attended by 416 inactive persons aged 16-64 years, of which 200 young people and 100 women who are part of the target group. 

The activities to be developed in the project are: ​​ insurance of special programs suited for individual career counseling; Development and implementation of 64 courses in Vidin -Dolj that will lead to the development of human capital in the area, increase its competitiveness by linking education and lifelong training with the labor market, the certification of 416 people by graduating from the course; through the cross border Mobile Business Incubator, we can support business development in a startup activity on both sides of the Danube. We ensure hosting for 10 social enterprises with headquarters in Vidin-Dolj; Developing a study to identify the main economic sectors that can enable workforce mobility; Creating a cross-border integrated website that will inform more than 5,000 people in Vidin-Dolj on jobs available in the two zones. Organizing two job Scholarships in both areas Vidin -Calafat to be attended by 200 people interested in the target group.

Local budget project is  743.323,47 EUR.

titleEn: Development of the Joint Labour Market and labour mobility in the Construction field from the Romania-Bulgaria cross-border area
summaryEn:
The main objective of the policy on the labor market is to increase employment and to lower unemployment through implementation of actions towards improving the socio-economic environment and the implementation of active programs and measures on the labor market.

Because the main common problems at the cross-border region are: low employment, poor developing economies and lack of social cohesion of the population, the project proposal will create balance between the market needs and potential qualified persons in construction area.

The objectives of the current project proposal are orientated to increasing employment and improving the economic situation in the cross-border region through initiatives that activate labour mobility in region. The main objective will be achieved through capitalization on results obtained under previously implemented project MIS ETC 559.

The project is envisaged the following activities, that will lead to achieving the set objectives and are directly linked to the Programme output and result indicators: project management;  research of the qualifications needs on the construction field in the project area; meetings to promote research results at all stakeholders of the project area; drafting and publishing an dictionary of specific construction terms; organizing and unfolding of authorized trainings for targeted groups; organizing the  internships and exchanges of experience; setting up centers for information and counseling; job fairs for job seekers; updating portal, developed under MIS ETC 559; information and publicity campaign. All the activities will be implemented jointly with clearly distributed responsibilities and costs between the partners.

Project budget is: 489533,94 euro.

titleEn: Advanced Competitiveness Through Improvement, Vision and Education
summaryEn:
The overall objective is to change the attitude regarding the support of elderly in the labor market, by ensuring healthier,more productive and  participative lives,for this social category, with positive impact on the overall system of social protection and in the benefit of national macroeconomic development and security.

The specific objectives are aiming, on the one hand,to increase the employment rate of the elderly people by reducing occupational incompatibility of supply and demand of jobs due to the low or outdated level of the education,and,on the other hand,to ensure the preconditions for the insertion and maintenance on the labor market of elderly people in order to sustain an active and healthy ageing.

Project`s value is 467.202,57 €,the activities being: project management, information&publicity campaign,project identity campaign,Training Center, CBC Strategy to increase the employment of the elderly,development of vocational trainings along with foreign languages & IT trainings,two Agreements between Labour Agencies in the partner regions, creating a web-based resources network among the stakeholders,  2 Job Fairs in partner regions.

The target group consists of the population aged between 55 and 70 years,employers, local,regional and national public authorities,NGOs acting in the sustainable development and social economy areas.

Given ACTIVE activities,the results address 2 of the output indicators of the  Programme.

titleEn: Interactive mobile application for promoting the historical and cultural heritage in the region of Calarasi and Silistra
summaryEn:
EasyGuide is designed to promote the cross-border region of Calarasi and Silitra as a tourist destination by developing an integrated virtual tourist guide environment (IVTGE). It addresses the challenge of inadequate knowledge on the common heritage, which hampers cross-border cooperation and social inclusion and result in unstable tourist flow in the region. By promoting and utilizing the cultural and natural heritage potential, EasyGuide aims at a joint development of the area through sustainable use of its human, natural and cultural resources. This project offers a unique opportunity to create a world-class tourist service, benefitting from the local resources and the latest IT trends, thus promoting tourism and economic development in both areas. 

The project will start with a research on the historical and cultural heritage in the region to identify sites and events of interest which will be included in the integrated environment. Based on the collected data the content for the virtual applications will be prepared. Simultaneously, the technical solution of EasyGuide will be developed. It will represent an integrated environment of a web portal, a mobile application and digital info displays at selected locations.

An extensive public awareness campaign will be commenced to attract the attention and support of stakeholders, the younger generation and potential tourists. Based on this, a common management plan on how to use our natural and cultural resources in a sustainable and profitable way will be developed and present it stakeholders.For a budget of EUR 990,320 will consider the project successful if the IVTGE is successfully launched and attracts a large number of visitors. This will contribute to the Programme’s output and result indicators by:
•        increasing the number of visits to supported sites;
•        introducing a new high-tech integrated tourist service which would trigger the creation of other cross-border tourist services;
•        increasing the number of tourist overnights.
•        The management plan to be developed is widely implemented.

The project will directly contribute to the Programme’s specific result and output indicators by ensuring the sustainable use of the heritage and increase the number of visits to supported sites and tourist overnights in the region.the result you’re going for (and how is that related to the Programme indicators).

titleEn: The streamline of the traffic in the cross border Danubian area
summaryEn:
Trans-European Transport Networks (TEN-T) play a crucial role in ensuring the freedom of movement of passengers and goods in the European Union, ensuring interconnection and interoperability of national transport networks, access to them, reduce road congestion, greenhouse gas greenhouse gas emissions and increase the safety and security of transport, ensure less impact on climate. The road network modernization is pre-condition for the economic and social development. MCC and DMM possess of wide range of roads in very poor condition. Such infrastructural works are usually very expensive to be included in the budgets of the small cross-border municipalities and in the same time the national government priority is to maintain the first class roads.

MO: Improving the planning, development and coordination of cross border transport systems for better connections to TEN-T transport network.


Activities: 

1.Project preparation,

2.Project Management,

3. Information and publicity,

4.Works execution (Technical project and technical assistance provided by the designer, supervision of the execution of works, Works ).


Results: Rehabilitation of 27.387 km in RO and 6.450 km in BG.

titleEn: Co-ordinated and efficient reactions of the authorities in the emergency situations in Dolj-Vratsa region
summaryEn:
The project is addressing the effects of the climate change upon the environment of DJ-VR and the common threats of natural and anthropic disasters they have to be prepared for at cross-border level, having a total eligible budget of 6,000,000 euro, to which 817,771.21 euro non-eligible are added.

The project is strengthening the joint risk management system by providing performant intervention and rescue equipment able to fight disasters and other natural hazards. For coordination, the project is establishing one operational base in each county, which will have well-trained human resources within joint exercises. The project is also addressing the low coordination among all stakeholders and the insufficient population preparedness for risk situations.

Its objective is improving the joint risk management in DJ-VR area. The main activities are: establishment and endowment of the Unit for Emergency Situations Interventions in cross border area, Craiova and of a Cross-border Point for improving the mitigation capacity in emergency situations and disasters in Vratsa; joint exercises, including trainings, in Dolj (aviation disaster) and in Vratsa (floods); awareness raising campaign for public and also for stakeholders involved in joint risk management; information and publicity.

The result will be an improved joint risk in DJ-VR area, through a better joint response capacity, preparedness and trained human resources, along with connection among stakeholders and with communities.

titleEn: Electric, Electronic and Green Urban Transport Systems
summaryEn:
Project eGUTS strives to exploit potentials of e-mobility in 8 Danube cities, regions and beyond. To do so, the existing network of 22 partners will develop innovative eGUTS Standards for cities supporting e-mobility, based on combined Feasibility Studies will elaborate and realize Local Action Plans for deploying them, develop and test the eGUTS APP smart tool, implement various Pilot Actions in the fields of road preference and parking policies, charging stations, rental spots, and more. 

Last but not least, consortium will actively intensify cooperation, exchange of experience and transfer of know-how among relevant actors both on transnational (via Expert Panel) and on regional/national level (via Regional Strategy Plattforms meetings) with strong focus on user needs (local citizens and tourists). As result, an improved and coordinated application of Danube eMOB Strategy is expected not only in participating regions but, with wider exploitation of results, in whole Danube area and further in entire Europe.

titleEn: NETWORKING IN PRESERVING THE FIRST WORLD WAR MULTICULTURAL HERITAGE IN THE DANUBE COUNTRIES
summaryEn: Fourteen project partners from nine DTP countries joint their efforts in the NETWORLD proposal to manage the sustainable use of the WW1 cultural heritage by combining it with a quality cultural tourism. Ten ASP participate. During the preparation phase the proposal needs was identified. In order to have a joint WW1 heritage evaluation there is a need to upgrade the national efforts and results on a DTP level with a heritage management plan, database, strategy, project, results capitalisation, educational events and conferences. The stock of information will allow the link to develop cultural touristic routes to battlefield and memory places. The access will be improved by using innovative ICT tools. In order to have a large public recognition on the effects of the WW1 a further need is to analyse the heritage sites availability for touristic purposes, and to attract the younger generation by educational materials, games, ICT applications, lectures on WW1 impact, testing and demonstration activities. The DTP website information will allow follow up activities. NETWORLD contribute to the DTP programme objectives SO2.2 by strengthening the joint and integrated approaches in preserving and managing the WW1 cultural heritage and resources in the Danube region as a basis for sustainable development and growth, in order to increase mobility, sustainability, common remembering and cultural tourism. NETWORLD apply a system approach in managing the WW1 cultural heritage by identifying the lacks/needs for change on the heritage topics and related target groups needs to have the linkage between the heritage management and sustainable cultural tourism. The possibilities to link people to people within different cultures in the DTP countries will be performed by a common strategy and database, increased mobility, cultural tourism, applying ICT tools,  demonstration and testing. The expected changes will be obtained by the performed activities and outputs.

titleEn: CREATIVE and INNOVATION DRIVEN ENTERPRISES’  NETWORK
summaryEn:
New ideas and innovative approaches to all production, organisation and marketing functions, if appropriately incorporated into enterprises’ strategies and planning, will assist enterprises in the MedBalkan countries to recover from the economic crisis affecting employment and growth potentials. Stimulation of enterprises’ creativity and innovation and, as a result, upgrading of their competitiveness and employment, particularly in this difficult economic climate, calls for newly designed and properly delivered entrepreneurial learning programmes. Deviating from conventional thinking suggesting that creativity and innovation are relevant for certain only “new” economic sectors, it may be argued that businesses in “older”, more “traditional” industries should also be encouraged to adopt new approaches to their growth and development strategies.  The “Creativity and Innovation Driven Enterprises’ Network” (CIDE-NET) project will be implemented by six (6) organisations from five (5) countries (Albania, Bulgaria, Cyprus, FYROM and Greece). It will support entrepreneurs in selected activity sectors to run competitive and viable businesses and enhance their effectiveness and viability. All sectors and all enterprises in which creativity and innovation could play an important role in strengthening efficiency and competitiveness are eligible project beneficiaries. Transnational cooperation among enterprises in different partner countries will be promoted through both practical and theoretical learning activities and support. Educational activities will be organized and supported by customised innovative online mentoring tools.  A digital platform will be designed and built to facilitate training and cooperation among partners, trainers and trainees and also to support entrepreneurs learning from each other. 

The CIDE-Net project’ main aims are:
(a) Development of entrepreneurial learning programs for the promotion of enterprises’ creativity and innovation in a number of selected activity sectors, in a number of Balkan States which, in many ways, lag behind richer countries in the rest of Europe. (b) Enterprises’ networking and cooperation, at both national and transnational level, to mitigate disadvantages inherent in small size and relatively poor skills. (c) Wide dissemination of Good Practices and stimulation of innovative entrepreneurship positively impacting on cross border cooperation, regional development, economic convergence and reduction of regional inequalities (d) Development of cross transnational Enterprises’ Networks ensuring project results’ durability, sustainability and transferability (e) Presentation through the Project “Legacy study” of recommendations for measures promoting cross border cooperation among “creativity and innovation driven” enterprises.

titleEn: Towards farms with zero carbon-, waste- and water-footprint. Roadmap for sustainable management strategies for Balkan agricultural sector
summaryEn:
Balkan agricultural sector faces strong challenges in terms of unsustainable resources management and GHGs emissions.Although some countries show positive development indicators,however the continuous economic crisis,the low level of participatory/initiatives undertaking by local/regional authorities and the lower capacity and educational level of Balkan farmers in comparison to other European farmers,inhibit the adoption of innovative approaches and conformation of Balkan agriculture to EU policies, mainly at farm/local level.The project conception shares deeply the willingness of the farmers to protect the environment but also their deep concern to develop their skills,modernize and increase the profitability of their enterprises by reaching EU and international markets.Hence,BalkanROAD will provide tools and policies for economic development,through the adoption of environment protective practices which is a strong motivation for farmers to adopt and implement project’s outcomes.

BalkanROAD has two orientations, which will be combined and integrated into a Balkan Roadmap and are anticipated to open new trade horizons for Balkan agricultural products, boosting also local and national economies; namely: 

(1)to improve Balkan agricultural environment by developing strategies, methodologies and technologies for natural resources conservation (soil, water, air), reduction of GHGs, reduction of waste generation/disposal and increase recycling/reuse ratio in farm systems, (2)to develop a common Balkan Protocol for the production of eco-labeled agricultural products, by putting in force sustainable practices throughout the entire production line (i.e from the field to the market) so that the final products will have measurable, comparable and ultimately the lowest possible environmental footprint. A fully automated, robust but also flexible system (the ROAD tool) for recording, calculating and reporting the environmental footprint of the marketable products will be tested and demonstrated in 3 agricultural pilot enterprises in Greece, Bulgaria and FYROM.Stakeholders have a strong participatory role. A multidisciplinary group of 15 stakeholders from all 5 five participating countries, operating in agricultural sector will be involved in the project’s actions and cooperate in order to (1)identify problems, gaps and propose most appropriate solutions, (2)provide the consortium with data for the development of the Roadmap, and (3)identify the appropriate policies and governmental instruments for Roadmap adoption by national policies and implementation at local/regional/national level.To ensure sustainability of project’s outcomes, a broader stakeholders’ network has already been established, namely “ROAD for Balkan Agriculture”, who are ready to follow project’s outcomes, express their point of view during transnational dialogue events and diffuse data and information to the wider agricultural, market and societal networks, in which they belong.

titleEn: Fostering resource efficiency and climate change resilience through community based Air Quality Internet of Things
summaryEn: Air pollution has been one of the first environmental problems to be addressed by the EU, in that sense clean air is considered essential to good health and a basic human need. EU law has recognised this need and given legal protection to it through Directive 2008/50/EC by imposing stringent limits on levels of harmful air pollution in ambient air. Late reports confirm that up to one-third of the EU urban population are exposed to air pollution which exceeds EU limit values. Direct economic damage includes €15bn from lost workdays, €4bn healthcare costs, €3bn crop yield loss and €1bn damage to buildings. Air pollution is the number one environmental cause of death in the EU, responsible for 406,000 premature deaths. In addition to premature mortality there are also substantial quality-of-life impacts, ranging from asthma to exacerbation of cardiovascular symptoms. Health-related external costs range between €330 - €940bn per year depending on the valuation methodology. Currently the primary responsibility for complying and monitoring of the air quality is assigned to respective environmental ministries and agencies, although it is evident that all public bodies, including regional and local authorities, must take coherent proactive measures to secure clean air. The transboundary component of air pollution is significant. A state's pollution emissions are not just its own problem but affect also its neighbors. To address this issue, common environmental objectives must be agreed, and these can only be achieved if a common multi country approach is in place. The project will leverage the emerging technologies through Internet of Things intelligent air quality measuring sensors providing new, real time data through internet - forming network of connected cities jointly monitoring air quality, cloud based "Open data" system with predictive analytics and advanced machine learning capabilities enabling public bodies timely actions and feeding the general public with easy understandable information fostering sustainable way of living.  In combination with city specific guidelines and methodologies for air quality monitoring, establishment of common policy framework analysis towards decrease of regional pollutants and  3D MEMO, 3D MARS-aero and 3D MIMO air quality assessments models the project will effectively address the air pollution and will enable information driven decisions to be taken by public authorities, citizens and businesses. Essentially, it will result in increased public authorities control over air pollutants which will naturally lead to decrease of air pollution levels, thus guaranteeing compliance with Air Quality Directive objectives on one side, and on the other, preserving citizens health and ensuring clean air as basic human right.

titleEn: AgroFood Innovation Clusters
summaryEn:
For Balkan Med region the agro food sector has an important social and economic role–especially in rural communities-and is emerging as a central element for the region’s development. Despite the diversity of production systems and the different degrees of obstacles,Balkan Med territories are facing common challenges that limit the development of the agro food sector and weaken especially the small producers. Most constraints are common in rural Balkan Med areas, such as lack of innovation and productivity, quality and food safety, difficulties in promoting typical products, access to funding and the structure of the value chain at a regional level. On top, agricultural policies implemented by Balkan Med countries in recent decades have led to their increasing dependence on imports and to their total exposure to volatile international markets.AgroLabs project aims to foster the production and distribution of innovative agro food products of the Balkan Med area by organising local value chains, supporting producers in their development projects and creating new markets for their products. To achieve these aims towards the sustainable growth of the Agro Food sector, all relevant actors should be engaged. The promotion of sustainable agrofood development requires that "enabling environments", in particular those aimed at ensuring innovation, continuing human resource development and capacity building, are promoted and maintained. This will be achieved through the development of Agro Food innovation clusters, a place where research, industry and authorities can meet to co-create the Balkan Med area’s competences in innovation of agrofood sector. This will contribute to the organisation of agrofood value chains, support SMEs and producers and promote their products in local and international markets.
The main output of AgroLabs project include the diagnosis of the agrofood chain in Greece, Cyprus, Albania and Bulgaria, 4 agrofood innovation clusters (AgroLabs), Joint conceptualisation of cluster projects, Participatory development of pilot cluster project to address common challenges, to be more competitive and to generate economies of scale etc, Innovative products through the implementation of pilot activities, Regional capacity building training sessions for SMEs and local support structures in the agro food value chain and raising local authority awareness. The outputs will benefit producers, SMEs and all actors in the Agro food value chain, local/regional authorities and the participating regions. The innovative “bottom-up” approach of AgroLabs will allow to meet the needs and the aspirations of the involved stakeholders and to ensure the appropriation of the AgroLabs clusters by building a joint strategy through cross-border exchange. This will lead to the creation of the Balkan Med network of agro-food clusters. In addition AgroLabs partners acting as facilitators will provide stakeholder support throughout the project lifetime.

titleEn: Utilising Pay As You Throw Systems and Autonomous Composting Units for Biowastes Management in Touristic Areas
summaryEn: BIOMASS is a municipal solid wastes (MSW) source separation scheme, specifically designed for the hospitality sector and small / decentralized communities, aiming mostly in BIOWASTES (food and green wastes). The main tools that utilizes in order to achieve a high quality separation,is the correlation of municipal taxes with the amount of wastes produced and managed, as well as,on site treatment of the BIOWASTESs. The pay as you through (PAYT) system uses specially designed weighing equipment in the wastes collection trucks and bins with recognition chips. It allows the direct correlation of each producer of the wastes, with the amounts that produces, irrelevant if these are recyclable (glass, paper, plastic, metals) or mixed wastes, and through that the respective charging is allowed. As far as the organic wastes these are collected separately and introduced in an automated composting unit (ACU) and composted on site, reducing the collection and transportation cost, the central unit treatment cost (if such a unit exists) and allowing the production of a high quality usable product. Both PAYT and ACUs are considered as state of the art process, in the wastes’ management sector, incorporating innovative technologies. The need from all the above originates from the legal requirements of the European environmental legislation and specifically the Wastes Framework Directive (98/2008). Especially regarding organic wastes (BIOWASTESs), the target that the directive sets for 2020 is that of separate collection of 10 % of the organic wastes produced in each municipality. For Greece this target was further increased at 40 % of organic wastes, through the new National Plan for Solid Wastes Management (NPSWM).For the touristic municipalities more than 50 % of the MSWare produced in such hospitality units. A source separation scheme focusing in exactly these facilities, could help achieve part or all of the required targets, with far less resources and effort,than if implementing a relevant scheme for the general public. As all source separation schemes, BIOWASTES is more or less a social interventions, relying in the acceptability and participation of the people involved, irrelevant if they are citizens or professional. As such, any pilot activity and implementation, have some transferability importance only in areas where there are significant social, economic and administrative similarities, with that of the test pilot. Irrelevant how successful the test would be, if the next area is different, then everything must start from the beginning. As a result, an effort that is realized in the same time in various different areas, with significant differences in social, economic and administrative characteristics, then is obvious that this effort will have far better efficiency results, than any effort conducted independently in the same areas, and at the same time will provide far more important data and experiences for achieving further transferability.

titleEn: Balkan-Mediterranean Centre for Entrepreneurship and Innovation
summaryEn: The BalkanMed INNOVA Project partnership will establish a practical & innovative e-learning platform, i.e. the BalkanMed INNOVA Web-School for Entrepreneurial and lifelong learning, with a clear added-value for the European community as a whole, mainly due to the broad number of the end-users, whose transversal competences & skills, such as learning to learn, digital competence & entrepreneurial culture, will reinforce while bridging the worlds of education & business. Furthermore, the main products of the project will be the result of the collaboration of all the partners, will be produced in English & will be freely available on the internet through the project’s website for anyone interested to use them. In addition, each partner participates in several transnational networks and, through these contacts, the results of the project could be disseminated also outside the partnership countries. The trainers coming from all 5 participating countries will collaborate before the training by participating in a transnational training-the-trainers day where they are going to have the chance to exchange experiences & ideas in order to make the training of  SMEs’ staff and young potential entrepreneurs more innovative & more interesting with transnational dimention. The stakeholders’ networks to be developed in each country are going to communicate & cooperate between them ensuring in this way the maximum transfer of knowledge & expertise. Conclusively, the philosophy of the project & the nature of the activities to be implemented will enhance European cooperation, as all partners involved will exchange experiences, knowledge, expertise, trends, will discuss & address common issues, thus increasing understanding & open-mindedness. BalkanMed INNOVA Project aims to create a unified Territory of knowledge from North Albania and FYROM to Cyprus and from Ionian Sea and Aegean Sea to Danude, where there will applied virtual based tools and novel approach for learning and vocational training of entrepreneurs, technology and knowledge transfer that will set-up the Web School. Beyond the joint training, it is expected that through the E-tutoring and peer mentoring consultations actions for start-ups young entrepreneurs  will create their own new businesses by the end of the project.

titleEn: Unlocking the potentials for business and social innovation in the Danube Region by equipping young people with new generation skills
summaryEn:
Young generations have the potential to be pro-active engines of innovation and become change-makers in their local communities.  However, 62% of young people in Central and Eastern Europe are not interested in starting their own business, whereas one in five would like to, but consider it too difficult. This weak entrepreneurial culture and missing innovation management capacities are recognized as a key challenge in the Danube Region. Unlocking youth’s unexploited potential starts at local level by developing their skills and competences and creating an enabling environment to help them become their ideas grow their innovative ideas into ventures with high social added value, potentially taken up by the private & public sectors transnationally. 

The project will upgrade existing cooperation mechanisms between its key target group of quadruple helix actors including local municipalities, as facilitators, along with organisations representing local youth, education, and the business sector to create innovative local support schemes going beyond existing fragmented initiatives taking the form of INNOVATION LABS joined in a transnational network. Interweaving innovation and youth entrepreneurship support will contribute to bridging the gap between education and new generation skills needed for navigating in the changing world of work. Through organic, community based learning programs – DYNAMIC LEARNING PACKAGE, this novel support scheme will reach out to the youth, in particular young people (aged 15-29) in transition from education to the labour market, faced with major career decisions, who are motivated, but inadequately skilled to generate new ideas and take the first steps towards socially responsible, transformative entrepreneurship.

This youth focussed innovation support process will ultimately lead to better economic performance, lower brain drain and have a positive impact on the quality of the local working/living environment.

titleEn: BalkanMed real time severe weather service
summaryEn: Abrupt and heavy precipitation events occur more frequently and are more intensified than they used to be due to climate change which is a scientifically accepted fact. Therefore the application of technological systems to monitor and provide forecasting and early warning of such events is crucial to a wide spectrum of societal sectors. The main objective of BeRTISS is to develop and establish a pilot transnational severe weather service by exploiting Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) tropospheric products to enhance the safety, the quality of life and environmental protection in the Balkan‐Mediterranean region. The project aims to provide timely information and warning regarding severe weather events as well as long-term monitoring of weather and climate change in the region, through the mapping and visualization of water vapor (the most abundant greenhouse gas that accounts for ~70% of global warming and most critical meteorological parameter for accurate weather prediction by forecasting models) for the first time in real time in this region.
