Holding of 10 Dragon boat festivals in Danube towns.
Organizing of cross-border dragon triathlon 2 cross-border Dragon boat mini marathons in Bulgaria and Romania;
Organizing of 6 1-day rowing simulation events in bigger cities in the cbc area;
Promotion of developed tourism products and project events with brochures, leaflets, website, film, press-conferences, promotion in radio and TV.

The main results of the project will be: Creating a joint capacity for offering a tourist product "Dragon boats"; Engaged local stakeholders to take part in the new tourism product offer through the management valorization plan; Promoted new joint tourism product with dragon boat events, information and publicity throughout CBC territory; organized project events with over 1720 participants.

The total budget of the project amounts to nealy 498 000.00 euro.

titleEn: Living human treasures
summaryEn:
Project “Living human treasures” focuses on the cross-border challenge to valorize the preserved authentic culture in the cross-border region of districts Montana, Vidin and Dolj county for the creation of tourism products and development of cultural tourism. It builds upon the results achieved by project “Valorisation of authentic culture for cross-border tourism” ROBG-13, implemented under call 1 of INTERREG V-A program to create 2 new integrated tourist products and facilitate tour-operators and individual tourists to organize tourism visits in the cross-border region following coordinated organized cultural happenings.

The overall objective of the project is to promote local authentic culture in the field of authentic dances, singing and typical culinary and through organization and coordination of culture events to provide professional tourism offer ready for sale from touroperators and use of individual tourists. Our project will establish 3 cross-border traveling folklore festivals in the 3 districts, organize a nationwide cross-border fair for authentic folklore and coordinate a continuous offer of local stakeholders, shaped in the form of cross-border tourism products that will attract at least 2000 tourists in the region for trips over 1 day!

The program outputs our living human treasures will contribute to are:
- Establishment of a joint cross-border management plan for continuous valorization of cultural tourism, resulting in the design and coordination of numerous weekend or holiday cultural events along a touristic itinerary and transmitting these offers directly to touroperators for development of “ready for use” tourism products.

- Creation of 2 new integrated tourist products: organization of 3 6-days traveling festivals of authentic culture and a Nationwide cross-border fair for authentic folklore;
- We expect our project to result in encouragement of 2000 overnights in the target region within project implementation resulting directly from the activities in the project.

The approach of the project focuses on the creation and coordination of continuous cross-border cultural tourism offer and its dissemination to touroperators for the encouragement of cross-border cultural tourism in the target region.

The project will turn the existing living human treasures in the target cross-border area into revenue generating human treasures by performing their folklore and culinary skills through the following activities:
A1: Selection of participants – all project beneficiaries have thorough knowledge about the folklore performers and typical culinary masters in the region within this activity they will select the participants, trying to provide opportunity to all performers and groups with potential to take part in the project events and to include their coordinated happenings in the joint cross-border management plan for continuous valorization of cultural tourism.
A2: Joint cross-border management plan for valorization of authentic culture – based on the lessons learned so far, project beneficiaries will develop this tool in order to design and coordinate various weekend or holiday cultural events along a touristic itinerary and transmit these offers directly to touroperators for development of “ready for use” tourism products. There will be at least 12 cross-border cultural offers, designed along different routes and on different thematic fields. Invitations to touroperators to organize touristic groups will be sent for each of the offers with the described performances along the routes. The routes will start from Romania or Bulgaria and will have strong cross-border impact! Project team will visit all performances and assist the performers in selling their products.
A3: Cross-border trainings for dancing, singing and cooking – within this activity 3 cross-border trainings for 45 participants will be organized in districts Vidin, Montana and Dolj county lasting 4 days each to train the living treasures in dances, songs or culinary, typical for the different places in the region and thus be able to include in their performances something well-known for the guests from the cross-border region. For example one of the performances of a Bulgarian dance group could be “Sarba” in order to surprise the Romanian tourists.
A4: Traveling festivals of authentic culture – 3 cross-border festivals will be organized in each of the districts, spending a day in 5 different localities with 100 guest performers from the other 2 districts and 50 local performers from the different localities. For this purpose a mobile scene and professional sound system will be purchased to enable the organizers to achieve sustainability of the project. The event will be promoted to attract many visitors.
A5: Presentation at 2 tourism fairs – the tourism products created within the project and all promotional materials for living human treasures will be promoted at the biggest tourism fairs in Sofia and Bucurest to raise awareness and encourage the tourism flow towards the target area. 6 performers will be invited to demonstrate live their skills and abilities.
A6: Nationwide cross-border fair for authentic folklore – a 3 days event with 150 cross-border performers will be organized in Belogradchik. The trained "talents" of authentic culture in 20 tents will teach the citizens and guests of authentic dances, songs and recipes, allowing tourists to participate and learn. The fair will be well promoted and will be the key event in the project.
A7: Promotional campaign – within this activity will be developed a 60 minute video book of Authentic culture containing songs, dances and recipes; catalogue with pictures, text and music of the songs, the explanation of the dances and the recipes from the trainings; 2 press-conferences in each district; at least 38 press-releases, sent to journalists and touroperators before and after each event and each coordinated tourist route with cultural happenings; promotional materials such as t-shirts, caps, diplomas, etc.
A8: Project management – 8 team meetings will be held in both countries to synchronise the efforts of project beneficiaries in order to implement activities most efficiently and achieve maximum results.

The project is innovative with the travelling festivals and the idea to support tour-operators with ready-for-use cultural offers along different routes in the cbc area in order to create a strong tourism flow towards the target region, thus developing cultural tourism. Main stress is put on participation of tourists in project events and enabling different performers receive revenues from the touroperators or individual tourists for the happenings organised and coordinated within the management plan for continuous valorization of cultural tourism.

The project is soft, not revenue generating. Project indicative budget is 499500euro.

titleEn: Improving quality and accessibility of social health care services in cross-border regions
summaryEn:
The project supports the effective implementation of public health policy in the territory of Thessaloniki Region and Blagoevgrad Region for improving quality and accessibility of social health care services in cross-border regions in accordance with the legislation and the recommendations of the EU, with a view to preventing possible risks to the health of the population in the CB region. It enhances  connectivity and mobility by providing mobile medical equipment for the project partners. It concentrates on actions that promote the quality and efficiency of primary care services and actions of cross-border added value such as telemedicine and mobile health services, increase  of capacity, efficiency and effectiveness of intervention in emergency cases. The project implements the European model of telemedicine, which allows for effective prevention of socially significant diseases such as cardiovascular disease, carcinogenic risk, diabetes, etc., in areas with limited access to highly specialized medical activity.

Information added on 2021-02-10, regarding the mitigation of the effects of COVID-19 (the coronavirus pandemic that started in 2019) (English language only): The consortium of “Heath Care Center” is in the first line of combating COVID-19. 
In Bulgaria, the Regional Health Inspection-Blagoevgrad is the main state institution coordinating the Covid-19 response in Blagoevgrad district. Thanks to the equipment purchased by the project - a mobile health station to make field exams in remote areas and an Elisa system to identify Covid-19 cases - it has significantly upgraded its capacity for conducting state health and anti-epidemic control, directly related to combating the pandemic. In addition, the Center for Emergency Medical Care-Blagoevgrad with the acquisition of a new mobile health care unit, with high-tech mobile medical equipment and a Telemedicine system, ensured the timely arrival to the remote CB area, and the provision of health services to all patients with suspected COVID-19. The patients were duly accepted and transported for examination and hospitalization in the nearest hospital. 
In Greece, Papageorgiou General Hospital has witnessed until now the highest number of Covid-19 cases in the region. The medical equipment, delivered with the support of the project was essential for meeting the operational needs of the Intensive Care Unit in view of the increasing number of patients. The equipment supported the medical staff to assess and treat many different cases, whereas Elisa system is constantly being used for the Covid-19 antibody detection tests. Finally, the training sessions on "Telemedicine" and "Emergency response plans and protocol in crisis situations" held by Papageorgiou General Hospital, increased the capacity of the Bulgarian partners to react to the Covid-19 pandemic.

titleEn: Improvement of the transport safety in the common Bulgarian-Romanian stretch of the Danube river through development of the emergency response by cross-border cooperation
summaryEn:
The project is developed by the partnering institutions as a result of years of joint cooperation, commonly conducted missions and bilateral activities in the Danube river basin and the cross border cooperation region Romania-Bulgaria. The Executive Agency "Maritime Administration" (EAMA) acting as a Lead partner is the central specialized authority in the field of safety and security of ships, subordinated to the Ministry of Transport of Bulgaria and is also the National Competent Authority responsible for the co-ordination of search and rescue and emergency response activities in accordance with the national legislation on the Danube River. In Romania, Ministry of Interior is supported by the Romanian Naval Authority (RNA) in search and rescue and emergency response activities on the Danube River.


The present project is directly addressing and tackling a few important common challenges of the programme area related to the Danube River safety and navigability all year round. The project partners are responsible for the identification of location of accidents on the Danube River. In Bulgaria the  search and rescue activities of people who may be in distress or who have been missing as well as handling of the emergency response in cases of shipping related disasters is performed by the lead partner and in Romania the beneficiary is supporting Ministry of Interior in the same field. The two institutions are often partnering and assisting for the above described activities in the common stretch of the Danube River and they often collaborate sharing all their resources and expertise. The usual activities are related to the following common issues addressed by the project:

- Reaction in Ice conditions on the Danube - this phenomenon could lead to freezing to 100% of the river surface and consequently causing material damage to both the vessels and the coastal infrastructure.
- Reaction in pollution of the river by oil products spill as well as other hazard and noxious substances as a result of shipping activity. Such disastrous events usually lead to contamination and water pollution in the areas of the ports and are particularly dangerous in the areas with water catchment (captivity) – source of water supply to large groups of citizen. Such unwanted events cause damage to the flora and fauna inherent in the Danube region.
- Reaction in case of Emergency in transport of radioactive and toxic cargoes on the river - particularly dangerous for the transport of used or fresh enriched nuclear fuel for the needs of the nuclear power industry.
- Reaction in case of Fire on board a vessel - this emergency situation can lead to human casualties and fuel-lubrication spill over board in large quantities.
- Reaction in cases of Cross-border pollution - usually occurring in major accidents in neighboring Danube countries and the measures taken cover the institutions of more than one country.

The overall objective of the project is to improve the safety of river Danube navigability for the whole length of the common stretch between Romania and Bulgaria through the development of common Geographical Information System for Emergency Response, supply by EAMA of specialized non-self-propelled crafts (barges) carrying emergency response equipment to be anchored across the common stretch of the river. As Romania already has such equipment this will provide even capabilities on both sides of the common stretch. RNA will supply multipurpose self propelled crafts which will be capable to reach high speed and will carry first aid equipment.

The expected change our project will make is providing more coordinated actions of the two institutions; development of an IT supporting tool for information sharing and coordination which will further improve the communication and synchronization of emergency response activities on the Danube; improve the capacity of the rescue teams and shorten time for reaction in calamity events and provide more adequate and up to date equipment for more efficient rescue missions on the Danube river.

The Programme outputs of the third call of Interreg Romania – Bulgaria 2014-2020 targeted by our project contributes to I3 - Number of studies, strategies and action plans to improve safety of the navigation on the Danube and the Black Sea supported and I4 - Total length of new or improved inland waterway.

Management of the processes of river safety requires systematic approach including the development of harmonized system “Human factor – machine - environment”, which has to be developed so that it eliminates all possible fatalities. In our project we address the improvement of safety through harmonization of action between the partnering countries. The approach is required due to the sensitivity of the matter namely the rescue of human lives, dramatic improvement of the safety of shipping even in ice conditions and environment protection. First and most important is the relevant and up to date Geographical Information System which will provide IT support for the coordinated use of the available resources. There were many cases where the most adequate reaction of a calamity alert could be provided by an emergency response team located and operated by the country on the other side of the river. The synchronized activities in events of distress require complete picture of the resource available (it ensures most adequate expert decision and emergency response management reducing the index and percentage of fatalities).

Cross-border approach is needed in order to achieve the required level of cooperation between the responsible emergency response (EAMA) and support (RNA) institutions, improve information sharing and synchronized action for improvement of the inland waterway navigability safety. Currently there is no geographic information system between Romania and Bulgaria although the two institutions need to know exactly where on the Danube stretch is located the nearest needed resource for coordination and support of emergency response.

The proposed project activities are new for the region both in matter of type of equipment to be provided, Geographic Information System to be developed integrated and used in missions.

The estimate budget for the project implementation improving significantly the navigability safety in the whole length of the common Bulgariamn-Romanian stretch of the Danube River of 470 km (292 mi) is 5.73 million euro.

titleEn: Remember the war, appreciate your liberty
summaryEn:
Project “Remember the War, to appreciate your liberty” addresses the issues of sustainable use of natural heritage and resource and cultural heritage. The historical heritage in the cross border area isn’t exploited at real value especially in the both representative towns, Calafat and Vidin, important locations in unfolding historical events from 1877-1878 period, considering that Calafat was the location where the Independence War started, from here it was launched the first salvo. More than that, across the Danube valley, on both sides, exists an impressive number of monuments dedicated to this event, monuments that are not included in a tourist product. We aim to create and promote a representative tourist product for the cross-border area Calafat - Vidin by bringing to life the athmosphere of 1877-1878 Independence War battles and inauguration of an event, “Calafat and Vidin in 1877-1878 period”, with cross-border resonance. The major challenge is the reconstitution of the battle “Calafat and Vidin in 1877-1878 period” in order to create epochal and historical atmosphere, which will be the emblem of the both towns, Calafat and Vidin, in order to attract more tourist in this zone. The aim is to create epochal and historical atmosphere through original items or uniforms and gear manufactured including edged weapons and fire arms replicas, congruent with the original historical items, for the period commemorated. Another target is to realize the public events linked on the importance of the microhistory event: military -historical reconstitution, public presentation, contacts with the lesser known aspects of the events. Another major challenge is the implication of young pupils in the reconstruction of this battle through the military trainings, putting them in direct contact with a military outfit and military everyday life for the corresponding historical epoch. Another objective is the identification of historical monuments dedicated for this major event “Calafat and Vidin in 1877-1878 period” and their introduction in one tourist product (brochure) for the entire cross border area. The historical monuments will be the location for the next reconstitution of battles in the representative area. The program outputs targeted by this project are:
- the creation of a new integrated cross-border tourism product based on the sustainable promotion of historical events and monuments bringing to life the athmosphere of 1877-1878 Independence War battles. The project will contribute to the increase of tourist overnights in the target region with at least 500.Target groups of the project are: Educational sector, young students, for which 6 workshops will be held in the CBC area with for promotion of cultural event with historical theme; Individual citizens, Private companies, NGOs, Public sector, for which 2 workshops will be organized in order to bring attention to the issues addressed by the project and to unite their efforts for the achievement of maximum effect on tourism development and authenticity of historical battles. Journalists and tour-operators. The approach adopted by the project is at first place cross-border, where citizens, students and institutions will be involved from both parts of the Danube to organize joint events, inspiring them all. The approach of selection of participants will be non-discriminative, following clear selection criteria, equality between men and women, equal opportunities. Most importantly, the approach for the creation of the new joint tourism product will rely on authentic historical sources and will try reproduce the events in most authentic way. Within the project will be elaborated a promoting movie which will contain the reconstitution of the battle also including a short presentation of the historical monuments dedicated to heroes fallen in 1877-1878 Independence War. Project activities will be: project management, 6 Workshops for high school pupils, 2 Workshops addressed to local authorities, 6 “Military trainings”, “Calafat and Vidin in 1877-1878 period”. The main result of the project will be a created and well-promoted tourism product based on historical potential of the region, untapped at his real value, based on the existence of many monuments lifted in honor of fallen heroes in 1877-1878, on both sides of the Danube, monuments which aren´t included and promoted in no any cross-border tourism product. This is an entirely new project idea, never implemented so far. It is most valuable with the inclusion of young people in historical events and bringing the institutions together, engaged to make the project achieve the best results. The approach of the project is to use the rich historical resources of the region in order to transform them in a winning tourists tourism product. The budget for our operation is nearly 500.000,00 euro.

titleEn: Tourism as a bond of perspective development of border region
summaryEn:
The present project is addressing the mutual problem of lack of investments in reconstructing, preserving and popularizing valuable cultural and historic monuments and sites in the CBC region which are lockated in smaller towns. The monuments which will be renovated are of great importance to the people of the towns of Dolna Mitropilia and Motatei. These are respecitvely the Roman Ad Putea Road Station (Dolna Mitropilia) and Church of St. Nicholas (Motatei village) . Through conservaton and restauration works, and investment in their socialization they can be included in the tourist routs in Dolna Mitropilia and Motatei which will help create an integrated tourism product for the two municipalities - "Archeology and culture". This product will not include only these two sites but also other cultural sites in the region - remnants of roman villages, churches, monasteries and others. It is expected that the results of this project will help the people from the municipalities to visit the historic and cultural sites more easily and will also attract tourists from other towns and countries. The work of reserchers in the filed of archeology, iconography and religion will also be stimulated. The created interest and development of the tourism will stimulate the municipalities as well as other organizations to look for additional funding and initiatives focused on reastauration and preservation of the cultural and historic monuments.

The main objective of the project is to bring together the people in the region through protecting their common cultural and historic heritage and further contribute to their economic wellbeing; to improve the cultural heritage of the Euroregion and to increase public awareness of the importance of the cultural and historic heritage of the region through creating integrated tourism product - "Archeology and culture".

The programme output indicators this project is contributing to are - I9 - Number of integrated tourism products/services created - one integrated tourism product - "Archeology and culture"; and I10 - Number of common strategies, policies or management plans for valorising (including raising awareness) the cultural and natural heritage through its restoration and promotion for sustainable economic uses - developed common management plan for restoration and promotion for sustainable economic use of historic and cultural sites; development of marketing strategy for promotion of tourism product "Archeology and culture".

The partners in the project are planning to implement it through common management and sharing of practices. In this case the CBC approach is needed due to the motivation of the partners to create a niche tourism product including less know cultural and historic sites. There are many projects impemented in the region that have put focus on creation of tourism destinations, but they include only bigger towns and already developed cultural sites. And in the CBC region there are many small villages with hidden trasures - cultural and historic monuments that are waiting to be descovered. Their popularization is of vital importance to their survival for the future generations.

The indicative project budget is 1 489 955.57 euro and it is entirely dedicated to conservation and partial restoration of stone walls, socialization public works and video surveillance, construction of a building of an information and visitor center with adjoining infrastructure, parking, public works and establishment of a park area for Roman Ad Putea Road Station; Church of St. Nicholas (Motatei village)- Consolidate of church and bell tower; Restauration of interior painting; Change and repair of the roof; Create Heating system for church; Build an exterior access for people with disabilities; Exhibition of heritage objects in church; as well as soft measures for developmen of strateging documents for common management plan for restoration and promotion for sustainable economic use of historic and cultural sites and creation and promotion of tourism product "Archeology and culture" and its popularization.

titleEn: Friendly destinations for seniors +55
summaryEn:
The proposed project focuses of the cross border challenge to create a new innovative touristic product. The cultural, historic and natural heritage, the folkloric tradition, have already constituted interesting and attractive touristic product. But unfortunately till the present moment still is not developed one important niche of tourism sector – tourism for seniors. No one touristic agency from Bulgaria or Romania is dealing a product for senior tourists. In general, seniors in retirement ages have more spare time and are willing to spend it on tourism. For this reason is the most important all stakeholders of both regions to use this and to developed product for senior tourists.

Project overall objective is to initiate development of tourism product designed for tourists aged 55+ in low season and set basis for promotion of such tourism product.The partners will prepare conditions and implement pilot for development of tourism product targeting tourists aged 55+, will facilitate promotion of tourism product and will improve capacity of stakeholders in the sphere of senior tourism.

The programme outputs, which our project will contributes are:
Development of an integrated touristic product for seniors (55+) in low season.
Elaboration of Needs assessment analysis on senior tourists preferences and Study on senior tourism development in Vidin, Montana and Dolj regions.
Development of Strategy and guidelines for development of senior tourism;

Our project will contribute to result indicator with 480 overnights in the Vidin, Montana and Dolj region within project implementation resulting directly from the activities in the project.The approach of the project is to use an undeveloped touristic niche and through innovative approach and available resources to attract senior tourists to the CBC region and to provoke their interest. The main idea of the project is to connect people and communities from both regions in order to  use in a sustainable way and natural heritage and increase the cross border tourism. To promote 3 regions as tourists destinations for senior tourists; to create conditions to improve the sustainable use of cultural and natural heritage in the regions; to present the new touristic products and potential for tourism development and to increase CBC.

Project provides positive impact to cross-border area where is no any tourism offer of that kind for seniors in low season. Thanks to the project, the partners will attract senior tourists to visit 3 regions. Indeed, senior tourism appeared as main opportunity for businesses so senior tourism will be a positive response to seasonality negative effects and will assists for development of both regions as wanted touristic destination for seniors. In general, seniors in retirement ages have more spare time and are willing to spend it on tourism.  It is necessary only to developed and promoted attractive touristic product for seniors to attract more tourists in the target region: Vidin, Montana and Dolj.

The project will achieved that through the following activities:
A1: Project management. Joint project team of 3 partners, 8 team meetings and regular skype meetings will be held to ensure proper project implementation.
A2: Elaboration of Needs assessment analysis on senior tourists preferences in BG and RO. The aim is to assess current state of the senior people’s (age 55+) travel and tourism preferences and to identify needs and constrains of seniors and their need for joyful vacation.
A3 Elaboration of Study on senior tourism development in Vidin, Montana and Dolj regions in BG and RO. The study will contain information of tourism facilities in 3 target regions about accessibility and attractiveness for people aged 55(local sights, restaurants, hotel suitable for seniors, all services, interesting places, etc) for 3 adequate for seniors touristic routes.
A4 Development of Strategy for development of senior tourism for business, public and civil sector. It will contain suggestions to business, public and civil sector and guidelines to stakeholders how to be more competitive in tourism market and to provide adequate services according demand of senior tourists. It will contain best EU practices for working with senior tourists and for promotion of 3 touristic routes.
A5 Organization of one Workshop in Vidin district for stakeholders in order to introduce them of benefits of development of senior tourism product in low season and test one destination- (2 days event). Participants 20 from BG and 20 from RO. They will be acquainting with Need assesment analysis (A2) study (A3) and strategy (A4). A6 Pilot testing of new product (20 seniors from BG, 20 from RO) 5 days duration. The purpose is feedback from direct target group and improvement of route.
A7 Promo campaign -1 promo interactive movie (15 minutes) for presentation of new touristic offers in Bg, RO, EN, 1 movie for four season offer. 2 Info brochures with new touristic offer in BG, RO and EN. Facebook page for promotion, 3000 colourful thematic touristic cards with sights of 3 regions,900 colourful calendars , containing objects from 3 regions, 1000 copies Mini CD-album- (50 MB), containing photos and short information of most interesting places, 3 roll up.
A8: Development of web senior friendly portal. On the basis of results from A2,A3 and A4, will be develop portal. It will contain all accommodation, bar and restaurants, historical and natural sights in 3 regions and provide for each criteria, level of hardness for seniors to reach the offer and convenience, 3 pilot routes. This portal will be used as a communication and a creative tool to brand CB region as the best destination for seniors for low season period. It will be adoptable for smartphones.
A9. Elaboration of 60 Smartpoint. The idea is to put 60 Smart points at key points in the 3 regions (20 in Vidin,20 in Montana, 20 in Craiova) which contain info about the objects and infrastructure.
A10 Demo tour for promo of new product and 3 target regions as wanted and suitable place for senior tourist. It will visit all places of 3 proposed routes and test and consume the new product. The tour will be attended by 40 representatives of tour agencies, medias and etc and will last 5 days (20 from RO and 20 from BG).
A11: Three Final promo conferences (2days event) in Vidin, Montana and Dolj district with 40 participants each. The aim is to present a new product for seniors in low season, 3 pilot touristic routes and test by one destination of each route in the CB area with stakeholders. 
A12.Media campaign 18 press realises, 4 press conferences, 6 TV spots.

The total budget of the operation is 455000 euro.

titleEn: Equipment save our lives
summaryEn:
Motatei municipality and Montana municipality, in partnership, created this project with a focus on establishment of measures for safer common region. The project presents a complex of activities, which are addressing the effective risk management, prevention and reaction of natural disasters in the CBC region with emphasis on the floods and fires.

The overall objective of the project is to improve joint risk management in the cross-border area. The current project aims to achieve reduction of the vulnerability of the environment and to prevent the consequences of social and economic disaster caused by flooding or fires in the border region. The logical line of the current project is that some measures are best suited to be managed at municipal level, such as the improvement of natural drainage to prevent pluvial flooding or ensuring the necessary equipment for quick reaction.

The project envisages for implementation a logically constructed set of measures (activities) for establishment of a risk management conditions in municipality of Montana (through supply of equipment - backhoe loader, rescue platform,Tipper with hydraulic crane, 4x4 Pick-up (2 pcs.), Mini front loaders (2 pcs.),  Agri tractor and trailer and municipality of Motatei (through supply of equipment, backhoe with hydraulic kits, cups and picnotes to decolmate the river and a fire truck); elaboration of analytic and strategic documents and training and awareness raising events which will help bring together the communities and management processes of the Romania-Bulgaria border region to participate in the joint development of a cooperative area in a sustainable way.

In most cases, during disasters the response time and resources in rural areas are greatly reduced. Handling disasters, those catastrophic events which stretch the capacity of municipalities, can only be approached with preparedness, pre-planned reaction and the availability of appropriate equipment. The partners aim to prevent this thought the supply, which is object of the current activity. The establishment of working CBC cooperation for joint actions aimed at improvement of the joint risk management in the cross-border area - a result of the project, will help CBC population to benefit from actions of risk management and flood protection measures.

The new about this approach to risk management is that preparedness will be achieved at a satisfactory level of readiness to respond to any emergency situation through programs that strengthen the technical and managerial capacity of the municipalities. These measures can be described as logistical readiness to deal with disasters. This capacity to respond to emergency situations will be further supported by the developed under the project strategic and analitical documents and the organized trainings and information campaigns.

The Programme outputs targeted by this call to which the project contributes are:

I16 - Population benefiting from flood protection measures - By the delivered equipment and the trained staff the two partners will be able  to provide fast support to the municipality and to neighboring localities, on the basis of  partnerships, which together with the commune of Motateis inhabitants 6935 inhabitants and for  Montana - 44 502 people - in total 51437 people from the CBC region will be benefiting from flood protection measures. In addition, in case of emergency situations, the two partners can help with their equipment to other neighbouting municipalities in the region.
I18 - Number of joint partnerships in the field of joint early warning and emergency response - this indicator will be achieved through the build capacity of the two municipalities for reaction to risks related to floods -  1 joint partnership between the partners under the project – Montana Municipality and Motatei Village. The partnership will be focused on establishment of measures for safer common region throught a complex of activities, which are addressing the effective risk management, prevention and reaction of natural disasters in the CBC region with emphasis on the floods and fires. After the end of the project the created partnership will continue operating for the future development, maintenance and promotion of the established measures.

The estimated project budget is 997 556.19 euro VAT included.

titleEn: Joint risk management for efficient reactions of the local authorities in the emergency situations
summaryEn:
Common challenge of the programme area:
Belene and Calarasi are two regions divided by the Danube river but linked together by history and common cultural, historical and natural heritage and unfortunately with joint threats and risks.
The catastrophic floods that affected Bulgaria and Romania last years’ proved that the two countries are also affected, more and more, by the global climate changes. The meteorological implications are already present in Bulgaria and Romania through phenomena like: quick switches between extreme precipitations and floods and extreme heat and drought as well as modifications in traditional season meaning.  The climate of the region is lately characterized as being hotter and dominated by extreme natural phenomena. The aftermath of this is expressed in human casualties and serious material damages. This imposes quick changes in conception and way of acting in fighting and managing natural disasters.
The direct and indirect consequences of the disasters on agriculture, environment and life of the affected people are also extremely important. Countrywide floods and natural disasters have a deep impact on human settlements, communication ways and fields along the rivers in Bulgaria and Romania. Belene municipality and Calarasi municipality are being situated in a highly risk areas.
The territory around the Romanian-Bulgarian border is not homogeneous and lacks a cross-border regional identity. However, a real potential for development exists and cooperation is taking shape, little by little.
The two municipalities lack enough resources to effectively react natural disasters. They do not possess the equipment needed as well as the know-how of modern and effective crisis prevention.
Overall objective of the project: 
Main objective of the project is to  improve joint risk management in the cross-border area covered by the two municipalities.
Other objectives of the project are:
- To improve the capability of the two local administrations to prevent and react in case of natural disasters;
- To increase the know-how of local authorities concerning the prevention of crisis situations;
- To establish an on-line platform providing information for prevention and management of  crisis situations - fires, natural disasters, accidents and floods.
Expected change:
The project contributes to overcome the specific problems resulting from the fact that the two municipalities are situated in a higly risk areas, through development of cooperation, establishing partnership networks and increasing the capacity on both sides of the border for working out, managing and implementation of joint projects with clearly defined cross-border effect; to improve the coordination between the authorities from the two countries and increase the administrative capacity; to enhance the cooperation at different levels in the municipalities of Belene and Calarasi.
The equipment will be used in any case of: Natural hazards; Technological accidents; Industrial accidents; Biological hazards; Risks of fire;Social risks: large public events etc.
This project shall stimulate the regular interaction between the local and regional authorities located on both sides of the border, in order to support the joint development of the risk prevention actions, with the help of the superior supporting services, of the professional assistance and other services completed with investment operations in the development of infrastructure, necessary on both sides of the frontier.
The developed on-line platform will be a ground for further projects in order to assure safe living environment for the population of both municipalities.
Programme outputs the project contributes to:
Output indicators
I16 - Population benefiting from flood protection measures: as per the National Statistical Institute of Bulgaria, the population of Belene municipality is 8 983 people to 31.12.2016 (http://www.nsi.bg/bg/content/2975/население-по-области-общини-местоживеене-и-пол) and as per the Ghidul Primariilor, the population of Calarasi municipality is 73 908 people (https://www.ghidulprimariilor.ro/list/cityHallDetails/PRIMĂRIA_CĂLĂRAŞI/41627). The total population benefiting is 82 891;
I17 - Population benefiting from forest fire protection measures; same as above - total population benefiting is 82 891;
I18 - Number of joint partnerships in the field of joint early warning and emergency response - one new partnership will be created and sustained under this proejct.
Result indicator
I20- The quality of the joint risk management in the CBC area - With the implementation of this project a sustainable resources and know-how for risk management will be provided in the cross-border region. We envisage increase in people trained in the two regions and better management of resources. All projects activities planned lead to the increase of the quality of joint risk management in the RO-BG CBC area based on the purchase of appropriate equipment plus provision of know-how through the Workshop for promotion of best practices for prevention and the development of a on-line platform providing information for prevention and management of  crisis situations - fires, natural disasters, accidents and floods.
Approach:
Main activities of the project are: Purchase of equipment for natural disasters  prevention in the two municipalities; Workshop for presentation of best practices in the field of risks prevention;Developing of an on-line platform providing information for prevention and management of  crisis situations - fires, natural disasters, accidents and floods.
A cross-border approach is needed for exchange of best practices and lessons learned as the chalenges are very similar for both sides of the border region. The cross-border approach will allow also the exchange of experts, trained people and volunteers in case of need.
What is new/original:
We plan to use new technologies in establishing new approach in joint risk management of different types of disasters and crisises.
Project indicative budget (for both partners; the budget is divided equally 50% to 50% for each partner):
Equipment- 900 000 EUR
Workshop - 8 000 EUR
On-line platform - 10 000 EUR
Travel and accomodation - 6000 EUR
Information and publicity - 4000 EUR
Staff cost - 45 000 EUR
Office and administration - 9 000 EUR
Total - 982 000 EUR

titleEn: Sustaining Rural Tourism in the Giurgiu-Ruse Area Through its Cultural Heritage
summaryEn:
Common challenge: Rural communities in both Romania and Bulgaria - and especially the ones situated in the cross-border region - face similar challenges in terms underdevelopment, aging and decreasing populations (with negative population growth rates), weak diversification of economic activities and in turn inefficient connections to markets that would be able to absorb agricultural production from the area (coupled with limited investments in irrigation and agricultural machinery). At the same time, a number of relevant opportunities need to be considered as well. More specifically, in both Giurgiu and Ruse, local communities have tended to maintain - despite modernization pressures – their traditions and customs specific and characteristic to their area. Moreover, the region formed of the two municipalities benefits of rich natural and cultural heritages, that when considered together with the world-wide trend among tourists towards seeking authentic experiences (and sustainable tourism for that matter) in their travels, provides communities with an untapped opportunity for sustainable development.

Overall objective: In this context, the project has as overall objective the development of an integrated approach to the promotion of the cultural intangible and tangible heritage of rural communities from both Giurgiu and Ruse in order to support local economic development and the evolution of rural tourism. As such, the project aims to develop a complex joint study (in accordance with Specific Objective 2.1.1  of PA 2) that would identify the villages from Giurgiu county and Ruse district with the largest touristic potential (rural authenticity preserved through traditions and customs, practices, local architecture, products, community events etc.). We estimate to select around 20 such villages in total (10 from each side of the border). The study will include a comprehensive and detailed documentation of the cultural elements which have justified the villages’ selection (traditions, histories, lifestyle, traditional buildings, products, community events etc.) and a series of accompanying professional photographic materials (depicting both tangible and intangible cultural elements). Finally, the project will include the elaboration of a valorization strategy for all of the rural communities analysed that would have as objective the safeguarding of  the most important elements of cultural heritage and their efficient and sustainable promotion. Both the study and the strategy will be disseminated to the most relevant local stakeholders (authorities, economic actors, initiative groups and associations etc.). In order to further promote the selected villages from both sides of the Danube, the project will also include the development of a common touristic guidebook and of a photo album which will be freely distributed at tourist information centers in the region, accommodation venues, restaurants, local authorities etc. The visibility of these two products will be increased through the organisation of two photo expositions where the best photographic materials developed during the documentation phase (and included in the photo album/touristic guidebook) will be displayed.

Finally, for the purpose of securing the materialisation in time of the proposals made in the strategy, we will also organise a series of roundtable debates/events (one per rural community selected in the study) on sustainable touristic development. The meetings will be moderated by experts in the field from Romania and Bulgaria and will be addressed to and attended by representatives of the local authorities, inhabitants of the communities, and economic actors from the area. During the meetings the audience will be presented with good practice cases in local development, and support will be offered in identifying the strategic priorities and lines of action for future development projects.

Contribution to Programme outputs: Through the proposed activities, the project’s contribution to the Programme outputs will be represented by one joint study and a strategy for valorising the cultural heritage of rural areas in Giurgiu and Ruse for sustainable economic uses. This result will be directly in line with Output indicator I10 of Priority Axis 2. Moreover, through the photo exhibitions and the promotional materials (guidebook and photo album) we assume an increase in the number of tourists overnights at the level of the two districts by 500 overnights during the implementation period (compared to the year before the start date of the project).

Approach: The implementation of the project will entail following the principles of Project Cycle Management, an exploratory approach (identification of relevant stakeholders and local actors, putting forward a vision and objectives for rural touristic development as well as a series of activities through which these targets can be reached), inductive approach (the proposed strategy being the basis for future local policies and decisions) and integrated approach (involving all relevant actors in order to enhance the chances of local stakeholders assuming the strategy and its targets). The opportunity and necessity of a cross-border approach are met due to a number of aspects:
A common set of challenges (despite the potential for the development of various products and services specific for rural tourism, no progress has been made so far);
An integrated approach developed by both partners in the project and based on the experience and expertise of both parties’ personnel;
An efficient methodology that - with limited resources - identifies the rural municipalities with the most potential for touristic visibility (while also creating the basis for future thematic cross-border touristic trails for example), documents and promotes important specific cultural elements (contributing to their preservation as well) and provides local actors with an instrument (objectives, proposed activities and targets) for coordinated development.

Originality: The implication of local relevant actors through the organisation of roundtable events represents one important original element of the project. The purpose of this activity will be to better communicate the results of the study to the local communities as well as to provide them with an instrument that could facilitate the comprehensive and coordinated development of these rural municipalities. Moreover, while seeking to improve the sustainable use of local cultural heritage, our approach is to focus not on larger cities, but on smaller, rural municipalities which can better coordinate themselves around a common objective.

Indicative budget: 329.308,67 EURO.

titleEn: Welcome to the middle ages
summaryEn:
Culture and history are strongly present in the municipalities of Mezdra and Dobrosloveni. The “Kaleto” fortress in Mezdra and Romula’s roman ruins of Dobrosloveni are outstanding national monuments preserving ancient and medieval culture of more than 70 ages. These important natural and cultural resources must be used to enhance cross-border tourism in the region in innovative and coherent with the best tourism development practices way. The project challenges tourism development based on the rich historic and cultural heritage of both municipalities by establishing medieval and roman festivals that will bring the tourists back in time to witness and experience the life of their ancestors, thus creating a joint touristic product, capable to boost tourism in the region.

The overall objective of project “Welcome to the middle ages” is to improve the sustainable use of natural and cultural heritage of Mezdra and Dobrosloveni municipalities by establishing two important festivals – roman and medieval, reconstructing in attractive for tourists way the authentic life and traditions of the time, bringing together stakeholders able to contribute from all cross-border region and promoting the culture and history of the region. The project will increase the popularity of both cross-border regions for tourism and will establish sustainable events attracting people to present the ancient culture in these lands.

The project will create two integrated tourism products – the medieval festival in Mezdra and the roman festival in Dobrosloveni and will promote both festivals and middle ages traditions in the whole cross-border area and at the two most important international tourism fairs in Bulgaria and Romania. At the same time the project will create a common strategy for promotion of ancient and medieval traditions for sustainable tourism development in the cross-border region.

The current cross-border territory of Bulgaria and Romania was settled by various tribes and people, each leaving its footprint on history and culture in our historical memory. Bringing these old forgotten traditions and lifestyle to life in authentic and attractive way is the modern trend for attraction of tourists and development of the regions.

The approach of enlivening cross-border culture and traditions of the middle ages in authentic and attractive way for sustainable tourism development will be applied through the following activities: Research of festivals, events and groups, presenting middle ages and roman traditions of Romania and Bulgaria. This activity will enable both partners to discover all present stakeholders active in reconstruction of ancient traditions, receive important practical information for organization of medieval and roman festivals and outline proposed strategic priorities for development of this type of touristic product.

Based on the results of the researches a two day conference with 50 stakeholders from the cross-border area representing groups for historical reconstructions, tourism companies and stakeholders will be organized in order to adopt a common strategy for promotion of ancient and medieval traditions for sustainable tourism development in the cross-border region. Filming of festivals is an activity that will quickly promote medieval and roman festivals organized in the whole cross-border region. Two films will be shot – one for the roman traditions in the cbc area and another one for the medieval ones. Both films will be uploaded on the project website and distributed during project events and at tourism fairs. Promotional campaign is an important activity for achievement of planned project results, namely popularization of the new tourism products. The partners will produce 3 catalogues in Bulgarian, Romanian and English languages on the following topics: festivals and events; medieval and roman groups; medieval recipes. A cross-border map with locations of medieval and roman heritage and festivals will be produced and disseminated. T-shirts and caps will be produced and distributed freely to the participants in project events. Promotion in national televisions will inform the population of the cross-border region for the upcoming festivals and a website of the project will be created to provide full information about the progress of the project and the two festivals. Purchase of equipment necessary for the organization of the festivals is a key activity important for the creation of the new cross-border tourism products. LB will purchase authentic Bulgarian yurta, used by the pre-Bulgarians as mobile home. Medieval costumes for 5 characters, sound system and benches will be needed in order to recreate the ambience of ancient times. B2 will purchase the necessary equipment for the holding of the roman festival. A 4 days medieval festival will be organized in Mezdra at the “Kaleto” archeological complex. Performers of medieval happenings from the whole cross-border region will be invited to present the medieval culture, art, spirit, activities, etc. The festival will last 4 days. It will consist of the following components, which will be scheduled in the details in the process of implementation:
- Presentation and open lessons of medieval military techniques.
- Presentation of medieval dressings and rituals.
- Medieval culinary.
A 4 days Roman festival will be organized in Dobrosloveni municipality. Performers of Roman happenings from the cross-border region will be invited to present the roman culture, art, spirit, activities, etc. The festival will last 4 days. It will consist of the following components, which will be scheduled in the details in the process of implementation:
- Presentation and open lessons of Roman military techniques.
- Presentation of Roman dressings and rituals.
- Roman culinar.

The last project activity will be promotion of both integrated tourism products at the biggest tourism fairs in Bulgaria and Romania – these in Sofia and Bucurest. For this aim each partner will purchase a pop-up expo wall and will present the produced within the project promotional materials, movies and web-site.

The new and original about the project is the method of enlivening historical monuments with the creation of an attraction, an event that will bring many spectators and tourists, promoting the culture and historical heritage of the municipalities in Dobrosloveni and Mezdra and at the same time promoting all other similar events and happenings organized in the cross-border region.

Our region is full of history and culture, but this project will see beyond and add greater value to the monuments for the sustainable tourism development bringing life to the stones and enabling tourists to live back in the middle ages.

The project budget is around 495000 euro.

titleEn: JOINT VOLUNTEERING FOR A SAFER LIFE
summaryEn:
JOINT VOLUNTEERING FOR A SAFER LIFE (JVSL) is a hard project designed to improve the emergency preparedness in the cross-border area of Romania and Bulgaria. The region is exposed to a number of weather-related, geophysical and anthropic risks. Although emergency response structures and relevant legislation are in place, it is recognized by local, state and international authorities that they lack sufficient capacity. Effective risk management requires capacity building at community level.

The project’s objective is to improve the theoretical and practical preparedness of volunteer emergency response units and enhance the coordination and efficient reaction in case of disaster in the cross-border area. This will be achieved through the development of a specialized community volunteer training center in the village of Belitsa, Municipality of Tutrakan. The training center will be the first of its kind on the Balkan Peninsular to provide the full range of facilities required for accommodation, classroom sessions and practical trainings. The selected location will offer training and sport facilities, water and forest areas, where disastrous events will be simulated. Additional equipment will be purchased to supplement the existing one.

Based on the extensive experience of DGFSCP and IGSU, a joint training program for volunteers will be developed to ensure that the proper set of theoretical and practical skills are acquired and collaboration at local level is enhanced. Lead by NAVRB, over 200 volunteers from the cross-border area of the two countries will be trained within the project timeframe as a pilot initiative which shall set the start of a continuous capacity building process in organized volunteer trainings.

Further opportunities for synergies and improvement will be explored through a risk analysis of the cross-border area.  A joint report on the emergency response preparedness in the CB area will be elaborated to provide the grounds for amendments in the municipal and state regulations for disaster preparedness and emergency response.

As a result, the quality of joint risk management in the CBC area will be improved providing significant benefits to the entire cross-border population. The local communities will benefit from enhanced protection against a wide range of risks ensured by inter-operable volunteer emergency response structures and common approach. Relevant information and publicity tools will be employed to inform the general public of the project achievements and the EU contribution.

The project activities will be structured as follows:
WORKPACKAGE M: PROJECT MANAGEMENT;
WORKPACKAGE T1: RISK ANALYSIS OF CBC AREA;
WORKPACKAGE I1: SET-UP OF A TRAINING FACILITY;
WORKPACKAGE T2: SUPPLY OF SPECIALIZED EQUIPMENT;
WORKPACKAGE T3: DEVELOPMENT OF A JOINT TRAINING PROGRAM FOR VOLUNTEERS;
WORKPACKAGE T4: THEORETICAL AND PRACTICAL TRAININGS;
WORKPACKAGE C: COMMUNICATION.

The expected project outputs targeted by the Programme in this call for proposals are:
Population benefitting from flood protection measures: 4 591 666 people (the cross-border population in the high-risk category, excluding Dobrich district - moderate risk),
Population benefitting from forest fire protection measures: 4 779 754 people (the entire cross-border population),
Number of joint partnerships in the field of joint early warning and emergency response: 5 partnerships.

-       1 partnership between IGSU and DGFSCP to develop a training program and a training plan for volunteer formations,
-       1 partnership between IGSU, DGFSCP and NAVRB to develop a joint emergency response plan for common actions of local volunteer formations,
-       1 partnership between the Municipality of Tutrakan, IGSU and DGFSCP to set up a training center for volunteer formations on the territory of the municipality,
-       1 partnership between the NAVRB, Municipality of Tutrakan, IGSU, and DGFSCP to carry out trainings of volunteers in the training center in the village of Belitsa, Municipality of Tutrakan, following the training program developed during the project implementation,
-       1 partnership between IGSU and DGFSCP to exchange experience, knowledge and trainers during the training sessions.

Financial indicator:  EUR 846 005.00 for project total estimated budget of EUR 995 300.

Since hazards, both natural and anthropic, recognize no administrative boundaries, the cross-border approach is the most appropriate one. In times of emergency the effectiveness of measures is highly dependent on the actions initiated in the first hours of disaster outbreak. When time is of the essence, the immediate help and coordinated cooperation between neighboring communities is essential to the containment of disasters. Therefore, the project is focused on exchange of good practices and building a common approach in risk management and volunteer training in the cross-border area.

In addition, the project is seeking opportunities for synergies from joint risk management which will allow for effective resource sharing during crises and relieve the burden on local administrations.

Last but not least, the participation in this project of the national bodies responsible for risk management in Bulgaria and Romania, DGFSCP and IGSU, is evidential of the willingness and common understanding that cooperation is required to efficiently solve the common challenges in this area.

By ensuring effectiveness of disaster management and protection of regional resources the project will boost cross-border cooperation and sustainable growth. Focusing on grassroots approach, it will improve the joint risk management in the CB area, thus fully complying with the Programme specific objective and overall goal.

titleEn: The Joint Strategy for the Touristic Development of the Giurgiu-Ruse Area
summaryEn:
Common challenge: One common challenge addressed by the project is embodied by the ineffective past approaches to developing both cross-border and county-level touristic development strategies, namely without basing them on thorough analyses of the needs and opportunities present on-site and most importantly without including the input and feedback of actors from the communities-subject of these strategies.

Overall objective: In this context, the main objective of the project is to contribute to the touristic development of the Giurgiu-Ruse area by providing local stakeholders (including public authorities, NGOs and economic actors) with a comprehensive strategy (based on a rigorous study of the cultural heritage of the area) to enhance the visibility of the two counties as visiting destinations and by facilitating the formation of a network of interested actors that would provide their input to the development of the strategy and provide the context for private-public collaboration as a means to put into practice the lines of action put forward by the strategy in the future.  As such, the project will firstly involve the elaboration of a joint (trilingual) study of the Giurgiu-Ruse area that would seek to identify, document and present all of the attractions that have the largest touristic potential (including communities with a rich intangible cultural heritage that could be valorised), as well as local products (specific to the area) that could be capitalised from a touristic point of view. This study will form the basis for the development of the joint strategy for the Giurgiu-Ruse area. Moreover, a series of workshops (estimated 3 per country) will be organised reuniting the most important local actors in order to present them with a draft of the strategy which will be discussed. The rationale of these workshops is twofold: to sustain the implication of all of the relevant members of the community in drafting (by provision of input) a strategic plan for the touristic development of the area in the following years and implicitly to raise the chances for coordinated action to reach the set targets and secondly to raise awareness among these stakeholders regarding opportunities, existing resources and cases of good practices. With these meetings we will lay the groundwork for the creation of a thematic network - continuing to facilitate communication between those who have participated to the workshops and representatives of relevant central authorities. In this way we seek to encourage more sustained involvement of local private actors in the efforts to raise the visibility of the two counties as touristic destinations. Finally, we plan on organising a final joint conference where the joint touristic development strategy would be presented and discussed with the larger public. The objective of this final activity is on the one hand to raise the level of awareness among the larger public with regards to the efforts that are being made to develop the area in which the inhabit and on the other hand to encourage a better engagement (and targeted to that matter) of the larger community in this process and in public decisions that are being made.

Contribution to Programme outputs: Overall, the contribution of the project to the Programme outputs will translate into a cross-border touristic development strategy for the Giurgiu-Ruse area - result in accordance with output indicator I10 of Priority Axis 2. Moreover, the project will contribute to a raise in the number of tourist overnights in the Giurgiu-Ruse area by at least 500 - in comparison to the previous year to the start of the project. This latter contribution is in accordance with the Result indicator no. 1 of the Priority Axis 2. Here, we would also include the development of a network comprising relevant actors and stakeholders from the Giurgiu-Ruse area which will facilitate/increase the chances for the application of the strategy in time.

Approach: The implementation of the project will entail following the principles of Project Cycle Management. Moreover, the project will include a documentation and research approach (collection of primary data and its presentation to the wider public), an analytical approach (identification of relevant stakeholders and local actors, putting forward a vision and objectives for touristic development as well as a series of activities through which these targets can be reached), and integrated approach (involving all relevant actors in order to enhance the chances of local stakeholders assuming the strategy and its targets). The opportunity and necessity of a cross-border approach are met due to a number of aspects:
·        A common set of challenges (absence of a more recent joint strategic planning for touristic development, absence of an integrated approach in previous attempts, absence of attempts to capitalise the rich intangible cultural heritage of the area);
·   An integrated approach developed by both partners in the project and based on the experience and expertise of both parties’ personnel;
·      An efficient methodology that - with limited resources - identifies the most important elements of heritage in the area that could become more visible if better promoted (while also creating the basis for future thematic cross-border touristic trails for example), documents and promotes them (contributing to their preservation as well), puts forward a medium-term joint strategy based on the input  of local stakeholders and facilitates the creation of a network - raising the chances for the lines of action and targets set in the strategy to be materialised.

Originality: This latter aspect - the implication of local relevant actors in the drafting of the strategy (itself based on a rigorous analysis and understanding of the situation on the field, the needs and opportunities) represents one important original element of the project. The purpose here is to reach not only a series of results (the strategy, the better promotion of the area), but to ensure more sustainable outcomes, namely to encourage various members of the communities from Giurgiu and Ruse to become better informed and more involved in setting the path for future development of their municipalities.

Indicative budget: 398,400,92 Euro.

titleEn: HÎRȘOVA-DOBRICHKA, TOGETHER ON THE BEAUTIFUL ROAD OF SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT THROUGH CROSS BORDER CULTURE
summaryEn: One of the common challenges is the discrepancy between the richness of cultural and natural resources and the lack of tourists in Hirsova-Dobrichka area, located in the historical and geographical region named Dobrogea. From a cultural perspective Dobrogea is a borderless region, the common history generating a tangible and intangible cultural heritage characterized by a magnificent diversity. So, both regions are real gold mines as cultural values, but, unfortunately, these issues are barely known and deficiently promoted at local and national level. The cultural heritage, together with natural resources and specific modern infrastructure is an important factor generating tourism. The tourism represents a real chance for socio-economic progress for cross-border area Hirsova-Dobrichka, given that in this region the industry is poorly represented. In the whole area of Dobrogea, the only touristic phenomenon with real impact on sustainable development is summer tourism, which, sadly, has a seasonal character and is manifested mainly in the seaside area. From this perspective, the lack of an active touristic phenomenon within the region to compensate the seasonality of seaside tourism is a common challenge for project beneficiaries, both located away from the seashore. One of the solutions to respond effectively to this challenge is to establish a common strategy on cultural tourism and to develop, promote and maintain on a long-term an integrated cultural tourism product. These joint actions are developed for the first time by the 2 beneficiaries and their role is to animate and revitalise the cross border area by stimulating tourism and at the same time to contribute to preserving the cultural heritage of a historical region in which two nations coexist. The cross-border approach is very necessary because the culture of Dobrogea region is a phenomenon without administrative boundaries and the preservation and promotion of tangible and intangible heritage is done in a unitary way, with a bigger impact than if it were fragmented. Cultural events, Dobrogeas’ traditions and customs become more interesting and attractive for tourists if they are presented in an integrated way, unifying two different nations who coexists in a common cultural space. The common challenges described above gave rise to the overall objective of the project: to improve the sustainable use of cultural heritage in the target cross border region of Dobrogea through the development and promotion of a joint tourism product, able to maintain tourists’ interest. The project is a joint solution identified by the 2 beneficiaries for problems related to the lack of concrete actions for sustainable use of cultural resources. As we said before Hirsova–Dobrichka area is characterised by a spectacular tangible and intangible cultural heritage, with great relevance in the identity and development of both nations. These cultural treasures are little known to the general public and both communities are shrouded in obscurity, although the hidden treasures can certainly generate development through tourism. The main objective of the project will be achieved by undertaking concrete actions, as follows: 1)Conceiving a set of strategic proposals at cross-border regional level for the development of cultural tourism in cross-border area of Dobrogea, in order to use the cultural heritage in a sustainable way; 2)Creating a common tourist product  by: a)modernize the touristic infrastructure related to the manifestation and maintenance of cultural phenomena in the cross-border communities: Modernization and endowment of the house of culture CARSIUM of Hirsova, Community Centre New life–1941 of Cherna, and Community Centre Light–1940 of Lovchanci, Dobrichka Municipality; b)Promoting and ensuring the visibility of the Folk Festival “Songs and Dances from Sunny Dobrudja” organized annually in the last 50 years by Dobrichka Municipality in Debrene c)Organizing a cross-border festival of traditions and customs in Harsova - DOBROGEA CU BUNDITA SI PRESTELCA, d)Organizing a training in the field of cultural tourism, with focus on event tourism, for 20 tourist guides (10 Ro&10 Bg) from the cross-border region of Dobrogea. e)Promoting the tourist circuits established in the Strategy, related to the cultural events taking place in cross-border area of Dobrogea. The project contributes to the programme outputs targeted by the present call as follows: a) it creates one joint strategy at cross-border regional level, focused on cultural tourism. The document will be approved and assumed by the local councils of both partners and also it will be forwarded to all decision-makers and actors in the field of culture and tourism in the cross-border area. After the completion of the strategy at least 10 protocols will be concluded with the travel agencies from Constanta and Dobrich to distribute the promotion materials of the established cultural touristic circuits and at least 6 partnership agreements will be signed between tangible and intangible cultural heritage management institutions of Dobrogea region, such as museums, memorial houses, historical sites, old churches, houses of culture, etc and tourism entities to integrate the cultural patrimony in their tourist recommendations. b)The project create a joint integrated tourism product. This consists of modernised cultural tourism infrastructure, able to maintain active cultural manifestations and events in the cross border area. The 2 Community Centres of Dobrichka modernised are among the most important cultural centres in the area, being directly involved in the organization of various cultural events and especially in the organization of the festival Songs and Dances from Sunny Dobrudja, by making the preselection of the festival participants. The Hirsova House of Culture is the most important cultural centre in the northern half of Constanta County territory and is the only entity which organizes complex cultural manifestation and events in the area. The institution will be involved, together with the local administration, in the organisation of the cross-border festival of traditions and customs, held in Hirsova.The 2 festivals included in the project (the Bg. one through promotion, the Ro. one through first organisation) represents a very important part of tourism product, an essential step in preserving, developing and promoting the intangible cultural heritage of Dobrogea region through cultural events with cross-border impact.The 20 tourist guides trained are also part of the tourism product, in their current work they will ensure both the quality of services in event tourism and the promotion of this niche.The project represents a new and original measure taken by public local authorities to preserve and promote the common cultural heritage in a sustainable way related to development of tourism in the area. INDICATIVE BUDGET: 1.500.000 EURO.

titleEn: Improved nodes Giurgiu-Byala for better connection to TEN-T infrastructure
summaryEn: The common challenge of both partners is poorly developed road infrastructure to ensure better connectivity at the TEN-T and better exchange of knowledge in order to improve the local public transport and traffic safety.The quality of infrastructure networks grow slowly over time,lagging well behind the growth in demand for transport.All localities from RO side link by County road 412A – communes Adunatii Copaceni,Darasti-Vlasca, Novaci and the city of Mihailesti and Byala Municipality(BY)  are tertiary nodes but not well connected to TEN-T, situation that leads to poor competitiveness, poor mobility and traffic issues.Quality of infrastructure networks is a major factor to attract (foreign) firms and their investments.Most important barrier to road infrastructure development for the 2 partners is the financial barrier.Overall objective of B-TeN is to improve the joint transport system through effective connection of Giurgiu (GR) and BY communities with core and comprehensive TEN-T transport network.The developed under B-TeN transport networks in the cb region will facilitate interregional cooperation and will help to increase competitiveness of the business sector, labor mobility and, however, to sustainable regional development. Rehabilitation of 17,33 km roads infrastructure, - 12,53 km in Gr and 4,8 km in By- will improve safety traffic conditions, competitiveness of both partners, will allow better exploitation of tourism potential & will improve the cooperation capacity of the 2 partners in transport and safety traffic issues¬ only. A rehabilitated road infrastructure will allow improved travel time&predictability for a journey, help reduce pollution to limit traffic jams. B-TeN will contribute to the consolidation of a sustainable EU & cross-border transport system connected to the main TEN-T network.All B-TeN activities contribute to the achievement of the Programme output & result indicators targeted by this call, as follows: I1 –17,33 km, which represent 43,26 % from the Programme indicator; I2 – a traffic study, joint monitoring system, 2 black-spot maps for areas of Gr. County & BY, awareness raising campaign for safety traffic to facilitate the connection of tertiary nodes to TEN-T infrastructure: 5,  which represent 22,73 from the Programme indicator to be achieved by the present call; I5 -  7.975.000 €, 15,83 % from the Programme indicator; I6 -  29450 inhabitants - 6621 inhabitants))&7923 inhabitants (Mihailesti city with Novaci & Popesti villages included)&14906 inhabitant from BY which represent  4,72 % of Programme target.
