Network activities will create significant momentum for a green energy transition, especially in the work environments of the industrial areas of the partner cities.

titleEn: Greener & closer communities
summaryEn: ECONNECTING focuses on sustainable urban-rural mobility solutions within the 30-minute territory. Our mis﻿sion is to advocate inclusive, digital, and ecological strategies, fostering the community engagement in co-designing climate-resilient towns. We promote accessible and welcoming cities, good governance for proximity territory, humanized and sustainable mobility, green communities, and a gender-balanced development.

titleEn: Transforming cities for women
summaryEn:
The objective of FEMACT-Cities is to support the drafting of eight “Local Action Plans on Gender Equality” about main challenges regarding women's liberty and empowerment:
- a society that adapts and protects,
- a society that enables education and personal development,
- a society that enables emancipation and economic autonomy.

These challenges come together in a transversal fight against stereotypes.

titleEn: Gender Inclusion in Public Procurement
summaryEn: GenProcure will address the gender equality in public procurement, many times referred to as Gender-Responsive Public Procurement. It consists of promoting gender equality through working purchases, supplies and services by the public sector, meaning that both suppliers and buyers include, in the agreed contracts, a part that concerns the interests both of men and women, paying particular attention to its development in a way that leads to a reduction of gender inequalities.

titleEn: Restoring “forgotten” urban areas into valuable places FOR and WITH residents
summaryEn: GreenPlace is an URBACT network consisting of ten partners who aim at developing a set of activities for "recycling" unused urban areas, using social participation tools. The project takes into account not only the regional specificities and conditions of each of the partners but also introduces greenery as a key factor in limiting climate change in urban areas.

titleEn: From black to green: Driving industrial cities towards a sustainable horizon
summaryEn: In4Green is a collaborative network of industrial cities from across Europe with a shared commitment: to lead transformative change within European industry and drive the sector towards a greener, more sustainable future. Comprising cities from diverse backgrounds, In4Green aims to reshape and modernise industrial areas by improving local governance and policymaking while benefiting from the collective expertise and experience of the partner cities.

titleEn: Virtual Solutions for Real People
summaryEn: Metacity aims to increase competitiveness of small and medium tech-aware cities, benefiting from the opportunity to enhance service efficiency and citizen satisfaction provided by the metaverse. By integrating metaverse technologies, cities can create immersive digital environments for education, healthcare, tourism and public services, enabling streamlined communication, remote access to services, and personalized experiences, leveling the playing field with larger cities. Metaverse-driven urban planning fosters innovation, economic growth, and ensures that citizens have access to cutting-edge solutions, ultimately improving their overall quality of life.

titleEn: Digital Transition of Youth Work
summaryEn: NextGen YouthWork aims to further develop and improve online youthwork through innovative digital solutions at city level. By this the network works towards better aligning youth work with the opportunities and challenges posed by the online world in which young people spend a lot of time nowadays.

titleEn: Cities in action for Human, Animal and Environmental health
summaryEn: The One Health 4 Cities network aims to promote the integration of the One Health approach into urban strategies and projects. It intends to develop tools that empower decision-makers and operational teams to increase the positive impact of urban projects on the well-being and health of people, animals and environment.

titleEn: Planning Urban Mobility Actions
summaryEn: Through the development of integrated mobility action plans, PUMA aims to achieve climate-neutram and sustainable mobility in small and medium_sized cities. This network wants to engage citizens and change their attitude towards sustainable mobility in a positive way by motivating everyone to get involved in improving the environment. PUMA promotes sufficient, safe, modern and convenient alternatives for private cars to all society members, despite their age, gender, nationality, health, level of income and other features.

titleEn: Youth and urban regeneration: let's take back public spaces!
summaryEn: Re-Gen is a European network of cities that aims to support sustainable urban development and social inclusion thanks to the protagonism of secondary school students from disadvantaged backgrounds. Young people, aged between 10 and 18, will be involved in the transformation of abandoned public areas into urban sports hubs, with the approach of tactical urbanism and inclusion of green and gender criteria in architecture.

titleEn: Remote and hybrid work for thriving cities
summaryEn: Remote-IT network tackles the new challenges cities are experiencing connected to the future of work. The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the transformation around how work is organised, with hybrid and remote work models significantly impacting the lives of citizens, as well as the organisational culture of major employers (public/private). Remote-IT partnerships of cities is collaboratively exploring this emerging topic in order to implement proactive policy making.

titleEn: Finding solutions to influence the urban shrinkage
summaryEn: Residents of the future wants to address the issue of urban depopulation within small and medium-sized cities. By focusing on digital transformation, economic diversification and city branding, it will explore innovative approaches towards evolving trends in work, lifestyle and communication, to enhance the cities’ attractiveness for prospective investments and inhabitants. The network enables cities to redefine their advantages in comparison to larger metropolitan areas, and develop holistic, citizen-centric solutions that support demographic revitalisation and sustainable urban growth.

titleEn: Sharing urban solutions towards Sustainable Mobility for ALL
summaryEn: The S.M.ALL network addresses urban challenges, promoting and implementing sustainable mobility solutions for all, including safe home-to-school journeys, accessible routes and tailored Sustainable Urban Mobility Plans, realizing targeted action plans for vulnerable groups. Using a transnational approach to reduce urban inequalities, harmonize sustainable mobility practices and enhance inclusivity, the S.M.ALL consortium brings together different experiences and expertise in sustainable urban mobility aiming to foster significant changes in the urban spaces, making them more inclusive and accessible for all.

titleEn: Safe, green and happy ways to school
summaryEn: SCHOOLHOODS puts children’s health and safety on the menu of how to get to school. The cities of this URBACT network work with pupils, parents and teachers to co-create solutions allowing pupils to actively go to school on their own. Parents can then choose sustainable modes for their trips as they no longer need to take their kids to school. The school neighbourhood should allow pupils to walk or ride alone safely. Ultimately, school neighbourhoods made for pupils moving around are the starting point for enabling short trips for daily needs for everyone.

titleEn: Boosting diverse communities in digital and tech sectors
summaryEn: TechDiversity is an URBACT network of eight partners representing small and medium-sized European cities, that aim to boost and facilitate diverse local communities that are not active in Tech & Digital sectors, facing specific challenges in terms of diversity, gender equality and inclusion. Furthermore, the partner cities will mainly focus on an identified pressing issue and will support at least one diverse local group in each of the participating cities, through the action plans.

titleEn: Prioritising social impact in urban regeneration
summaryEn: U.R. Impact focuses on addressing a key policy challenge: to develop effective strategies for empowering local communities during processes of urban regeneration. The goal is to prioritize social impact and community-based practices by reimagining the way urban regeneration actions are conducted. This entails placing citizens and their social and ecological well-being at the core of the strategy, and defining a methodology for collective decision-making and civic participation in local urban regeneration strategies.

titleEn: Building welcoming communities for migrants
summaryEn: In order to build more inclusive and resilient societies, local authorities need to ensure that migrant reception and support policies guarantee that migrants overcome obstacles in accessing their rights. The WELDI network empowers local authorities to put human rights at the heart of their efforts to develop dignified and innovative approaches to welcoming newcomers. In achieving this goal, cities of this network work hand in hand with migrants and other residents, as well as with local, national and international partners.

titleEn: Danube Strategy Point – A Secretariat for the Danube Region
summaryEn: The Danube Strategy Point (DSP) is the secretariat of the EUSDR and a strategic working unit for the implementation, communication, capacity building, monitoring and evaluation of the EUSDR. DSP supports both the core strategic decision-makers (NCs) and the operational-thematic level (PACs). Also, DSP enhances the connection of the EUSDR to the EC (DG REGIO) and the DRP. DSP secures and supports smooth and efficient communication and coordination among the (TRIO) PCY, the EC, NCs, PACs (SGs) and further (core) stakeholders. Through its communication activities DSP reaches out to the wider public as well as to specific target groups and also serves as first point of contact. DSP offers technical support to PAs and supports the development of capacities of all actors involved. Taking into account the multiple challenges posed by different fields and their interconnected nature, DSP also provides necessary cross-thematic and cross-pillar exchange, where needed. Special focus is laid on support and capacity building for non-EU states. Through its wide range of activities, its stakeholder reach-out and support in core processes within EUSDR implementation and its Action Plan, DSP also elaborates and provides information, expertise, studies and data to the NCs, for streamlining and supporting the operational and political decision-making processes. DSP supports the alignment of the Strategy and funding instruments (Embedding) by facilitating the exchange and cooperation with EU programmes and the responsible authorities. DSP also provides support for closer collaboration with a wide range of strategic actors, organisations, initiatives as well as other MRS. DSP’s day-to-day work follows in close cooperation with the incumbent EUSDR Presidency while ensuring the institutional memory of the EUSDR and its operability. Since 2018, DSP is hosted by two initiator states of the EUSDR: City of Vienna and Ministry of Development, Public Works and Administration of Romania.

titleEn: DRP support to Project Area Coordinators of PA 11 Security of the EUSDR
summaryEn:
The current project is a follow-up to the two projects developed under the Danube Transnational Program under the first and second CfP. It aims at providing further support to PACs of EUSDR PA 11 in better performing their management activities related to the Strategy Implementation: day-to-day coordination between PACs, Steering Group members and stakeholders; preparation of Steering Group meetings, involvement in the work of EUSDR Presidency and the Danube Strategy Point, participation of the EUSDR Annual Fora, etc., involvement with the EU Commission etc. The project will also contribute to policy development by organizing specific events linked to the implementation of the PA 11 Targets and Actions and the EUSDR Action Plan that was adopted in April 

2020. A focus will also be places on horizontal cooperation with priority areas with which PA 11 has established common initiatives like PA 1a Water land Mobility. Contacts with Interact and other Macro-regional strategies could be established within the project duration if this could be beneficial for Priority Area 

11. Whenever possible, involvement of non-EU- members states and young people in the implementation of the project should be encouraged. Ensuing publicity and better communication are to be considers as horizontal tasks throughout the project duration. Out of the 5 pre-defined specific project objectives, our project focuses on SPO 1, 3 and 

4. Therefore the overall aim of the project is to work together to tackle security and organized crime within the Danube region. In the light of the above, the international cooperation between all stakeholders is a core part within the project. By achieving this solid framework cooperation and regular mechanisms for information exchange the project will influence positively the security environment of the EUSDR States.

titleEn: PA9 "People and Skills"
summaryEn:
In order to support the governance and implementation of EUSDR PA 9 "People and Skills" as the main objective of this project, the following activities (according to the Work Programme of PA9 and the revised EUSDR Action Plan) are planned:
Coordination: The aim is to maintain the Steering Group of PA9 as the main coordination body (network of national counterparts relevant to the Priority Area). Furthermore, the network of stakeholders will be enlarged through targeted activities like Stakeholder Conferences.
Cooperation: The goal is to deepen know-how transfer in the region and to support policy development and cooperation among institutions through Stakeholder Conferences, Steering Group meetings, thematic workshops, peer learning as well as evidence-based tools. 
Embedding/ESF MA Network: The aim of the network is to find a common ground for ESF relevant policy proposals in order to develop and establish state-of-the art policies in labour market policy, governance and social inclusion that take into account macro-regional dynamics and interdependencies in the Danube Region with competent and viable transnational partnerships.
Communication and information: To raise public awareness and to inform stakeholders about ongoing activities of PA9, there will be regular updates of the PA9 website and social media, newsletters, information materials etc. Information (about financing possibilities, relevant stakeholders and partners in the EUSDR countries, existing projects etc.) will be provided to promote the development and implementation of new projects and initiatives in the fields of the PA9 actions.

titleEn: Priority Area 10 Coordination
summaryEn: The PA10 project focuses on three objectives: capacity building and coordination of the Steering Group, strengthening the embedding process in EU funding, and enhancing coordination and cooperation among macro-regional stakeholders. The capacity building framework for the PA10 Steering Group aims at supporting outreach and strategic stakeholder mobilisation for institutional capacity and cooperation. Stakeholders such as civil society, public administrations, funding institutions, and representatives of the EUSDR Governance are coordinated in different frameworks such as the Bled Strategic Forum, the Danube Participation Days, and the framework for coordination between Priority Areas and macro-regional strategies. Likewise, PA10 supports the strategy embedding in EU programmes with measures such as the cooperation in the Network of ESF Managing Authorities in the Danube Region.

titleEn: PA1b: To Improve Mobility and Multimodality – Road, Rail and Air Links
Priority Area 8 - Competitiveness
summaryEn:
The project's main objective is to further support the effective and efficient EUSDR implementation. The well established structures of EUSDR and PA 8 support for SMEs including the Working Groups, the close, intense cooperation between Steering Group members and further relevant stakeholders are crucial and great benefit for mastering the multiple crisis’ with Corona pandemic, Russia's invasion of Ukraine and the impacts and threats due to climate change. These crisis’ have dramatically demonstrated the enormous risks to companies (value chains, energy supply, etc.) in the Danube Region. With PA8, Baden-Württemberg and Croatia have assumed responsibility for the key area of business in the EUSDR. Increasing resilience offers great opportunities for the Danube Region, which must also be further developed in the course of the work of PA 

8.

The European Green Deal and the Fitfor55 package are also of great importance for the further implementation of EUSDR and the competiveness of companies.

By fostering the linkages among relevant stakeholders, spreading information including best practice, offering education, enhancing cooperation concerning relevant topics like digitalisation, artificial intelligence, innovation, resource efficiency, circular economy or bioeconomy, initiating projects, the coordination of PA8 is creating an added value to all stakeholders and companies in the Danube Region. Implementing and further developing the action plan in a close discussion with all PA 8 stakeholders, identifying the various needs and then implementing the decisions and resolutions of the SG members is the focus of the project. In detail the project will facilitate on embedding of the EUSDR into EU-funded programmes, support policy development and policy initiatives as well as usage of cutting-edge knowledge. Thus, two Flagship projects will be developed. Finally, the objective of the project is to improve the visibility of the EUSDR.

titleEn: DRP-PAC3-PA7 Knowledge society
summaryEn: The Slovak Centre of Scientific and Technical Information (SCSTI) - Slovakia together with the University of Belgrade (UoB) - Serbia will continue as a team responsible for the coordination of the PA7 “To develop the Knowledge Society (research, education, and ICT)” within the EU Strategy for the Danube Region (EUSDR). Based on the previous years of cooperation between Slovakia and Serbia, both countries decided to continue in their common effort and focus the new project in the upcoming period 2023-2028 foremost on improving the effectiveness of PA7 coordination, supporting the PA7 Steering Group members, and other stakeholders in implementing EUSDR, enhancing policy development and policy initiatives contributing to capacity building in higher education, research and innovation in the DR and increasing inclusion of the Danube countries into European Research Area, communication and increased visibility of the PA and dissemination of PA’s achievements, as well as capitalisation activities within EUSDR and beyond.

titleEn: PA3_CLOSE – Recovery through CuLture, tOuriSm and peoplE-to-people contacts in the Danube Region
summaryEn:
The project is structured along the following lines of action: 
- strengthening the involvement of Steering Group Members in the decision-making process regarding the development and improvement of the activities related to the EUSDR Action Plan
- operationalizing PA3 Action Plan based on the roadmap developed within the previous application with a focus on the role of urban areas in the mobilization of culture and tourism resources, the linkages between challenges, trends related to culture and tourism and local development. The Project puts into practice the objectives of European strategies, such as ‘Culture & Cultural Heritage’ Partnership of the Urban Agenda and the New European Bauhaus initiative which promote culture and the preservation of urban landscapes and heritage not as an objective in itself, but it also as a powerful tool aimed at achieving social, ecological and economic goals. Also, the Territorial Agenda 2030 mentions that natural and cultural heritage are assets of local and regional development, which offer unique opportunities for development and a high-quality living environment. Both culture and tourism sectors, as well as urban areas were strongly affected by the pandemic (according to the studies carried out in the previous project). If large cities have the capacity to better cope with crisis situations and uphold measures to increase resilience, small and medium-sized cities require a targeted and coordinated policy approach in the fields of tourism, culture and urban development. Culture and tourism can positively drive local development, encouraging the establishment and development of new investments, providing sustainability to local businesses, thus securing the sustainability of the communities themselves
- understanding new forms of tourism and cultural expressions to support youth participation and social inclusion, avoiding the digital divide and the amplification of inequalities between different types of territories.

titleEn: PA 6: Biodiversity, Landscapes, Air and Soils
summaryEn:
The Project shall continue to support the implementation of Priority Area 06 of the EU Strategy for the Danube Region, adapted to current needs and challenges ahead. PA 06 consists of Priority Area Coordinators, Steering Group and Task Forces. The chairs of the Task Forces are observers to the Steering Group and participate in the Steering Group meeting. Beside the content-oriented work, the connection to the policy level shall be strengthened. At the point of time when applying for the project, the EU is in its early years of implementation of the EU Green Deal and released new EU Biodiversity Strategy, both giving strong momentum to the PA 6 objectives, which shall be exploited to the best extent. The expected change from the implementation of this project is an improved coordination and implementation of the Strategy in PA 

06.

Generally, the project for PA 06 for the period 2023-2028 is based on the Action Plan, the PA 06 Road Map, the knowledge, experiences and results of the ongoing work of the Task Forces in the framework of PA 

06. Specifically, it aims at sound management procedures for implementing PA 06 objectives, thus support the PACs work to coordinate and manage the implementation process, including cooperation with relevant EUSDR actors, other PA's and the Steering Group. Furthermore, it shall contribute to facilitate effective work of stakeholders connected to PA 06 issues, raise awareness of the policy level and the wider public accordingly and gain in-depth knowledge on specific topics. Overall, the project shall contribute particularly to systematically network various stakeholders in the Danube Region with the policy level in the EUSDR states.

titleEn: PA 5 - Environmental Risks
summaryEn:
The project supports the sustainability of improved governance of the PA5 (securing staff and covering related costs for
co-coordinating countries for a 6-year period) which ensures continuous, stable, and effective coordination of the PA activities to implement its Targets and Actions in order to realize the regulations of the Floodrisk Directive (2007/60/EC) and the related elements of the WFD (2000/60/EC) in the Danube Basin, also the Decision No 1313/2013/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on a Union Civil Protection Mechanism. Eventually, the project results in a more strengthened international and institutional cooperation (with other PAs, international organizations like ICPDR, ISRBC, EC, JRC, GWP, and Carpathian Convention, Regional Public Authorities, Higher Education institutes, other MRS of EU, Volunteer Rescue organizations and Disaster Management authorities) in the field of flood protection, climate change adaptation (e.g increased floods, drought management, support the EU Climate Change Adaptation Strategy) and accidental river pollutions in the region. Additionally, improved and consolidated management of the PA will be led to increased project generation and to reach a higher involvement of the stakeholders in the implementation of the Strategy. The project supports the harmonization of policies and planning processes, also discovering transnational challenges and finding common solutions on a macroregional level. Facilitates the realization of solidarity principle in the watershed with the involvement of non-EU countries, but evident on an
upstream-downstream relation as well.

titleEn: PA04 - Water Quality
summaryEn:
EUSDR Priority Area 4 (PA4) “Maintain and restore the quality of waters” supports the activities - the Safeguard Europe’s Water Resources, assistance in implementation of the EU Water Framework Directive (WFD) and the Urban Waste Water Treatment Directive (UWWTD), improvement of fish migration, promotion of measures addressing agricultural pollution, plastics and hazardous waste, facilitation of sub-basin activities. EUSDR PA4 provides assistance in project generation, partnership search, networking and dissemination. Furthermore, it deepens synergies with water protection organizations, such as the International Commission for the Protection of the Danube River (ICPDR) and the Sava Commission. The project partners will work with close cooperation with relevant international organisations, such as ICPDR that will be an ASP within the project and the Sava Commission, Carpathian Conventions, GWP-CEE, Danube Sturgeon Task Force and the relevant DGs of the EC. The project will continue to focus on the following target groups: PA4 Steering Group members, national authorities focusing on water management issues, international organisations and other interested stakeholders, NGOs related to water quality. As the result of the transnational cooperation the actions of the revised EUSDR PA4 Action Plan will be implemented and the cooperation between relevant target groups will be further strengthened. The crucial strategy background document is the revised EUSDR Action Plan, and the project will contribute to its implementation. 

Specific issues identified in the revised EUSDR PA4 Action Plan will be also addressed: challenges related to hazardous and emerging substances (A1), pharmaceuticals; waste water (A2) and water reuse; strengthening cooperation with the agricultural sector (A3); drinking water (A4); migratory fish (A5) and climate change (A6). Within climate change specific focus will be paid to the issues of droughts, water scarcity and water retention.

titleEn: PA 2 - Energy
summaryEn:
The project reflects the path PA2 aims to follow to reach the expected changes by 2028 in 4 main areas:

1) It plans to strenghten its Steering Group and its activities in order to support the implementation of the EUSDR AP, and to back PA2 that it has an increased influence on shaping Europe's energy policy by representing interests of the region. A main aim is to revitalize the SG after the pandemic situation of weakened cooperation. 

2) The field of energy is one of the most important areas shaping our future. The eager needs for a green energy transition result in rapidly evolving new areas and technologies and increasing decarbonisation targets. Furthermore, unexpected geopolitical situations may fundamentally change energy systems and security of supply.
PA2 continues the in-depth analysis of actual key energy topics and consecutive policy recommendations, strategies addressed by actions under SO

2. In the 2023-28 period it will focus on 3 crucial areas: (a) increase energy security of the EUSDR by gas supply diversification, (b) enhance the development of hydrogen economies in EUSDR, (c) boost green energy transition at local levels by advocating the development of citizen driven low-carbon energy actions. All these 3 topics are Flagships of the PA

2. 
In addition PA2 continues addressing key topics by expanding previous results, such as renewables, energy efficieny and comparative analyses of the NECP-s of the EUSDR countries, as a comprehensive framework for energy policies. 

3) In order to strenghten policy shaping activities, an enhanced coopertion with respective stakeholders at all levels (EU/international, EUSDR, national, regional, thematiclly scoped) will be addressed in the form of workshops, conferences, study tours, networking platforms, etc. A special attention will be paid on the involvement of non-EU countries. 

4) Finally a stong emphasis is put on assisting project generation, as these are real motors of changes.

titleEn: Priority Area 1a Mobility - Waterways
Share Balkani: experience the virtual reality tourism in Kyustendil and Leskovac
Safegurading and Promotion of Intangible Cultural Heritage

Innovation, Ideas and Initiatives for Youth - i3

SustainabiLIty of tourism By EnhaCing Cooperation and dIgital transformatiOn
summaryEn:
Tourism is one of the driver of the global economy and an early adopter of digital transformation technologies in Mediterranean basin.
Covid-19 pandemic hit severely, showing vulnerability and non-resilience to unpredictable risks and governance rigidity in reacting and mitigating them then finally demanding more timely information for policy and decision makers.
LIBECCIO faces this challenge enhancing tourism governance, destination management and sustainability then resilience against risks too. Through digital transformation, it addresses the need for improved destination management, supporting policy makers with informed data driven decision making, positively impacting the policies implementation for a more sustainable tourism paradigm.
It follows an intersectoral and transdisciplinary approach in Euro Med by involving together with partners the Q Helix tourism community, through the Euro Med Tourism Innovation Platform (ETIP), in testing and transfer planning of suitable solutions following a Living Lab methodology.
LIBECCIO Destination Management Support System (DMSS) is a semantically enriched web-enabled platform that integrates sustainability indicator datasets and Big Data analytics to exploit data driven policy and decision making. The DMSS test in thematic tourism partner areas and the lessons learned are assessed and evaluated by ETIP that draws up a capitalization plan how the partners will transfer and make operational in local ecosystems the ETIP platform and its main tool DMSS after the end of the Project. 
LIBECCIO benefits ETIP with community institutional capacities, through solutions, methodologies and policies for a more efficient, sustainable and resilient tourism paradigm.
It capitalizes previous projects outcomes equipping regional and local public administrators and BSOs with innovative solutions, integrating tourist sustainability indicators and real time Big Data, enabling timely analysis, advanced benchmarking and decision making.

titleEn: Planning for autonomous mobility on demand in the Euro-MED area
summaryEn:
In Euro-MED, 

40.6 million people live in sparsely populated areas with poor or without public transport services (IEMED, 2021). These areas are expensive for Public (Transport) Authorities (PTAs) to operate due to low number of paying passengers per kilometre. This leads to high private car dependency or isolation of people (ESPON, 2020), resulting in high carbon emissions (156M tons of CO2) or inaccessibility to public services and labour market.

A solution recognised by researchers and pilot projects in Europe is autonomous mobility on demand (AMOD), offering higher quality services while reducing operating costs (41% quality-cost ratio improvement, Malmö Uni, 2022) and CO2 emissions up to 72% (K2Centrum, 2022). However, it is difficult for PTAs to start planning AMOD without the ability to easily estimate its potential socio-economic and environmental impact.

The AVENUE (H2020) and MultiDEPART (EIT UM) projects successfully developed methodologies to assess local impact of AMOD. Currently, these methodologies cannot easily be applied by PTAs outside of these projects. Therefore, the primary objective of ArtMED is enable PTAs to plan for AMOD by transferring methodologies from École Centrale de Lyon (AVENUE) and CARNET (MultiDEPART) to 4 PTAs in Slovenia (PO), Portugal (TML), Italy (ALOT), Greece (PF) and beyond through jointly optimising and implementing a publicly accessible AMOD impact assessment tool in a transnational approach.

The tool will support PTAs in ArtMED to analyse the potential AMOD impact for local use cases and develop: 4 vision statements (for political support), 4 investment plans (for budgeting) and 2 transport model designs (for planning AMOD systems).

As AMOD hardly exists yet in Euro-MED, ArtMED is the first project to make state-of-the-art insights available to PTAs through a user-friendly tool, that assesses AMOD impact to plan for more accessible, inclusive, and sustainable public transport for people in sparsely populated areas.

titleEn: SMart Industrial Tourism in the Mediterranean
summaryEn:
Before COVID-19, tourism accounted for about 15% of Med countries GDP and 

11.5% of their total employment. With the lockdown and travel restrictions the pandemic totally disrupted the sector. Now that the pandemic is subsiding and the sector is recovering, a new risk has arisen, that old unsustainable tourism patterns are re-proposed, generating undesired effects like over-tourism and seasonalization, with their unbearable pressure on the environment and the communities. 

The challenge in the post-pandemic time is to change tourism, by e.g. focusing on alternative destinations and by exploiting technology (particularly those that have been boosted by the pandemic) to make the tourist experience more rewarding and yet more sustainable.

Many Med regions and cities with important industrial sites are considering Industrial Tourism as a way to attract tourists to their areas. On the other hand, the common-place visit to productive sites could be greatly enhanced by integrating additional cultural and historical elements through the use of advanced and immersive technologies that can make the experience more informative and enticing for the visitor (Smart Industrial Tourism).

The project aims to exploit transnational cooperation to explore the social and economic potential of Smart Industrial Tourism (SMIT), as a sustainable economic activity that can benefit tourism actors, SMEs, the industry, CCIs, R&D centers, HEIs and technology providers, and the local communities.

The project will create transnational working groups involving 4helix stakeholders to explore industrial tourism and related advanced technologies applications. It will eventually define a common strategy and Action Plan for the development of SMIT in the Med regions. The result will be a diversification of the economy and of the sector, a reduction of over-tourism and seasonalization, and a boost to social and economic growth and to technological innovation of tourism at large.

titleEn: MONITORING OF MACRO-REGIONS IN EUROPE
summaryEn:
The ESPON European and Macro-regional Territorial Monitoring Tool — MRS. ESPON — aims at providing a practical and operational online platform to continuously observe the territorial development trends and patterns taking place in Europe and its macro-regions. It includes 4 geographical modules: Europe, Baltic Sea Region, Danube Region, Adriatic Ionian Region and Alpine Region.

MRS. ESPON provides the European, macro-regional, national and regional policymakers and other stakeholders with complementary territorial information, data, maps, graphs, analytical features and short reports. It brings together information from different data sources, such as the ESPON Database, Eurostat, National Statistical Offices, Worldbank, OECD, ILO, UNCTAD, and other regional collaboration partners.

Reading and interpreting the quantitative statistical information in the light of policy objectives the tool helps to:
monitor territorial development trends in the four macro-regions,
identify development opportunities and territorial challenges,
better understand the diversity and position (benchmarking) of regions in the European context.
position the four macro-regions in a European perspective by providing narratives for MRS in the 2021-2027 EU Cohesion Policy Objectives.
Several indicators of the tool are automatically updated via web services linking to the data sources. Other data sets are to be updated regularly.

Users Stakeholders are also welcome to contact ESPON directly through a dedicated email address (mrs@espon.eu) or via the online form for any additional information, proposals for additions or to request specific data sets or any other questions/suggestions in relation to the MRS. ESPON tool.

titleEn: State of the European Territory Report
ESPON Cross-border Public Services 2.0
summaryEn:
Cross-border Public Services (CPS) address joint problems or development potentials of cross-border regions. Being provided on a long-term basis they aim to generate benefits for the general public or a specific target group in the cross-border territory in which the service is provided, thereby contributing to improving living conditions in border regions. 

The ESPON CPS 2.0 study focuses on an upgrade and update of the CPS inventory produced within the ESPON targeted analysis in 2018. Establishing a solid inventory is aimed at making this Pan-European territorial evidence easily available for public authorities and other (public or private) stakeholders. 

It is being implemented in a complementary effort and coordination with the Cross-Border Public Services project by the DG REGIO which further developed the previous conceptual and methodological framework for collecting and analysing CPS data across the European Union including the internal and external borders and an interactive web application. This framework revision also aimed to widen the variety of information potentially relevant for CPS. 

The ESPON CPS 2.0 study focuses on updating the CPS inventory by adding new CPS and updating information on existing ones. This inventory is designed with sustainability and robustness in mind for continuous monitoring of CPS. In 2022, it contains information on about 1500 CPS across the EU including borders with IPA and neighbouring countries. 

The CPS 2.0 is an outcome of a coordinated effort of the different tasks of the two study teams involved in the ESPON CPS 2.0 study and the DG Regio CPS project.

titleEn: LET'S INVITE THE NATURE IN OUR CITIES
summaryEn:
In the era of modernization, urban green spaces (UGSs) are attracting increasing attention in eco cities development. There is currently a paucity of UGSs, and their importance has become crucial in enhancing life expectancy and health. To meet people's demands, we are busy in designing green cities. The deployment of UGSs is particularly relevant to fully enhancing residents' lifestyles and health. Bansko Municipality and Vinica Municipality are facing similar challenges. Both municipalities have identified the challenge of the unbalanced development of green areas in the region and the need of investments for development of urban green areas. That is the reason why we plan to collaboratively develop the needed green zones along with velo alleys in a way to actively engage people and raise awareness about the importance of preserving green spaces.
In recent years, Bansko municipality, known as one of the most preferred winter tourist destinations in Bulgaria, has faced a serious challenge related to land pollution. As the city's popularity as a major tourist destination grows, the number of visitors increases significantly, which automatically leads to an increase in the amount of land pollution. The combination of these factors makes the problem of soil contamination in Bansko increasingly relevant, calling into question the sustainable development of the region and the protection of the environment. The sectoral relationship between tourism and all forms of pollution in the context of GI is also acknowledged in the Biodiversity Information System for Europe (https://biodiversity.europa.eu/green-infrastructure/gi-related-sectors). 
During the last decade Vinica has highly improved the tourist infrastructure. Due to that fact Vinica is very attractive for tourists. Both Bansko and Vinica face similar difficulties in prevention and management of land pollution. Through that project we intend to embrace the opportunity to introduce a pilot land pollution information management system in Bansko Municipality and to transfer the practice in Vinica through presenting the advantages of the pilot action.
Another challenge we identify is change in peoples' mind. We aim to sustainable green and eco oriented people who keep and preserve our nature. We intend to approach their self conscience by an "Eco mind campaign" .
Overall objectives of the project proposal:
By implementing Green Infrastructure (GI) investments along with contemporary information management solutions to mitigate environmental degradation, we help to reduce the accumulation of harmful pollutants in soil and groundwater. In more practical terms, we aim to: 


1.	Develop 0,744 ha of urban green areas in Bansko and 0,306 ha in Vinica Municipalities


2.	Develop 1 velo alley and 1 pedestrian lane in Bansko and 1 pedestrian path in Vinica connecting green spaces


3.	Introduce 1 pilot land pollution information management system (LPIMS) in Bansko Municipality


4.	Transfer 1 good practice (LPIMS ) in Vinica Municipality by presentation of the advantages of its use.


5.	Organise a mutual "Eco mind" campaign
Target groups: 2 municipal administrations , 250 000 residents and visitors of the municipalities;
The output of the executed activities are:
0.744 hectares of green zone in Bansko Municipality
0.306 hectares of green zone in Vinica Municipality
1 velo alley and 2 pedestrian paths , connecting the urban green zones
A developed and working land pollution information management system which includes the key features described in activity 

2.

1.
Conducted mutual "Eco mind" campaign
Transfer of 1 good practice (land pollution information management system) in Vinica Municipality by presentation of the advantages of its use.
Ecosystems and their services can be maintained and enhanced by establishing Green Infrastructure (GI) and restoring degraded ecosystems. In order to provide a lasting impact on the ecological infrastructure, the current partnership interacts with in fostering "green" infrastructure in the urban areas and reducing land pollution. Our project proposal pays attention on the positive impact of green infrastructure on land pollution, particularly by promoting and piloting solutions to strengthen the cause-and-effect linkages between them..
We seek cross-border impact with its implementation which is not possible without that specific cross-border partnership. "Ecomind" campaign have an especially positive impact on the cross-border area due to the fact it is conducted in partnership.
The current project proposal is innovative by combining and developing three different approaches for development of the cross-boarder region:


1.	UGSs development


2.	Pilot introduction and implementation of land pollution information management system


3.	Eco mind campaign.

titleEn: “ESTABLISHMENT OF A NEW BORDER CROSS CHECK POINT (BCCP) STRUMYANI-BEROVO (“KLEPALO”) BETWEEN BULGARIA AND NORTH MACEDONIA”
summaryEn:
The project proposal is submitted for financing under Policy objective 3 „A more connected Europe by enhancing mobility“, specific objective „Developing sustainable, climate resilient, intelligent and intermodal national, regional and local mobility, including improved access to TEN-T and cross-border mobility“. 
The common challenge of the programme area jointly tackling in our project is strengthening the regional connectivity and facilitating the increasing traffic of people by developing sustainable, climate resilient, intelligent and intermodal national, regional and local mobility, including improved access to TEN-T and cross- border mobility.
The need for strengthening the regional connectivity and to facilitate the increasing traffic of people and goods between Bulgaria and North Macedonia has since long been on the agenda. The regional consultations in 2019 have clearly identified the BCCP Strumyani – Berovo as an investment of strategic importance to be supported by the Interreg VI-A IPA Bulgaria-North Macedonia programme, taking into account the gradual expansion of the socio-economic interlinkages between the two countries due to positive prospects of the EU enlargement. On 14 June 1999 in Skopje, an agreement between the Government of the Macedonia and the Government of Bulgaria for opening new international road Border Crossing Check Points (BCCP) Strumyani – Berovo and Simitli – Pehchevo was signed.
Missing links in the CB provision of business services and such of general interest are a main factor behind the negative demographic dynamics that the area exhibits. The lack of infrastructure favouring the provision of services of community and business interest further impose severe social implications including increased social exclusion and inequalities, as well as challenges for recreational service provision, labour markets and housing. 

The project’s overall objective is "Developing sustainable, climate resilient, intelligent and intermodal national, regional and local mobility, including improved access to TEN-T and cross-border mobility". Having a new BCCP built and operated on both sides of the border the expected changes will be related to facilitating the increasing traffic of people and goods between the two countries; strengthening communication links between the two countries and improving and extending access to core TEN-T, including the connection with Corridors IV and VIII, which is to improve regional connectivity and boost the economic growth of the programme area.

The project output is BCCP facility constructed for the Bulgarian part and BCCP reconstructed/upgraded on the part of the Republic of North Macedonia. Main target groups who will benefit from the project are the residents, visitors, and businesses in the CBC area. 

А functioning BCCP requires the infrastructures on both sides of the border to be built and fully put into operation at the same time. Applying a strong cross-border partnership approach is the only possible one to ensure mutual
performance and completion of project activities by both partners for successfully achieving the set project objective.

What is new about the project is that the investments under this priority will contribute to the EU external policy by adhering to most up-to-date standards in safeguarding security and border control by establishment of new sustainable climate resilient, intelligent, and intermodal national, regional and local mobility infrastructure to strengthening the regional connectivity and support business activities, including improved access to TEN-T and other important connections.

titleEn: PARKS - Preserving Areas through Regional Knowledge and Sustainability
summaryEn:
Common Challenge:
The programme area, encompassing vital urban spaces like Kriva Palanka and Dupnitsa, faces an overarching challenge concerning urban green infrastructure. As urban areas progress, the essential greenery that contributes to the ecological balance, aesthetic appeal, and well-being of the residents often gets overshadowed. Such gaps in urban planning not only diminish residents' quality of life but also curtail the cities' resilience against environmental concerns like pollution and the urban heat island effect.

Overall Objective:
At the project's core is an ambition to metamorphose urban landscapes within the programme area. We aim to augment green infrastructure by revitalizing urban zones with verdant parks, vibrant green spaces, and cutting-edge technology for constant environmental monitoring. By bridging urban planning, ecology, and technology, we're creating a roadmap for sustainable urban communities. We anticipate cities pulsating with lively green spaces, where residents are conscientiously linked with nature and sustainability.

Main Outputs and Beneficiaries:
Several pivotal deliverables form the bedrock of our initiative:

Green Park in Kriva Palanka: More than a green area, this space exemplifies the integration of nature, recreation, and environmental responsibility.
Development of Diverse Green Spaces: Transformation of currently barren areas into green oases that cater to myriad community requirements.
Plant Growth Manual: This tri-lingual manual will empower communities with knowledge on optimal plant care, growth patterns, and protection against potential threats.
Air Quality Monitoring Dashboard: Collaborating with education institutions, this innovative platform will offer live insights into environmental parameters.
Green Cadaster: A specialized registry detailing the green assets and infrastructure, ensuring systematic recording, and management of these vital resources.
The principal beneficiaries of these efforts are the residents of Kriva Palanka and Dupnitsa. These urban dwellers will experience their cities' metamorphosis from mere urban hubs to green, sustainable sanctuaries. They'll gain access to vital environmental data and be equipped with resources that promote green practices.

Approach and Cross-border Relevance:
Our strategy intertwines infrastructural augmentation with knowledge-sharing. Parks and green zones are envisioned as hubs of education, community interaction, and sustainability. A cross-border approach is imperative, given the transboundary nature of environmental challenges. Collaborative endeavors, pooled resources, and a unified strategy across regions magnify the cumulative impact, ensuring widespread benefits.

Novelty of the Project:
This project's distinctiveness lies in its comprehensive vision, transcending mere green space creation. It synthesizes infrastructure with innovation—employing advanced technology like air quality sensors and real-time analytics. By rallying diverse stakeholders – city planners, environmentalists, educators, and the populace – we're crafting a community-centric initiative, promising sustainability and continued relevance in the evolving urban landscape.

titleEn: Urban greening for healthy breathing
Transforming of urban sites with Green infrastructures
summaryEn:
EcoScape project proposal was created in response to the need to address the following key common challenges:
Challenge 1: Lack of ecosystem-based practices and services to address natural hazards and biodiversity loss and Challenge 2: limited readiness for green transition. The focus of the project is on the introduction of green infrastructure in the CB region and the creation of conditions for green transition. 
The overall objective is to promote and facilitate the adoption of environmentally friendly solutions within urban areas across the cross-border region establishing an environment conducive to increased greenery in urban and peri-urban zones within the cross-border region and facilitate the transition towards sustainable practices . This involves the development of strategic documents, an action plan, and a concept, as well as enhancing our understanding of relevant factors related to green infrastructure and sustainable urban development via promotion. Advance the safeguarding and conservation of natural ecosystems, biodiversity, and green infrastructure, with focus on urban areas, with expected change that the project in enhancing the ability to adapt and fostering support for proactive measures, coordinated risk management and readiness for unforeseen situations, promoting awareness regarding the challenges posed by climate change, promoting cross-border collaboration for the sustainable utilization and stewardship of shared natural resources.
EcoSpace is structured around 3 WPs both project-specific and foreseen by the CBC program. Each WP corresponds to grouped activities with distinctive characters and purposes.
Apart from introducing green infrastructure to the region main outputs of regional impact will be: Strategic Documents, Capacity Building and promotion of green infrastructure concept and benefits 

1. green infrastructure strategy, 

2. action plans, 

3. Concept for green transition, and 

4. capacity-building measures for relevant stakeholders, creating a foundation for development of green infrastructure in the region. Environmental Improvement are expected in project's implementation of green infrastructure initiatives but also managing the entire urban sustainability transition in the project-covered cities creating better conditions in the central part of the town in Shtip and Goce Delcev in the spirit of the new European Bauhaus will promote among the population the strategic goals of the European Green Deal, educational playground Building a recreation area that combines environmentally friendly power supply with solar batteries will create conditions for the development of ecological thinking in adolescents as well as in their parents. 
The benefit that the project has over the cross-border regions can be defined in the following more important aspects: 

1. Raising public awareness of the green infrastructure and green transition topic; 

2. Develop skills and knowledge of the representatives of the municipalities, regional authorities, public communal enterprises, and other stakeholders in the area of green infrastructure and green transition; 

3. Climate change resilience; 

4. Preparation of the municipalities and other stakeholders for future green infrastructure and green transition-related challenges; 

5. Improvement of quality of air and quality of life in the tackled cities on both sides of the border.
The EcoScape project partnership was established among two municipalities Gotse Delchev number of residents 20 047 , area of intervention 0,775 ha and Stip number of residents 40000, area of intervention 1,135 ha and one regional development center (the Center for Development of the East Region). Municipalities play a fundamental role in green infrastructure development, formulating green transition policies, and urban planning with sustainability in mind. Collectively, the partnership forms a well-balanced framework capable of effectively pursuing and achieving the planned results. All partners bring extensive experience from various EU CBC projects, particularly in the environmental domain, promoting an environment, with each sector contributing its unique perspective, experiences, and ideas. This collaboration leads to the generation of innovative pilot solutions and approaches that may not have emerged within a single-sector framework.
The project aim is sustainable development of the region by implementing direct initiatives aimed at enhancing the urban environment in cross-border regions. Tackling economic, social, and territorial disparities as well as inequalities, the project will propose adequate investments for improving the quality of life of local citizens, and inclusiveness of education and training, and addressing the territorial disparities gap. Within the project existing solutions for sustainable urban drainage systems and Urban food production (as an example of green infrastructure mentioned in the EU green infrastructure strategy).

titleEn: Green Pulse Cross-Border Pact
summaryEn:
The G-PACT project is a collaborative effort between the Municipality of Petrich (MP) as the Lead partner, the Municipality of Strumica (MS), Association "Center for Development and Promotion Promo Idea - Strumica" (Promo Idea) as Project partner 3 (PP3), and Association "Together for Sandanski" (TS) as Project partner 4 (PP4). 
The project addresses several common challenges faced by the region. These challenges include the imperative to enhance nature preservation, protect biodiversity, improve ecosystem services, strengthening ecological connectivity, reducing forms of pollution that fall within the eligibility scope of project actions and promote sustainable urban development in the cross-border region of Bulgaria and North Macedonia. Both countries confront the dilemma of reconciling urban development with nature conservation while prioritizing the well-being of their citizens. 
The overarching objective of the G-PACT project is to create green urban spaces, improve ecosystem services, and increase public awareness in Petrich and Strumica. By doing so, the project aims to enhance the quality of life in the cross-border area and promote sustainable urban development.
The project seeks to bring about several key changes. G-PACT will lead to the development of green urban areas, specifically twinning parks in Petrich and Strumica, providing residents with access to nature within their urban environments. By enhancing green spaces, the project will improve ecosystem services such as air purification, temperature regulation, and opportunities for recreation. These improvements will benefit both urban residents and local wildlife.
Through the project activities the raise public awareness about the importance of green spaces, biodiversity, and sustainable development will be raised. The "Urban Nature Lens" photo contest will engage local residents, photographers, and nature enthusiasts in capturing the beauty and benefits of urban green areas.
The project will produce several key outputs among which is the construction and renovation of green urban parks in Petrich and Strumica, offering improved green spaces for local communities.
 The development of Joint Urban Ecosystem Services (EsS) Assessment Methodology for assessing ecosystem services, enabling both municipalities to evaluate the impact of their green spaces is also very key moment within the project. This will lead to elaboration of Action plans for the sustainable development and maintenance of the Green Pulse twinning parks in both municipalities. 
Training modules on green project management and renewable energy sources, empowering stakeholders with knowledge in sustainability and the training packages dedicated to the development and understanding of the EsS services ensure the project’s long-lasting effect. The establishment of a cross-border network focused on urban ecosystem services, fostering cooperation and knowledge exchange is an integral part of the project.
The beneficiaries of the project include local residents of Petrich and Strumica who will enjoy improved green spaces and ecosystem services. Additionally, local and regional authorities, NGOs, and young people will benefit from capacity-building initiatives. The "EsS development agents" competition will engage youth in promoting sustainable development.
A cross-border approach is vital because it allows PPs from different types to collaborate, share experiences, and jointly address common environmental challenges. By working together, they can maximize the impact of their efforts to enhance green spaces and promote sustainable urban development.
G-PACT project itself is an innovation due to all its elements as it engages the public in documenting and celebrating the transformation of urban green spaces, fostering a sense of community involvement. The establishment of the G-PACT Urban EsS Network encourages cross-border cooperation and knowledge sharing, promoting a unified approach to urban ecosystem services. The project empowers youth through the "EsS development agents" competition, involving them in the sustainable development of their communities.
The emphasis on renewable energy sources aligns with the broader goal of sustainable urban development and showcases the potential for eco-friendly initiatives in the region.
In summary, G-PACT project addresses common challenge of significant importance to the territories of the PPs and to the CB area in general. Each and every specific activity can be transferred, adapted and applied on other territory of the cross-border area and not only as PPs have ensured to set a positive example which needs to be further developed and integrated so that a greener and brighter future can be ensured.

titleEn: Unleashing Youth Power in Transnational Innovation for a Thriving Blue Economy
summaryEn:
The Interreg project "Unleashing Youth Power in Transnational Innovation for a Thriving Blue Economy" focuses on developing and enhancing research and innovation capacities and the uptake of advanced technologies. It aims to address the common challenge of fostering sustainable economic growth and job creation in the blue economy sector across multiple regions.

Common Challenge:
The programme area faces the challenge of harnessing the potential of the blue economy while ensuring its long-term sustainability. This includes addressing issues such as environmental degradation, limited research and innovation capacities, and a lack of integration and collaboration among different regions.

Overall Project Objective:
The main objective of the project is to stimulate economic development in the blue economy sector by leveraging the power of youth, research, and innovation. By providing opportunities for young people to engage in transnational cooperation and by fostering the uptake of advanced technologies, the project aims to drive sustainable growth and create new job opportunities.

Expected Change:
The project expects to bring about a significant change in the current situation by strengthening research and innovation capacities in the blue economy. This will be achieved through the active involvement of young people, who will contribute fresh ideas, skills, and perspectives to address the challenges faced by the sector. The project also aims to promote the adoption of advanced technologies, which can enhance the efficiency, sustainability, and competitiveness of blue economy activities.

Main Outputs and Results:
The project will develop several outputs and results, including:

Capacity Building Programs: Training and skill development initiatives for young people in the blue economy sector, focusing on areas such as entrepreneurship, innovation, and technology adoption.

Transnational Collaboration Platforms: Creation of platforms and networks to facilitate knowledge exchange, collaboration, and joint initiatives among youth, researchers, entrepreneurs, and industry stakeholders across different regions.

Innovation Support: Provision of resources and support for the development and implementation of innovative ideas and projects in the blue economy, including mentorship, incubation, and access to funding.

Technology Demonstrations and Pilots: Implementation of pilot projects and demonstrations showcasing the application and benefits of advanced technologies in various blue economy sectors.

Beneficiaries:
The project's outputs and results will benefit various stakeholders, including:

Young people: They will gain valuable skills, knowledge, and opportunities for employment and entrepreneurship in the blue economy sector.
Researchers and Innovators: They will have access to transnational collaboration and knowledge exchange, enabling them to develop innovative solutions for sustainable blue economy development.
Industry Stakeholders: They will benefit from the adoption of advanced technologies, improved competitiveness, and increased access to a skilled workforce.
Local Communities: The project's activities will contribute to the economic development and environmental sustainability of coastal regions, leading to improved livelihoods and well-being.
Planned Approach and Transnational Cooperation:
The project will adopt a collaborative approach that involves transnational cooperation among multiple regions. This is essential because the challenges faced by the blue economy sector, such as sustainable growth, innovation, and technology adoption, require a collective effort and the exchange of experiences, expertise, and best practices. By fostering collaboration, the project can leverage the strengths and resources of different regions, facilitate learning, and promote the transfer of knowledge and technologies across borders. Transnational cooperation will enable a more comprehensive and impactful approach to addressing the common challenges and realizing the project's objectives.

titleEn: Clean areas, green and open streets
summaryEn:
The project "Clean areas, green and open streets" aims to solve the following common problems and challenges in the transnational region, part of the Black Sea area:
- Need to conduct training activities to build institutional capacity at the municipal level for successful implementation and management of activities in the field of mitigation and adaptation to climate change.
- The need to increase the knowledge and awareness of public bodies and citizens regarding the green transition, the circular economy and environmental protection.
- Need to increase environmental self-awareness, strengthen the skills and desire of young people to protect the environment.
- Application of innovative practices and technologies to implement public policies to make cities and regions more socially and environmentally sustainable. Development of a strategic document "Green Transnational Region".
- Investing in green infrastructure and promoting sustainable lifestyles by improving common spaces and protecting the environment.
- Rehabilitation of existing public green areas and their transformation into attractive park areas to enable different age groups to spend quality and varied time outside.
This project is integrated. Partners from each side of the border contribute different elements to achieve the project's goals.
Partners: General Toshevo Municipality, territorial administrative unit - Murfatlar, Tarakli District Council, Bolgrad Municipal Council.
Each of the four regions, depending on its specificity, will engage with different methods and tools in different activities, but with the same goal: Investing in green infrastructure to reduce air, water and soil pollution. Promoting sustainable lifestyles and providing sustainable, affordable and inclusive products and services. Reducing pollution through education, awareness and implementation of good practices. Increasing the environmental self-awareness, skills and desire of young people to protect the environment.
The following investment goals will be realized with the support of the program:
Reconstruction of a covered concrete walkway, summer scene and park space in a city park. Development of the territory by investing in green infrastructure to mitigate air, water, soil and degradation pollution.
Rehabilitation of two existing public green spaces and their transformation into an attractive park area that will enable different age groups to spend quality and varied time outside.
Reconstruction and landscaping of a traffic-free square space and a summer scene in a city park. Development of the territory by investing in green infrastructure and creating recreation areas with modern architectural elements.
All investment goals are subordinated to one general decision: "Green areas and cities and increasing the quality of life".
The development of the new green spaces will contribute to the creation and provision of sustainable, affordable, inclusive and beautiful products and services in line with the New European Bauhaus initiative.
According to the project, 3 seminars will be held, one thematic camp for young people, environmental actions and initiatives.
The project meets the general objective of the program and specific objective 7: Enhancing protection and preservation of nature, biodiversity, and green infrastructure, including in urban areas, and reducing all forms of pollution.
After the implementation of the project, we expect a transition to green cities and municipalities, oriented towards the environment, economically viable and improved quality of life of the population.

titleEn: Interdisciplinary Solutions for Smart Sustainable Tourism and Services for Blue Growth in the Black Sea Basin
summaryEn:
Sustainable tourism is an integral element in blue growth due to its potential to contribute to economic development while preserving the integrity and resilience of marine and coastal ecosystems. Innovation plays a crucial role in driving sustainable tourism and blue growth. However, tourism and related services in the Black Sea Basin are still considered knowledge- and technology non-intensive, which entails economic but also environmental and social losses. Black Sea tourism is troubled by overdevelopment, pollution and waste, seasonality and ineffective transfer of knowledge to novel business and practical solutions. This decreases the added value of the sector and makes its improvement over-vulnerable to various global shocks. 
The regional challenges can be overcome with novel context-relevant solutions based on cross-fertilization of state-of-art social, natural and engineering knowledge and expertise and via raising the innovation absorption and technology take-up in tourism. The rationale is that the stakeholders should innovate locally, in order to use the maritime resources effectively for all economic activities and to protect the marine life and environment.

The project “INTERSMARTS: Interdisciplinary Solutions for Smart Sustainable Tourism and Services for Blue Growth in the Black Sea Basin” aims to improve the sustainability performance and innovation absorption of tourism and services via interdisciplinary research, networking, co-creation and holistic knowledge generation. The goal will be achieved through establishing an open interdisciplinary network for applied research and technology transfer and valorizing novel solutions for smart and sustainable tourism and services. In the long run, the project seeks to change the traditional perceptions and to raise awareness on the knowledge-intensive nature of tourism within the blue growth framework.
The project intervention logic is aligned with the quintuple innovation helix which brings together the academia, business, government, civil sector and environment in a knowledge economy. 
The project results in: 
* INTERSMARTS Network for Interdisciplinary Solutions for Smart Tourism and Services with task forces on sustainable infrastructure and resource management, anti-pollution and waste management, seasonality solutions, technology transfer and innovations - uniting the project partner organizations work for sharing knowledge, experience and collaboration about raising the sustainability and blue growth performance of tourism and related services in the Black Sea Basin
* Needs assessment research about sustainability and blue growth perspectives of tourism and related services regarding the main sectoral challenges 
* INTERSMARTS Innovation Management Platform with a data-base of novel solutions and technology advancements that demonstrate how sustainability tourism entities can be improved as well as with idea-generation and crowd-sourcing functionalities 
* Four transnational Interdisciplinary research and networking events for smart sustainable tourism in Bulgaria, Republic of Moldova, Greece and Türkiye. 

INTERSMARTS implementation is based on delivering challenge-specific studies, interdisciplinary, comprehensive intervention, cross-border applied research and open civic participation engaging citizens as active participants in the research processes. The project will bring benefits to business, academia, communities and policy-makers in the partners’ countries and in whole Black Sea area. 
Sustainable smart tourism and blue growth are issues that go beyond the national borders. Answering the identified regional challenges in this regards requires the informed participation and cooperation of all relevant stakeholders in the neighbouring countries that rely on the Black Sea as a shared asset. The main feature of sustainability is that it is not limited to a certain type of services or products such as nature-based tourism or eco-tourism but is rather a philosophy that underlies both the demand and supply side of tourism businesses. Enforcing the perception that tourism can drive innovation and technological advancements in the blue economy requires wide-spread recognition and celebration of the innovative tourism initiatives in the Black Sea Basin – particularly when these initiatives are still scarce. 

INTERSMARTS is a joint initiative of the Varna University of Management (Bulgaria), International Hellenic University (Greece), Moldova State University (Republic of Moldova) and Istanbul Development Agency (Türkiye).

titleEn: Smart and innovative solutions for green and clean rural areas in Black Sea Basin
summaryEn:
Smart4Rural project is focusing on enhancing the joint efforts in supporting sustainable development and resilience of rural areas in Georgia, Moldova, Romania, and Turkey by the introduction of modern and smart approaches to reducing nature pollution and biodegradable waste impact and providing environmental protection in the BSB.
The project involves 6 PPs representing 4 BSB countries, 3 of them are municipalities of Tskaltubo (GEO), Rize (TR), Ungheni (MD), and 3 NGOs such as the Imereti Scientists Union “Spectri” (GEO), Galati Tehnopol Association (RO) RCSD (MD).
The project approaches consist in addressing common challenges that are to be solved by the joint efforts of PPs, and exchanging and introducing best practices of EU countries to make local rural and urban communities resilient and attractive. The communities of participating countries are facing significant environmental challenges that are common and equally relevant for these BSB countries. One of them is the growing rates of municipal waste generation, especially the generation of biodegradable waste in rural communities is particularly high, which is due, in many cases, to high agricultural growth rates. Biodegradable waste is a large polluter of the environment (land, rivers, and sea) and a significant source of GHG emissions in BSB regions. The experience of municipalities of GEO, MD, and TR in biodegradable waste management is very low, waste prevention and reduction approaches have not been used so far. Composting as biodegradable waste recycling approach, has not yet found proper distribution and development, which is due to insufficient experience and lack of information.
Through the joint efforts and involvement of PPs, Smart4Rural project is aimed:
-	To support resilience and improvement of rural areas by introduction and demonstration of innovative solutions to biodegradable waste recycling/composting based on EU countries’ best practices in selected municipalities of GEO, MD, and TR as a way to becoming greener and smarter communities in BSB.
-	To build the long-term capacity of local communities for the promotion and development of modern approaches to composting by the establishment and implementation of an effective and strong learning and training joint platform/resources.
-	To increase awareness and provide the behavior changing of representatives of local communities in GEO, RO, MD and TR through the joint implementation of the environmental educational programs, engagement in environment protection activities and improvement of young talents capacities for smarter and greener areas. 
A unique experience will be created of cooperative solutions to common problems, which can be replicated and capitalized on by other municipalities of the participating countries and other BSB countries.
Rural Composting Plant will be established in Tskaltubo municipality, which will be focused on composting agricultural waste. A special building will be constructed for this composting plant, which will be equipped with a solar power plant and where smart solutions will be used for the technological process needs. This will be the first similar plant in western Georgia to provide composting of agricultural waste.
A small-scale facility for open windrow composting of rural green waste will be established in Ungheni (MD). Other approaches to community and individual composting will be introduced in rural communities of 11 municipalities in selected countries.
The best practices of composting in Germany and Romania will be studied by the PPs and target groups. Also, the PPs will share the experience of Kutaisi composting center, which was created within the project BSB457 Waste Free Rivers for a Clean Black Sea.
Learning and training resources will be significant contributions to the project. A Joint e-Learning platform and short-term training course on composting will be established for practitioners and stakeholders which will also be available after the project completion. The joint educational program for schools will be developed and implemented in selected 40 schools in all 4 countries 
Smart4Rural project supports young talents in accelerating innovative and creative ideas in related project fields and implementing eco-smart initiatives. The Academy of Eco-Innovations will be organized for young talents from 4 selected counties
The project provides cross-boundary cooperation between representatives of participating countries, the joint activities will be carried out in 4 countries as well, in particular: 
-	International Scientific Conference “Smart solutions to urban and rural resilience” (GEO)
-	International conference “Waste Management through Composting: Challenges and Potentials” (RO)
-	Community awareness campaign “Composting to each household yard!” 
-	Common cleanups, 
-	A Green camp for teenagers (MD).
The project activities will be implemented with a view to creating green and clean, responsive and resilient rural areas in BSB

titleEn: Open environmental eFolio for joint maritime spatial planning and conservation of the valuable Black Sea Basin marine ecosystems
summaryEn:
‘Open environmental eFolio for joint maritime spatial planning and conservation of the valuable Black Sea Basin marine ecosystems’ addresses the environmental issues of the Black Sea, the shared large marine ecosystem, underpinning the BSB Programme’s overall regional approach. Black Sea environmental problems have received much attention since the end of the last century, alongside political, economic and social hurdles. The main identified transboundary problems are eutrophication, overexploitation of marine living resources, chemical pollution and changes in biodiversity and habitats. Conservation of the Black Sea biodiversity and habitats resonates with the Programme’s specific objective RSO 

2.

7. Three other environmental challenges have been pinpointed: preservation of commercially valuable marine living resources, reduction of eutrophication and ensuring good water quality for humans and marine organisms. They also relate to the project’s objective of protecting and promoting biodiversity and the natural heritage by supporting initiatives to conserve the valuable Black Sea ecosystems, as they address the root causes of the problems, the main pressures from human activities: industry, agriculture, domestic wastewater, sea transport (oil spills, ballast water), urbanisation, tourism leading to coastal zone degradation.
