EnerCmed responds to INTERREG MED goal of facilitate plans&strategies for energy transition and resilience in cities and reinforce citizens engagement for more sustainable living area and delivers a multi-city replication programme to enable further MED cities to adopt the solutions

titleEn: Governing sustainable tourism in territories with high environmental value: reconnecting tourism and nature for addressing the climate crisis with an ecosystem-based approach
summaryEn:
The Mediterranean is a vulnerable hotspot in the current Climate Emergency. Tourism is and will be one of the most impacted economic sectors, with heightened risks, including flooding and erosion of key coastal assets. The recent Transition Pathway for Tourism and the Glasgow Declaration are building a global momentum for Climate Action in Tourism, but policy makers and destinations need support and new approaches. Nature can be a cornerstone to address this challenge, while ensuring the protection of key destination assets, such as beaches. How? Through climate mitigation and adaptation using ecosystem-based approaches, which can only be accomplished through strong governance, robust planning, and the engagement of the private sector and citizens.
NaTour4CChange will build on successful experiences at Med and global level to test solutions for increasing the resilience of coastal destinations in the Mediterranean. The project will set common methods to allow participating regions to assess their tourism-related climate adaptation and mitigation priorities, and take climate action via plans and strategies, supported by cooperative governance. In coastal destinations, cross-sector teams will deliver specific tourism climate action plans, focusing climate adaptation, where Nature-based Solutions will be tested to ensure their feasibility, while innovative destination marketing and communication approaches will engage private stakeholders, visitors and residents in climate action. Finally, NaTour4CChange will promote cross-fertilization among participating regions and destinations, to achieve common methods and to compare the different tested plans and solutions, which will lead to lessons, best practices and policy recommendations. Associated partners and external stakeholders —at regional, national and international scale— will benefit from these learnings in order to make a significant Med contribution to this global challenge.

titleEn: Supporting Adaptation to Mediterranean Sea Level Rise
summaryEn:
Climate change is evident in many aspects, among them there is the progressive increase of the average sea level, which is affecting the rare extremes too, both on their frequency and intensity.

The assessment of risks deriving from sea level variations requires a robust quantification of all the elements bringing the sea level to become a hazard thus, for an effective adaptation to future sea conditions, it is mandatory to have reliable knowledge on scenarios for sea level trends.

This is the challenge addressed by this project with the objective of improving the assessment of risks deriving from the Mediterranean sea level variations, through a robust quantification of its hazardous source.

Mediterranean coastal impacts are deduced from global sea level trends or climate simulation each affected by significant uncertainties, furthermore, there is an open debate, in the scientific community, on them. As a consequence, there is an urgent need to quantify the likelihood of available scientific information on the expected XXI century sea level trends, in the Mediterranean sub-basins, with an estimate of the uncertainties.

This project outputs are expected to contribute in meeting this need, defining best practices on sea level trends usage, in the risk assessment processes, according to the sensitivity of impacts to the hazard information likelihood. Best practices, supported by examples of applications and summary datasets, will help stakeholders to flow the scientific information into the risk assessment logic. Benefits are expected to reach a wide spectra of stakeholders from the economic and safety to the coastal ecosystem preservation sectors.

The project transnational partnership brings the inter-regional portrait of the challenge together with the interdisciplinarity required to understand how anthropic solutions and better preservation of the coastal ecosystems have to be involved in resilience and adaptation actions to the progressive sea level rise.

titleEn: HERItage and territory resilience through sustainable Tourism, climate change ADAPtation and ciTizen engagement
summaryEn:
Tourism represents an important industry for Euro-MED with Heritage tourism being a significant element of the overall tourist product. Yet, human activity and climate change pose risks to both cultural heritage (CH) and natural heritage (NH) assets in rural and urban environments. Impacts on heritage and subsequently to tourism have not yet been adequately examined and dealt with, posing additional socio-economic pressures to destinations that already suffer covid-19 consequences. In order to enhance sustainability and resilience of the sector, increased innovation, adaptation and mitigation capacities are needed, in line with quality principles to ensure the CH and NH protection. Proper action plans and strategies need to be developed or improved to address current challenges on one hand and unleash the untapped potential of CH and NH towards climate neutrality on the other. At the same time, sectoral fragmentation needs to be tackled to enable effective decision making.

HERIT ADAPT will foster cooperation among key stakeholders by activating interdisciplinary Territorial Working Groups (TWGs) to co-design the data-driven HERIT ADAPT Sustainable Tourism Model (STM) that will be tested in 8 pilot Euro-MED regions of different typologies, including UNESCO sites and lesser known monuments in coastal, hinterland and mountainous areas. The STM will take into account territorial needs and visions, existing frameworks and plans and the global technology offer, enabling the use of existing tools and solutions and the valorization of transnational knowledge gained from other projects. Following a co-creation approach HERIT ADAPT will truly engage target groups to identify lessons learnt and co-develop Sustainable and Resilient tourism Strategies. Finally, it will turn challenges into opportunities by using heritage as a vehicle for communicating CH and NH assets in the context of climate change and inspire the uptake of HERIT ADAPT innovative solutions from other regions.

titleEn: Testing Circular Economy solutions for the green transition of the Mediterranean area
summaryEn: CircleMED aims to convert the Euro-Med area into circular economy based territories, accelerating the diffusion of circular and climate-neutral practices and the green transition of the local civil, industrial and institutional systems. It points at reconciling our economies and human activities with the planetary boundaries. CircleMED’s integrated and systemic approach targets all the four helix stakeholders to promote the transition process to circular and sustainable production and consumption models, stimulating awareness and testing innovative circular solutions working closely with citizens, policy makers, business support organisations, academia, research entities and additional stakeholders, sharing knowledge and responsibilities for the green transition. Key elements CircleMED stress on are those considered fundamental for sustainable development: economic prosperity, environmental protection and social equity, balancing them to benefit current and future generations, targeting the three dimensions of citizens, SMEs and policy makers. CircleMED could be considered an evolutionary innovative project, testing solutions that already exist, but that have never been used together. It focuses on promoting circularity and testing resource efficiency particularly through an innovative circular assessment tool for SMEs, the creation of a transnational network of territorial circular hubs and the elaboration of plans for transferability of results in the whole Mediterranean area. The project aims at redesign, repair, reuse and recycle as driving scheme leading citizens, institutions and companies’ choices to a resource-efficient and competitive economy, further developing and scaling up circular approaches, methodologies and strategies easily adaptable to any kind of territory.

titleEn: TOURism Innovative and Sustainable Management of flOws
summaryEn:
The tourism industry, in the pre-pandemic years, focused almost exclusively on growth, with little concern for long-term impacts on territories. Thus, persistent challenges, like overtourism, continue to affect destinations & communities across the Med region.
TOURISMO acknowledges that a shift to conscious and sustainable tourism requires innovative approaches, participation of various ecosystem stakeholders, an improvement of the tourist experience & a stronger engagement of end users.
TOURISMO aims at addressing these challenges by using innovative technologies that offer new solutions and novel services to monitor and manage tourist flows.
By exploiting the foundations laid by its predecessor HERIT-DATA, TOURISMO will keep boosting innovation through new methodologies and tools in areas with high tourism pressure. 
Better flows handling will be implemented through the development of a monitoring & decision-making support management structure and testing in 8 MED pilot sites. The approach is based on utilizing data from various datasets and on-site technologies (ie thermal cameras, pax counters, drones, tags) relevant to tourists’ presence, density, trajectories and behaviors, 
with the support of an enriched version of HERIT-DATA platform, developed and managed by University of Florence. 
The partnership embeds a variety of location profiles (UNESCO areas, ports, city centers, beaches, cultural monuments, parks etc.) from 7 European countries (GR, IT, ES, CY, BG, HR & MT) & different stakeholders of the value chain (Development Agencies, RTOs, Scientific experts, Innovation Institutes and Intermediaries, NGOs) allowing to test solutions in different environments, as well as capitalizing previous experience, guaranteeing simultaneously a high degree of innovation.
Actions foreseen address directly or indirectly the key groups of stakeholders namely public authorities, tourist agencies, DMOs, solution providers &the traditional tourism SMEs.

titleEn: MAking Sustainable Tourism possible
summaryEn: The common challenges addressed by the project are: (i) overcoming differences and uniting Mediterranean SMEs accommodation around the common objective of reshaping tourism in more sustainable ways; (ii) stimulating and supporting them in the implementation of sustainable management systems, through the development of easily applicable solutions. The overall objective is to facilitate and support Mediterranean SMEs accommodation in implementing a sustainable management system, which is currently a critical factor for the success and competitiveness in the long term. The expected change is to facilitate the transition towards sustainable tourism by such SMEs, enabling them to implement a sustainable management system and to pave the way for achieving the ISO 21401:2018 certification. To this end, the project foresees the development of two outputs: sustainability protocol and the self-assessment tool. The latter will enable these SMEs to check their current degree of sustainability; based on the results obtained, the protocol will indicate the activities needed to comply with the standard. The approach will be to conduct a study based on ISO 21401:2018 and the identification of the barriers and needs of SMEs accomodation in terms of sustainable management. Given the different socio-economic realities and stages of tourism development in the five partner countries, transnational cooperation is a crucial factor in ensuring the high-quality achievement of the objectives as well as the dissemination of the results. The project represents a novelty compared to current practices in the accommodation sector; it proposes a study aimed at defining solutions that balance the specificities of all dimensions of sustainability. To date, most tourism professionals and scholars have proposed the sustainability of accommodation facilities based almost exclusively on the environmental dimension, causing a delay in the full development of a sustainable organisational culture.

titleEn: improving WEtland GOvernance through a COmmunity Of Practice
summaryEn:
Mediterranean Wetlands are extremely vulnerable ecosystems, often under environmental protection. The Ramsar Convention defines them as one of the most productive and biodiverse environments in the world, providing the habitat on which countless species depend. They are highly subject to external pressures including i) the state of health of the river basins to which they refer; ii) intensive agriculture causing water consumption and water and soil pollution; iii) heavy urbanization.
Wetlands are often challenged by the poor coordination and capacity of institutions to manage complex territorial dynamics needing different levels of planning. Thus, the active protection of wetlands biodiversity requires overcoming the current sectoral approach and addressing the problem systemically. 
WE GO COOP addresses these issues by promoting the implementation of the Wetland Contract, a multilevel collaborative governance tool tested in several EU-funded projects, fostering coordination between organizations previously involved and new central stakeholders.
The project will:
1- Set up a Community of Practice (CoP) amongst actors engaged in Wetland Contracts at the Mediterranean level, capitalizing on the outcomes of former EU-funded projects, sharing challenges and solutions;
2- Exchange experiences, methodologies, and strategies, and transfer the Wetland Contract tool to new contexts in the Euro-Med region (Croatia, Portugal, Albania) and the South and Middle East Med region.
Transnational cooperation becomes the tool through which WE GO COOP forms the CoP uniting different perspectives facing similar challenges, enabling the project to meet the needs of wetlands on a large scale, ensuring the transferability of its results.
WE GO COOP is expected to:
1- Improve knowledge about wetland collaborative governance processes,
2- Improve collaboration between researchers, policy-makers, experts, environmental associations, key stakeholders, and communities.

titleEn: REPair PERspective
summaryEn:
Why not? Re-thinking traditional business models, re-discovering the centrality of human value in the pursuit of innovation and competitiveness, re-viewing behaviors, all toward a circular economy model, is more urgent than ever.
Why not? To support SMEs in the repair economy, increase repair skills, and pursue the transition to more sustainable choices by overcoming the existing repair barriers. 
The REPper project aims to address these challenges and propose concrete solutions to meet them.
A global challenge such as sustainability, by reducing waste, increasing reuse, adopting regenerative practices and - heart of the project- implementing repair, can only be met by acting on a transnational scale.
How? Through 3 action areas strongly focused on cross-border cooperation: 

1. Setting-up a REPper HUBS NETWORK - a unique contact point, physical and/or digital - with the aim of designing and testing a transnational network of pilot services. 

2. Creating a REPper FACTORY for upskilling and reskilling, providing training at the highest EU level, to reduce imbalances between Mediterranean regions. 

3. Building a new repair culture through "gentle nudges" - NUDGING - that can trigger positive changes and new habits. 
These actions will inspire joint solutions such as business model canvas, blueprint, and Nudge; strategies and action plans (Roadmap, recommendations, and policy papers); and, finally, cooperative outputs with an eye to the future: an e-pledge and a letter of interest. 
To do this, REPper brings together highly qualified and diversified partners, capable of capitalizing on the past results, implementing them with new actions for public and private targets: SMEs, public authorities, sectoral agencies, business support organizations, schools and, last but not least, citizens. 
And if "Why not?" is a question that offers multiple solutions bringing us closer to a Greener Europe, REPper wants to take up the challenge by offering a different perspective.

titleEn: Transformative co-creation innovation labs for the Blue Sustainable Economy
summaryEn:
BLUE ECOSYSTEM will test innovative methodologies focused on supporting territory-making processes through knowledge production in the blue sustainable economy, building on existing experiences achieved thanks to previous MED projects ( MISTRAL, Blue BIo MED and B-BLUE). The strong and complementary partnership, led by Emilia-Romagna Region, will assure effective results and concrete attempts towards a more sustainable and resilient blue economy in the Mediterranean area. Shared conceptual framework approach with Dialogue4Innovation project guarantees a wider impact on institutional dialogue and innovation policy governance. BLUE ECOSYSTEM will design, test and validate:
- a Transformative co-creation innovation labs (TRAIN labs) in each pilot region: Balearic Island, Emilia-Romagna, Sud Paca-Occitanie, Zadar County, Alentejo, Attica, Albania, in coherence with regional action plans on blue economy.
- a BLUE ECOMATCH program: a MED transnational open innovation process to address MED complex challenges and match, connect and identify transnational opportunities for the solution acceleration;
- a Transformative Book for Blue sustainable economy, sharing the overall project approach, the main outcomes and best practices for the mutual learning about Transformative innovation.
A wide use of TRAIN Lab methodology, supported by initiatives of mutual learning such as the BLUE ECOMATCH program, will make possible a change in the mindset of 5 helix stakeholders and key-players of the Blue economies, towards a wider use of co-designed innovation and cutting edge technologies, lastly generating the adoption of more sustainable business models in the private sector, the development of new skills in the blue sectors markets and contributing to the removal institutional and cultural barriers that hamper advanced innovation in blue economies.

titleEn: Capturing and Storing Atmospheric CO2 for Improvement of Soil Quality
summaryEn:
Two of the biggest challenges of human civilization are how to reduce CO2 in the atmosphere and how to preserve the soil quality. Too much carbon in the air causes greenhouse effect, and too little carbon in the soil reduces soil quality. 

Proposed project will prepare scientific foundations for reducing CO2 in the air and storing it into the soil, using SUSTAINABLE SOIL MANAGEMENT, called "CARBON FARMING". Since carbon farming is innovative topic in EU (policy emerged in 2021), there is an urgent need to quickly define standards, monitoring procedures and socio-economic models to test carbon farming in future. 

CARBON 4 SOIL QUALITY project will prepare "Toolbox for carbon farming" consisting of (i) Catalogue of soil organic reference values, (ii) Methodology for organic carbon analysis and soil quality monitoring (iii), Guidelines for carbon farming techniques, (iv) carbon farming business models, (v) Recommendations on agriculture carbon credit schemes and environmental certification systems.

Action plan will be prepared on the transnational level to properly plan testing phase. It will consider at least 5 testing sites in different countries, including at least one IPA country and one new Interreg Euro-MED territory. 

Transnational cooperation is needed for studying different Mediterranean climate zones (sub-tropical, oceanic, semi-arid, arid), different erosion conditions and different types of soil.

Project follow-up will test carbon farming techniques to support farmers with practical knowledge, how to increase soil organic matter. This will improve plant nutrients, increase soil water storage and provide good habitat for soil living organisms, which enhances soil biodiversity. 

Carbon farming is considered as one of the European Green Deal climate actions and related EU policies will be developed in the 2023-2030 period. If approved, this project could become SUSTIAINABLE SOIL MANAGEMENT lighthouse example of Euro-MED territory and showcase for the EU.

titleEn: Clepsydra - Groundwater monitoring and Decision Support System development to optimise decision-making in sensitive and water-scarce agricultural environments in the Mediterranean context
summaryEn:
A clepsydra is a water clock, where water measures the time and, in this project it is the water which will be "measured" in time. In fact, there is a need to improve conventional aquifers monitoring networks which mainly control aquifer saturated zone, having a limited value for the assessment of the impact of pollution prevention measures taken. Additionally, a smart tool to interpret hydrogeological data is needed because current numerical flow models to predict groundwater pollution and level is not friendly for all users. Also, raising awareness of civil society about the importance of aquifers is needed.

Clepsydra aims to develop and test a smart system for monitoring and interpreting hydrogeological data on the behaviour of aquifers (including the development of a Decision Support System - DSS), with special attention to groundwater quality in agriculture to be able to make decisions. By improving current monitoring networks and developing a DSS, water and agriculture professionals will be able to make environmentally friendly decisions based on reliable scientific data.

In the project, the increased cooperation and capacities of the 4helix stakeholders is a guiding principle to generate project results with greater impact. The project involves 9 partners from 6 Med countries (PT, ES, FR, IT, MT & EL), made up of public authorities, academia, agriculture, groundwater users and a water cluster. 

In the pilot sites, Clepsydra Project will harness the innovation potential of the DSS and align it with upgraded groundwater monitoring practices. 4helix stakeholders will be involved in the project and public-private partnerships will be generated with the incorporation of final users and private sector in the improvement of monitoring networks.

titleEn: Enhancing MED sustainable cultural tourism through the creation of eco-itineraries inside European Cultural Routes
summaryEn:
Cultural Tourism is a key asset in MED economies, however it has a strong, mutually detrimental relationship with climate change when tourism industries do not effectively incorporate sustainable practices. The MED area therefore needs to strategically re-shape its cultural tourism offer by matching its focus on local cultural heritage with greater sustainability. Cultural Routes of the Council of Europe (CRs) represent a key instrument to sustain and promote cultural tourism all over Europe, from mainstream destinations to small-scale local contexts. 
 
MEDRoutes overall objective is therefore to establish and disseminate a local-based, low-impact model of sustainable tourism across CRs in the MED area, in particular, to establish a specific model of Mediterranean "slow tourism" rooted in the common heritage of 4 CRs. 

To tackle the project general objective, MED-Routes’ approach is rooted in a TRANSFER rationale:
 -transfer mechanisms are put into place to cross-reference the most relevant, field-tested outputs from INCIRCLE & EMbleMatic projects for the design of eco-itineraries; 
-transfer mechanisms are further encouraged in application to MED-Routes experience through capacity building and institutional networking, especially in WP

4. By exploiting Cultural Routes’ plural and transnational dimension, MED-Routes will encourage the diffusion of its eco-itinerary model in the context of other CRs and by the initiative of similar institutional actors transnationally.

The combination of all these elements defines transfer & capitalization as the core assets in MED-Routes’ approach in an innovative perspective for sharing the main outputs:
-Transnational Strategy for sustainable tourism & eco-itineraries in the MED area 
-Green Label of Mediterranean CRs for the certification of eco-itineraries
-MED-Routes Action Plans outlining key actions to apply the Transn. Strategy into CRs’ agenda.

titleEn: Testing New European Bauhaus Solutions for Deep Green Transformation of Cities and Regions in Euro-MED area.
summaryEn:
Average citizen usually considers ecology and green transformation as something that “must be” done, instead of something they would “love to” do. To change this perception, the New European Bauhaus (NEB) initiative introduced aesthetic (beautiful) aspects along with citizens participation to support urban green transformation.

Project Bauhaus4MED will test innovative NEB solutions integrating sustainability, inclusion and aesthetic aspects into decision making process, for improvement of green living areas. Results from Interreg MED BLUE CROWDFUNDING project will be upgraded into a new “CROWDVOCACY” tool combining crowdfunding, crowdsourcing and participative democracy principles, with aesthetic green architecture design resulting in citizens tailor-made solutions for better living.

Each of the 5 testing regions/cities will identify participative green community challenges, use crowdsourcing to co-create solution ideas, run civic crowdfunding campaigns to co-finance solutions and use participative budgets to implement pilot solutions. Pilot solutions will be focused on circular building materials, regenerated green urban spaces, green products, or green lifestyle. Transferrable toolbox will be offered as a solution including best example catalogue, lessons learned and CROWDVOCACY digital tool. To mainstream NEB principles into the decision making process, and ensure long term sustainability, the regions/cities will develop green transformation action plans, using green, participative, and aesthetic principles.

Project will improve policy impact, transferability and durability of outputs and deliverables by organizing significant number of regional and EU level events taking advantage of PP10 IFLA Europe unique position as member of NEB COLLECTIVE. Actions will include high-policy NEB annual conferences in Brussels, regions joining NEB initiative, Transnational Green Transformation Challenge event and preparation of Applications to NEB Rising Stars 

2025.

titleEn: Invasive Alien Species Observatory and Network Development for the Assessment of Climate Change Impacts and Contextual Ecosystem Services Evaluation in Black Sea Deltaic Protected Areas
summaryEn:
The Black Sea Bioregion is under pressure from the massive presence of non-native species from the Mediterranean Sea, Indian Ocean or other parts of the world, in terms of maritime transport, climate change or expanding human presence, economic development, etc. In present, the “Mediteranization” of the Black Sea is widely debated in the scientific community, starting with the topic of climate change. A significant number of entities develop economic activities in the coastal areas of the Black Sea, especially in deltaic areas, known for their population density and growth potential.
IASON+ Project focuses on the influence of Invasive Alien Species (IAS) on Ecosystem Services (ES) in the Black Sea Basin (BSB) area, specifically targeting the deltaic ecosystems of the rivers from five countries – Danube (Romania and Ukraine), Nestos (Greece), Kızılırmak (Türkiye), Chorokhi, and Kolkheti (Georgia). The project aims to address the common challenge posed by IAS in these deltaic regions and the impact on ES. These deltaic regions are particularly vulnerable to the introduction and spread of IAS due to their unique ecological characteristics, including diverse habitats and high biodiversity. IAS can disrupt the delicate balance of these ecosystems, threaten native species, and negatively impact the provision of ES such as water purification, flood regulation, coastal protection, fisheries, and tourism.
The overall objective of the project is to enhance the management and mitigation of IAS in the deltaic regions from the BSB to safeguard and restore ES. The project aims to bring about positive change by reducing the spread and impact of IAS, improving the resilience of ecosystems, and ensuring the sustainable provision of ES in the deltaic regions.
The project will develop several outputs and achieve specific results to meet its objectives. These include:


1. IAS Monitoring and Warning System: the project will establish a robust monitoring system to track the presence and spread of IAS in the deltaic regions. This will involve the development of standardized protocols, data collection, and analysis, and the establishment of an early warning system to detect and respond to the presence of IAS.


2. Integrated Management Strategies and Action Plans: the project will formulate integrated management strategies and action plans to effectively control and manage IAS in the deltaic regions. These strategies will include measures such as prevention and interception of IAS, eradication and control efforts, and habitat restoration initiatives.


3. Capacity Building and Training: the project will provide capacity building programs and training workshops for various stakeholders in the deltaic regions. This includes local communities, policymakers, land managers, scientists, and relevant authorities. Capacity building efforts will enhance knowledge and skills related to IAS management, detection, and prevention.


4. The main outputs of the project: involve the development of tools that will be made available to stakeholders for a better management of the presence of IAS and their influence on ES - (I) ICT tool referring to the storage and management of environmental monitoring data from deltaic area of the project; (II) ICT tool referring to the upload of field data from IAS and ES monitoring; (III) ICT tool referring to the map-based IAS and ES distribution outputs; (IV) ICT tool referring to the Living-Lab & mobile application for citizens; (V) ICT tool referring to the gamification use.
The main beneficiaries of the project's outputs and results:
- Local communities living in the deltaic regions, whose livelihoods depend on the sustainable provision of ES.
- Biodiversity conservation organizations and agencies responsible for managing and protecting the unique ecosystems of the deltaic regions. 
- Policymakers and government authorities involved in environmental management and decision-making processes. 
- Scientists and researchers interested in studying the impacts of IAS and developing effective management strategies. 
- Industries and sectors that rely on ecosystem services, such as tourism, agriculture, fisheries, and water resource management.
The project adopts a transnational approach due to the nature of the deltaic regions from different countries in the BSB, this being crucial to effectively address the challenge of IAS in these regions. The planned approach involves collaboration, knowledge exchange, and joint efforts among partners from different countries and deltaic regions. This cooperation enables the sharing of experiences, expertise, best practices, and resources, facilitating a more comprehensive and coordinated response to the issue of IAS in the BSB deltaic regions. By working together, the project partners can leverage their collective strengths, learn from each other's experiences, and develop integrated management strategies that are tailored to the specific characteristics of the deltaic regions.

titleEn: Pilot action for increasing the capacity of local and regional administrations to develop and implement innovative food waste public awareness actions
summaryEn:
The common challenge FoodWISE project will address, is to reduce the consumer-related food waste and encourage citizens and guests in the BSB area to rethink and adopt more sustainable habits regarding consumption and disposal of food. In the four project countries millions of foods are lost annually. The main reasons are the unwise buying, wrong storage and cooking without planning. To that extent, targeted policies and measures to prevent food waste are needed. Their main objective shall be to reduce the amount of food waste generated by the population of the region. As local households and tourists in the summer season are the main contributors to the huge amounts of food waste in the BSB region, raising their awareness of the problem of food loss and waste, and on examples aimed at inspiring behavior change that prevents food waste will be main subject of all project actions.
Considering that curbing food waste requires targeted continuous actions at local, regional and international level for raising awareness and empowering people to change their resource-intensive consumption patterns, the project aims at empowering authorities at local level, as they are closest to the citizens in the rural areas, where the non-governmental sector is underdeveloped. To that end, the project activities will bring together 20 small coastal rural municipalities from 4 BSB countries dedicated to curbing food waste out of their territories. To achieve this goal the project will equip 50 of their employees with knowledge and expertise to drive together the progress towards sustainable food consumption in their territories.
FoodWISE`s general objective is to enhance the potential of local and regional administrations in rural areas in the BSB region, in particular settlements with high tourism pressure during summer season, to jointly educate and raise awareness of local citizens and tourists as regards food waste prevention and reduction as a tool for reducing all forms of pollution in their territories. In this respect, four organisations from Bulgaria, Turkiye, Georgia and Greece with substantial experience in non-formal education provision, will join forces to develop and validate a comprehensive training program (FoodWISE). The project approach involves a series of complementary actions for promoting innovation and knowledge transfer in the field of reducing the human impact on the regional natural resources and biodiversity, intensive capacity building and public awareness campaign, as well as events with high transnational added value and potential for achieving the common goal to tackle food waste in the region.
The project will begin with assessing the existing and desired competencies for effective public food waste promotion. By identifying the capacity gaps and skills` needs of the local and regional administrations` employees, the project partners will be able to design tailor-made training curriculum and Toolkit for development of skilled, adaptable workforce with the right mix of competencies for effective communication, motivation, and engagement of citizens in environmentally friendly actions related to food waste. The Toolkit will illustrate examples of food waste prevention in action and guidance how to use and up-take these proven experiences. The International training targeting 50 public and municipal civil servants in local authorities will empower them with knowledge and practical skills and tools to design and implement innovative actions focusing on educating citizens on how to curb food waste from the BSB region. Once the local actors have been trained, they would be able to validate the skills acquired by joining forces with the project team in the organization of innovative awareness raising actions targeting local households, students, tourists vacationing in the region. Trainees will be integral part of the joint organization and implementation of 1 International “I VALUE FOOD” student contest, 4 “FOOD WASTE PATROL” campaigns, 4 REPLATE festivals, 1 International high-level conference under the supervision of the project team. These actions will teach how to cooperate with organizations from different countries and design and implement joint actions, which bring people in the region closer together.
In the long term, the local actors are expected to work together to making the BSB territory more resilient to climate change and ensure its common natural heritage and its unique value is protected from the growing pressure of human activity. Considering that the environmental resources of the Black Sea Basin are shared across borders and go beyond national interests, cooperation is crucial, otherwise good work in one place is quickly undone by neglect elsewhere. Accordingly, the project aims at BSB rural territories to lead the process of spreading and mainstreaming food waste prevention, in order to achieve a drastic reduction of the pollution deriving from it.

titleEn: Acting Together for Greener Cities
summaryEn:
The GREENCITIES project addresses environmental and socio-economic challenges arising from rapid urbanization and industrialization in the Black Sea Region. Its focus is on developing green areas in underutilized land plots to mitigate pollution, restore biodiversity and improve air and water quality.

Transnational cooperation is crucial to achieving the project's objectives. By sharing knowledge, best practices and experiences among project partners, it enables collaborative efforts in developing green alternatives, promoting sustainable development and implementing effective strategies to address common challenges. This approach allows for pooling resources and expertise to undertake ambitious initiatives with a greater impact.

The project takes a comprehensive and innovative approach to tackle the identified challenges. It focuses on developing green spaces, engaging local communities and raising awareness about the benefits of greening initiatives and climate change adaptation. Underutilized land plots are transformed into vibrant green spaces through the installation of vegetation and features for greening and public use. The project emphasizes the concept of green infrastructure, strategically planning natural and semi-natural areas to deliver ecosystem services and enhance environmental conditions.

The project's outputs will benefit various stakeholders. Local and national public authorities will gain knowledge, expertise and guidelines for urban greening initiatives, improving the quality of urban areas and promoting sustainable development. NGOs focused on environmental protection and community well-being will receive support and resources to strengthen their initiatives. SMEs will benefit from business opportunities, networking and collaboration in the sustainable urban development sector. The general public, including citizens of all age groups, will enjoy the positive impacts of urban greening, such as improved well-being, recreational opportunities and aesthetic enhancements.

The project partnership involves local public authorities responsible for urban planning and development. They collaborate to develop master plans that guide city growth, comply with urban planning regulations, create and maintain green areas, conduct environmental impact assessments, manage waste collection and disposal and promote sustainability. The LP, IPA, a subsidiary of IMM, plays a central role in managing and coordinating project activities. Their expertise in project management, urban planning and environmental protection ensures effective communication and successful project delivery. They also have experience in risk assessment and mitigation and proficiency in using innovative tools such as 3D and heat maps.

The project aims to improve the urban environment by creating green spaces. It involves selecting suitable locations and developing concept plans for these spaces. Stakeholder engagement is crucial and various materials and reports will be generated to involve the community in decision-making. Detailed technical plans and designs will ensure compliance with regulations. Once established, the green spaces will be equipped with resources, monitoring systems and waste management tools. Training sessions, conferences and workshops will enhance knowledge and collaboration. The project will result in improved urban aesthetics, enhanced biodiversity, increased community engagement and effective planning. It will also promote environmental monitoring, recreational opportunities and long-term sustainability. The outcomes will contribute to evidence-based decision-making, raise awareness and foster international collaboration in the Black Sea Region.

The Greencities project ensures sustainability in terms of ownership, lasting effects and transferability. Financial sustainability is achieved through resource allocation and budgeting by participating municipalities. Institutional sustainability is ensured by establishing ownership of project outputs and maintaining dedicated staff for maintenance. The project also aims for political sustainability by influencing policies and legislation. The project's outputs, such as selected green space locations, concept plans, stakeholder engagement materials and maintenance plans, will have lasting effects on urban planning, community engagement and environmental practices. These outputs will be shared and applied to inspire and guide future initiatives. The project also promotes transferability by providing blueprints, documentation and knowledge-sharing on green space creation, stakeholder engagement, vegetation strategies, equipment implementation, monitoring, evaluation, training and communication. The project website will serve as a platform for dissemination. Overall, the Greencities project seeks to create a long-term impact in the Black Sea region, promoting sustainable and livable cities.

titleEn: Cooperation for Sustainable Energy and Climate Actions’ Planning and Monitoring in BSB
summaryEn:
Cooperation for Sustainable Energy and Climate Actions’ Planning and Monitoring in BSB: STEP2CleanPlan is a cross-border cooperation instrument for capacity building and awareness in the field of climate change adaptation planning, with outputs ready to be used by the local and regional policy-makers. 
The goal of the STEP2CleanPlan project is to improve the ability of local decision-makers to plan strategically in accordance with national climate adaptation plans and to carry out effective actions in support of previously existing local plans in this area.
The fundamental issue with climate change planning procedures is building the adaptive capacity of diverse actors and communities to deal with the adverse effects of climate change. 
Cities contribute to pollution and climate change. However, they also have the ability and opportunity to deliver the highest savings. They can be inspiring role models in driving climate adaptation and the energy transition.
However, in some cases local and regional authorities lack the capacity to develop and implement such plans and strategies, including small municipalities, rural and isolated areas and carbon-intensive regions that are lagging behind in the clean energy transition, and have the potential to have a high impact on reducing their fossil fuel consumptions. Many municipalities, particularly those in border regions of EU and non-EU countries, still require assistance in developing medium and long-term transition plans and strategies, such as Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plans or similar plans.
One of the main aim of the current project is to ensure better informed decision making in line with the EU Climate Adaptation strategy and all National Adaptation Plans of the targeted countries and establish local capacity in responding to the assessment, reporting and implementation requirements of these plans.
The main challenges in the targeted three countries in their path in putting certain measures for urban climate change adaptation are related to the need for adoption of local adaptation strategies into national/regional and local legal frameworks in urban, spatial and coastal planning, transport and energy. 
The project outputs are: 
- Ensured engagement and awareness of the policy -makers in the BSB on the adaptation tools and strategies: Building awareness and supporting the local policymakers for application and awareness the EU policy, tools and instruments in Climate Change Adaptation strategic planning. Deep analyses of the existing situation in the target areas will be done and joint GUIDE for policymakers with networks, providing ongoing support, tools, lessons learned and best practices in planning for and implementing mitigation efforts for climate change issued. 
- All partners will be responsible for the continuation of the established partnership and after the end of the project. They will sign a memorandum of partnership which will involve also the target municipalities as Byala Municipality in BG and Kalamaria Municipality in Greece with determined cooperation roles in exchange of good practices, lessons learned, participating in joint networks stimulating and guiding the local policy -makers in the adaptation to the climate change and their promotion. 
- Established sustainable cooperation for capacity building and awareness of the policy-makers on the climate change adaptation planning and mitigation initiatives: four partners together with two target municipalities will establish sustainable partnership and cooperation for exchange of good practices, policies and joint measures in climate change adaptation in the Black Sea Basin. 
- Promotion Climate change adaptation through taking certain Climate Mitigation Planning Steps in BSB: Four certain frameworks/ plans will be developed in the frame of the project that actually will directly contribute for the mitigating the negative effect of the climate change at local and global levels. The frameworks will be the important one in the field of energy efficiency observation, sustainable urban mobility and plan for decreasing carbon footprint of the waste management practices of the local municipality. 
- Increased Awareness and Capacity for climate adaptation and sustainable planning for mitigating its effect in the BSB: implementation of three monthly mentoring program for local and regional policymakers in the BSB, together with joint study visits in GR and BG, workshops, information meetings with the target groups and stakeholders and final joint conference in BG. 
The main approach that the project will use for tackling the identified common challenges will be establishing sustainable transnational cooperation for joint capacity building of local and regional actors in analysing, applying, preparing, and implementing climate change adaptation strategies and supporting local policymakers in implementing certain adaptation measures.

titleEn: Cooperation and Awareness for Pollution-free and Environmentally Sustainable Black Sea
summaryEn:
The CARE SEA project is proposed by a partnership of 5 higher education and /or research organizations. The lead partner is LP1 - BSU - The Batumi Shota Rustaveli State University from Georgia. The other partners are from Moldova (PP2 - USPEE which is a private university from Chisinau), Türkyie (PP3 - KTU - The Technical University in Trabzon), Greece (PP4 - AUTH - Aristotle University in Thessaloniki) and Romania (PP5 - DDNI - the National R&D Institute for Danube Delta in Tulcea). The partners have both experience in previous projects as well as experience in co-operation among each other within other partnerships. The overall objective of the project is enhancing protection and preservation of nature and biodiversity by raising awareness on different types of pollution among communities and providing practical means of action towards a greener and cleaner Black Sea region during a 24-month period. The overall objective is in line with Programme's Priority 2 and relates to Policy's objective 2 by assessing risks and providing management instruments. All activities relate to Specific objective 

7. CARE SEA addresses the common territorial challenge of pollution with various components including plastic and microplastic which is acknowledged as a major threat for the Black Sea ecosystem. The Work Plan is divided into 6 activities: A.

1.

1. Development of common instruments and methodology for smart environmental observation (period 1 - 5), A.

1.

2. State of art of plastic pollution in study areas of the BSB ecosystem, analysis of the challenges and measures to reduce it (period 2 - 5). A.

1.

3. Exchange of experience / cross-border monitoring and assessment (period 3 - 5), A.

1.

4. Development of recommendations for the ecological rehabilitation of the studied ecosystems (period 4 - 6), A.

1.

5. Advancing public engagement with science and environmental knowledge production (period 3 - 6) and A.

1.

6. Valorization and dissemination of the collected data (period 4 - 6). Among the main outputs of the activities there are a common methodology and instruments for monitoring and assessing pollutants including a numerical model able to simulate the transport, advection, dispersion and weathering of small plastic particles that flow/float in a water body, a cross - border (Romanian and Moldovan) impact assessement of Prut River pollutants and cross - border (Georgian and Turkish) management plans and action plans for the Choroki river corresponding areas, an International Conference. Results understood as changes determined by outputs of the project include 4 organizations that will continue to cooperate after the end of the project as the implementation of the management and action plans for the Choroki River Georgian - Turkish border will require further cooperation between LP1 and PP3 - KTU and PP2 - USPEE and PP5 - DDNI will cooperate for implementation of common solutions on the Romanian - Moldovan border after the end of the project. Among the results is expected an improved management of the Choroki river target regions. LP1 - BSU and PP3 - KTU are in a position to provide assistance to local / regional authorities as well as to local communities to put into practice nature - based solutions and mitigation measures regarding pollution risks. Also, contribution to citizen science leading to increased awareness on pollution factors in BSB target regions within local communities and valuable information resources, based on sound scientific research but explained for layman use that can support local decision making processes and direct actions for fighting the effects of plastic and other types of pollution.
The CARE SEA project activities are targeted towards a wide array of stakeholders, from local communities and local and regional communities, to national authorities and agencies, but provide also information and solutions for businesses in the area, students, people and NGOs that are simply interested in improvind their living conditions by enhancing controll upon pollutants and implementing mitigation measures. In order to reach all these target groups, the communication objective is to provide accessible information to larger categories of public and to local communities on various types of pollution in the project's area, means to reduce it and actions that can be taken. As citizen science grows more and more prominent, it is more and more important to bring in front of the public the results of reasearch as soon as they are available. The other communication objective is to highlight the funding that makes possible all the endeavours in the project in a way that complies with the visibility rules of the Programme.

titleEn: Green Climate Change Adaptation Solutions for Smart and Resilient Cities in BSB
summaryEn:
The project is tackling the common challenge of the Black Sea Basin's area and actually globally: climate change and especially its heat-stress effect that are more sensitive and strong in the urban areas. 
Climate change is the biggest challenge of our time and its impacts are being felt more and more especially in the urban areas. As the global climate warms, cities are facing frequent and extreme heat waves that have significant impact on society, including a rise in heat-related deaths. For sure the cities are at the frontline of climate change.
Though cities are a big driver of planet-warming emissions, they are also engines of climate action and at the forefront of delivering solutions.  
Green Climate Change adaptation solutions for Smart and Resilient Cities in BSB: Green Urban Resilience project is a tool for cross-border cooperation aiming development of sustainable green climate solutions to promote adaptation to climate change and their integration into the planning work of local authorities, supported not only by the infrastructural green restoration, but also from the scientific knowledge and expertise of the landscape, urban planning and forest experts who will actually transfer the academic intelligence to the local sustainable planning and action, by development of the international LANDLAB, services to all target countries.
Cities and towns are not investing in green infrastructure. In order to reduce heat islands and create climate-resistant green cities, local municipalities should cooperate, work on combating climate change in line with the realistic and
sustainable strategies, that includes clear information about the current heat-stress and thermal discomforts of the citizens and are based on the green/blue urban infrastructural solutions for mitigating the urban warming. In this cooperation project the PPs aim to respond to these needs and to make resilient Europe and BSB by sharing joint academic intelligence in the green urban sustainable planning, provide communities with accessible green
infrastructure and a better environment for healthy, sustainable and resilient cities, as well as to reduce the increasing risk from heat and its consequences.
The main project outputs will be capitalization of the European experience in measuring of the urban heat -stress and application of this knowledge in the BSB's cities and regions through establishing International Urban LANDLAB servicing to all regions and guiding them in development of Heat Resilient Strategies as a part from the planning measures that the local policy makers are taking in the climate change adaptation. Four target cities: Uzunkopru, Sozopol, Tbilisi and Kavala will receive the expertise of the LANDLAB for measuring their heat-stress and evaluating the thermal discomfort of the citizens on the basis of the joint approach. Based on this measure they will receive their Heat-stress maps and clear view of their warming and the need of the green/blue infrastructural solutions. The expertise of the LANDLAB will support these cities for elaboration of their Heat Resilience Strategies by preparing a Planning Pathway tool. The tool will be a roadmap for all policy makers in the Black Sea Basin presenting main steps for elaboration of sustainable Heat Resilient Strategies.  Case studies such as green recovery initiatives - practice-based examples of heat stress interventions in public spaces in three target areas will be done: Uzunkopru town will decrease the heat-stress by establishing the first urban community garden with a center for public-awareness and capacity building in green sustainability. Sozopol town's nature-friendly pedestrian alley will be built as a part of the  socialization of the park territory. There a rainwater collection facility will be built, which will be used to water new afforestation and build flower patches. Kavala will demonstrate green sustainability by introducing the circularity in green resources and attempts a small change and the local climate conditions, planting trees for shading in one of the most affected areas by climate change, namely the Faliro junction road and Ergatico Kentro Square urban corners that share the same characteristics as areas with high density, absence of trees or vegetation, and urban spaces that facilitate ad hoc parking spaces instead of serving as public spaces in use for recreational activities. All green initiatives will be in line with the New European Bauhaus policy: inclusive and sustainable. 
Capacity building of local environmental and planning experts in heat-measuring will be made by realization of joint heat-walks and workshops. Training for trainers and local training will be done as a tool to emphasize the importance of the local communities, citizens in the fight against climate change and promoting the importance of green spaces. Strong involvement of the community will be ensured by a work with the local initiative groups at each project stage.

titleEn: Transnational Technology Transfer Network for Black Sea Basin
summaryEn:
The Territorial Analysis (TA) was conducted and published to identify the main joint challenges and needs of the Black Sea Basin (BSB). According to this;

- Most of the companies are SMEs and their competitiveness is relatively low and they operate in low value-added sectors.

- The global competitiveness and innovation indexes show that the weakest point of the project partner countries are research and innovation capacity. Particularly in the field of university-industry R&D collaboration, which is one of the innovation linkages under the business sophistication pillar and one of the important tools of technology transfer (TT) processes.

- The TA shows that the BSB area has rich scientific potential, although it faces difficulties such as the migration of researchers and rather low R&D expenditure. However according to SWOT analysis within the TA identified one of the weaknesses as "ineffective transfer of knowledge into innovation"

- Strategic Research and Innovation Agenda for the Black Sea proposed activities by 2030 such as networking events and meetings towards capacity building to transfer knowledge, support the dialogue between researchers and business, develop and enhance networks to ensure interaction between the ongoing projects and research activities, create, integrate and support incubators and techno parks for promoting SMEs, start-ups and innovative businesses, to reach its goals.

- The third implementation report of the Black Sea Synergy (2015-2018) stated that important progress had been noted in some the fields while less and no significant registered progress was made in others.

- The TA indicates that the countries in the BSB area have low levels of innovation infrastructure and investment. However, the countries have not enough resources to satisfy the needs. In other words, joint actions needed to be taken to ensure basin-based prosperity.

- At the international scale, networks of structures in the field of technology transfer have been established in different structures, but there are no network structures in which all or some of the countries in the BSB are involved

- The efforts of TT interfaces are not at the desired level due to the breadth and activity of the network owned by the relevant structures, the competence of the relevant personnel and not having the same motivation of the potential institutions, organizations or interface structures to cooperate with.

The overall objective of the project; is to contribute to the developing and enhancing research and innovation capacities and the uptake of advanced technologies with creation sustainable transnational network structures and for sharing good practices and know-how on the use of innovative technological developments especially in blue economy, low carbon economy, resilience and adaptation to climate change fields.

The framework of the project has been designed to cover the potential cooperation actions in which the Joint paper on Interreg NEXT Strategic Programming 2021 - 2027 for BSB in order to tackle and develop solutions to the above mentioned common territorial challenges. 

The project will address the lack of sustainable transnational network structures and platforms for sharing good practices and know-how on the use of innovative technological developments especially in blue economy, low carbon economy, resilience and adaptation to climate change fields. In this respect, Transnational Technology Transfer Network for Black Sea Basin (T3N-BSB) will be established within the scope of the project.

The main outputs of the project are comprehensive study report of TT ecosystem, practical learning activity, training modules, trainings, multidimensional analysis tool, online catalog of technology cases and model project database, the T3N-BSB Portal, Transnational Technology Transfer Network for Black Sea Basin and Grand Black Sea Forum. The target group that will contribute or take part in the implementation of the project activities and benefit from the outputs of this project consists of all actors of the technology transfer ecosystem, namely HEIs and RIs, academics, entrepreneurs and industrialists, students, staff working in TT interfaces, relevant actors (clusters, companies, organised industrial zones-OIZs, business support organisations, chambers of commerce and industry etc.).

Although the ways of doing business are different in each country, the challenges mentioned above often arise due to the nature of research and innovation. TA has also revealed that this problem cannot be easily tackled by the individual efforts of the countries and that joint efforts are required. However, countries have established various mechanisms at national scale for the development of research and innovation ecosystem and commercialisation of the outputs. Therefore, transnational cooperation is needed in order to properly commercialise research and innovation projects’ results and create international impact.

titleEn: Nature-Based Solutions to Increase Community Resilience Against Climate-Induced Disasters
summaryEn:
The project titled "Nature-Based Solutions to Increase Community Resilience Against Climate-Induced Disasters" aims to address the shared challenge of climate-induced disasters by implementing nature-based solutions (NBS) that enhance community resilience in Georgia and Turkey. Leveraging the experience from Greece, the project emphasizes transnational cross-border cooperation among the Black Sea 4 project partner organisations (GIPA, Ecolution, WRI Turkey and FRI) to achieve its objectives and deliver sustainable change. 
The main objective of the project is to reduce community vulnerability to climate-induced disasters by implementing NBS. Recognizing that conventional approaches may not offer long-term solutions, NBS provide innovative and sustainable alternatives. By restoring and conserving ecosystems, the project seeks to enhance community resilience, mitigate disaster risks, and adapt to climate change.
To achieve these goals, the project will develop various key outputs and results. It will conduct comprehensive assessments of the project area's vulnerability to climate-induced disasters, considering the specific contexts and challenges faced by communities. This assessment will inform the design and planning of NBS interventions tailored to local conditions, ensuring their effectiveness and long-term sustainability.
A participatory approach will be employed to engage with local communities, government agencies, civil society organizations, and other stakeholders. Through training programs and workshops, communities will be empowered with the necessary knowledge and skills to implement and maintain NBS. This approach fosters ownership and ensures the long-term success and replicability of the project's outcomes.
Transnational cooperation plays a vital role in the project's success. Collaboration between partners from Georgia, Turkey, and Greece, who face similar challenges, will facilitate the sharing of experiences, best practices, and lessons learned. This cooperation will enable the project to access a broader range of expertise, innovative technologies, and opportunities, thereby increasing its impact and effectiveness.
The project's benefits will extend far beyond its immediate scope. Local communities, particularly in six municipalities in the Ajara region of Georgia and seven municipalities in Northern Marmara Region of Turkey will directly benefit from increased resilience and reduced disaster risks. By implementing an NBS action plan in selected municipalities, the project will contribute to the restoration and protection of ecosystems, preserving biodiversity and ecosystem services that benefit both people and the environment. Furthermore, the project will contribute to sustainable development by promoting climate adaptation, poverty reduction, and social well-being.
In conclusion, the project "Nature-Based Solutions to Increase Community Resilience Against Climate-Induced Disasters" highlights the importance of transnational cooperation in addressing the shared challenge of climate-induced disasters. By implementing NBS, engaging local communities, and fostering partnerships, the project aims to achieve sustainable change, enhance community resilience, and contribute to a more adaptable and climate-resilient future.

titleEn: Seed Guardians for Biodiversity, Agrobiodiversity, Ecosystem Services and Climate Adaptation
summaryEn:
In many countries of the world, including in the Black Sea region, a decrease in the diversity of plant genetic resources (PGR), considered a significant factor for environmental protection and mitigating the effect of climate change, is reported with concern. Particularly alarming is the systematically increasing loss of traditional local, authentic, old varieties of vegetables grown by small farmers, heirloom gardeners and hobby growers. These vegetables are increasingly losing the battle to the ones industrially produced, even though they are in daily demand and are preferred by the customers on the market, regardless of their higher prices. According to the UN FAO, local and indigenous varieties of food may have 1000 times the nutrient content of the more common varieties, which makes them extremely valuable for the humanity. This makes this proposal of high contribution to the people’s healthy diet. 
The decline in the production of local traditional vegetables leads to the loss of their seeds as genetic resource. In seed stores, the share of the traditional vegetable seeds is very small, if any. Authentic vegetable seeds can only be found from small agro-producers who continue to harvest and store seeds for their next production using traditional old methods. The increasing inaccessibility of seeds of traditional local vegetable varieties has engaged the attention of scientists and drove policy measures and actions of many national governments, the national genetic banks and a number of representative institutions, such as the Biodiversity International, the EC, the UN, etc. In Europe, the Scandinavian genetic bank, NordGen, is very active in reviving old vegetable landraces. The UN FAO initiated a legally binding global agreement, into force in 2004, the "International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture", ITPGRFA, for the conservation and sustainable use of all plant genetic resources for food and agriculture and the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising out of their use, in harmony with the Convention on Biological Diversity, for sustainable agriculture and food security. Currently, it has 149 Contracting Parties (countries) including the EU.
One of the actively implemented practical solutions in some countries is the creation of local community seed collections (CSCs) and community seed banks (CSBs), to store the seeds of old local traditional vegetables for reproduction and expansion of their territory. CSCs and CSBs are created, maintained and operated by local vegetable producers and communities, which are recognized by the international organizations as the contributors to the diversity of crops that feed the people and are part of a system to provide farmers and plant breeders with seeds and the scientists with access to plant genetic materials.
CSCs and CSBs are instrumental for mitigation of climate change and guaranteeing the food security of communities and citizens in general. They also support agrobiodiversity, healthy food production and diversity of food products on the market. The local authentic traditional vegetables have built integrity with the surrounding environment during a long period of time and have adapted to it. This makes them more resilient to diseases than industrial hybrid vegetable varieties which allow growing them without using artificial stimulants (chemicals).
With this project, we will establish CSCs on pilot territories of the PPs countries with a prospect to become CSBs at a next stage, with modern equipment for full potential and functionality and support from the national gene banks and research institutes, as part of enabling ecosystem environment for their sustenance. The members of the CSCs will be selected among small farmers, heirloom and hobby gardeners from the local communities after a careful procedure. Public media campaigns will be announced for collection of seeds of local vegetable landraces, thus giving a good example to follow by other Black Sea territories. 
The following outputs will result from the activities’ execution: Development and introduction of the innovative CSBs model in the pilot locations; Capacity building activities for the target groups including training & tutoring actions and organization of peer review exchange meetings of the seeds providers; Info events organized on the PPs territories for raising awareness and stimulation of joint initiatives for seeds’ preservation; Digital tools promoting CSCs in the four pilot territories; A Policy Document with recommendations for measures to be taken by policy and decision makers in support of the CSCs. 

SeedGuard is a partnership initiative of four partners representing four Black Sea countries: the Union of Bulgarian Black Sea Local Authorities as a lead partner, the Eastern Black Sea Development Agency (Turkey), the Association Global Project (Romania) and the National Association of Local Authorities (Georgia).

titleEn: Improving Emergency Response Capacities to Natural and Man-made Disasters in Small Communities across the Black Sea Basin Region
summaryEn:
Some of the most pressing challenges faced by countries in the Black Sea Basin region include their susceptibility to natural disasters and vulnerability to the impacts of climate change. This is particularly true for small communities, which are disproportionately affected by climate change and lack sufficient prevention, acknowledgement, and training activities. These communities are often ill-equipped to cope with the consequences of disasters, and relevant state institutions experience longer response times due to their remote locations. In light of these challenges, the project aims to enhance disaster risk prevention, climate change adaptation, and emergency response capacities in small communities of the Black Sea Basin region, with a specific focus on rural areas.

The overall objective of the project is to reduce the impact of natural disasters on the residents of Black Sea Basin region and improve their resilience to climate change. Through the implementation of this project, we anticipate that small communities in the Black Sea Basin will have access to user-friendly tools that will help mitigate the impact of climate change on the most vulnerable populations. The expected outcome is the development of enhanced disaster risk prevention, climate change adaptation, and emergency response capacities in the targeted small communities.

The project will deliver several important outputs and results, with a significant emphasis on Institutional Capacity Building of small communities. One of the key outputs will be the development of a common methodology to improve preparedness for emergency situations in rural areas. This methodology will include a common emergency response plan and a user-friendly manual for adapting the plan to specific communities. Additionally, study visits and best practice exchange seminars will be organised to facilitate knowledge sharing and foster collaboration among stakeholders.

Another innovative solution developed within the project is the creation of an e-learning web platform that offers online courses in emergency situation preparedness and management. This platform will benefit communities across the four partner countries and serve as a centralised hub for accessing project materials, training resources, and informative documents. It will be designed to be user-friendly and accessible to the target communities and beyond. Furthermore, both offline and online trainings will be conducted for the local population, focusing on disaster preparedness and first aid. These trainings aim to empower community members to effectively respond to emergencies, thus increasing overall resilience and reducing vulnerabilities.

Simulation exercises will be carried out to test the developed methodology, ensuring its effectiveness. Additionally, reforestation campaigns will be implemented in areas prone to landslides, promoting awareness and mitigating the effects of natural disasters. The project will also organise conferences, seminars, and round tables to facilitate the exchange of best practices, enhance cross-border cooperation, and promote innovative methods for disaster management.

The outputs generated by the project will have lasting effects on the territories and target groups. The methodology, curricula, and training materials created during the project will continue to be used and maintained after its closure, ensuring the sustainability of the project's impact. This will enable other communities and target groups to benefit from the project's outcomes.

The beneficiaries of the project include local populations, local public authorities, NGOs, and other initiative groups in the Black Sea Basin region. The project will improve their awareness, preparedness, and capacity to handle emergency situations, reducing the risks to their health, lives, and infrastructure. Furthermore, the project will contribute to the sustainability of its outcomes by establishing enduring partnerships, signing cooperation agreements, and fostering cross-border cooperation even after the project closure.

Transnational cooperation plays a crucial role in the success of the project. Recognising that acting solely on a national level may not be sufficient to address the scale and complexity of the challenges faced by the region, the project emphasises the importance of transnational cooperation. This approach allows for the sharing of best practices, leveraging knowledge and resources, and improving the efficiency of efforts. It also promotes regional integration, cooperation, and understanding, while building trust and strengthening relationships between neighbouring countries. The project's transnational approach will have a multiplying effect, reaching a wider audience and addressing more complex challenges. By pooling resources and expertise, the project aims to maximise its impact and create a sustainable framework for climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction efforts in the region.

titleEn: Less vulnerability, more adaptability – pilot remote sensing assisted restoration of green spaces in coastal and urban areas within the Black sea region
summaryEn: Climate change is affecting the Black Sea area, despite not being sufficiently addressed at the regional scale. The region is particularly vulnerable to: erosion, landslides, sea level rise, flooding, storms, heatwaves, new types of plant diseases and droughts. Adaptation to the consequences of climate change is a key challenge in the BSB territory. New technologies in the environmental sector, such as artificial intelligence, data science, and small sensors, can be used to collect real-time geospatial data and make it more accessible, preventing disasters and increasing climate change readiness and adaptability. Transnational and cross-border cooperation is at the heart of the vision and methodological approach of the project. It derives from its overall objective - to enhance transboundary cooperation for increasing the regional readiness and adaptability to climate change related hazards through application of nature-based solution assisted by highly innovative remote sensing methods. The MoreAdaptBSB is making involved stakeholders from local and regional level, to exchange experiences, use common knowledge tool and get familiar with state of the art on adaptation planning. By taking this approach, the dialogue and co-design of measures for restoring urban and coastal green spaces will be increased. The reason why these targets cannot be efficiently achieved acting only on a national, regional, or local level, is that climate change is intrinsically not addressable by a single region and nation. The main outputs are: i) tool for visualizing climate change vulnerability and resilience (incl. the areas of Greece, Bulgaria, Romania and Ukraine within the programme territory); ii) a nature-based adaptation plan and a catalogue of restoration measures; iii) 60 dka restored green spaces in a New European Bauhaus manner in coastal and urban areas within Kassandra (GR), Constantsa (RO), Primorsko (BG) and Odessa (UA); iv) 3 conducted knowledge exchange groups and 1 Living Lab in the form of multi-actor approach. The main results are: i) well-established transboundary cooperation for increasing the regional readiness and adaptability to climate change related hazards; ii) improved capacity of the relevant authorities. Regional and/or local authorities will directly benefit from MoreAdaptBSB's results through knowledge exchange and further application in their daily work; from a science perspective, higher education and research institutions can gain familiarity with highly innovative remote sensing methods; being a part of restoration activities will benefit NGOs and citizens associations.

titleEn: Innovative joint learning for environmental-friendly behaviour of communities in the Black Sea Basin
summaryEn:
Five organisations in four countries in the Black Sea Basin (Romania, Bulgaria, Georgia and Türkiye) considered the identified needs and challenges in the region and their long-term common objectives regarding environment protection and decided that specific, innovative and efficient solutions and actions are needed to tackle the pressing problem of pollution. The common main idea is that the serious gap between the level of pollution and the mentality and behaviour of the citizens needs to be addressed more consistently and using tools allowing a better understanding of the issues in order to bring the willingness to act and support environmental-friendly behaviour in all segments of the general public.
