titleEn: Danube Integrated System for MARking
summaryEn:
As an environmentally-friendly and safe transport mode, inland waterway transport (IWT) is an important enabler for economic growth and competitiveness in the Danube Region.
The Danube is an international waterway. For coordinated basic infrastructure quality, the transnational cooperation of national waterway authorities is crucial.
The common Romanian – Bulgarian sector of the Danube is an important section of the Danube and also, an important sector of the TEN-T Rhine-Danube Core Network Corridor.
Transnational harmonised waterway infrastructure for an entire TEN-T transport corridor is an important prerequisite for public authorities in order to be capable of satisfying user needs of the commercial IWT sector. For instance, data about fairway conditions from both Danube countries, Romania and Republic of Bulgaria will help vessel operators to optimise their voyage and transport planning, which is in most cases international.
The objective of the project is to enhance and maintain a sustainable and climate resilient transportation network by further developing effective waterway infrastructure.
In addition to consolidating common standards and tools, the project’s results and outputs include user oriented information services. These enable rapid information transfer on the quality of the waterway’s infrastructure. 
The project will consolidate the quality of waterway infrastructure and waterway maintenance, resulting in a higher utilization of waterway transport in the region.

Through collaboration, innovative technologies, and careful planning, the project aims to create a safer and more reliable waterway for all users (trade, transportation, and tourism companies), ensuring the preservation of this invaluable European resource.
Planned Approach:


1.	Systematic Assessment: The project will start with a comprehensive assessment of the current marking system and its limitations. This assessment will have the scope to identify the optimal solution for different component of the integrated marking system.


2.	Technology Upgrade: Based on the assessment, the project will introduce advanced technologies for the marking system, including solar-powered lights and GPS-based positioning. These upgrades will enhance accuracy and reliability while reducing energy consumption and carbon emissions;


3.	Implementation of the pilot actions: Based on the results of the installation methods analysis, using the new technologies, taking into account the local hydrological conditions, will be installed the marking necessary infrastructure in order to develop the new integrated system. After the new integrated communication system installation, will be done the testing activities, in order to verify the interconnection capacity and monitoring the system parameter’s. 


4.	Monitoring and Evaluation of the pilot actions: The project will include a robust monitoring and evaluation process to measure the effectiveness of the upgraded and integrated marking system. Continuous feedback will be used to make any necessary adjustments and improvements.
The proposed project for improving the marking system on the Danube River introduces several new and original elements that set it apart from traditional approaches. The project's novelty lies in its adoption of sustainable technologies, GPS-based positioning, regional collaboration for the marking activity, and commitment to environmental preservation. These elements make the project unique and promising, addressing navigational challenges on the Danube River in an innovative and inclusive manner.
Moreover, DISMAR project, efficiently capitalises on previous project results (i.e. SEE project NEWADA duo, TEN-T Project IRIS Europe 3, CEF Project FAIRway Danube and Romanian Operational Programme – POIM project) to build on existing knowledge and to deploy results for consolidate the quality of waterway infrastructure.

titleEn: Strengthening the local intervention capacities for climate change in the Black Sea Region
summaryEn:
The LAP-BLACK project aims to enhance the intervention capacities of local authorities in the Black Sea Region to mitigate the effects of climate change. The project's overall objective is to create a sustainable and climate-resilient region while highlighting the importance of local intervention and collaboration. The specific objectives include building adaptation teams, developing Local Adaptation Plans, establishing pilot applications, monitoring and updating Local Adaptation Plans and engaging stakeholders to raise awareness and disseminate project results. The communication objectives are to raise awareness, engage stakeholders, disseminate results and promote best practices.

The project highlights the climate projections for the Black Sea region, emphasizing the need for action due to increasingly Mediterranean-like characteristics, such as warmer and drier conditions, heatwaves, longer, hotter summers and changes in rainfall patterns. These changes have extensive implications for agriculture, human health, ecosystems and various aspects of life. The economic consequences include changes in agriculture productivity, damage to infrastructure, increased costs of disaster response and strain on regional economies.

To address these challenges, the LAP-BLACK project proposes a transnational cooperation approach, focusing on the development of Local Adaptation Plans and the integration of adaptation and mitigation measures. The project aims to establish adaptation teams, develop Local Action Plans, implement pilot projects and engage stakeholders. The project outputs will benefit local and national authorities, sectoral agencies, infrastructure providers, interest groups, higher education and research organizations, SMEs and business support organizations, contributing to improved adaptation capacity, sustainability and quality of life in the region.

The project emphasis the EU Adaptation Strategy and the approach of the Covenant of Mayors (CoM) to support cities in developing urban adaptation strategies. The project brings together academia and municipalities to address climate change challenges in the Black Sea region. Istanbul Technical University (ITU) serves as the lead partner, providing scientific expertise, coordination and guidance. Other partners are local authorities representing the affected communities and UABSC executing activities on behalf of Mykolaiv Municipality, offering local knowledge, governance experience and implementation capabilities. The partners' diverse expertise covers areas such as international projects, technical research, governance, urban planning, infrastructure resilience, sustainable development and community engagement, enabling a comprehensive approach to tackling climate change in the region. Through collaboration, the partners develop Local AdaptationPlans, implement pilot projects and monitor progress.

The LAP-BLACK project’s outputs and results include the establishment of Local Adaptation Teams, conducting research and field studies to investigate climate change impacts on sectors such as agriculture, tourism and water resources, producing a Risk Assessment Analyses Report, developing locally tailored action plans, establishing sustainable parks, establishing a monitoring and evaluation framework, conducting capacity building and knowledge dissemination activities and enhancing collaboration and stakeholder engagement.

The LAP-BLACK project emphasizes financial, institutional, political and lasting effects sustainability. Financial sustainability is ensured through resource allocation and leveraging funds from various sources. Institutional sustainability is achieved by establishing ownership and dedicated staff for maintenance. Political sustainability is pursued through influencing policies and legislation. Lasting effects are fostered through the utilization of project outputs, dissemination, capacity building and knowledge exchange. The project also emphasizes transferability by providing documentation, guidelines, training, dissemination and international cooperation to benefit other regions facing similar climate change challenges. Stakeholder engagement, communication, outreach, policy advocacy and knowledge exchange are key strategies to ensure effective utilization and transferability of the project outputs.

titleEn: Empowering Blue and Smart Transformation of the Black Sea Basin - Blue Gates
summaryEn:
According to, the EU Blue Economy report 2022 and EU Blue Economy Observatory, Blue Economy is an important sector in European Union, as being a source of employment for almost 

4.5 million and generating € 

667.2 billion in turnover and € 183,9 billion in gross added value. Blue economy is mainly composed of sectors as marine living resources(fisheries and aquaculture),marine non-living resources, marine renewable energy, port activities, shipbuilding and repair, maritime transport, and coastal tourism. These sectors have immense potential for an economic growth, employment and sustainable development for regions of Black Sea Basin and Europe in case they are enabled as globally competitive and innovative. Use of of advanced technologies, increasing digital skills and sustainability of blue growth sectors are internationally acknowledged means to achieve much needed dual transformation paving the way for a blue and smart Black Sea Basin.
To tap and trigger potential of blue economy in BSB a more sustainable and innovative ecosystem of blue economy actors is needed. At the moment, Black Sea Basin as a whole is lagging in dual transformation. The European Innovation Scoreboard (EIS) which, provides a comparative analysis of innovation performance in EU countries, other European countries, and regional neighbors categorize countries under 4 categories as 1-Innovation Leaders, 2-Strong Innovators, 3- Moderate Innovators, and 4- Emerging Innovators. According to this Innovation Scoreboard project partner countries Romania, Bulgaria and Turkey are all in 4th level. Ukraine (not included in scoreboard) estimated as similar to 4th level. EIS 2022 report further indicates that "Almost all EU Member States have increased their innovation performance since 2015 but the lowest performing countries are falling further behind." Thus, it is clear that low innovative status of Black Sea Basin is a common challenge hindering the potential of blue economy and others in the basin. The NEXT Black Sea Basin programme document also states that “Black Sea Basin have low levels of innovation infrastructure and investment and R&D investments of basin are below the European average.(EU 28) of 2%.” Based on this background, to contribute into efforts to overcome Black Sea Basin being a region of low innovation , the project shall, focus on creating a transnational cluster on blue economy investing in uptake of innovative and advanced technologies, developing joint digital tools and R&D capacities for common solutions increasing sustainability and efficiency of blue growth sectors in medium and long term. 

Project is built upon an innovation favoring transnational Blue Economy Cluster to be called BlueIN4BS due to the fact that adapting to cutting-edge techs, global standards, investing in research and development and creating joint tools for benefit of all Black Sea Basin countries and for all layers of science, policy, industry realms requires massive efforts that no single local actor can achieve alone. Therefore, project approach employs quadruple helix model of innovation uniting efforts of blue economy involved regional and local bodies, universities and research centers and channel them to produce joint tools, platforms, knowledge, capacities and joint solutions for blue economy ecosytem. Thus, this transnational basin level cluster based cooperation under BlueIN4BS is expected to contribute to innovative and smart transformation of Black Sea Basin by leveraging existing research and innovation capacities mainly, to uptake cutting edge advanced techs in blue-growth niches for innovation and smart specialization and to develop joint tools for common benefits of BSB Blue economy actors harnessing the talent and potential of the BS region. 
Blue Gates project activities are organized in following groups to produce certain outputs and results as;
I-Formation of a transnational Black Sea Blue Economy Cluster(BlueIN4BS) focusing on two areas 
1-intra-regional and international cooperation to ensure science, industry and policy interconnectivity bringing innovative and advanced technologies, best practices, global standards in blue economy sectors into BSB actors' agenda 
2- establish a digital platform/hub to virtually transfer research and technology .
II- Joint Capacity Building Programs for uptake of advanced technologies, knowledge, models, methods and standards
- Organization of Demo Days for advanced techs such as AI apps, aquatic drone and sensor use in blue growth sectors
-BSB Blue Economy Summer Schools on topics such as marine pollution monitoring, ecologic quality surveys, R&D based innovative products complying with circular economy approach and valorizing on previous Project outcomes like blue accelerators
III- Developing Joint solutions by applying advanced techs into existing 
-Developing a Rapid Detection Kit and
- Color Detection test for sustainable marine resources and potential contamination risks.

titleEn: Black Sea Smart Marine Environmental Outcome System
summaryEn:
The Black Sea has an important blue growth potential providing unique opportunities for a variety of blue economy sectors. Increasing ecosystem resilience, assessing, and mitigating the impacts of the increasingly complex array of multi-stressors, revealing their poorly understood interactions from the land-sea interface, including the connection with rivers and supporting the development of blue sectors, have become important challenges for the Black Sea. Advancing a shared vision for a productive, healthy, resilient, sustainable and highly valued Black Sea by 2030 has become an urgent priority in preventing the negative synergistic impact of natural and human induced pressures and supporting a clean and green region. For this reason, continuous observation is necessary to understand the ecosystem dynamics in coastal areas and to follow the changes.

BS-SEOS is aiming to obtain a standardized communication means for databases collecting environmental and associated data from online mobile stations (smart buoys and autonomous surface vehicles) and from other national/European databases so as to enable partnering institutions and third-party organizations running their own environmental models including data from all regions and sharing their results. The main objective of this project is to establish a standardized communication system for collecting and sharing environmental data from mobile stations and existing databases in the Black Sea region. This will facilitate cross-border cooperation, bridge data gaps, and enable partnering institutions to run environmental models and share their results effectively. By leveraging AI forecasting techniques, the project intends to bring about a transformative change in the current situation. The integration of AI forecasting into the project allows to harness the power of data analysis, machine learning, and predictive modeling to generate accurate and reliable forecasts. This will enable us to make informed decisions, anticipate future trends, and effectively address the challenges in Black Sea. Within this scope, it will be possible to test both in situ and innovative methods, choose indicator parameters with high representative values for observing the marine environment, and implement methods that will provide continuous data flow. The most important five key parameters are chosen for continuous monitoring such as temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, Chlorophyll-a and pH for comprehensive assessment while monitoring marine ecosystem health. Key parameters will be observed by passive samplers and sensor technologies, which can complement satellite observations and provide continuous and real-time data flow by adapting to floating buoys, as well as by in situ research to validate and calibrate data collected through novel technologies. 

BS-SEOS has the potential to benefit scientists, environmental managers, policymakers, conservation organizations, fisheries and aquaculture industries, coastal communities, recreational users, and education and outreach initiatives. The project's outputs contribute to scientific knowledge, inform decision-making processes, guide conservation efforts, promote sustainable practices, and raise public awareness about the importance of marine ecosystem health. BS-SEOS will develop a dedicated platform for sharing data and results. This platform will serve as a centralized hub where participating organizations can upload, access, and analyze regional data, fostering collaboration and maximizing the collective benefits of regional efforts. The planned approach involves close collaboration among partnering institutions, environmental agencies, and relevant stakeholders across the Black Sea region. This cooperative effort will ensure the harmonization of data collection methods, data sharing protocols, and analysis techniques. By pooling resources, expertise, and data, the project will leverage the collective knowledge and capabilities of the participating organizations to address the common environmental challenges faced by the Black Sea region effectively. The establishment of a standardized communication system and the implementation of innovative data collection methods will require cross-border coordination and information sharing. By fostering transnational cooperation, the project will maximize the utilization of available resources and expertise, leading to a more comprehensive and robust understanding of the environmental dynamics in the Black Sea region.

titleEn: Harmonisation of joint monitoring and modelling of groundwater system of Pannonian Plain
summaryEn:
Shallow groundwater is directly recharged by precipitation and other water balance components. 
Global pattern of water table depth provides vital support for terrestrial ecosystem by sustaining river base flow and soil water balance in the root zone. According to scientists (Fan et al, Science 339, 2013) shallow groundwater influences 22 to 32% of global land area, including app. 15% as groundwater-fed surface water features and 7 to 17% with the water table or its capillary fringe within plant rooting depths.
All countries of observed region have more or less dense network of observation wells but there is no connection between fragmented monitoring systems. Lowland regions of Danube countries: Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Slovenia, Romania, Slovakia and Bosnia and Herzegovina belongs to the Pannonian Plain - large alluvial region surrounded by Alps, Carpathian Mountains and Dinaric Alps. It is characterized by large portion of agricultural area with dense drainage network and rich ecosystem in grassland, wetland and forests. Its area is app. 200.000 km

2.
The only possible way of groundwater analysis is through transnational approach.Due to the fact that many countries share this large valley there are administrative limitations which obstruct access to whole spatial aspects of natural characteristics and present processes. Patterns in water table depth explain patterns in wetlands at the global scale and vegetation gradients at regional and local scales.
This project will present global observations of water table depth compiled from national data basis and connect them to be representative and harmonised transboundary basis for further activities. The basic hypothesis is existence of groundwater lowering mainly caused by climate change impacts. This problem was detected in some other European regions and partially in countries in the Danube River basin ( Romania, for example) and published in scientific publications. The main outputs of the project are: Report on the state of play in the field of monitoring shallow groundwater system, including description of the existing gaps in observation wells network which will be addressed by the new initiative of joint approach to the problem and description of the target groups addressed by the future project and their needs (i); Main project work plan, containing work plan, describing activities, outputs and expected results of the main project, including potential partners and indicative budget of the main project (ii) and Report on funding possibilities, presenting the analysis of funding sources for the main project and defining steps to be taken after the seed money project is finalized (iii). Projected warming in the 21st century anticipates more or less significant changes in precipitation pattern, including less snow during winter periods and shifting in the timing of runoff. This will effect spatial variable changes in the timing and quantity of groundwater recharge. In order to develop mitigation platform transnational approach is essential for understanding trends in groundwater systems and undertaking initial steps for future activities.

titleEn: Pathways to empowering energy communities and mitigating energy poverty in Central-Eastern Europe - a case study based approach
summaryEn:
In a time when Europe aims at a less centralised structure of its energy system for technical, social, environmental and economic reasons need and opportunity for a more democratic governance of energy generation, distribution and consumption arrise - and, at the same time the question emerges: “how to provide citizens with the keys to this complex framework that has historically been managed and operated by large political and technical stakeholders?”

To answer, a social approach has been formalised in EU law especially with the Clean Energy for All Europeans package, the policy framework aiming to make the EU comply with the Paris Agreement. Existing initiatives promoted at the EU and national levels have investigated technical solutions for the participation of prosumers in the grid flexibility, others have dug into the creation processes of energy communities and governance approaches. 

The energy.eu project to be developed in the present call falls within and beyond this historical background. Energy.eu aims to eridicate energy poverty and enable the European energy “paradigm shift”, by developing solutions that improve and integrate the results of existing approaches into a clear methodology and a single framework to support various forms of effective citizen participation in the energy market, and the development and application of new ideas and services linked to the green transformation in the Danube Region. 

The main activity of energy.eu is developing a full fledget project plan in line with the “energy community paradigm shift” through a multidisciplinary approach based on an iterative social innovation methodology. The methodology will link citizens, market, regulations and technologies, by the development and tailoring of social and flexibility tools, the co-design of governance and business models for energy communities presenting economic, social and environmental sustainability, and the facilitation of energy communities’ establishment within the current administrative framework and with recommendations for an evolution of regulation. The overarching goal for all activities is to contribute to a better energy governance in the Danube Region by offering an evidence-based set of methodologies to place the consumer at the centre of the European energy market.

With 4 partners (a reseach non-profit, a geothermal consulting and engineering company, a regional authority and an environmental NGO) from 4 countries representing EU and non-EU states, as its core team, energy.eu aims to develop a pathway towards empowering the European consumer to act as a prosumer inside the energy market. To do so, energy.eu will 
- report on the state of play in energy communities, prosumer networks as well as crowdfunding based on socio-economic analyses and case studies (output 1)
- develop a project plan that sets out to engage, then involve and finally to evolve and improve its solutions based on participative planning and feedback gathered at community and stakeholder consultations, as well as dedicated programmes to engage young people (outputs 2-3-4), and,
- report on funding possibilities (output 5)

The expert team of energy.eu will develop the core methodology whose in-depth description and application will be the central activity of the main project - this will include tools, both social and technical to allow the empowerment of citizens and foster the development of energy communities and utilize alternative financing tools. To ensure the replicability and the sustainability of the results of the main project a diverse and capable partnership will be sought, demonstration sites studied, and funding opportunities considered. Energy.eu will ensure that various regulatory and societal contexts will be addressed in the project development and that the solutions to be offered secure strong replicability and maximise exploitation potential. 

Energy.eu is expected to result in a complete main project that respects HORIZON EUROPE guidelines.

titleEn: Advanced Thermal Storage Solutions for Sustainable Energy Management in the Danube Region
summaryEn:
Main project goal is to enhance thermal energy storage capacities, focusing on long-term storage to replace fossil fuels in building heating with renewable energy. Long-term storage solutions can bridge the gap between the availability of renewable energy sources (RES) and the need for thermal energy, which rarely coincide. The aim is to go beyond the existing practice of water tank storage by utilizing emerging technologies.

The Danube Region faces several significant challenges that impact its energy landscape, particularly in relation to seasonal variability, dependency on fossil fuels, intermittent renewable energy supply, and underutilized infrastructure. These issues are critical in understanding the broader context of energy management and sustainability within the region.
Seasonal variability significantly affects energy demand within the Danube Region, with a pronounced need for heating during winter and a surplus of renewable energy, especially solar, in summer. This fluctuation challenges the energy system's ability to balance supply and demand efficiently throughout the year. The inherent variability of renewable energy sources, notably solar and wind, exacerbates this issue by introducing intermittency into the energy supply. Such intermittency requires innovative solutions for energy storage and demand management to ensure a reliable energy supply.
Key Components:
Phase Change Materials (PCMs): These advanced materials store and release thermal energy during melting and solidifying processes. They can be integrated into building materials or standalone storage systems, offering high energy storage density and stable temperatures over a broad range.
Thermochemical Storage: This method utilizes reversible chemical reactions for long-term heat storage, allowing for energy preservation over extended periods with minimal losses.
One promising approach involves high-temperature sand thermal energy storage (HT-STES). This technology utilizes commercially available sand as a thermal storage medium. 
Another intriguing technology involves molten metal thermal storage (MMTES). This approach utilizes metals like aluminum or silicon, which melt at relatively low temperatures compared to traditional molten salt options. When molten, these metals possess a high heat capacity, enabling them to store large amounts of thermal energy.
Underground Thermal Energy Storage (UTES): UTES systems use the earth's natural insulation to store heat, including both shallow geothermal systems and deep borehole storage. They are especially suitable for seasonal storage of excess renewable energy.
Heat Pumps and Solar Thermal Collectors: These are used to efficiently transfer heat between the storage system and its end use. Solar thermal collectors capture solar energy as heat.
Sand Battery: A novel approach that uses sand or sand-like materials for high-temperature thermal energy storage. It functions as a high-power and high-capacity reservoir for excess wind and solar energy, which can be used for heating or industrial processes.

Innovative Applications:
Municipality Heating Systems: Implementing advanced heat storage solutions in unutilized spaces such as cellars and yards on municipality properties. This approach is designed to optimize local resources and improve the efficiency of municipal heating systems.
Industrial Heat Recovery: Capturing and storing waste heat from industrial processes for later use, enhancing energy efficiency and reducing carbon emissions.

Collaboration and Knowledge Transfer:
StoreMoreWarm engages with industry experts, researchers, and policymakers to co-develop and refine these technologies. Workshops, webinars, and conferences will disseminate knowledge and encourage the adoption of heat storage solutions. Tailoring solutions to specific regional needs and resources is a priority, made possible through collaboration with local communities and stakeholders.

Impact and Benefits of StoreMoreWarm:
-	Enhanced Renewable Energy Utilization: By effectively storing excess wind and solar energy, StoreMoreWarm significantly improves the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy sources, reducing dependency on fossil fuels and lowering carbon emissions.
-	Innovative Use of Space and Resources: The project's unique approach to utilizing unutilized spaces like cellars and yards for municipality heating systems exemplifies innovative resource management, maximizing local infrastructural potential.
-	Boost to Energy Independence: The integration of technologies such as PCMs, UTES, and the Sand Battery enhances regional energy independence, providing a buffer against energy market fluctuations and supply disruptions.
-	Catalyst for Local and Global Sustainable Development: StoreMoreWarm sets a precedent for sustainable energy management, potentially influencing policies and practices both locally in the Danube Region and globally, contributing to broader environmental and sustainability goals.

titleEn: Regional cooperation for a greener Danube fleet - preparation of the DEMETER project
Strengthening INnovation Excellence in the Secondary Raw Material Economy in the Danube Region
summaryEn:
The EU depends on the import of raw materials from outside Europe, especially on critical raw materials (CRM) such as cobalt, nickel or lithium. These raw materials are essential for digital and green technologies. There are currently 37 materials charaterised as critical (EU Critical Material Act)
- as they are essential for Europe's industy
- come with a high risk of supply disruption from outside Europe, due to geopolitical risks and often depending on monopoly sources
- the extraction and mining activity of these materials are associated with ethical (child labour) and environmental issues (high resource consumption, contamination of nature etc)
That is why the sourcing, processing and recycling of these raw materials in Europe is of utmost importance (EU Green Deal Industrial Plan, Net-zero Industry Act, EU industrial policy on batteries).

The Danube region needs to play a key role in this secondary raw material economy:


1. competitive strength
It is a great opportunity for the DR as it has a strong tradition in metal production and mining in the economy, the research and education sector is also quite developed 


2. strategic importance
The Danube regions as key region within the EU to reduce the dependency on markets outside the European continent. These materials are in the beginning of supply chains and their demand is increasing. Many of these supply chains start in the less developed part of the DR, thus for the companies there it is essential to have access to materials and develp the respective recycling technologies to secure a supply with sustainably produced materials. 


3. Research and innovation for securing a green, digital and resilient Danube region
Many regions and countries of the Danube region have recognised the importance of the secondary material economy in their RIS and S4 strategies, but their research and innovation ecosystems are lagging behind.

Research and Innovation eco systems are still evolving in the Danube region, especially in this very new and dynamic sector. The actors have difficulties to establish Research and Technology transfer and an efficient research and innovation management and valorisation policy. Cooperation among the research institutions, business, policy and society is low. There is a considerable administrative fragmentation as well as a lack of human resources and funding in research and innovation systems.

The IN4SerMat consortium, consisting of four partners and 5 strategic associated partners, has identified the HORIZON WIDERA programme as well as the I3 instrument as appropriate to tackle the above challenges. We will prepare a proposal on Strengthening innovation excellence in the Secondary Raw Material Economy in the Danube region.

The main proposal is highly relevant to the EUSDR action plan. It relates to Priority Area 7 - Knowledge Society and PA 8 - Competitiveness of Enterprises, as the project will promote and strenghten cooperation of actors in the Research & Innovation ecosystem.

The partnerhsip covers the key connection between research and business in the Widening countries innovation ecosystems and will be extended to policy makers and civil society actors (quadruple helix approach).

The IN4SeRMat project has three outcomes/specific objectives:

SO1: Report on the state of play in the Secondary Raw Material Economy in the Danube Region
Providing a comprehensive analysis of the value chain including a gap analysis and an overview of key stakeholders, providing further an overview on past and current initiatives and projects relating and contributing to the secondary raw material with focus on identifying key stakeholders, the potential and framework to capitalise on the results and outputs of these initatives and projects, as well as other synergies and benefits that could arise from collaboration.

SO2: Work Plan to Set up an Ecosystem for the Secondary Raw Material Economy
Draft all key parts of the application for setting up an excellence hub including the general and specific objectives, relateds KPIs and target values, the definition of the support methodology, dissemination and exploitation strategy/WP, outcomes and impact description, work plan with all WPs defined including task leaders, risk and mitigation measures, gender equality and the DNSH compliance, the budget, and the partnership compositions.

SO3: Report on Funding Possibilities
Starting with a report on potential calls in 2025 & 2026 work programmes of HORIZON WIDERA and I3, following the decision for a specific call, a radmap to proposal submission will be prepared covering the actions to the proposal submission date including activities, partner responsibilities and deadlines. Finally, we will capitalise on the knowhow generated regarding suitalbe calls around the Secondary raw Material Economy.

titleEn: Harmonisation of Missions in the Danube region
summaryEn:
The main objective is to harmonise the implementation of the European Missions on the Danube region level. We observe significant disparities in the level of understanding, setup, and implementation of the European Missions among European regions. Therefore, within the proposed project, we aim to minimalize these disparities and help set up an effective Missions governing model on the Danube region level.

In the HARMONMISSIONS project, we want to aim at two concrete areas of the EU Missions: 


1. Adaptation to Climate Change
4.100 Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities by 2030

In addition to concrete solutions to the problems in these areas, the EU Missions also aim to establish new forms of governance, cooperation and citizen involvement. The primary objective of the HARMONMISSIONS project is to facilitate these forms of cooperation as set out in the EU Missions. The interest of the project is to create channels for cooperation between partners in the areas of Missions 1 and 

4. The need for cooperation lies in the fact that climate change cannot be tied to a specific country. On the contrary, it transcends national borders and therefore there is a need to cooperate to tackle climate change. The aim of the project is therefore to create a platform that facilitates cooperation between partners and raises awareness of the missions among the professional and lay public.

The concrete specification of the project on two selected climate mission areas also aims to create a platform within a narrowly specified framework, whose best practices and established organisational structure could be used in the region for cooperation in other EU Mission areas. In this way, the sustainability of the results and outputs of the project will be ensured for other EU Mission projects. The aim is to promote active stakeholder participation in the EU Mission projects, facilitate project involvement and increase project success. The project also seeks to create networks of contacts that will enable partnerships to be established in specific EU projects related to the EU Missions. 

EU Missions’ ambitious goals are related/connected to wider EU policies, strategies, and initiatives. By focusing on the creation of an organisational structure in Mission 1, the project subscribes to the EU Adaptation Strategy and the European Green Deal. These strategies aim to contribute to climate change adaptation through international cooperation. International cooperation will be the main ambition of the project.

Mission 4 emphasizes the involvement of local, regional, and national governments, citizens, as well as investors and entrepreneurs to achieve the goals set out in this mission. Their cooperation is essential for the sustainability of the mission's results. As cooperation is also essential for success in this mission, the HARMONMISSIONS project aims to create an organisational structure composed of all these actors. Within it, knowledge sharing and collaboration will be able to take place, to create synergies between existing initiatives and to target the current needs of cities and other partners.

Based on the focus on creating an organizational structure for the platform in the areas of climate missions, we have defined the following target groups: government, researchers and innovators, education institutions, small and large businesses, investors, and civil society. We see the involvement of the expert community in the platform as an essential means to increase country and partner engagement in mission-related challenges. Successful projects will be able to directly address current needs. We see the involvement of the general public as beneficial in terms of raising awareness in the field and consequently exerting bottom-up pressure. It will also increase the formation of civil society.

Moreover, their timeline extends to 2030 when concrete results are expected. In the meantime, the EU policies will continue developing and Missions will (may need to) be adapted and enriched by new strategies and objectives. An EU policy observatory (EMO platform) will be developed that will gather information on relevant EU policies, produce a user-friendly description and make them available to National Contact Points (NCPs) and the public on the project’s website. 

Furthermore, other EU programmes and strategies, such as the Cohesion Funds and the Recovery and Resilience funds, EUSDR contribute to similar goals and policies. Collaboration with national and regional networks supporting such EU programmes will be built to organise joint events/raise awareness of the common challenges.

Within the project we aim to set up an EU policies observatory tool (EMO platform) that will be designed to collect information about the most relevant EU policies impacting the EU Missions how they evolve/change during the lifetime of the project, and what impact these changes have on the Missions. This tool will help DR countries to set up proper national measures.

titleEn: Artificial Intelligence, Smart Management and Gamification for Technologically-advanced and Energy-efficient heritage buildings
summaryEn:
The EE-Heritage main project revolves around three priorities:
- improving energy efficiency in heritage buildings: saving energy, cost and reducing the carbon footprint of the building stock in the Danube Region
- contribution to the preservation of cultural heritate buildiongs by offering non-intrusive renovation options to achieve the goal above.
- improving building occupant and user comfort and health by monitoring the parameters of heritage buildings and providing automated inverventions for improving these parameters which are pivotal for health and personal comfort.

The EE-Heritage project emerges as an ambitious initiative within the Danube Region, aiming to reconcile the preservation of cultural heritage with contemporary demands for energy efficiency and sustainability. This innovative project stands at the crossroads of tradition and technology, seeking to implement energy-efficient solutions in heritage buildings without compromising their historical integrity. Spanning several countries within the Danube Region, EE-Heritage leverages a collaborative approach, drawing upon the expertise and resources of a diverse consortium of partners. These include a development agency of a local municipality, an energy service company (ESCO), a research institutions of a University, and a non-governmental organizations dedicated to the preservation of cultural heritage and environmental sustainability in buildings.

At the heart of EE-Heritage is the ambition to address the significant challenge of reducing energy consumption in heritage buildings. These structures, often bound by strict conservation regulations and characterized by outdated construction techniques, represent a unique challenge in the quest for energy efficiency. The project aims to navigate these challenges through the integration of advanced AI-driven building management systems and non-intrusive sensory technologies. These tools promise to optimize energy use dynamically, accounting for the specific needs and constraints of heritage buildings, thereby reducing their carbon footprint and operational costs.

Furthermore, EE-Heritage places a strong emphasis on user engagement and public participation. Recognising that the success of energy efficiency measures greatly depends on the behavior of building occupants, the project incorporates gamification strategies designed to encourage energy-conscious behaviors. By making energy saving both engaging and rewarding, EE-Heritage seeks to foster a culture of sustainability among residents, visitors, and operators of heritage buildings.

The project's geographical focus on the Danube Region is particularly significant, given the area's rich cultural history and diverse architectural heritage. By targeting this macro-region, EE-Heritage not only addresses the specific challenges faced by heritage buildings in these countries but also leverages the opportunity to create a model for sustainable heritage preservation that can be replicated across Europe and beyond.

The consortium's approach to project development is methodical and inclusive, beginning with a comprehensive data collection effort to map the existing stock of heritage buildings and assess their energy performance. This foundational work informs a regulatory analysis aimed at understanding the legal landscape surrounding heritage building renovations in different countries, identifying both opportunities and constraints. Concurrently, the project explores the latest advancements in sensory technology and AI, seeking innovative solutions that are both effective and respectful of the buildings' historical value.

As the project progresses, the drafting of the main project work plan represents a critical phase, synthesizing insights from research, stakeholder engagement, and technical analysis into a coherent and actionable plan. This plan outlines the specific activities, expected outcomes, budget allocations, and timelines, ensuring that all project components are aligned and geared towards achieving the overarching goal of sustainable heritage preservation.

EE-Heritage embodies a forward-thinking approach to cultural heritage preservation, one that harmonizes respect for the past with a commitment to a sustainable future. Through its emphasis on technological innovation, community engagement, and cross-border collaboration, the project not only aims to enhance the energy efficiency of heritage buildings but also to inspire a broader shift towards sustainability in the management of cultural assets. As such, EE-Heritage stands as a beacon of hope and innovation, offering a path forward that preserves the legacy of the past while embracing the possibilities of the future.

titleEn: Greening Communal Heating Systems by Integrating Renewables
summaryEn:
The project aims to propose a complex strategic transnational project (main project) for development of a combined system that will integrate renewable energy sources into existing heat supply infrastructure and manage their effective operation. The main project will contribute directly to the EU Strategy for the Danube Region (EUSDR), particularly Priority Area 2, Action 

2. District heating networks offer great potential for efficient use of low-carbon energy for heating. However, the decarbonisation potential of district heating is largely unused, as a big deal of the heat supplied in district networks mainly in Danube region countries is produced from fossil fuels.
The SMF project will lead to significant increase in efficiency, reduce natural gas consumption, and lower CO2 emissions which is in line with the need to decarbonize energy and heating systems in Europe. It will pave the way for a more sustainable future for the entire Danube region, reducing the dependency on Russian gas. 
It will enable our consortium of three partners from Ukraine and Slovakia to start preparation of the main project and gradually widen the consortium by additional partners mainly from the Danube region. It will also allow us to thoroughly analyze possibilities of funding for the main project and to choose the most suitable one.

titleEn: Biotechnological Innovations for Sustainable Flat Panel Displays Recycling
summaryEn:
The project introduces a novel perspective on addressing the recycling challenge associated with Flat Panel Displays (FPD) waste—a resource of valuable metals such as indium, germanium, and gallium. This waste, originating from devices like smartphones and tablets that utilize LCD, LED, OLED, and QLED technologies, represents one of the fastest-growing group within electronic waste (e-waste). Currently, the amount of indium recovered from End-of-Life (EOL) products is negligible, being less than 1%. This statistic illustrates the pressing issue and underscores the huge need within the recycling industry. FPD waste, being a readily available source of critical metals crucial for the European economy, requires a comprehensive and sustainable approach to recycling. This becomes even more important in light of the urgent requirement to establish a closed loop for indium and other metals in Europe, ensuring raw material independence. Numerous biotechnological processes are developed within laboratories, however, there are not combined into one complex interdisciplinary technology and their translation into practical application is often limited. The BioPrep project responds to this critical need and challenge, proposing the integration of sustainable biotechnological processes into the FPD waste recycling chain. The primary objective is to develop an efficient, low carbon footprint FPD recycling technology based on microbial biotechnological processes. The BioPrep project serves as a basic step towards the main project, which aims to introduce an innovative concept of FPD recycling. In the main project we aim to combine several biotechnological processes to recover all possible materials from waste displays. It combines applications of bacteria producing bacterial cellulose for application in textile industry in the first step with bacteria dissolving metals in the second step. Consequently, several biotechnological processes to recover obtained metals from solutions in forms of nanoparticles and use them in photovoltaic panels will be studied. Remaining glass will be recycled in the form of geopolymer for removal of various pollutants from soil. The idea is to develop the innovative technology for sustainable hazardous waste management fully in line with the circular economy principles listed in various European strategies such as Green Deal or EUSDR. Our goal is to demonstrate that eco-friendly biotechnologies are not only available but can be swiftly incorporated into our daily lives with existing scientific knowledge. Consequently, alongside scientific objectives, the project is dedicated to educational and social pursuits. It will strengthen cooperation among universities in the region, will give the opportunity to share best practices and enrich study programs across all participating universities by newest knowledge and motivate students to study environmental science. Through the BioPrep initiative, we aim to showcase the viability of green technologies and their potential to change the recycling practise. To optimize the efficacy of FPDs recycling, the public needs education on proper recycling behaviours. Despite the increasing emphasis on recycling, a significant part of the population does not fully understand the complexity of e-waste processing. In the EU, the total electrical and electronic equipment introduced to the market in 2021 amounted to 

13.5 million tonnes, yet only 

4.9 million tonnes of e-waste were collected, representing only 36% of the total production. This statistical contrast highlights the disparity between consumers' recycling practices and the quantifiable impact of recycling. Bridging this awareness and knowledge gap is achievable through educational initiatives and programs. One of the primary challenges of the main project involves disseminating research results and fostering awareness about e-waste recycling, specifically in the context of FPD, among the general public. It aims to enhance public knowledge in the field of sustainable recycling and biotechnology, fostering local awareness and macro-regional significance within the Danube Regions. BioPrep's initiatives strategically combine the knowledge and experience of partners in the field of biotechnological solutions within the Danube region, specifically Slovakia, Czech Republic, and Slovenia, with support from associated partners beyond the Danube Regions. This activity will be supplemented with carefully developed and implemented dissemination and communication strategy.

titleEn: RuBIO to boost innovation and competitiveness of entrepreneurs
summaryEn:
The RuBIO initiative aims to support and propose action focused on innovation and economic development in rural areas of the Danube Region. The RuBIO initiative will explore the potential for adopting bio-based solutions (such as within the sectors of biotechnology and biomanufacturing) among entrepreneurs (startups, SMEs and bigger companies) in the Danube Region and broader. This project will analyse and discuss the state-of-the-art but also mitigate challenges and further strengthen (the competitiveness of) the region’s rural bio-based ecosystems and broader ecosystems. This way, the project will directly address the goals of Priority Area (PA)8 and capitalise on the work of the Working Groups (WG) on ‘Innovation and technology transfer’ and on “Circular Bioeconomy”. 
RuBIO represents a strategic initiative towards developing and supporting rural economies by promoting sustainable practices in the Danube Region. By exploring the potential of empowering rural entrepreneurs with the knowledge, resources, and networks needed to embrace bio-economy principles, this project aims to work towards unlocking the full potential of rural communities. This way, the RuBIO will create a more inclusive and resilient economy in the Danube region.

The RuBIO initiative aims to address the main challenges faced by different areas in the Danube Region, such as the decreasing population, ageing population, the lack of skilled workforce, and the developmental disparities between the Western and Eastern regions. These issues have led to economic stagnation and social problems in many communities. By focusing on innovation and economic development and emphasising the importance of manufacturing, RuBIO hopes to offer a response to reverse these trends and create growth opportunities. The initiative aims to attract and retain a skilled workforce in different areas by discussing support for entrepreneurs and startups in bio-economy, biotechnology and biomanufacturing, making communities more sustainable and vibrant.

Additionally, RuBIO recognises the need to reduce the development gaps between the Western and Eastern regions along the Danube. The Eastern areas often lack infrastructure, resources, and economic opportunities compared to the West. Additionally, depopulation causes land abandonment in rural areas and low knowledge and use of best available practices. These processes increase developmental disparities within the Danube Region. By promoting innovation and uptake of technologies and best practices in biotechnology and biomanufacturing, the RuBIO initiative desires to uplift the developmental potential of rural areas across the entire region. Bio-economy itself, as well as biotechnology and biomanufacturing, is recognised as a potential tool to promote and invigorate innovation systems. Recognising the need for joint work, RuBIO will deliver the baseline for creating long-term partnerships and successful collaboration. The initiative promises to seek and ensure that all communities have access to the support and resources needed to succeed in the bio-based economy.

Furthermore, the RuBIO initiative desires to address the challenge of workforce migration from rural to urban environments in the Danube Region. By fostering innovation and economic development in rural areas, RuBIO aims to create opportunities for employment and entrepreneurship, thereby offering the potential for individuals to remain in or return to rural communities. Through initiatives that support the adoption of bio-based solutions and the development of rural economies, RuBIO seeks to support the diversification of local economies, contributing to the creation of job opportunities and thus enhancing the quality of life in rural areas. By supporting the revitalisation of rural communities and outlining viable alternatives to urban migration, RuBIO desires to preserve rural livelihoods and the sustainable development of the entire region.

Lastly, RuBIO is closely aligned with Priority Area 8 (PA8) of the EU Strategy for the Danube Region, which focuses on improving the competitiveness of businesses. By building on the work of existing working groups (WG on Innovation and Technology Transfer and WG on Circular Bio-economy), RuBIO aims to use its expertise and resources to succeed in its aims. This way, the RuBIO initiative will contribute to and strive to drive innovation and economic growth in different areas of the Danube region. Delivering a comprehensive set of activities, RuBIO will result in being a long-term initiative and will offer a strong base for further shaping bio-based innovation ecosystems in the Danube Region and wider. In doing so, RuBIO aims to create a more inclusive and resilient economy in the Danube region, paving the way for sustainable development in the future.

titleEn: MEntal WEll-being in Education for disadvantaged YOUth
summaryEn:
The MEET project will promote the mental health of (vulnerable) young people in AT, BG, BH, CZ, HU, ME, RO, RS, SI, SK, UA and the DR. In 2019, 10-12% of young people aged 10-19 years in the Danube Region (DR) were affected by mental disorders. Multiple crises (COVID, Ukraine war, Climate) are an increasing threat to young people's mental health and well-being. The global nature of these crises and the shared challenges in the DR call for a transnational approach. MEET aims to building capacities for youth mental health promotion in formal and informal educational settings at three different levels: At the practice level, MEET will collaboratively develop and pilot inclusive, innovative and youth-centred tools and learning materials for educators, social workers, practitioners (O

2.2) and young people at risk (NEETs, ESLs) themselves (O

2.3). At the level of organisations and intermediaries, MEET will bring together key actors of health and education in Youth Mental Health Labs to form new and cross-sectoral mental health coalitions, boost their knowledge on mental health and equip them with a methodology on how to cooperate in the future (O

1.2). At the policy level, MEET will develop a transnational strategy (O

3.1) and local action plans (O

3.2) to integrate mental health in education giving policymakers of all levels guidelines on how to make education policy more inclusive. MEET’s innovative approach not only targets formal education like schools, but also non-formal education, like after-work schools, youth NGOs who are key in reaching disadvantaged learners and vulnerable youth. Moreover, it will address different dimensions of social inequalities by reaching out, e.g. to young people in rural areas and to Roma people. As a result, the project will help to combat mental health problems among young people, especially among vulnerable groups of young people. In the long term, the MEET outcomes will lead to a reduction in poor school performance and drop-outs, reduce the number of NEETs, enable a better educated workforce and contribute to reduced labour shortages.

titleEn: Innovative pathways for efficient involvement of girls and young women in the forestry sector
summaryEn:
Forestry and forest-based industries are facing labor shortages, while the number of those choosing careers in forestry is declining. At the same time, the sector is known for providing so-called "green jobs" that help maintain forest ecosystems and ensure sustainable production of forest products and fair treatment of workers. 
Fem2forests aims to (1) develop innovative career pathways for girls and young women, (2) strengthen the capacity of forestry education institutions through mainstreaming of the gender perspective, and (3) facilitate the framework conditions for efficient involvement of women at different levels and stages in forestry organizations and relevant labour markets. To achieve these objectives, the Fem2forests concept follows an interactive and multi-stakeholder-driven innovation model that covers career paths in forestry from early orientation stages to leadership positions. Workshops, surveys, and interviews are used to identify the needs and interests of girls and young women in the forestry sector. Education and training institutions, as well as employers, business support organizations, and other stakeholders, will be closely involved throughout the project to help change awareness and create a framework for a more diverse workforce that promotes sustainable development, especially in rural areas. Through all these activities, we aim to increase the proportion of young women in the forestry sector by 2030 and beyond. The project is built from the bottom up, so the communication and involvement of target groups from the start of the project is essential. We believe that the participation of the key target groups will bring change in the forestry sector in DR. 
Fem2forests project is built on the solid ground laid down by its successor Fem4Forest (DTP3-500), which gave us a first insight into the status of women in the forestry sector in DR. Experiences, methodologies developed and gathered information will be our solid background, and it is our motivation to work with your girls and women. The Fem2forest project is proposed at a time when all countries in DR are facing a shortage of working force in the forestry sector. We believe that changing the perception of forestry as labour intensive and man-dominated sector among youngsters can change the labour market and bring "fresh wind" into the sector.

summaryEn:

4.0, across the Danube Region.
