titleEn: Moving PLastics and mAchine iNdustry towards Circularity
summaryEn:
Plastics are a versatile material omnipresent in modern life, but by far not sufficiently recirculated after first use. The goal of the EU circular economy action plan, i.e. a recycling quote of plastics packaging of 50% until 2025, remains challenging, for the Western countries and even more for the South/Eastern Danube region that shows severe deficits in waste management systems and a lack of industrial processing knowledge for the recirculation of secondary plastics materials. 
The Plan-C project consortium of 14 partners from DE, AT, CZ, SK, HU, RS, BiH, RO, and MD aims to boost the transformation of the plastics value chain in the Danube Region towards circularity through the transnational cooperation of plastics processors/producers and the machine industry. Close cooperation among partners across the Danube Region countries is required to introduce a fundamental change in this complex plastics value chain, implying a radical shift of mindsets, behaviour, and business paradigms. As a result, the main actors in the value chain - plastics producers and machine firms - increase their competitiveness, which contributes to the achievement of the EUSDR PA8 goals.
Based on a transnational technology transfer and utilizing a design thinking process, the PPs + plastics producers co-create and immediately demonstrate circular plastics prototypes. The resulting Circular Plastics Guideline aims at building up knowledge and capacities for its practical implementation in regional companies. The Associated Strategic Partners ASPs together with further involved policy stakeholders ensure the transfer of the related Strategy for enhancing circularity in the plastics industry to RIS

3.
Similarly, PPs + machine firms analyze, ideate, and prototype circular solutions for each machine life cycle phase and create related digital business models along the whole machine life cycle, summarized in a Guideline for circularity in the machine industry. The related Strategy for boosting circularity in the machine industry ensures transfer to the RIS3 of the partner countries, with strong support from ASPs.
Both actor groups - PPs and at least 140 enterprises from the plastics + machine industry in the Danube region - are joining forces to develop a vision for a transformed plastics value chain designed for circularity, demonstrating the benefits of reuse/recycling of plastics and maintenance, redistribution, refurbishing/remanufacturing and recycling of machines. The final Transnational Action Plan to anchor circular economy in the holistic plastics value chain addresses SMEs, large enterprises, BSOs, sectoral agencies, and public authorities. At least 70 organizations will increase their capacities to implement circular concepts along the plastics value chain.

titleEn: Increasing capacities of PTO and PTA in the EURO MED area by testing novel solutions to effectively manage public transport’s transition towards energy-efficiency and resource-efficiency
summaryEn: E-MED tests and validates solutions to increase energy-efficiency and resource-efficiency of public transport systems to reduce public transport's environmental footprint drastically, and to react flexibly to changing energy prices caused by the current energy crisis. This challenge affects in particular local public authorities, public transport infrastructure and energy providers, but also industry suppliers of electric vehicles and service operators. Thus, E-MED solutions are developed to increase energy-efficiency and share of Renewable Energy Systems (RES), (e.g., tools for fleet, network planning, driver support, Artificial intelligence supported maintenance of energy systems), and to increase resource-efficiency and resilience, (e.g., re-use of batteries and washing water recycling systems, maintenance of tires, procurement guidelines) support in the evidence-based planning and introduction of e-bus systems to help objective decision-taking and smart planning, investing and procurement from the start. This way, E-MED solutions support the right design of a Public Transport (PT) system through smart organisation and planning of networks and operations, optimised charging concepts, optimal use of engineering technology, and capacity building around more “human” topics like eco-driving. As key enablers to reduce energy consumption and to increase the lifetime of PT fleet and infrastructure, E-MED solutions with focus on end-user needs provide orientation to both buyers and industry. Based on the testing and validation of E-MED solutions, strategies and action plans are optimised in a participatory co-design approach with stakeholders from the public transport and energy community. E-MED is composed of 10 partners ranging from public transport organisations and authorities to cities, as well as knowledge partners renowned in the transport and energy field. To enlarge this cooperation, associated paratners like UITP, University of Lisbon, and CARNET are strategically involved to maximise communication outreach and knowledge transfer of results.

titleEn: COoperation and CO-designing PArtnership for CliMAte Neutrality
summaryEn:
Mediterranean islands will start their transition to climate neutrality thanks to the CO2 Pacman project.
Building on outcomes and tools from the previous projects Interreg Med BLUE DEAL and COMPOSE Plus and the FP7 CityZen, CO2 Pacman will provide knowledge and tools to drive the implementation of integrated strategies and policies for the challenge of climate change mitigation and adaptation; with this purpose it will engage public authorities, citizens and stakeholders in co-creation of scenarios for the transition towards climate neutral islands.
Project activities will be showcased in three target islands: Brac in Croatia, Crete in Greece and Elba in Italy. 
Based on results from testing, the project will develop an integrated cooperative planning framework and deliver a joint strategy/action plan embedding policies and strategies for climate change mitigation and adaptation to be potentially replicated in islands and coastal areas. The new CO2 Pacman assessment and visual tool will be developed to assess current challenges (i.e. Carbon Footprint and its drivers) and then to identify multi-sectoral solutions and to quantify their effects in terms of Carbon Footprint mitigation and compensation to achieve the goal of climate neutrality in the islands. These solutions, including ecosystem based approaches, will concern the sectors of energy, buildings, mobility, water and waste management, tourism, industry, etc.
The cooperation and co-creation approach will target: public authorities (increasing their capacity in effective planning), enterprises, groups of interest and citizens to foster both transnational and local cooperation, support innovation and capacity building.
The shift to a climate neutral society requires a cultural transition: the project integrates scientific and technical information in a new clear and fun communication and social engagement system, composed by new visual tools able to help plan climate neutrality transition roadmaps for islands.

titleEn: Towards Climate Resilient Mediterranean Cities
summaryEn:
Urban areas are known to be among the main contributors to climate change worldwide. At the same time, they are especially at risk from the impacts of climate change. There is a growing recognition that climate change is here for the long term, and that actions is needed, not just mitigation, but also to adapt to the impacts that we can expect to see now and in the future. Consequently, innovative responses for raising the resilience and adaptation of Mediterranean cities are needed. Capitalising and combining the results of previous and ongoing projects (CESBA MED Sustainable MED Cities, Sustainable MED Cities, ARTACLIM and Habit.A), ReMED will develop an innovative set of affordable tools, along with an overarching decision support framework, to help cities in:
- assessing and understanding the level of climate risk at urban and building scale
- designing optimal climate adaptation measures in relation to local conditions
- implementing climate adaptation measures through the most suitable policy instruments
- monitoring and evaluating the results of adaptation measures over time.
ReMED will support a Multi-Level Governance (MLG) in climate adaptation, as recommended by the UN COP

26.
ReMED methods, tools and decision support framework will be organised in a friendly web-based tool, the ReMED Platform. ReMED will deliver capacity building measures towards public authorities in the use of the ReMED Platform to facilitate its practical use and uptake. The focus of the capacity building process will be the test of the ReMED Platform to support the implementation of adaptation measures through policy instruments. The main output of the project will be an overall raised capacity of public authorities in deploying effective measures to improve the resilience of cities.

titleEn: INnovative FInancing solutions for climate planning of REsilient and carbon neutral living areas
summaryEn:
The Mediterranean is at the forefront of the fight against climate change, requiring cities and regions to act quickly and cooperate to prevent further negative environmental, social, and economic implications. INFIRE addresses two key aspects of the slow transition towards climate neutrality and climate adaptation in the Euro-MED region: low capacities of public authorities for the development and integration of strategic planning documents and the inability to properly evaluate and mobilize public and private capital for large-scale investment projects needed for reaching EU’s 2030 targets. 

INFIRE gathers experienced partners with highly complementary skills that cooperate to establish a long-lasting support structure to build capacities of public authorities in the involved regions for developing, implementing, and monitoring holistic climate adaptation and carbon neutrality (CACN) solutions and policy instruments. INFIRE provides jointly developed and practical solutions in form of:
-	Green Finance Evaluation Toolkit for triggering financing of CACN projects and long-term strategies with innovative financing schemes
-	Enhanced and aligned strategic planning documents and public financing programmes to support the transition to resilience and carbon neutrality
-	Tailor-made curriculum and intensive capacity-building programme for public authorities of the Euro-MED region
-	Citizens’ engagement through co-creation process and civic-crowdfunding models, promoting behavioral change
-	Piloting 8 concrete and innovative CACN solutions for future replication and upscaling.

The originality of INFIRE project arises from a holistic bottom-up approach that addresses both the supply (public authorities as project developers) and demand side (financial institutions and citizens as investors) by understanding their drivers and shortcomings and bridging the gap through intensive cooperation with both sides and promotion of best available practices.

titleEn: Adapting IUCN Green List Standard to the Mediterranean Marine Protected Areas
summaryEn:
The “GreenList4MMPAs” Project aims to adapt, for the first time, the IUCN Green List Standard (GL) to the Mediterranean marine context. The GL is the first global and only universal Standard of best practice for area-based conservation. It aims to provide an international benchmark for quality that motivates improved effectiveness and achievement of conservation objectives. GreenList4MMPAs will develop specific indicators and methods to assess marine protected areas (MPAs), providing an actionable and useful tool for MPA managers and practitioners. The common challenge that GreenList4MMPAs will tackle is the need for Mediterranean MPAs to enhance their capacities in preserving marine biodiversity and ecosystems in order to mitigate the overall degradation of the Mediterranean marine environment (fully in line with the Programme S.O. 

2.7). GreenList4MMPAs will support Mediterranean MPAs in achieving their conservation and social objectives through a reliable system for the assessment of the effectiveness, based on a tool that will ensure MPA effective management. The main project’s outputs will be the Mediterranean MPAs-tailored IUCN Green List Set of Indicators and the establishment of the MED MPAs EAGLs (a committee of experts trained by IUCN that examine protected areas’ applications for the Green List Standard). These outputs will largely benefit local public authorities such as MPAs’ management bodies, but also national public authorities (e.g. Ministries and technical agencies) and IUCN, which represents globally the largest international organisation about nature conservation.
The “GreenList4MMPAs” Project will adopt an approach based on the use of a large number of case studies in seven EU countries, two IPA countries, and six Third Med countries (thanks to an additional funding by IUCN), in order to represent all the existing seven Ecoregions in the Mediterranean Sea. In this perspective only a true transnational approach can allow project’s goals to be met.

titleEn: Danube River Environmental Assessment and Monitoring (DREAM) Project
summaryEn:
The Danube River Environmental Assessment and Monitoring (DREAM) Project aims to identify and address environmental issues along the Danube River in the Ruse/Giurgiu-Silistra/Calarasi region. The initiative intends to comprehensively assess air and water quality, noise pollution, and other environmental aspects using cutting-edge technology like UAV, and a solar-powered boat.
The Danube River serves as an important waterway for many countries, but it is currently struggling with pollution problems in both its waters and the surrounding ecosystem. The towns that rely on the river for recreation and sustenance are also impacted by this, in addition to the aquatic life. These problems have been made worse by unsustainable behavior, industrialization, and insufficient monitoring techniques.
The main objective of the project is to provide thorough, precise, and up-to-date data on the environmental condition of the Danube River in the Ruse/Giurgiu-Silistra/Calarasi region. It aspires to achieve the following goals through this: - Facilitate prompt actions to lessen negative environmental effects; - Serve as a model for other Danube basins and comparable ecosystems internationally; - Promote awareness and cooperation among local communities, governments, and industries.
The expected change includes improved community involvement in conserving the river's health, more sustainable industrial practices, and better-informed decision-making procedures.
The Outputs of the project are:
-Comprehensive datasets on air and water quality, noise pollution, and broader environmental metrics.
-A sustainable energy model integrating solar-powered boat and UAVs for wider research areas and power independence.
-Regular reports and recommendations for stakeholders.
The Beneficiaries of the project are:
-Local communities that rely on the river for various needs.
-Governments and policymakers to frame regulations and interventions.
-Industries seeking to adopt sustainable practices.
-Environmentalists and researchers.
The strategy incorporates cutting-edge technology, community involvement, and cross-disciplinary cooperation. Real-time, accurate monitoring is made possible by using UAV and solar-powered devices, and sustainability is guaranteed by community involvement.
Due to the Danube River's transnational nature, environmental issues in one location might have an impact on nearby areas. A cooperative, international strategy guarantees coordinated, thorough efforts by combining resources, expertise, and best practices.
The DREAM Project integrates UAV systems for environmental monitoring with renewable energy technologies, such as solar-powered boats, in an inventive way. This provides greater data collection accuracy in addition to sustainability. It also serves as a model for tackling common environmental problems in interconnected ecosystems because of its focus on a cross-border, cooperative approach.
Beyond its technological advancements, the DREAM Project places a lot of emphasis on community involvement and education. The initiative seeks to promote a feeling of group accountability among citizens, companies, and decision-makers. The initiative will provide communities with knowledge about the state of their environment and methods they can use to improve it through holding workshops, public forums, and educational campaigns.
Despite being founded close to Ruse, Giurgiu, Silistra, and Calarasi, the DREAM Project's approaches and frameworks are flexible. Other places along the Danube facing comparable problems or in other river ecosystems throughout the world can scale or reproduce the lessons learned, technologies used, and best practices produced.
The project involves academic and scientific institutes to guarantee the validity of interpretations and the quality of data. The DREAM Project will benefit from these partnerships' experience in environmental research, data analysis, and technological application. In exchange, these institutions will have access to a large dataset for research and educational purposes.
The DREAM Project's emphasis on long-term effects is one of its defining characteristics. Once installed, the solar-powered infrastructure provides a long-term means of maintaining surveillance after the project's first stages. The project also secures the continuation of its goals and benefits by fostering environmental awareness in nearby communities and establishing institutional relationships.
Through a special website, the public will have access to the collected data. This online resource will function as both an interactive tool for education and awareness as well as a database. The approach creates confidence and promotes public involvement in environmental conservation efforts by making information openly accessible.

titleEn: Streamlining cross-border cooperation: Joint approach in disaster resilience – STREAM 2
summaryEn:
The outcomes of climate change are more pronounced in vulnerable regions, as in the case of the regions in the proximity of the lower Danube from Romania and Bulgaria. The main common challenges related to climate change that are tackled in the project are floods, heatwaves and extreme weather events. The cooperation between the project Partners is necessary for incidents on Danube river, incidents that affect both sides of borders. These challenges hinder the effectiveness of disaster response efforts and endanger lives and property. Establishing effective communication and collaboration protocols is important.
The primary objective is to increase the safety and protection of the population in the eligible area by improving and enhancing climate change adaptation and disaster risk prevention resilience through the establishment of cross-border disaster response and situational operations centers, capacity building and joint interventions.
The project aims to bring an important change in the current emergency response landscape. By enhancing cross-border cooperation, common trainings, and establishing well-equipped disaster response centers, we anticipate a substantial improvement in the speed, efficiency, and effectiveness of emergency interventions, with a significant reduction in loss of life, property and environmental damage during disasters.
The main outputs of our project will include:
-Updated joint intervention plans and common procedures for coordinated disaster response, and a new developed Intervention Procedure on Danube river.
- Enhanced training curricula for volunteer and professional firefighters, ensuring they possess the necessary skills and knowledge.
-Well-equipped and newly-built cross-border disaster response centers.
-Newly-built zonal vessel base in Giurgiu and a mobile pontoon procured;
-Procured equipment and special vehicles to bolster intervention capacity.
The beneficiaries of these outputs will be local communities, firefighting personnel (professional and volunteers) which will receive improved training and enhanced resources, resulting in increased confidence and competence during interventions, Municipal and regional governments which will benefit from strengthened disaster resilience, minimized economic losses, and improved public safety. The project approach involves a comprehensive strategy that encompasses training, infrastructure development, and procurement of essential intervention resources. By collaborating across borders, we can ensure a coordinated response that is not hindered by administrative boundaries. This approach leverages the strengths of both Romania and Bulgaria and allows for a more robust disaster management system. What sets our project apart is its holistic approach to addressing every facet of emergency response. From updating intervention plans to establishing cutting-edge disaster response centers and enhancing training, we are leaving no stone unturned. The project's focus on both volunteers and professional staff, as well as the establishment of specialized centers. To this approach is added the investment in the infrastructure on Danube river, with the zonal vessel base and pontoon, which will play a critical role in supporting the operations of emergency boats used by first responders.
In conclusion, our cross-border project between Romanian and Bulgarian partners represents an effort to further develop the emergency response in the region. By addressing challenges through comprehensive training, infrastructure development, and collaboration, we aspire to build a more resilient and effective disaster response system that safeguards lives and property on both sides of the border.

titleEn: Development of Environmentally Friendly Cultures in Giurgiu and Ruse Counties
summaryEn:
Most border regions share similar challenges. These regions due to their geographic positions are economically disadvantaged, bur their key position is a good opportunity for establishing cross-border/ International cooperation. The project areas main challenge addressed by the project is that initiatives and attractions are mainly isolated from each other, their operators are rarely cooperating.and the initiatives are covering smaller areas or less members.
Finding a solution to the common needs is a common cause for the two countries and can only be realized in an investment transcending the border as national initiations would not reach the goal.
Our project will improved cooperation in different fields - nature protection, pollution, biodiversity, green infrastructure and education sector; also, will deliver pilot actions and solutions in the above mentioned sectors and trained participants.
General objective is the joint promotion and development of niche crops on small areas and related ecosystems services, such as lavender, berries, sea buckthorn up to 1 ha in Giurgiu and Ruse County. The project will contribute to the INTERREG VIA Rom-Bulg program's objective of protecting nature and biodiversity. At the end of the project, we will increase the number of niche crops in the region.
So far, according to the summaries drawn up on the basis of written notifications submitted by farmers, more than 20000 ha have been affected by soil drought in Giurgiu and Ruse Counties in 2022, especially corn, wheat, sunflower and barley crops. Also one of the problem in Giurgiu and Ruse counties is soil pollution by pesticides is one of the most common forms of pollution today. The widespread use of pesticides in agricultural production can degrade and damage microorganisms living in the soil. Even more so, in cases where these chemicals are misused or in excess, chemical compounds accumulate in the soil. Thus, the use of pesticides decreases the overall biodiversity of the soil.. The type of soil and type of pesticides can also affect the persistence of pesticides. Intensive exploitation of croplands have several significant effects on the soil. Some of the main ways in which soil can be affected by intensive agricultural practices include:


1.	Chemical Pollution: The intensive use of synthetic pesticides, herbicides, and fertilizers can result in the accumulation of chemicals in the soil. Over time, these chemicals can impact soil microbial communities, beneficial organisms, and overall soil health.


2.	Loss of Biodiversity: Intensive monoculture practices can lead to a reduction in biodiversity in the soil ecosystem. A diverse range of microorganisms and organisms in the soil contribute to nutrient cycling, disease suppression, and overall ecosystem resilience.


3.	To mitigate these negative effects and promote sustainable soil management, it's important to implement niche crops on small areas, such as lavender, berries, sea buckthorn, , on 1 hectar in Giurgiu and Ruse County
Incorporating these herbs into an agricultural system can contribute to biodiversity, attract beneficial insects, and potentially provide some pest management benefits.. it's important to consider their interactions with the main crops, their contribution to soil health, and their overall role in the farm ecosystem

Finding a solution to the common needs is a common cause for the two countries and can only be realized in an investment transcending the border as national initiations would not reach the goal.
The field of biodiversity has not received increased attention from structures that have allocated funding from European fund. Having in regard this lack of funding, the developed results will have a long term multiplier effect, which will last after the project will be closed, on both sides of the border. 
The project will tackle new, very limited fields until the current call for proposals: biodiversity and green infrastructure and will provide pilot actions in the above-mentioned areas . Also,will put together pubic administration, NGO s and actors from the local labor markets (local agricultural workers to reduce migration).

titleEn: Green Harmony: Fostering Ecosystem Resilence Through Investments in Urban And Peri-Urban Green Areas in Vetovo And Giurgiu
summaryEn:
The common territorial challenge that will be tackled by the project is the need for enhanced protection and preservation of nature, biodiversity, and green infrastructure, including in urban areas, and the reduction of all forms of pollution. There is a growing recognition of the importance of nature and the environment,as well as the need for sustainable and responsible practices to protect and preserve it. GREEN Harmony aims to enhance the protection and preservation of biodiversity and green infrastructure in urban and peri-urban areas and to reduce pollution levels in the target territory. 
Measurable Change:
 

1. Increase in the percentage of green space in urban areas;
 

2. Decrease in pollution levels
Urban parks are a vital component of green infrastructure, provides multiple benefits, including biodiversity conservation, climate mitigation, and improved quality of life. Investing in green infrastructure supports the Territorial Agenda's objective of enhancing territorial cohesion and sustainability. Green Harmony recognizes the pivotal role of urban green spaces in promoting a harmonious relationship between urban development and nature. The project contributes to the broader vision of territorial cohesion and sustainability, aligning with regional and EU goals for a greener, more resilient future. Green Harmony exemplifies the transformative power of green infrastructure investments in addressing common challenges and fostering a harmonious coexistence between urban environments and nature.
Common Challenge:
 Both partners share the challenge of deteriorating urban and peri-urban green spaces, impacting the quality of life for their residents. Pollution and neglect have degraded these areas, undermining their ecological value and potential for recreation and education.
The overarching goal of the Green Harmony project is to rejuvenate and modernize urban and peri-urban green spaces in Vetovo and Giurgiu, ultimately enhancing the quality of life for their citizens. By investing in these areas, the project seeks to create attractive, accessible, and environmentally sustainable spaces that promote biodiversity, mitigate pollution, and serve as educational hubs for the communities.
The project will produce several key outputs:
Infrastructure Enhancement: In Vetovo, this involves renovating and upgrading the green infrastructure along the Beli Lom riverbank, including repairing or expanding existing embankments, cleaning the riverbed, creating transportation access points, and restoring the inlet canal. These improvements will serve as a foundation for a recreational and educational public zone.
Park Development:
 In Giurgiu, the project will focus on modernizing the urban green space adjacent to Lake Prietenia. Activities include constructing pedestrian alleys, landscaping green spaces, designing nature observation areas, replacing old furniture with new urban furniture, installing ambient lighting with photovoltaic panels, and restoring areas affected by construction.
CB Approach: 
The cross-border approach is essential because environmental challenges, such as pollution and biodiversity loss, do not respect political boundaries. Collaborating across borders allows for a more comprehensive and effective response to these shared challenges. By working together, partners can leverage their resources, expertise, and best practices to create sustainable green spaces that benefit both communities.
What's New/Original: 
The project stands out for its comprehensive approach to revitalizing urban and peri-urban green spaces. It combines physical infrastructure improvements with educational initiatives, making it a holistic effort to promote environmental sustainability. The inclusion of student exchange programs and workshops for community engagement is a novel aspect of the project, fostering a sense of ownership and responsibility among the younger generation. Additionally, the use of bio-engineering methods and visible natural stone cladding on embankments adds an eco-friendly touch to the project's design, aligning with modern sustainability practices.
The primary beneficiaries of the project are the residents of Vetovo and Giurgiu, who will enjoy improved green spaces for recreation and relaxation. Additionally, the entire region benefits from enhanced biodiversity, reduced pollution, and increased awareness of environmental issues.
In conclusion, the project is a pioneering project aimed at not only enhancing urban and peri-urban green spaces but also fostering environmental consciousness and sustainability among the residents of the programme area. This holistic approach will have a lasting impact, transforming these areas into vibrant, eco-friendly spaces that benefit the environment and the communities.

titleEn: Choosing Health And Nature for Global protEction
summaryEn:
According to the World Health Organization (WHO),some 

4.2 million deaths every year are a result of exposure to outdoor air pollution,and 91% of the world’s population lives in places where air quality exceeds WHO`s guideline limits.
Also,a study developed by UNICEF,has found that children experienced 15% of their daily black carbon exposure while travelling to school,and 44% during their time in school.
In accordance with the provisions of the framework documents specific to the areas of the project partners-Lumina Strategy for Local Development 2023-2030,Integrated Development Plan of Krushari Municipality 2021-2027 and Integrated Development Plan of General Toshevo Municipality 2021-2027,the main anthropogenic factors that influence the qualities of the environment in all partner areas,are:industry,transport, communal/municipal and household activities,use of artificial fertilizers and pesticides in agriculture.These factors have an impact on the state of the atmospheric air,waters,soil and ecosystems.
The overall objective is to deliver a school community of environmentally-minded thinkers,based on educational programmes and pollution mitigation tools, in support of the entire community,consolidating and applying project promoted knowledge and skills.
The project regards building youth motivation to actively participate in identifying solutions for the environmental problems.
Public administrations and public schools supporting environmental education and recognising the importance of awareness,are fundamental in order to improve the quality of life in the cross-border area.
CHANGE project will ensure the achievement of the Programme`s PA2 output indicators through the partnership between three organisations from neighboring regions,namely Lumina commune from Constanta county (Romania),Krushari Municipality from Dobrich district (Bulgaria) and "Hristo Smirnenski" Primary School from General Toshevo municipality (Dobrich district Bulgaria) (RCO87) and the associates schools-Lumina School no. 1 and "Hristo Smirnenski" School from Krushari,and through the development of 2 distinct tools to mitigate pollution,namely the CHANGE-App/car sharing application for the project schools and CHANGE integrated environmental teaching tool (PSO3),more than 26000 inhabitants just within the partner areas (resident population) benefitting from the pollution mitigating tools.
All 5 public project organisations acknowledge the reality that environmental education based on life experiences must begin during the very earliest years of life.Beginning this process in the early years,when children’s attitudes toward the world around them are forming,is essential,each experience playing a critical role in shaping lifelong attitudes,values,and patterns of behaviour toward natural environments.
Project consortium`s approach is a multilevel one,targeting in the same time and measure-pupils and teachers (1), parents and next-of-kins (2),and the larger community.CHANGE activity plan begins with and from the theoretical view of environment endangerment and pollution,and moves on to real and measurable actions by introducing mitigation tools reachable to everyone–an online application and an integrated teaching tool. 
CHANGE project focuses on the transboundary character of nature protection and reducing pollution, addressing pollution as a regional and global challenge,where no boundaries or borders can control the atmosphere,and loss of nature as a direct effect of pollution.
The impact of initiating project`s tools,exceeds the administrative boundaries of the partners, being Lumina commune, Krushari and General Toshevo municipalities,the results serving the entire crossborder area,first of all as tool for mitigating pollution,and second, as an exemple to follow and easy to be replicated in other regions also,the targeted problem being a current problem in all communities,no matter the national boundaries.
Project CHANGE will mitigate pollution by working on 2 complementary levels: 
-on the one hand,through behavioural interventions aiming to encourage positive behaviour among pupils,teachers in order to limit childrens' exposure to pollution and protect every piece of nature (through the Environmental Event Calendar A

1.5),
-on the other hand,through the development of 2 distinct tools to mitigate pollution,namely the CHANGE-App/car sharing application (tool 1) for the project schools,and CHANGE integrated environmental teaching tool (tool 2) consisting of an indoor environmental lab,an outdoor environmental lab,small green areas and a rainwater harvesting system.
Both tools are innovative, their novalty giving the possibility of easily being replicated

titleEn: EnviroConnect: Synergizing Green Resilience Efforts in Ivanovo and Piatra Olt
summaryEn:
EnviroConnect is a cross-border project aimed at synergizing green resilience efforts in the regions of Ivanovo - Bulgaria and Piatra Olt - Romania. These regions, although located in different countries, share common environmental challenges, making collaboration essential to address these issues effectively. The project brings together various stakeholders to tackle these challenges and promote sustainable environmental practices. It is dedicated to enhancing the protection and preservation of nature, biodiversity, and green infrastructure within the program area. This project operates under Priority SO 

2.7 , A Greener Region, with a specific objective to enhance environmental sustainability.
The common challenge faced by the programme area in Ivanovo (located in BG) and Piatra Olt (located in RO) is the degradation of natural ecosystems and the associated impacts on biodiversity, water resources and overall environmental quality.In Ivanovo, Bulgaria, the project aims to enhance and improve the green infrastructure in four specific areas: South Park - Shtraklevo, Ecopark - Shtraklevo, Memorial Park - Shtraklevo, and Pirgovo Park. These green spaces are vital for the well-being of the community and the environment in the project area. The Interreg EnviroConnect project focuses on upgrading and developing these parks to promote sustainability, biodiversity, and community engagement. In Piatra-Olt, Romania, there are 2 land plots where the development of green infrastructure is proposed: one in Bistrita Noua and one in Enosesti. 
With the view to avoid degradation of the land and the risk of being filled by invasive species, and foreseeing making good use of these natural sites, the Interreg EnviroConnect project foresees the development of 2 green modern eco-parks in the mentioned areas.
Overall objective: Enhancing the environmental resilience and sustainability in Ivanovo (BG) and Piatra Olt (RO) regions by developing 6 green infrastructure areas.The project seeks to make a substantial change in the current situation by acquiring the following achievements: 


1.	Enhanced Environmental Quality: The project will lead to improved green infrastructure, including increased tree cover, reduced pollution and better water management. 


2.	Improved Community Well-being: By creating attractive and accessible green spaces, the project will provide opportunities for relaxation, recreation, social interaction, games and practicing sports and exercises. 


3.	Increased Education and Awareness: Educational activities and signage within the parks will inform visitors about the importance of green infrastructure and environmental conservation, aiming to create new habits for respecting and protecting nature, while fostering a sense of stewardship. 
The project will produce the following Outputs:


1.	Tools implemented for mitigating pollution - Within the SOFT Measures, the project foresees Educational Activities.


2.	Pilot actions developed jointly and implemented in projects Pilot actions developed jointly and implemented in projects
Organizations cooperating across borders - One of the main achievements of the project is the connection that is created between the 2 regions, Ivanovo and Piatra Olt. Cross-Border Coordination Mechanisms have been initiated, communication channels and protocols for the cooperation have been established between the 2 regions, the national border becoming insignificant.
 The project beneficiaries are: the population from the 2 regions, Ivanovo and Piatra Olt for the general enhancement of the well being, the part of population that participates to project activites for the educational benefit, the local authorities for learning environmental practices, the 2 states of Romania and Bulgaria and of course, the environment itself.


1.	Cross border approach is essential when taking into consideration the holistic overview of the shared ecosystem, when the resource sharing and environmental learning are a must for obtaining the best results, when increasing tourism potential and environmental resilience depends on the best collaboration.


2.	Shared Ecosystems: The parks share ecosystems that extend across borders. 


3.	Resource Sharing: Sharing knowledge, expertise, and resources across borders is needed in order to make the project more efficient and cost-effective.


4.	Tourism Potential: Collaboration between the 2 regions is needed in order to facilitate the promotion of tourism between the regions, and to attract visitors from neighboring areas in the well-maintained, modern parks.
This holistic, cross-border, and community-centered approach makes EnviroConnect an innovative and impactful initiative in the realm of environmental conservation and resilience.

titleEn: Safeguarding biodiversity and combating poaching
summaryEn:
The project will be in the benefit of the Programme area and will focus also on the Green Deal objectives in respect to supporting the preservation of biodiversity, safeguarding protected areas and promoting green urban spaces. Poaching and Illegal activities in the Danube river has been a major problem for both Romania and Bulgaria for years.
This illegal activities are not only causing economic and environmental damage but is also undermining the efforts of both countries to protect and conserve their biodiversity.
The materially outdated base of EAFA from Bg, as well as the morally outdated equipments, require taking measures to improve the way that the institutions that are involved with this project, will work together against illegal activities in the area of interest.
Trough the project, both Ro and Bg will work together to address this issue and find ways to support and protect the river’s valuable resources. By developing a joint action plan will increase enforcement of fishing regulations and also, by performing events on raising public awareness of the importance of biodiversity protection will increase the public knowledge and understanding of the issue, its impact and consequences, and how individuals can help in protecting the biodiversity and Danube ecosystem and the protected areas in GR, CL and TR counties and Ruse, Silistra, V. Tarnovo and Pleven districts. Due to his project large area could be considered as semi strategic.
The specific objective of the project is the increasing the intervention capacity for the environmental protection, through the development of the training infrastructure and the corresponding endowment of the authorities in charge, by implementing:


1.Joint strategies and joint action plans tackling biodiversity protection and the issue of illegal actions that affect the Danube ecosystem and the protected areas;


2.Development and implementation of conservation and protection measures of Natura2000 sites on the RO side and equivalent natural protected areas on the BG side, according to the EU Nature Restoration Plan and the BG National Framework for Natura 2000 Priority Actions 2021-2027 (applicable for the Bulgarian partner).
Following the construction of the Zonal Operational Center will be a proactive step toward enhancing coordination, response capabilities, and resource management against illegal activities that affect biodiversity. 
We intend to use this ZOC for the training and continuous specialization of the personnel in charge of preventing and combating illegal actions in eligible area, and for the storage of goods confiscated following the actions of institutions in charge, from RO and BG also.
After we will finish the investment we have proposed that all the Steering Committee Meetings will take place in the zonal operational center, and also after the project implementation will end, we will like to continue the collaboration with the partners involved in this project. 
The specialized equipment that the partners PP2+PP3 are going to purchase in the project and the joint training in the field of border management, will deliver a more efficient response to prevent and counter illegal exploitations and poaching in both countries.
Also, all the equipment purchased by PP4 under the project will be used in the department "Fisheries and Control - Central Danube" for the regions of Veliko Tarnovo, Pleven, Ruse, and Silistra and will bring benefits and added value to both: Bulgaria and Romania.

titleEn: Green modeling of urban areas, creation of new systems for recreation and outdoor activities
summaryEn:
The cross-border cooperation project “Green Modeling of Urban Areas, Creation of New Systems for Recreation and Outdoor Activities” brings together the Municipality of Giurgiu in Romania and the Municipality of Ruse in Bulgaria, under the funding program Interreg Romania-Bulgaria. The project addresses the common challenge of enhancing the protection and preservation of nature, biodiversity, and green infrastructure in urban areas while reducing various forms of pollution.
The program area, encompassing both Giurgiu and Ruse, faces pressing environmental issues such as pollution, habitat degradation, and the fragmentation of natural areas due to urbanization. These challenges threaten the well-being of the local communities and the ecological balance of the region. A collaborative effort is needed to mitigate these issues effectively.
The overarching goal of the project is to contribute to the sustainable development of Ecosystem Services in urban areas in Giurgiu and Ruse by improving their green infrastructure, promoting biodiversity conservation, reducing pollution and behavior change initiatives. The project aims to create healthier, greener, and more sustainable urban environments that benefit both nature and local communities.
The project seeks to bring about a positive transformation in the current environmental and urban landscape. It aims to achieve the following changes: By developing and enhancing green spaces, including parks and recreational areas, the project will create more attractive and functional urban environments, thus improving green infrastructure. Through biodiversity conservation efforts, such as planting native species and creating habitats, the project will increase the local flora and fauna, promoting ecological balance and enchaining the biodiversity. The project will empower local communities and stakeholders to actively participate in the development of ecosystem services in their respective areas, thus reducing pollution in the cross-border area (CBA).
The project will produce several key outputs:
A standardized approach to assess ecosystem services, including protocols for data collection and analysis, will be developed - Comprehensive Urban Ecosystem Services Assessment Methodology. A Joint Action plan for development of Ecosystem services will be created, thus laying foundations of newly established Urban ReNature EsS network. Will be create and establish the Danube Bauhaus Twinning Parks in Ruse and Giurgiu as flagship green urban spaces, exemplifying innovative approaches to green infrastructure, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable urban development. These parks will serve as focal points for community engagement, environmental education, and the promotion of ecosystem services, fostering cross-border collaboration and inspiring similar initiatives in the region. The parks will be the first members of the Urban ReNature EsS Network. Training packages, workshops and competitions will empower local stakeholders and communities to engage in sustainable ecosystem service development. A comprehensive communication strategy will promote project objectives and outcomes, encouraging public participation.
The project's outputs will benefit a wide range of stakeholders, including local communities, local authorities, environmental organizations, youth and educational institutions, public health, etc. 
A cross-border approach will be used and the same is essential because environmental challenges often transcend political boundaries. Giurgiu and Ruse share the Danube River and face similar urbanization issues. Collaborative efforts will enable the sharing of knowledge, resources, and best practices, resulting in more effective solutions.
What sets this project apart is its innovative approach to urban sustainability, biodiversity and ecosystem services conservation. It combines the principles of the New European Bauhaus, green infrastructure development, and community engagement to create a holistic model for urban revitalization. The project's focus on enhancing ecosystem services in a cross-border context is a pioneering effort, demonstrating the potential for harmonious coexistence between urban areas and the natural environment.
Municipality of Ruse, will include ineligible expenditure to ensure the equipment named "Modular administrative structure/container type/ with facades of wooden elements" which was eliminated from the Technical Project. It will be purchased by LP using its own financial funds. According to the bill of quantities in the Preliminary Design value is 2,556.50 EUR excluding VAT (3,067.80 EUR including VAT).

titleEn: Cross-border attractiveness - smart tourism in region Kyustendil - Kriva palanka - Nevestino
summaryEn:
The implementation of the project concept "Cross-border attractiveness-intelligent tourism in the region Kyustendil-Kriva Palanka-Nevestino " will contribute to achieve sustainable economic growth by creating conditions and prerequisites of increasing the competitiveness and attractiveness of the Kyustendil-Kriva Palanka-Nevestino cross-border region by diversifying tourist mobility and attractive sustainable tourist products capable of attracting a significant number of visitors.The construction of appropriate infrastructure for the needs of tourism will stimulate the development of small and medium-sized enterprises and will contribute to the transformation of the region into an attractive destination for Bulgarian, Macedonian and foreign tourists and businesses. Through measures improving the transformation of tourism into an industry with year-round employment, sustainable economic growth, opening of new jobs, increasing people's well-being, getting to know the cross-border cultural and historical heritage and maintaining warm and friendly relations between the cross-border population will be supported.
The implementation of the project will contribute to the transformation of the cross-border region Kyustendil-Kriva Palanka-Nevestino into an attractive place for life, work and recreation, with a developed economy, modern and diverse forms of tourism, with environmentally friendly mobility of international importance.
The newly created competitive tourist product on both sides of the border will be aimed at the Bulgarian, Macedonian and last but not least the international market with the aim of getting to know and preserving the natural and cultural-historical heritage and will be an effective springboard for entering international markets.The growth of tourism sector in the economy and of tourism business in general will be higher, the number of tourism companies will grow and the share of people employed in the tourism business will increase, the supply of tourist products within the cross-border region will increase, the share of overnight visits by Bulgarians and foreign citizens will increase, which will lead to an increase in income from the development of the tourism industry.The implementation of construction activities and the attraction of investments in the sector for the construction of new and modernization of the existing tourist infrastructure will be of crucial importance for its development in the next years. The measures will be focused on the tourist product, marketing and advertising, with a view of securing financial assistance from EU programs, as well as attracting private capital.
Increasing the interest of potential tourists and increasing the tourist flow will become an engine for development of cross-border tourism business and revitalization of other branches of service and production sphere in the short and medium term.
The joint integrated pilot solution will enable the project partners from both sides of the border to adopt, develop and test new approaches, products and techniques to promote tourism in the Kyustendil-Kriva Palanka-Nevestino cross-border region, taking advantage of its territorial potential.
The main goal of the project and the achievement of the set indicators could not be realized through national or local and regional mrograms, because only through the development and implementation of common new competitive tourism products could the policy of cohesion, which aims to solve cross-border problems and jointly develop the potential of the different territories, be developed and multiplied. While most internal EU programs (programmes covering territories of EU Member States only) provide support for solutions to global challenges, TGS-IPA territories still face the need to catch up in their socio-economic development. Therefore, the main joint challenge of the target region of the cross-border cooperation between Republic of Bulgaria and Republic of North Macedonia is to leave the group of lagging regions and take a more advanced course of development, while at the same time it still faces persistent problems related to risk of poverty and income inequality, which is due to negative demographic changes, underdeveloped regional chains of value creation and entrepreneurship development, low technological specialization, unattractive and uncompetitive economic environment.

titleEn: Balkan alternative mobility routes for sustainable all-season tourism
summaryEn:
Many common challenges of the programme area are jointly tackling by the project and partners itself. Some are:
Ensuring connectivity between natural and cultural sites is affected by the project through investments and creating a network of traced, categorized, marked and digitalized routes for year-round tourism.
Strengthening joint actions in the field of heritage exchange we strive to overcome by supplementing and expanding the developed site and mobile app under previously developed project.
Taking steps in overcoming the differences in the administrative systems and approaches to the protection of our heritage and increase product competitiveness by research activities and development of joint strategies of CB region under the project.
Increasing the knowledge, skills and competitiveness and reduce disparities between covered municipalities.
Developing an all-year tourism product, which raises the level and combines opportunities for development and diversification of the forms of tourist services with emphasis on ecotourism development, raising the level of development of ecological tourism, diversifying strong seasonal nature of tourist services in the CB region and it is resistant to the vulnerability of services in the tourism sector due to pandemic situations.
Developing modern digital solutions for Increasing the demand for eco-friendly tourism and bioproducts and improving technological competitiveness at the global level.
Investments in new tourist and cultural assets with ecological approach, and etc.
The overall project objective is to create a competitive all-season alternative mobility tourism product BankanVelo which offers routes network for safe, diverse, pandemic-resistant tourism in CB project area. Developed with multi-sector integrated approach, BankanVelo offers opportunities for sport&recreation outside the cities for residents & visitors needs using horizontal approach; connects natural, tourist and cultural sites; creates new assets; follows an ecosystem-based approach; offer smart solutions and brings marketing on new level.
The main project outputs will produce are investments in tourist and cultural infrastructure in Gevgelija, Bogdanci and Razlog; an all-season, integrated and resilient regional and CB effective tourist product with strong regional brand; multi-sectoral network and advisory board (cluster); pilot activities “Marketing on e-wheels” and social tourism; new smart apps and technologies.
Developed new and reconstructed tourist & cultural infrastructure are as follows:
Reconstruction and adaptation of an existing building in Gjavoto, Bogdanci into a space for tourists and cyclists;
Reconstruction for Multifunctional tourist friendly center and construction of a bike path in Sermenin, Gevgelija;
New Attraction park for tourism and recreation in the area of Golak, Razlog. 
The stakeholders, who will benefit from the project are the whole population, tourist and visitors of more than the four partner municipalities. Tourist business and tour operators and Tourist Service Providers outside the CB region. Local, regional and national authorities will also benefit from developed research and analysis, but also by achieving objectives from strategy plans. 
The approach in the implementation of this project we plan to take is holistic, multi-sectoral, more results-oriented, ecosystem-based. 
To achieve our objectives of a large-scale flagship project contributing to a wider impact on the entire cross-border (CB) area, we need to activate a broad multi-sectoral partnership at supranational level. In addition, this way of cooperation achieves a balanced territorial CB development, i.e. unifying the standards of offered services, the equal start of employees in supported sectors and access to equal digital, green and sustainable general solutions.
CB cooperation is also a key element of the European neighbourhood policy, for which BalkanVelo project carefully and in detail directs actions to the needs through a comprehensive and effective approach. Joint cross-border activities develop integrated CB labor markets, improve employment prospects, contribute to openness to the world and strengthen European citizenship. 
The development of new, attractive infrastructure strengthens socio-economic cooperation and enhances cultural exchange, while at the same time enabling creation of common services that will benefit the citizens and visitors of our CB space. And etc. 
The new and original about the project is mainly the pilot activity. It is combination of social tourism along the completed and newly designed routes for alternative mobility for disadvantaged people incl. of disabled and marketing on e-wheels, for improvement the area attractiveness. It leads to underpin the branding and marketing strategy and disseminate project ideas, activities and results over a long horizon and after the project end.

titleEn: Integration of Creative, Digit, Green and Eco Tourism for sustainable development of territories and communities in Kresna, Strumyani and Vasilevo
summaryEn:
Tourism is the sector with the greatest economic impact on the cross-border region. The implementation of focused support for its development in the municipalities of Kresna, Strumyani and Vasilevo will contribute to the overall development of cross-border tourism, will strengthen business relations in the region and opportunities to attract foreign investments.
Improving the business environment in the three municipalities will lead to sustainable economic growth, new jobs and prospects for the local population.
This will have a positive impact on the demographic processes in rural areas, creating conditions for the young generation and the population of working age for professional realization and development in their native places.
The current project idea aims and is focused specifically on the use of the potential of the local population, the cultural-historical and natural resources of the municipalities of Kresna, Strumyani and Vasilevo in order to create and develop attractive and all-season tourist products and services that distinguish them and give them a competitive advantage in the tourist market and have the potential for development and expansion of the territorial scope to neighboring cross-border territories and at the international level.
Integrated solutions will be implemented to deploy and develop the local potential of the municipalities of Kresna, Strumyani and Vasilevo, through focused actions in the following directions:


1.Improving socio-economic conditions for sustainable growth through investments in infrastructure providing a competitive advantage for the development of cultural and eco-tourism


2.Bringing together the potential of local communities and territories to create attractive all-season tourist destinations through intelligent solutions, creativity and a multi-sectoral approach of action


3.Implementation of digital and green solutions to improve the business environment and employment opportunities in tourism


4.Positioning of Kresna, Strumyani and Vasilevo as an attractive all-season tourist destination in the cross-border region
The House of Culture in the Vasilevo municipality, and a tourist base converted into the Sinanitsa Eco Center in the Kresna municipality will be rehabilitated. These investments will contribute to strengthening the links between culture-nature-environment and tourism.
Two integrated tourist routes will be developed with the potential for their development on a cross-border and international level, which will be pilot tested by tourists attracted through large-scale advertising campaigns and participants from both sides of the border.
– Tourist route "In the footsteps of Miss Stone" covering the municipality of Vasilevo, but with potential for development at the cross-border level given the common history covering the territory of many municipalities on both sides of the border in the cross-border region.
- Tourist route "In the Lands of the Keratsuda", covering the municipalities of Kresna and Strumyani - the lands of the wine grape variety "Keratsuda", which grows only on part of the territory of the two municipalities, but with potential for development at a cross-border level as part of the created opportunities for wine tourism in the region.
The local population will participate in the processes from the actual creation of the tourist packages to their actual offering on the tourist market. By including them as suppliers of products and services for the needs of the routes, we will contribute to creating a short supply chain and create added value to the destinations.
A partnership forum and a cross-border youth eco-camp "Friends of Pirin" will be held at the Sinanitsa Eco Center, and a 360° virtual tour will present it online.
Creation of a digital database for the sights of Vasilevo municipality and published on the e-TourGuide app.
Training for Creating Digital Stories for Local Tourism is a key activity and pilot for the cross-border territory. Representatives of the local communities will be trained for the so-called STORYDOERS (good practice of "Erasmus+" program), the aim of which is to promote the skills of responsible tourism and digitization of people of local communities - aspiring local entrepreneurs, artisans, creators, storytellers, tour guides who lack the necessary skills to create digital stories that present history in an appropriate way online.
The created partnerships and networking will contribute to the development of the destinations and their inclusion in regional, national routes offered in the international tourist markets.
Pilot training of STORYDOERS is a new approach which, if successful, will be implemented in other territories. Another original solution is the involvement of the local community in the entire process of creating the two tourist routes, thereby creating a practically short supply chain of goods, products and services for the tourist route.

titleEn: The Future is Green!
summaryEn:
Medgidia and Dobrich face several common territorial challenges in the environmental field. Some of the key challenges are: decline in biodiversity and insufficient conservation of nature, water pollution and air quality - a problem frequently encountered in the big cities , waste management - still far from being correctly implemented at the local level, infrastructure development - the development of gray infrastructure was a priority of local authorities, to the detriment of green and blue infrastructure, environmental problems - unknown to their true dimension.

Both used to be important industrial cities during communism period. Accelerated industrial development, without the imposition of strict environmental protection rules, the horizontal expansion of heavy industry investments, affected large areas of land, irreversibly destroying the local flora and fauna. The reduction of industrial activity after the fall of communism left behind degraded, unused lands.Even after more than 30 years since the communism fell, the 2 cities could not cancel the negative effects of industrialization and the rapid expansion of built-up areas.

Now, Medgidia has 40 ha of green area, respectively 9,30 sqm per inhabitant, which is much lower than the minimum threshold imposed by law - 26 sqm / inhabitant. Dobrich has 246,61 ha of landscaping, parks and gardens (most of them poorly maintained), respectively 31,11 sqm per inhabitant, being in European average for green areas, but let's don't forget that WHO recommends 50 sqm/ inhabitant.

Starting from these considerations and from the need for sustainable development, sharing the same principles and values ​​of respect for the community, the 2 municipalities have established as a common obj. increasing the quality of life of the residents in cross-border area by implementing actions to enhance the protection and preservation of nature, biodiversity and green infrastructure in urban areas, reducing all forms of pollution. 

Almost 100,000 people residing in the Medgidia - Dobrich cross-border area will have access to over 6 ha of improved green infrastructure.

By investing in green spaces, Dobrich proposes the modernization of 8 areas located in different part of the city, while Medgidia proposes the rehabilitation and modernization of park 1 Mai, the main park of the municipality.

The investment in the 1 Mai park in Medgidia has the potential to represent an essential landmark in the city's urban landscape, being one of the most important green spaces in town. The investment is relevant in the context of a low percentage of green space per inhabitant in the municipality, of the desire to offer residents quality services supporting social cohesion, well-being and health (a continuous objective for the last two FESI programming periods), but also of the accentuation of urban climatic discomfort phenomena. With an area of 81,552 m2, the park benefits from a strategic positioning in the immediate vicinity of the Danube-Black Sea Canal, which represents the main green-blue axis of the locality, constituting a valuable resource for the local community and the surrounding environment.

The park will be unique in the area, both through the spectacular architectural and landscape concept, using exclusively environmentally friendly materials, as well as through the numerous points of interest designed to intertwine the need for relaxation, meditation and break from stressful everyday life, with the need to walk in the open air, but also with the educational side. In the park, an Educational route was created to the Future Smart House (a pilot house - a model of energy independence that will become a pilot action): Noxious Plants Pavilion, Creative Recycling Area, Interactive Weather Station, Composting and Bird Watching Area, Renewable Energy Exhibit, Climate Change Simulation Touch Screen, Bicycles for Power Generation.

Through the involvement and empowerment of the community, various pilot actions and solutions will be implemented jointly with Dobrich, all the results of the project being able to be easily taken over by other organizations: the rehabilitation of 2 degraded areas following a competition for solutions offered by civil society, Lover's wall, Green police, Nature based expo, contest on environmental thematic.

The investment proposed by Medgidia in FiG is part of a larger project that was divided into 2 components submitted for financing under INTERREG VI-a (Medgidia-Dobrich component and Balchik-Medgidia component). Although the 2 components can be implemented separately, their simultaneous financing will contribute much faster to the improvement of the man-nature tandem, will really highlight the originality of the whole concept of the park and the activities, becoming emblematic not only for the community, but also for the financing program.
From general estimate the non-eligible expenditure is 12.521.831,84 lei/ 2.533.757,96 euro.

titleEn: Urban Climate Adaptation and Recovery Efforts through Green Infrastructure in Black Sea Basin
summaryEn:
The project is focusing on enhancing the joint efforts in supporting sustainable development and resilience of cities from Moldova, Romania and Greece in their attempts to introduce modern and smart approaches to creating resilient communities applying climate change mitigation and adaptation. The targeted cities face significant environmental challenges, particularly in urban areas. Rapid urbanization has led to the degradation of green spaces, adversely impacting biodiversity, air quality and residents' well-being. Climate changes exacerbates these issues, making urban areas more vulnerable to extreme weather events and reducing their resilience. Restoring urban parks and green spaces is critical for improving climate resilience, enhancing urban biodiversity, and building sustainable urban environments.
Involving 4 Project Partners (PPs), 3 Local Public Authorities (Ungheni City Hall, MD, Municipality of Tulcea, RO and Municipality of Thermi, GRC) and one Civil Society Organization (Regional Centre of Sustainable Development, MD), the action will address common challenges that are to be solved by the joint efforts of PPs and exchange and introduction of the best practices to make the Black Sea Basin (BSB) region resilient and attractive.
The primary objective of the project is to restore urban green areas in the PPs countries, thereby enhancing climate resilience and promoting sustainable urban living. By undertaking comprehensive restoration actions, the project aims to transform degraded urban parks into thriving green spaces that can withstand climate impacts and provide environmental, social and economic benefits to urban communities. 
The project will be oriented towards restoring actions of the three urban parks through restoring the greenery, pruning, planting and sustainable landscaping practices which will help maintain biodiversity and also ensuring the park's resilience to climate change impacts. Restoration efforts will focus on repairing and upgrading pathways, creation of bicycle lanes, recreational facilities to enhance accessibility and safety. The materials used during the parks design will be eco-friendly and natural. Implementing sustainable water management practices, such as rainwater harvesting will ensure efficient resource utilization while minimizing environmental impacts. These management strategies ewill mitigate erosion, enhance soil stability, and promote water infiltration, thereby safeguarding the park's long-term ecological health.
The project will develop a suite of outputs tailored to address the multifaceted challenges confronting urban green spaces. Implementing targeted restoration activities to rehabilitate degraded urban parks, including habitat restoration, infrastructure improvements, and community engagement initiatives. Conducting comprehensive inventories and mapping exercises to document the diversity of plant species within urban green areas, facilitating informed decision-making and conservation efforts.
Facilitating knowledge exchange and capacity building among stakeholders through exchanges of experience and peer learning activities within the created Green Deal network, thereby disseminating best practices in urban park management and restoration. Organizing educational campaigns, seminars, and outreach events targeting youth to raise awareness about the importance of urban green spaces, climate change mitigation, and sustainable urban planning. 
The beneficiaries of these outputs encompass a wide spectrum of stakeholders, including local governments, urban planners, environmental NGOs, community groups, youth organizations, academia, and the general public. By enhancing the quality and resilience of urban green spaces, the project will directly benefit urban residents by providing them with access to healthier, greener, and more livable urban environments. Developing an online platform offering educational resources, tools, and guidelines for climate-responsive urban planning, accessible to municipal planners, policymakers, and stakeholders.
Transnational cooperation is essential for addressing the shared environmental challenges faced by the Black Sea Basin countries. By collaborating, Moldova, Romania, and Greece will: 
-	Share knowledge, experiences and best practices, enhancing the effectiveness and sustainability of urban park restoration efforts.
-	Create scalable models of urban green areas restoration and climate resilience that can be replicated across the region and beyond.
-	Foster a sense of regional solidarity and joint commitment to tackling climate change and promoting sustainable urban development
The project is expected to significantly improve the quality and accessibility of urban green spaces in the participating cities creating green and clean BSB communities.

titleEn: Assessing the Vulnerability of the Black Sea Marine Ecosystem to Human Pressures - Promoting Collaboration with Business, Governance, and Citizens for a Sustainable Blue Region
summaryEn: The Black Sea marine ecosystem faces significant challenges due to human activities such as nutrient introduction causing eutrophication, pollution from contaminants, non-indigenous species, overfishing, and habitat destruction, all intensified by climate change. These pressures threaten biodiversity, ecosystem services, and the livelihoods of communities dependent on the sea. Effective and sustainable management is particularly crucial given the recent impacts of the Ukraine war. Despite the economic significance of sectors like transport, shipbuilding, oil and gas exploitation, fisheries, aquaculture, and tourism, there is an urgent need for environmental sustainability improvement. Disparities in research and innovation between riparian countries further exacerbate these challenges, highlighting the need for digitalization and sustainability measures to promote local innovation, stakeholder engagement, and technological progress for a smart and sustainable blue economy. The primary objective of ANEMONE PLUS is to enhance the resilience and sustainability of the Black Sea marine ecosystem by improving the assessment of its vulnerability to human and climate pressures. This will be achieved by advancing collaboration among scientists, businesses, governance bodies, and citizens to develop and translate research findings into practical tools. The expected change is a transformed approach to addressing marine environmental challenges in the Black Sea region, characterized by improved stakeholder engagement, informed decision-making bodies, and the adoption of advanced technologies and sustainable practices, leading to a more competitive, innovative, and environmentally friendly economic landscape. ANEMONE PLUS will develop a comprehensive database categorizing key stakeholders within the Black Sea region and establish a structured framework for ongoing collaboration between organizations in different countries. This framework will facilitate the integration and applicability of research findings across borders, promoting regional cooperation. A series of workshops will be organized to refine the project's outputs based on stakeholder feedback, including advisory groups meeting for the Black Sea Commission, ensuring they are practical and meet real-world needs. Collaborative studies involving multiple research organizations from four riparian Black Sea countries (Bulgaria, Romania, Türkiye and Ukraine) will be launched to address common environmental challenges. ANEMONE PLUS will develop a suite of tools to enhance biodiversity assessment, pollution monitoring, and environmental management. These tools will be based on advanced methodologies such as underwater cameras, eDNA barcoding, remote sensing technologies, passive samplers, passive acoustics, machine learning and modelling. Comprehensive guidelines and best practices for environmental management will be created, providing actionable recommendations for policymakers, businesses, and community groups. To ensure accessibility for non-specialists, ANEMONE PLUS will package these tools in user-friendly formats (WebGIS), with intuitive interface and comprehensive user manuals. Training sessions will be conducted to familiarize scientists with the new tools and methodologies. A detailed dissemination plan will maximize the impact of ANEMONE PLUS findings, including presentations at conferences, publications in scientific journals, and digital media outreach. This strategic approach ensures that research content is relevant and applicable to end-users, with comprehensive dissemination and scaling activities maximizing the impact and sustainability of the project's outcomes. Transnational cooperation is essential for the success of ANEMONE PLUS due to the shared nature of the Black Sea ecosystem and the interconnected challenges faced by riparian countries. By aligning strategies and increasing regional expertise in the Black Sea Commission, the project can address disparities in research and innovation capacities, promote technological advancements, and ensure the widespread adoption of sustainable practices. Moreover, by aligning with Horizon Europe projects, ANEMONE PLUS ensures synergies that amplify the impact of marine conservation initiatives, using shared knowledge and resources to achieve a healthier, more resilient Black Sea ecosystem. This coordinated approach maximizes the effectiveness of each project and enhances a comprehensive and unified strategy for marine environmental protection and sustainable development.

titleEn: Strengthening and Promoting Earthquake Emergency Response and Rescue Capacity in the BSB Area
summaryEn:
The project SPEER-A will be implemented by the research institutes Natural Hazards Research Center (RO) & Assen Zlatarov University (BG) along with the local authorities Bolu Disaster and Emergency Management Directorate (TR) and Municipality of Pella (GR). It aims to answer a question in active and not theoretical way: how can the local authorities and the research community of the Black Sea Basin area contribute to the better preparedness for an earthquake disaster? 

The project idea came up after the recent paralyzing earthquakes in Febr.2023 in Turkey. The partners agreed that the better preparedness for an earthquake in the Black Sea Basin area is a common territorial challenge that is worth working for and collaborating.

The overall objective of the project is to strengthen and promote the response to earthquake emergencies and the rescue capacity in the Black Sea Basin area, with advanced preparedness and resilience against earthquakes ‘disasters by 


1.Improving cooperation & knowledge exchange between stakeholders in an earthquake emergency response, and building stronger cross-border cooperation and collaboration;


2.Enhancing capacity of disaster risk management through the pilot use of new technologies.
