In order to achieve the 1st objective, the four partners will implement participatory activities that will contribute to the cultivation of strong bonds between them but also with the community. Training for the rescue teams, support of the volunteers network, education of children at schools will take place in the Black Sea Basin area, in the four countries. The local authorities will be the main actors, but the research institutes will also contribute to this axis. The training material will be decided jointly, part of it will be common for the partners while some training will be jointly implemented via e-technologies.

In order to achieve the 2nd objective, the joint development, implementation, testing and evaluation of three pilot actions will take place. New "instruments" are going to be produced for improving readiness against earthquakes. The Natural Hazards Research Center will develop an innovative virtual reality laboratory in order to represent the hazard framework of earthquakes (including other hazards that are inevitably related to it, such as landslides, floodings etc) and provide the decision makers with an improved perception of the parameters of the phenomenon in a territorial perspective.The interaction among the conditioning factors of hazards, exposure and vulnerability will make evident the fields of action.
The University of Burgas will develop an innovative mobile application that will target the general public,the rescue teams, the volunteers and the students. Its functions will be split to two: "online use" and "offline use".The "online use" will include (a) Emergency Preparedness Guides, (b) educational material for children and (c) will support the community of volunteers with the creation of a network of volunteers from the participating countries.The "offline use" will be developed like an "emergency info kit" in cases of earthquakes with no internet access.It will give the instruction of what to do within the next minutes of an earthquake and the first days. 
An original research will be developed by PB3, for the design of a new residential unit that has host people after an emergency situation such as an earthquake.This design will take into account the different aspects of the BSB area (climate conditions, social characteristics etc) and will properly entriched, as thematic workshops will be organized by all partners that will participate in the process.The final outcome will be an adjustable proposal for an emergency residential unit of the BSB area. 
These three pilot actions will be tested and evaluated by all partners. 

The project will result to the consitution of a network of 4 organizations in the Black Sea Basin area, along with the adoptation/scale-up of the pilot actions by insitutes of the region. 

The benefit will be for the total population of the four countries.The specific target groups are decision/policy makers, research insitutes,rescue teams,volunteers and school students. 

The transnational cooperation is needed because:
-Earthquakes are a natural phenomeno that can affect two or more countries at the same time. This means that especially countries that are close to each other (neighbouring countries) should create a strong network that be be activated in cases of emergencies. 
-For better coordination between different countries in an issue so important like this, a common ground is needed. Time is precious and the decisions must be taken very quickly. That's why, the actors must have the same level of information and perception of the various data. The pilot actions offer a concrete solution on this. 
-The networking of the volunteers and joint training of the rescue teams can support the sense of a transnational community.

titleEn: Smart Local Services for a Sustainable Future
summaryEn:
The eLocal project aims to address several common challenges within the Black Sea region, including the need for digital transformation, improved public and municipal service efficiency, and enhanced civic engagement. The region faces disparities in digital literacy, outdated technological infrastructure, and limited citizen participation in local governance. These issues hinder the delivery of efficient public services and the overall inclusivity and sustainability of municipal operations.

The overall objective of the eLocal project is to enhance the efficiency, inclusivity, and sustainability of public services in Lüleburgaz (Türkiye), Tomai (Moldova), and Targovishte (Bulgaria) through the implementation of innovative digital solutions, capacity building, and strategic planning. The project aims to create a significant shift from the current situation by modernizing digital infrastructure, increasing digital literacy, and fostering greater civic engagement. This will lead to improved public service delivery, reduced environmental impact, and a more inclusive and participatory governance model.

The primary beneficiaries of the project are local authorities, particularly, Lüleburgaz Subgovernorship, Tomai Municipality, and Targovishte Municipality, and their staff by improving digital infrastructure and enhanced capacity. The final and secondary beneficiaries are the citizens of these three cities, who will experience better public services, increased opportunities for civic engagement, and improved environmental conditions.

Main Outputs and Results:


1. Development of Digital Infrastructure: 
 Luleburgaz: 
	Modernizing technological infrastructure to improve public service quality.
	Development of smart waste management system for the villages of Luleburgaz.
	Development of an APP to encourage public involvement to engage citizens to the management of city. 
Targovishte:
	Implementing a Geographic Information System (GIS) for better management and decision-making.
	Personalized Mobile Notifications and Expanded Administrative Services:
	Advanced Document Management System:
	Development of an APP to encourage public involvement to engage citizens to the management of city. 
Tomai:
	Upgrading digital systems for enhanced municipal services.
	Installation of advanced digital security system to the public spaces
	Development of an APP to encourage public involvement to engage citizens to the management of city. 


2. Digital Literacy and Capacity Building:
 - Training of at least 75 public officers in digital skills, including AI applications in three cities.
 - Conducting digital literacy seminars to engage at least 150 citizens in three cities.


3. Strategic Planning for Digital Transition: Developing digital transition strategies tailored to each municipality to ensure long-term sustainability and continuous improvement.

Transnational cooperation is crucial for the success of this project due to the following reasons:
-Shared Challenges: The municipalities in Türkiye, Moldova, and Bulgaria face similar challenges in digital transformation and public service delivery. Collaborative efforts will allow them to share experiences and solutions that are effective across different contexts.
- Resource Optimization: By pooling resources and expertise, the project partners can achieve greater efficiency and impact than if they acted independently.
- Innovation and Knowledge Exchange: Transnational cooperation facilitates the exchange of innovative ideas and best practices, helping each municipality to implement the most effective solutions.
- Harmonized Standards: Working together will ensure that the digital solutions and strategies developed are compatible and can be scaled across the region, promoting regional integration and coherence.

Through this collaborative and integrated approach, the eLocal project aims to create a lasting positive impact on public service delivery, civic engagement, and environmental sustainability in the Black Sea region.

titleEn: Black Sea Unites Against Natural Disasters
summaryEn:
Disaster is defined by the United Nations as "all kinds of natural, technological or human-induced events that cause physical, economic and social losses for people, affect societies by stopping or interrupting normal life, and cannot be coped with by local means." Disasters cause loss of life, injuries, diseases and property losses, and their negative effects on social and economic life can continue for many years.

The effects of disasters can be very large-scale and devastating. At the same time, the process requires preparation for different periods, including before, during and after the disaster. For this reason, it is not always possible for countries to act alone in the field of disaster management, and it also creates various difficulties. Nowadays, international aid calls are made by countries in major disasters. This situation creates the need to approach the issue from an international perspective in the field of disaster management. For this reason, it has been concluded that approaching the issue by centering international cooperation in the field of disaster management will be an effective solution.

The general aim of our project is to ensure permanent and sustainable collaborations through national and international activities to be carried out in Turkey, Bulgaria and Greece, to develop the capacities of public-academic and non-governmental organizations in the field of disaster management, to make mutual knowledge and good practice transfers and to support the disaster-related civil initiative in the Black Sea region to contribute to the strengthening of the region.

One of the most effective methods to reduce the negative effects of disasters is pre-disaster preparation. In addition to having the necessary technological equipment, having sufficient awareness and awareness of human resources capacity also plays a critical role in reducing the negative effects of disasters. In this context, our project will approach the issue with a multidisciplinary approach and aims to both improve the service capacity of relevant institutions and increase the level of consciousness and awareness of citizens living in the relevant regions against natural disasters.

The project includes directly relevant institutions from countries that are included in the Black Sea Basin Cross-Border Cooperation Program and are vulnerable to disaster risk. The institutions include a development agency, a municipality, a non-governmental organization and a university, and it is aimed to develop common solutions in combating disasters by trying to bring together different perspectives of different institutions.

The lead partner of the project, Trakya Development Agency, operates in the provinces of Tekirdağ, Edirne and Kırklareli as one of Turkey's 26 Development Agencies. In Turkey's National Earthquake Strategy and Action Plan, Development Agencies are given the responsibility to take into account earthquake hazards and risks within their areas of responsibility and to carry out activities that will not increase or will decrease the risks. Due to this responsibility, Trakya Development Agency, operating in Tekirdağ, which is located in the first degree earthquake zone, felt the need to lead a project of this nature in the field of disaster management. Tekirdağ Metropolitan Municipality, which is among our project partners, is the only metropolitan municipality of the Thrace region. The Municipality's Earthquake Risk Management and Urban Improvement Department has active work in the field of disasters, especially earthquakes, and the institution has an accredited search and rescue team consisting of 135 people. Varna Free University is located in the Bulgarian leg of our project. The security and safety department of this university carries out both academic and project-based studies on disasters. Hellenic Rescue Team, the representative of our project in Greece, is a non-governmental organization that specializes in search and rescue activities and is very experienced in international disaster response practices. Contribution to the goal of the disaster-resistant Black Sea Region will be made by carrying out and developing studies together with the synergy to be created between these institutions for disaster management.

In order to increase the resilience of the Black Sea to disasters, disaster awareness trainings, visits to an exemplary disaster training center, increasing the equipment and hardware quality of search and rescue teams, disaster awareness activities for students in schools and citizens in public areas, international experience sharing meetings for both professional and volunteer disaster management workers, the creation of suggestions for policy makers regarding the problems they experience for the effectiveness of non-governmental organizations operating in the field of disasters are among the activities of the project.

titleEn: Interregional Cooperation for Adaptation to Climate in Agriculture
summaryEn:
The ADAPTAGRI is a collaborative initiative aimed at addressing the common challenge of enhancing resilience in agriculture and mitigating the impact of climate change in the programme area, which includes Turkiye, Greece, and Bulgaria. These countries face various challenges such as decreasing precipitation, water scarcity, longer droughts and heatwaves etc. in their agricultural sectors caused by climate change.

The project focuses on smart and green production techniques in field crop agriculture to increase resilience and adapt to climate change. The geographical focus of practical activities is the regions where three of the partners operate, i.e. Thrace region of Turkey (Tekirdağ, Kırklareli and Edirne), Evros region of Greece, and Dobrudzha region of Bulgaria. On the other hand, the project will enlarge its impact field to the whole of BSB through various activities.
The overall objective of the ADAPTAGRI project is to develop and implement innovative solutions that promote smart and green practices in field crop agriculture, leading to sustainable and resilient food production systems. The project seeks to bring about a significant change in the current situation by improving environmental sustainability while enhancing the sustainability in agriculture. 

To achieve these objectives, ADAPTAGRI will deliver a range of outputs and results. These include the establishment of the BSB Platform for Smart and Green Recovery in Agriculture, which will serve as a collaborative space for stakeholders from the partnering and other countries to come together, exchange knowledge, and share experiences.

The project will conduct comprehensive research and analyses to provide insights into the current situation, identify needs and challenges, and explore best practices in the field of smart and green practices in field crop agriculture. This will involve literature reviews, assessments of the existing conditions, and identification of successful case studies and best practices.

Based on the research findings, the project will work on analyzing research and data to influence policy-making processes. It will contribute to the development of local and national policy proposals that align with the principles of smart and green agriculture. Collaborative action plans will also be developed at regional and interregional scales.
ADAPTAGRI will establish a comprehensive database of funding sources related to smart and green agriculture, providing information on available funding opportunities, grants, and support programs. The project will organize webinars and events to disseminate information and facilitate access to funding opportunities. The lead partner, Trakyaka, will also develop financial and technical support programs to be implemented in its region, which are expected to serve as a model practice in the field.

The project will develop informational materials, including digital brochures highlighting sustainable farming practices and smart technologies in field crop production. An informational video focused on smart and green field crop production will be produced to reach a wider audience.

To enhance capacity and knowledge exchange, the project will organize technical training programs for farmers, agricultural professionals, and stakeholders. A joint network of mentors will be established to provide guidance and support to farmers throughout the project area. Through these outputs and activities, ADAPTAGRI will benefit a wide range of stakeholders, including farmers, agricultural professionals, policymakers, researchers, and local communities. 

The project's transnational cooperation is essential for its success as it is established based on complementary sectoral aspect and brings diverse perspectives, expertise from different countries. This transnational cooperation will foster cross-border collaboration to support climate change adaptation and resilince in agriculture, accelerate the adoption of smart and green agricultural practices, and contribute to the development of a resilient and productive agricultural sector in BSB, starting from Turkiye, Greece, and Bulgaria.

titleEn: Quadruple Helix-Based Enhancement of Stakeholders at Black Sea Territory
summaryEn:
The project, under the Interreg VI-B NEXT Black Sea Basin Programme, addresses significant common challenges in the Black Sea Basin (BSB) region by enhancing the institutional capacity of various stakeholders to access available funds and apply for calls for projects, particularly those linked to the blue economy. The BSB region is of strategic and economic importance but faces several multifaceted challenges that hinder its development and integration. The Territorial Analysis (TA) published in November 2020 highlights these challenges and emphasizes the need for better collaborative governance. The project aims to transform institutional capabilities, making the cooperation in the area more effective and sustainable by leveraging the quadruple helix approach, which involves the collaboration of universities, businesses, civil society, and public sector organizations.

The overall project objective is to improve the capacity of stakeholders in partner countries to access open funds and apply for projects related to the blue economy. This objective will be achieved through several planned actions designed to enhance institutional capacities and establish sustainable partnerships. By addressing the challenges identified in the TA, such as the low level of involvement of public authorities in projects, the lack of resources for implementing cooperation initiatives, and the organizational focus of NGOs, the project seeks to create a more inclusive and effective framework for cross-border cooperation.

The expected change from this project includes a significant increase in the number of institutions from the BSB region applying for and receiving international funds. By enhancing the skills and knowledge of stakeholders, the project will help overcome barriers such as insufficient project preparation and implementation capacity, lack of human resources, and inadequate networking opportunities. The project will also foster a collaborative environment that encourages the sharing of resources and best practices among different types of organizations.

The main outputs of the project will include a series of capacity-building activities, training sessions, consultancy services, and the establishment of the Grant Gate Portal. These activities will target a wide range of stakeholders, including national, regional, and local public authorities, higher education and research institutions, NGOs, business support organizations, and others. By integrating stakeholders into the quadruple helix structure, the project will create clusters that facilitate knowledge sharing, innovation, and sustainable cooperation.

The Grant Gate Portal will be a crucial tool for sustaining the project's impact, providing stakeholders with access to information on available funds and potential project partners. It will streamline the project preparation process, saving time and effort, and addressing the significant barrier of networking deficiencies. Additionally, the project will organize the Black Sea MetaExpo, a virtual platform that will enable stakeholders to form international consortia and collaborate on project proposals in the metaverse.

Transnational cooperation is essential for this project as the challenges faced by the BSB region are too complex to be addressed by individual efforts. The project will foster cooperation between institutions across the region, creating a unified approach to tackling common issues. The collaborative governance model promoted by the project will ensure that knowledge and resources are shared effectively, leading to more successful project outcomes.

titleEn: RAISING AWARENESS FOR THE BLACK SEA PEOPLE TO RECOGNIZE AND PROTECT BLACK SEA BIODIVERSITY
summaryEn:
The idea of the project may hide in this pharese "if you introduce you know, if you know you protect". 

Biodiversity in the Black Sea faces threats such as overfishing, introduction of alien species, habitat destruction, ghost fishing, by-catch, climate change, marine litter, pollution, and overexploitation of natural resources. These anthropogenic threats require collaborative efforts from governments, organizations and individuals to develop and implement effective protection strategies. 
The overall objective of the project is to raise public awareness and protect the biodiversity of the Black Sea by introducing local, alien, endangered, and extinct species in the Black Sea basin to stakeholders in Romania, Bulgaria and Türkiye. Selected stakeholders of this project are fishermen, divers, students, youth, Coast Guard, local administrators, etc. In order to inform the marine organisms (from plankton to marine mammals) in the food chain to the Black Sea inhabitants, 3D printed marine organisms, t-shirts, sea survey, underwater images and videos, e-booklet about Black Sea organisms, posters, etc. will be used. The reasons behind the extinction and threat of species in the Black Sea will be effectively communicated and evaluated to all stakeholders, both in the field and with 3D-printed marine organisms (miniatures). Workshops, meetings, and seminars will be held with all these stakeholders to protect these species. Stakeholders will work on how to take measures to protect these species and the importance of protected areas for biodiversity will be stated. 
In addition, an application within project website will be designed with partners' opinion on biodiversity in the Black Sea to support the Citizens Science. This application, called BLACKPYRAMID (included digital map), will raise citizen’s awareness of the species living in the Black Sea ecosystem, ensure their protection and sustainability. The BLACKPYRAMID will serve as an interconnection between citizen and webbase archive to quick response together with public participations. For example, fishermen, divers, or other citizens will be able upload to the application images of alien species, stranded dolphins, endangered species, etc, from their mobile phones. Detailed information on the distribution of these species will also be collected with data from Turkey, Bulgaria and Romania. 
The main outputs that will occur from the project as a result of the common opinion and cooperation of the partners are;
- 3D printed marine organisms in the Black Sea will be exhibited on a food pyramid and will be opened to all stakeholders and will be used as educational materials in workshops and meetings.
- Citizen Science "BLACKPYRAMID" application will be created to help the protection of the Black Sea biodiversity.
- An e-booklet containing information about selected native, invasive alien, endangered and extinct species in the Black Sea will be prepared, 
- Banners, posters and t-shirts consisting of endangered species will be distributed to citizens during the trainings to increase public awareness in the Black Sea.
 - On the project website, there will be a dropdown menu called "FOOD WEB" will be demonstrated of the Black Sea native, alien, and endangered species introduced in details together with their photographs.
- The past and previous information about partners' coastal biodiversity will be prepared as a nation reports to demonstrate the present situation, gaps, and main threats. 
- Local workshops and meetings will be held to disseminate information about Black Sea biodiversity.
- Transnational collaboration in each partner country in the events such as field studies (sea surveys) and workshops. In the sea surveys, fishing practices (planktons, invertebrates and fishes) and the impact of fishing gear on biodiversity will be explained. The participants (partners and stakeholders) will be able to see fish and other invertebrates through sampling with dredge and fish nets. They will also have the opportunity to see plankton through a microscope by using a plankton nets.
- A recommendation policy will be prepared for the relevant Ministry of each partner country about the protection of Black Sea biodiversity.
The protection of biodiversity in the Black Sea requires joint actions of the countries bordering the Black Sea. Issues such as migratory species, pollution, marine litter and alien species, and overexploitation of resources pose common threats to the biodiversity of the region. By working together, joint solutions can be sought to effectively address these common challenges. In order to protect the biodiversity of the Black Sea, a collaborative approach is essential to increase the awareness of the people living on the Black Sea coast.

titleEn: Capacity Building and Training for Public Sector Using Artificial Intelligence
summaryEn:
Common Challenge
The AI4Capacity project addresses a significant challenge faced by small and medium sized public organizations, particularly local authorities: the need for enhanced administrative capacities and efficient management frameworks. In the programme area, these organizations often struggle with limited resources, outdated administrative practices, and varying levels of governance efficiency. These challenges hinder their ability to effectively serve their communities and manage cross-border cooperation initiatives.

Overall Project Objective and Expected Change
The primary objective of AI4Capacity is to promote and implement capacity-building tools such as the Common Assessment Framework (CAF) (*) and Management by Objectives (MbO) (**) system within small and medium public organizations. By integrating an AI Suite, designed to support these frameworks, the project aims to modernize administrative processes, improve decision-making, and enhance the overall efficiency of public service delivery. The expected change is a significant improvement in the administrative capacities of local authorities, leading to more effective governance, increased transparency, and better service outcomes for the communities they serve.

Main outcomes:
- AI Suite: A tailored AI Suite will be developed to support the implementation of CAF and MbO. This tool will streamline administrative tasks, provide data-driven insights, and facilitate more efficient resource management.
- Training: A comprehensive training package will be created and delivered to 32 partners' staff members. This training will equip them with the skills needed to implement CAF and MbO effectively.
- Pilot Implementations: The project will conduct pilot implementations of CAF and MbO in four organizations, providing real-world testing and refinement opportunities.
- Assessment and Refinement: Post-pilot assessments will be conducted to refine the AI Suite based on user feedback and performance data.
- Expansion and Capitalization: The project will promote the reuse of knowledge and tools developed through regional demonstration events, training courses for 240 public servants, and individualized support for 40 public entities.
- EduLab Platform: An "EduLab" platform will be established, combining an Open Educational Resource (OER) with a Living Lab to support ongoing education and innovation in public administration.
- AI4Capacity Network: A transnational network will be created to ensure the durability and transferability of the project's outputs and results.

Beneficiaries:
The primary beneficiaries of the project are local public authorities. By enhancing their administrative capacity, they will be better equipped to manage resources and deliver public services. Additionally, higher education and research institutions will benefit from access to the EduLab platform and the data generated by the project, supporting academic research and professional development. Ultimately, the communities served by these authorities will benefit from improved governance and more efficient public services.

Planned Approach - Transnational Cooperation
AI4Capacity employs a collaborative approach, bringing together partners from GR, BG, and TR to develop, implement, and refine the project’s tools and methodologies. Transnational cooperation is essential for several reasons:
- Shared Expertise: Partners bring diverse experiences and expertise, enhancing the quality and relevance of the project’s outputs.
- Cross-Border Challenges: The administrative challenges faced by local authorities in the Black Sea region are similar across borders, necessitating a unified approach.
- Resource Efficiency: Collaborative efforts allow for the pooling of resources and knowledge, reducing duplication and increasing the project’s impact.

Innovative and Original Aspects:
The project’s innovative approach lies in its integration of AI technologies to support traditional management frameworks like CAF and MbO. By leveraging AI, the project introduces advanced data analytics and automation into public administration, a relatively new concept in the region. The creation of the EduLab platform and the establishment of the AI4Capacity Network are also novel, providing sustainable avenues for ongoing education, collaboration, and the dissemination of best practices.

After all the above, it is clear that this project is a significantly efficient investment in the project area



(*) CAF is a unique management tool for self-assessment and performance evaluation for public organisations. Developed and recognized by the EU, it is considered as the European quality tool for good governance and excellence in the public sector, with a focus on digitalisation, agility, sustainability, diversity and innovation.

(**) MbO is a strategic management model that aims to improve the performance of an organization by clearly defining objectives that are agreed to by both management and employees.

titleEn: Black Sea Initiative for Sturgeon Sustainability
summaryEn:
The BLISS project addresses critical environmental challenges in the Black Sea region, focusing on the conservation and sustainable management of sturgeon populations. The project's overarching objective is to protect and sustainably manage sturgeon populations through international cooperation, scientific research, monitoring and conservation activities. Key challenges include overfishing and illegal fishing, habitat degradation, pollution, climate change, genetic erosion, inadequate conservation policies and limited research data.
The project aims to enhance regulation and enforcement by strengthening legal frameworks and improving monitoring and enforcement mechanisms to combat illegal fishing. It will implement comprehensive monitoring programs using advanced technologies such as satellite telemetry, acoustic tags, genetic tagging and hydro-acoustic devices to track sturgeon migration patterns and behaviors. The project also focuses on addressing pollution sources and enhancing habitat connectivity through habitat suitability assessments and targeted restoration efforts. Public education and community engagement are key components, with workshops, seminars and public awareness campaigns designed to educate stakeholders about sturgeon conservation. Furthermore, the project will facilitate international cooperation and policy development by establishing an International Sturgeon Conservation Network to foster collaboration and harmonize conservation strategies.
The main outputs and results of the BLISS project include joint sturgeon monitoring programs, cross-border cooperation frameworks, public awareness campaigns, development of advanced sturgeon monitoring technologies, a comprehensive data management and sharing platform, mobile monitoring stations and action plan recommendations for sturgeon conservation. These outputs will benefit research institutions, local public authorities, NGOs, educational institutions, local communities, fishermen, policymakers and government agencies. The project ensures that its outputs are impactful and adaptable for other target groups and territories beyond the Black Sea region, promoting long-term conservation and sustainability efforts.
The project adopts a comprehensive and collaborative approach with joint development and implementation involving partners from the project's inception. Partners are engaged through consultations, workshops and meetings, ensuring their input shapes the project’s design, objectives, strategies and implementation plans. Activities are distributed among partners based on their expertise, ensuring a balanced and collaborative effort. Advanced monitoring programs, cross-border cooperation, public awareness campaigns, data management and sharing and policy development are key components of the project.
Transnational cooperation is essential for addressing transboundary challenges, harmonizing conservation policies, pooling resources and enhancing regional collaboration. Sturgeon populations migrate across international borders, making coordinated conservation efforts among Black Sea countries crucial. Transnational cooperation ensures harmonized policies and collaborative enforcement mechanisms, enhancing the quality and impact of conservation efforts. It fosters regional collaboration, leverages diverse perspectives and ensures long-term impact, promoting sustainable environmental practices in the Black Sea region.
The BLISS project will establish a comprehensive digital platform, including a website and data-sharing portal, serving as a central hub for information dissemination. Advanced data management and sharing systems will ensure that all collected data is available to researchers, policymakers and conservationists. The project will deploy mobile sturgeon monitoring stations equipped with advanced technologies, develop action plan recommendations based on project findings and create a repository of educational materials for public awareness campaigns. Formal agreements and established networks of organizations from Türkiye, Bulgaria, Romania and Ukraine will be documented and shared as best practices for fostering international cooperation. Workshops and training programs developed during the project will be documented and made available on the digital platform, enabling other organizations to replicate and customize them to fit their local contexts.

titleEn: Cross-Border Governance for Sustainable Development
summaryEn:
The Governance project endeavors to enhance social, economic, and environmental development in the Bulgaria-North Macedonia cross-border region, aligning with Priority 3 of the INTERREG VI-A IPA Bulgaria – North Macedonia 2021—2027 Programme. It confronts challenges by streamlining tasks within the Strategy Board (SB) to bolster decision-making and monitoring capabilities. Through the augmentation of SB capacity, the project strives to cultivate a self-sustaining milieu conducive to integrated territorial development.

The Project seeks to establish a robust structure capable of meeting future demands and identifying regional challenges proactively. By pursuing key strategic objectives delineated in the Territorial Strategy (TS), it contributes to sustainable economic development across the cross-border region. Embracing a localized and holistic approach, the project collaborates closely with local communities to address territorial disparities comprehensively. Through capacity-building initiatives within the Strategy Board (SB), the project nurtures collaboration and integration among stakeholders, imperative for effective cross-border implementation.

In essence, the project ensures direct benefits for partners, target groups, and the Programme area, accentuating cross-border cooperation to tackle shared challenges and foster regional development.

titleEn: Low-carbon InFinity Trail
summaryEn:
The main objective of the project “Low-Carbon InFinity Trail” (LIFT) is to unlock the region's tourism potential, drive sustainable economic growth and improve regional competitiveness of southern BG and MK CB region, based on streamline the utilization of the tourism resources and improve tourism marketing and branding practices, through development and test implementation of new approach for low carbon tourism, by developing and upscaling a pilot tourism product "Low-Carbon InFinity Trail" following the newest trends.
The project “Low-Carbon InFinity Trail (LIFT)” jointly tackles well-known territorial challenges which are still unresolved like unevenly developed conditions for year-round tourism across the CB area; underdeveloped year-round tourist infrastructure of the CBC area; underdeveloped tourism product as a whole, underdeveloped network of companies for services and offers in tourism, insufficiently qualified staff in the field of tourism services, poor condition and limited access to natural and cultural-historical heritage sites. CBC Programme BG – MK states that when economic pushbacks take place in a weak CB institutional context and the absence of carbon-free practices are further challenged to enhance the territorial cohesion in line with EU objectives (Territorial Agenda 2030; Green Deal). The overall underperformance of the CBC area is addressed by PO5 “Europe closer to citizens” measures which require integrated and multilevel governance responses in tourism and industry domains who are main driving forces behind the advanced course of territorial development. CBC Programme BG – MK identifies joint investment needs, and inter alia (i) Investments for integrated development of sustainable tourism practices and (ii) Investments in improving cross-border connectivity and mobility. Further challenges are related to poor marketing and branding of tourist routes and products and to their construction and maintenance
The current project is a pilot initiative for developing and promoting a new tourism product LIFT as a joint solution for increasing tourist attractiveness of the southern part of the cross border region of BG and MK in order to unlock the region's tourism potential, drive sustainable economic growth and improve regional competitiveness, based on streamline the utilization of the tourism resources and improve tourism marketing and branding practices. (RCO84 – RCO116 – RCR104). 
As a an output of the project in total 4,5 km length of dedicated cycling infrastructure will be newly built. Cycling path in village of Mikrevo, MoStr will be constructed with length of 

1.3 km, and 

3.2 km of separated peri urban cycling trails will be constructed in MoS. Both will be connected with the infinity off-road velo route. It is estimated that 500 of cyclists will use the newly built infrastructure. It will be measured one year after the project end with a field survey at a single point (Output indicatorRCO58 – RCR64)	
Another output of the project is that 1 cultural (H. Sintika/St. Petka Ch.) and 2 tourism sites (Kozhuh M. and Berovo lake) will be supported. The physical investments in Velo Hubs along the trail "LIFT" will offer a convenient resting place with facilities for cyclists, allowing them to refresh and address self repair needs. With the electrical tourist train 2 tourist sites in Petrich will be accessible for people with disabilities while offering low-carbon tourism services for 1 500 tourist yearly (one year after the project ends). (Output indicator RCO77 – RCR77)
112082 population from 4 municipalities (2 in BG, 2 in MK) will benefit directly from the project from local economic growth. Project creates new job opportunities & stimulates entrepreneurship. Bicycle friendly infrastructure creates excellent opportunities for greater inclusion of people with disabilities in CB connectivity & mobility. Population is positively affected by cleaner environment, alternative mobility, reduced air pollution & noise, and established stakeholders’ partnerships. (Output indicator RCO74).	
The current project cannot be developed and implemented without applying a cross-border approach. The reason for that is that tourist attractions cannot solely address the needs of an integrated tourism product and cannot covers the concept for low carbon tourism. The current project offers a solution (comprehensive Action Plan (AP) for low-carbon tourism development) as a pilot initiative for increasing tourist attractiveness of the southern part of the cross border area between Bulgaria and North Macedonia.

titleEn: Integrated development of distinctive cultural and close-to-nature tourism in East planning and Blagoevgrad region
CULTURAL AREA - CULTURAL heritage community and AttRactive all-sEAson tourism
summaryEn:
The challenge for the cross-border region is to use the connectivity of the CULTURAL AREA, to generate integrated actions, to exchange good practices and to develop a sustainable, attractive, all-season, and accessible tourism and increase in employment in the tourism sector.
The main objectives are (1) to raise the visibility, strengthen and upscale the good practices for the cooperation between the municipalities of Kyustendil, Dupnitsa, Kriva Palanka and Kratovo; (2) to use the cultural and natural heritage as a strategic factor for the sustainable development of tourism, by developing/upscaling cultural routes, building a common tourist product and increasing the employment in the tourism sector; (3) to foster integrated development through tourism marketing approaches; (4) to revitalize the urban and peri urban area through linking projects/events at cultural and natural heritage sites, as well as using the opportunities of the cultural and creative industries; (5) to conserve cultural heritage sites and implement digital technologies for virtualization (holograms/ 3D models/ VR and AR/gamification/ QR/ mobile applications/ digital platform with common cultural routes and a common cultural calendar/ online catalog on the connecting theme "Old houses tell stories") and for enriching the visitor experience and attract different audiences; (5) to use cultural heritage sites as spaces for culture as open museum spaces, open-air museum, co-working spaces as well as for cultural events will attract various tourists and stakeholders. 
The main initiatives that will show the joint efforts of the partner municipalities (in both renovated places or newly built under the project) are: (1) a three-day festival by the theme of “Everyday life of the region in the 19th century”; (2) connecting the specifics of local Balkan traditions and European influences and cultural traces on everyday life though the “A la franga” initiative – seen as a door to Europe, architecture, art decoration and values, old technologies, fashion, lifestyle, the path of modernity – commerce, education, etc.); (3) the Audience Monitoring Laboratory – a smart system solution for monitoring the visitors interest in the partners` museums and gathering data for culture monitoring purposes. 
The public importance of culture and heritage implies a shared responsibility not only regarding the preservation of cultural heritage, its memory, its socialization, and management, through its inclusion in the life of the community. Multisectoral interaction and the role of the local community, authorities, and institutions are of key importance not only for the implementation of initiatives aimed at the development of the cross-border region but also of particular importance for the sustainability of the results.

titleEn: Integrated crossborder tourism actions in Blagoevgrad-Delchevo region
summaryEn:
The main goal of the current project proposal is directed towards diversification of the supply of tourist services in the cross border area by developing an integrated tourist product in an attractive and nature-friendly way, thus stimulating local economy and quality of life in the Blagoevgrad -Delchevo region. The specific objectives are related to the following:


1. Improvement in the quality of services in the tourist sector by offering attractive products with potential to combine various sector activities for different target groups.


2. Effective utilization of the available natural resources of the cross border region by implementation of joint measures thus reducing costs and achieving long-term effects.


3. Turning the region Blagoevgrad-Delchevo in an attractive tourist destination by effective marketing activities and promotion on the tourist market.
The project will have significant contribution to utilization of the potential of resources in the tourism sector available in the cross-border area. The partners are aware of the fact that joint actions will have quicker and more lasting in time effect with regard to tackling challenges related to development of tourism. This is the reason why Blagoevgrad and Delchevo municipalities plan to implement common activities which will lead to expanding the potential of the tourist supply by creating a new integrated tourist product which will be actively promoted to get successful market realization. In addition the project envisages the development of marketing strategy including innovative digital solutions which will be used to promote the product in an attractive way.
The project brings together efforts for joint measures to expand and effectively manage the tourist supply in the cross-border region by means of diversification, creation of complex products with complementary activities and their active popularization, overcoming city boundaries. The proposal is a combination of investment component intended for creation of tourist sites as well as soft measures for their promotion and successful marketing. The integrated product which will be developed will not be limited only to the newly created tourist infrastructure though. The approach which will be applied suggests by means of development of concept for tourist product and marketing strategy to explore further opportunities to incorporate existing products and tourist routes from both sides of the border in the newly designed product in search for broader effects on local economies. The Blagoevgrad-Delchevo Region will receive its distinctive brand and logo for the first time through the implementation of the current project. The effective marketing strategy will explore the strong sides of the region as a whole and communicate it to the public in an attractive way. The Planetarium which will be constructed in the center of Blagoevgrad will be the first building of that kind not only in the city, but in the whole Blagoevgrad District and will have a hall equipped with modern technologies to provide knowledge for those interested in science. The activities in Delchevo mostly in the sphere of green tourism and sports will complement to these activities by creating conditions for positive attitude towards environment, increasing public awareness and providing infrastructure for activities in the open.
The project brings together efforts for joint measures to manage the tourist offer in the cross-border region. After the completion of the project, cooperation will be established between the responsible institutions in the field of tourism management and it will serve as a basis for further joint activities. The project activities will have a significant cross-border impact in promoting the sustainable management of tourism and available resources through the preparation of offers for tourism in which offers in addition to touristic infrastructure and opportunities will also be offered the potentials of the region for gastronomy, sports, education, culture and tradition promoting new measures and approaches for managing potentials and achieving a better quality of life in the CB region.

titleEn: Supporting a smarter & innovative Open Lab network in Euro-MED area
summaryEn: Sole MED aims to create a network of Open Labs across the Euro-Mediterranean region to support innovation, business growth, and training for young people. Inspired by a successful project in Italy, it will be adapted to other areas like Spain, Greece, and Bulgaria. These collaborative spaces will help new businesses and small companies through training, digital tools, and science and technology programs. A key part of the project is a Startup Creation Lab focused on the sustainable bioeconomy, offering young entrepreneurs hands-on training in business development, innovation, and eco-friendly practices.

titleEn: Transformation of Schoolyards to Combat Climate Change Effects and Promote Healthy and Active Environments
summaryEn:
The escalating effects of climate change pose significant threats to cities; in particular, heavy rainfall, flooding, rising extreme temperatures, and urban heat island effects significantly impact the urban environment, life quality, and health in the Mediterranean. The Re-Act Schools project addresses these challenges by focusing on climate change adaptation and risk prevention in school outdoor spaces. Schoolyards, especially in cities where public green living areas are limited, are valuable assets that offer unique opportunities to test and promote Nature-based and innovative technological solutions for climate change mitigation and adaptation capable to reduce the climate hazard. 

To achieve this goal, the project brings together a diverse and complementary partnership that comprises 2 research institutions, 5 public bodies, and a territorial development agency from 6 Mediterranean countries (Italy, Spain, France, Croatia, Bulgaria, and Cyprus), that will work together to transform 6 schoolyards through Pilot Actions into green, climate-resilient and innovative spaces that promote healthy and active lifestyles among students and the wider community, according to the goals of the New European Bauhaus and Green Deal Program. 

The testing activity will be accompanied by a capacity-building phase finalised to define an innovative design methodology to mitigate heat stress, manage water resources efficiently, enhance biodiversity, and offer climate shelters to the citizens in the Mediterranean urban context based on the use of ENVI-met microclimatic simulations and Digital Urban Climate Twin models to test advanced methods for analysing, designing, and monitoring climate-resilient schoolyards. 

The knowledge developed during the project will be collected in an innovative Action Plan and a multimedia tool to support the Public Administration of the Med Area in managing the regenerative transformation of schoolyards and public spaces.

titleEn: AQUAtic systems’ evaluation for the Mitigation of wAter scarcity in mediterranean islaNds and coastal tourist destinations under severe pressure
summaryEn:
Two facts. Agriculture accounts for 80% of water consumption in the Euro-MED region. The daily water consumption of a tourist is 2 to 4 times higher than that of a household.
AQUAMAN aims to reduce water scarcity by taking action on three levels: 1) Increasing the use of non-conventional water sources such as rainwater or wastewater; 2) Reducing water demand in the most consuming sectors; 3) Optimising local water distribution systems.
AQUAMAN will not solve the problem on its own. But it can engage many actors to do so with its knowledge of transferable successful EU projects. Its Water Scarcity Mitigation Living Labs based in 6 countries will promote them, along with training programmes.

titleEn: Advancing Green Infrastructure in Small and Medium Cities
summaryEn: UrbanGreenLeap helps cities, especially small and medium ones, address climate change by protecting and expanding green spaces. The project supports local governments in creating Urban Nature Plans that include parks, green roofs, and urban forests, promoting nature-based solutions. It also empowers citizens to take part in improving their environments and raises awareness among decision-makers about the importance of green spaces for climate resilience.

titleEn: Port-City Regions To Wave Med Cruise Destinations As Smart, Sustainable And Striking Eco-Tourism Systems
summaryEn:
Cruise tourists are increasingly seeking tailor-made inland tours. They want to discover more authentic places in a sustainable way, in tours that suit their curiosity as well as their physical abilities.
The eco-tourism platform PortCREW will be tested in 5 Mediterranean cruise ports located in Spain, France, Italy, Slovenia, and Greece. What is it about? Providing cruise managers, port or tourism authorities with new inland tourism packages. How will it help tourism management? By avoiding overtourism in the same seaside areas, valorising new natural and cultural assets and increasing the social acceptance of the cruise sector in MED cities.

titleEn: Green Participatory Budgeting for Local Environmental Action and sustainable Future
summaryEn: Green B-LEAF helps rural Mediterranean communities adapt to climate change by combining participatory budgeting with detailed climate data. It gives residents and local governments the tools to plan and fund green projects, strengthening resilience and sustainability. By connecting communities across the region and promoting values like beauty, sustainability, and togetherness, Green B-LEAF builds lasting local capacity to face climate challenges

titleEn: Fostering innovative and sustainable bio-waste management and circular bio-economy in the Mediterranean area
summaryEn:
CirBioWaste helps Mediterranean regions improve bio-waste management by promoting sustainable, circular practices. Despite EU rules, only 16% of food waste is properly collected and recycled, with many areas still relying on landfills. The project supports local governments and universities in six countries by adapting proven solutions, improving collection systems, boosting composting, and encouraging use of organic fertilizers. It combines local and international efforts, offering training, tools, and shared strategies to reduce environmental impact and support a circular bioeconomy across the EU MED region+B

20.

titleEn: Testing a holistic model to co-design and co-implement healthy urban green spaces for climate resilient cities and towns
summaryEn: Urban green spaces are vital for fighting climate change, but they face threats from rising temperatures and pollution. RealUrbanGreen will test a new model in eight pilot sites to help communities and local authorities create greener, healthier, and more resilient spaces. The project combines community involvement with expert knowledge to develop a practical tool for improving urban green spaces and boosting climate resilience.

titleEn: MEDiterranean 4 REGENerative Tourism and Culture
summaryEn:
Adapting to climate change is not just a set of actions, it is a state of mind. Therefore, cultural institutions such as museums or historical sites have a role to play in encouraging their visitors to adopt a lifestyle based on sustainability, accessibility and inclusiveness.
MED4REGEN aims to engage the tourism industry in this change, from cultural institutions to businesses and local authorities, by providing them operational and collaborative tools.
Thanks to the ancient remains of its millenary history, the Mediterranean is the most popular tourist destination in the world. Let it also be the cradle of its sustainable future!

titleEn: INSPIRE: INtegrating biodiverSity Preservation and agrobIodiversity valorisation In touRism managEment in the MED area
summaryEn: The INSPIRE project wants to transform agrobiodiversity conservation into touristic opportunities. Agrobiodiversity is the term used to describe the way natural ecosystems work in areas of farming activities.How can this be achieved? First, by getting the 8 partners working on designing a sustainable tourism model based on agrobiodiversity. It will then be tested in five regions, where public and private tourism groups, farmers, and local communities will work together to apply it. In the end, all these initiatives would be transferable to a wider sample of territories in the future!

titleEn: Monitoring cumulative Impact to guide mitigation and RestorAtion in the MediterrAnean Region
summaryEn: Humans are placing increasing strain on ecosystems exposing them to multiple, concurrent stressors. The Mediterranean region is a biodiversity hotspot hosting almost half of all the plant species, about a third of all the vertebrate species on our planet and an exceptional number of species found nowhere else in the world. This biodiversity, however, is heavily exposed to stressors like legacy and emerging contaminants, marine litter including microplastics, noise, habitat destruction from ever-increasing human activities, exacerbated by climate change, resulting in long-term impacts on ecosystem stability. These stressors are often tackled in isolation. The urgency to address these threats and the cumulative impact of multiple stressors requires cohesive, transnational efforts that combine fragmented knowledge to develop a new, integrated approach. In response to these challenges, the MIRAMAR project has identified three ecologically significant ecosystems in the Euro-Mediterranean region: seagrass meadows, wetlands, and habitats of endangered species. Seagrass meadows serve as crucial breeding, feeding, and sheltering grounds for numerous species, are vital for oxygen production and as blue carbon sinks. Wetlands are biodiverse transition ecosystems containing river deltas, brackish waters, salt lakes, and marshes, supporting a variety of flora and fauna, that play a critical role in maintaining ecological balance. Healthy endangered species habitats, including those of seabirds, cetaceans and wetland birds, are vital for the survival of these vulnerable populations. MIRAMAR’s 8 partners represent 6 countries across the Euro-Med region (Albania, Croatia, France, Greece, Italy, and Spain), and come from academia (UNISI), research institutes (CSIC, HCMR, SZN, RBI), NGO networks (MIO-ECSDE), as well as regional (OEC) and national authorities (MTE).Thanks to this transnational collaboration, MIRAMAR aims to develop an innovative harmonized methodology to monitor cumulative impact of selected stressors in 9 pilot areas in the three identified habitats. Drawing support and upscaling previous project results (INTERREG, ADRION, LIFE, H2020) MIRAMAR will design, test, and validate a new holistic monitoring method to identify suitable nature-based mitigation and restoration solutions. By aligning with national monitoring strategies and the management plans of parks and protected areas, MIRAMAR will address the common challenge of preventing, mitigating and restoring environmental degradation of these ecosystems. MIRAMAR is committed to aligning with key environmental initiatives and programs such as, Zero Pollution Action Plan of the European Green Deal, EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030, EU Marine Strategy Framework Directive, Barcelona Convention's Integrated Monitoring and Assessment Programme, Union for the Mediterranean, UN Environment Programme/Mediterranean Action Plan, Ramsar Convention on Wetlands, among others. These frameworks emphasize the interconnected nature of climate change, biodiversity loss, land and sea degradation, stressing the importance of addressing these challenges in a coherent, synergetic, and holistic manner based on best available scientific knowledge.By engaging with these international agreements and frameworks, MIRAMAR will contribute to global efforts to tackle environmental issues and promote sustainable development practices. MIRAMAR’s collaborative approach and focus on stakeholder engagement, benefitting from Living Labs, underscores our commitment to harnessing collective expertise and fostering innovative solutions to address the complex challenges facing the Euro-Mediterranean region. Fourteen associate partners, representing key stakeholders in each targeted pilot area, will be proactively engaged in the project. They will see their scientific knowledge and capacity to implement environmental management practices and policies increase; more importantly, they will benefit from the project outcomes through the monitoring protocols and operational roadmap. This process of engagement will take concrete form with the signing of Declaration of Intent to adopt MIRAMARs harmonised monitoring protocol to assess cumulative impacts, as a key commitment to identify the "best" mitigation and restoration solutions. Through partnerships with diverse stakeholders, alignment with international initiatives, and a focus on science-based solutions, MIRAMAR is positioned to make a meaningful impact to protect nature, biodiversity, and green infrastructure for the benefit of current and future generations. With a comprehensive and inclusive approach, MIRAMAR aims to lead the way in addressing complex environmental challenges and charting a resilient, biodiverse, and sustainable future for all.

titleEn: Green and circular transformation of services in Med tourism
summaryEn:
The Mediterranean tourism sector is largely made up of small and family businesses. That is why GreenSET develops a business support infrastructure to encourage as many of them as possible to innovate services they provide to reduce their environmental impact and better use resources.
Each business will create new competitive and sustainable service, enabling new revenues from existing resources and capabilities, supported by local MED experts, trained and certified in service innovation methodology. In this way, GreenSET aims for the long-term adoption of sustainable practices by a wide range of businesses, with each successful experience having the potential to spread to other ones!

titleEn: Towards a Mediterranean model of Regenerative Tourism as Climate Change adaptation and risk prevention
summaryEn:
More than 70% of European citizens say they are willing to change their travel habits to a more sustainable model. Regenera4MED wants to go further!
Its concept of Regenerative Tourism goes beyond sustainability, it actively seeks to restore and revitalize natural ecosystems, strengthen local cultures, and empower communities. It promotes climate change adaptation and resilience while fostering meaningful connections that generate long-term, shared value for both people and the planet.
Regenera4MED will be tested in 6 high-profile tourist destinations: Catalonia (Spain), Corsica (France), Liguria and Abruzzo (Italy), Split-Dalmatia (Croatia) and Crete (Greece). Its long-term goals? To reposition the Mediterranean as a global benchmark for Regenerative tourism and to promote the region as a destination for the tourism of the future.

titleEn: Supporting the implementation of blue and circular tourism in the Mediterranean
summaryEn:
The RECIRCLE MED project for sustainable coastal tourism has two characteristics that make it stand out.
First, it integrates two approaches that are often considered separately: the circular economy, i.e. the reuse of resources, and the blue economy, i.e. the protection of coastal areas. How? By building on the tools and results of two previous successful projects: INCIRCLE and REBOOT MED.
Then, by bringing these approaches to smaller tourist destinations that do not have the capacity or funding to implement them. How? Through a step-by-step transfer process that facilitates their adoption and ensures the development of local plans tailored to their needs.

titleEn: Enhancing the capacity for prevention and response in case of floods and subsequent natural disasters and emergencies in the cross-border region
summaryEn:
The FLOODGUARD 2 project aims to build on the results achieved under the FLOODGUARD project "Integrated actions for joint coordination and overcoming flood risks in the cross-border area", funded by the Interreg V-A Greece-Bulgaria Programme 2014-2020, by increasing the capacity of first responders to act in case of floods and subsequent disasters and emergencies in the cross-border region Greece-Bulgaria. This includes ensuring proper and timely response to various disasters and crises through the supply of specialized equipment, conducting joint trainings and exercises, raising awareness and preparedness of the population in the cross-border region and the construction and equipment of Joint Training Center in the region of Blagoevgrad. This will reduce disaster risk and the consequences of possible emergencies and ensure greater resilience in the event of floods and subsequent disasters and emergencies.
During the implementation of the project, specialized and rescue equipment, as well as equipment for evacuation camps, will be delivered. Several joint trainings and field exercises will be organized. In Bulgaria there are going to be identified suitable evacuation sites and the relevant procedures will be updated/developed. There are going to be trainings in case of floods for children and information campaign among adults, also in Bulgaria. In Greece there will be information events for young people on flood protection. 
At the end of the project's implementation there will be a final press conference in the Blagoevgrad district in Bulgaria, where both partners will participate and present the achieved results.

titleEn: Improvement of mobility and travel safety in the CB area
summaryEn:
The improvement of the secondary connections in the cross-border area was supported with significant resources from the previous Greece-Bulgaria programs. Now, in the 2021-2027 programming period, this strategic choice to complete the results of the investments done previously remains, because the current state of the road network is still characterized by unsatisfactory conditions in terms of functionality and safety. 
The current strategic project has been designed in common by the two partners, Road Infrastructure Agency (RIA) and Egnatia Odos S.A. (EOSA) has integrated both their ideas, priorities and actions. The partners identified the most important road sections, which need to be upgraded in order to have the best benefit in the CB region and to consolidate the road sections in the current project. From Bulgarian side the project consists of upgrading of 2,6 km section along Road II-86 (Rudozem bypass), upgrading of 2.49 km section along Road I-5 Kardzhali-Makaza and Technical design for Smolyan bypass road. Upgrading of remaining parts in the Road Axis Xanthi – Echinos – Gr.-Bg. Borders - “Xanthi – Sminthi” subsection (600 m) [Bridge G3, Stavroupoli roundabout and Isaia cross-section] are the construction activities from the Greek side.
The modernized infrastructure will benefit mostly the population of local communities, where the proposed road sections are located, through enhanced mobility and safety, improved environmental conditions, better access to markets, labor mobility, goods, and services, improving their quality of life. Improving the transport infrastructure of the CB area contributes to the promotion of its sustainable development and cohesion, mitigating regional disparities, and providing equal opportunities for all.
The total budget of the project is approximately 22 000 000 EUR (EU and National Funds) divided between the partners according to a balanced distribution of activities to be carried out by them. The project’s duration is 36 months

titleEn: Education, training, lifelong learning - inclusive and accessible
summaryEn:
Project Summary

This project aims to address significant challenges in the cross-border region between Bulgaria and Romania by enhancing educational infrastructure and creating new learning opportunities. By leveraging the strengths of diverse organizations, the project seeks to foster sustainable development and social cohesion across the region.

Expected change:
At the local level: Improve the quality of the educational environment in two schools - in the village of Djulyunitsa, Bulgaria, and in the city of Slatina, Romania; create new learning opportunities for youth and adults; develop practical skills; integrate resources and expertise from training and educational institutions to enhance digital literacy and professional readiness; ensure equal access to educational infrastructure; and support marginalized communities and vulnerable groups.

At the cross-border level: Strengthen cross-border cooperation and develop new curricula. Create conditions for the economic development of the region through joint initiatives between the labor market and the education and training system.

Expected results:
Improved access to quality education and training in the cross-border region through the modernization of educational infrastructure and the implementation of new training programs.

Specific results:

Renovated and equipped educational infrastructure:

In Bulgaria: A training center has been established with classrooms and facilities for digital skills and balloon piloting at the school in Djulyunitsa.
In Romania: A digital classroom has been established at "Radu Greceanu" High School in Slatina.
Balloon Piloting Simulator Center: A realistic training center has been created in a controlled environment in Slatina District, Romania.
Provision of modern digital learning equipment:

Classrooms and centers have been equipped with modern digital technology, supporting new teaching methods and ensuring digital literacy among the target groups.
Development and implementation of new training programs:

Programs for digital technologies, game design, and balloon piloting have been developed in Bulgarian, Romanian, and English.
Secure online access has been provided, removing language, territorial, and time barriers.
Online training in foreign languages and digital technologies has been developed for students and adults.
Beneficiaries and users:

Direct: 50 participants in Romanian and Bulgarian courses, 80 participants in digital skills courses, and 2 graduates of the balloon piloting course.
Indirect: Nearly 600 students and teachers; hundreds of business and NGO representatives; and the local communities in Slatina and Lyaskovets, covering over 90,000 inhabitants.
Approach and need for cross-border cooperation:
The project unites organizations with diverse experiences and focuses, working towards a common goal. HRDA has extensive experience in digital technology and game design training in underdeveloped regions, such as the award-winning CODE project in Latvia. "Oltenia de 10" offers innovative training for balloon captains, a profession with high added value, particularly for tourist regions. The school in Djulyunitsa is small, with limited opportunities, and receives support from the municipality of Lyaskovets to expand its educational programs. The school in Slatina offers specialized courses, fostering a strong partnership to achieve the project goals.

The project will enable partners to exchange and adapt methodologies, developing new skills applicable to other projects. Cross-border cooperation will create sustainable solutions to common regional challenges and strengthen links between educational institutions and training organizations, establishing structures for future cooperation and knowledge exchange.

The project will integrate modern technologies into learning processes, preparing participants for the contemporary labor market. Positive social and economic impacts are expected on local communities through new educational and employment opportunities, especially in the less developed and rural areas of the region.

Innovation and originality of the project:
The project is distinguished by the integration of modern technologies and digital tools into the educational process. The creation of digital classrooms and simulators for training balloon captains provides learners with opportunities to develop skills that meet labor market needs. The training of balloon captains is unique to the region and addresses the demand for new professions with high added value, particularly in tourist areas. Online learning platforms remove barriers to education, providing access to knowledge anytime, anywhere. The project also incorporates sustainable practices crucial for the region's future development, as well as social and economic integration of vulnerable groups, particularly in rural and less developed areas.

titleEn: Virtual classrooms and generating educational content in VR in the field of cultural-historical heritage with a focus on the common Roman heritage of the Lower Danube and Neolithic settlements
summaryEn:
The cross-border region between Belene, Bulgaria, and Alexandria, Romania, faces significant educational challenges, particularly in providing modern, technology-driven learning experiences. Both areas struggle with limited access to advanced digital tools and resources, which hampers the ability of students and educators to engage with innovative educational methods. Additionally, preserving and promoting the rich cultural-historical heritage of the Lower Danube, especially the Roman heritage and Neolithic settlements, requires new, engaging methods to capture the interest of younger generations.

 The overall objective of the project is to bridge the digital and educational gaps in the Belene-Alexandria region by creating virtual classrooms equipped with cutting-edge technologies like Virtual Reality (VR). This initiative aims to revolutionize the learning process by making education more immersive, interactive, and accessible. The project will focus on generating educational content in VR, particularly related to the cultural-historical heritage of the region, thus enhancing students' ability to retain information and deepening their understanding of local history. By the end of the project, the current situation—characterized by traditional, less engaging teaching methods—will be transformed into a dynamic, modern educational environment that better prepares students for the digital age and fosters a deeper appreciation for their cultural heritage.
 The project will produce several key outputs:
-Fully equipped with VR technology, located in the Multifunctional Youth Center in Alexandria and the Municipality of Belene, these classrooms will serve as the primary learning spaces for the project.
- Custom-created VR modules focusing on the Roman heritage of the Lower Danube and Neolithic settlements, allowing students to explore historical topics in an immersive manner.
-Trained Educators. Teachers will be trained to effectively use VR systems, ensuring they can facilitate these innovative learning experiences.
-A platform for sharing educational content, experiences, and best practices across the region and beyond.
The primary beneficiaries of these outputs are the students and educators in Belene and Alexandria, who will gain access to advanced educational tools and methods. The broader community, including local historians and cultural institutions, will also benefit from the preservation and promotion of regional heritage through modern technology.
The project adopts a collaborative cross-border approach, essential for pooling resources, expertise, and cultural insights from both Bulgaria and Romania. This cooperation is critical for creating a unified educational experience that transcends national boundaries, fostering a sense of shared heritage among students. The joint development of VR content and the exchange of best practices between the two municipalities will ensure that the educational programs are comprehensive and culturally inclusive. This cross-border approach is not only efficient but also necessary to address the shared challenges in education and cultural preservation in the region.
What sets this project apart is its innovative use of VR technology in education, particularly within the context of cultural-historical heritage. By integrating modern digital tools with historical education, the project offers a new way to engage students and make learning more relevant . The use of VR to explore historical sites and events provides an immersive learning experience that is far more engaging than traditional methods. Additionally, the project’s emphasis on cross-border collaboration ensures that these innovative educational practices benefit a broader audience and promote cultural exchange between Bulgaria and Romania. This project not only modernizes education in the region but also sets a precedent for how technology can be used to preserve and promote cultural heritage in an engaging and meaningful way.

titleEn: Cross-Border Youth Safety and Inclusion: Modernizing Training Facilities and Developing a Comprehensive Good Practices Guide
summaryEn:
The project aims to address a common challenge faced by the programme area: the need to improve youth safety, inclusion, and employability, particularly for vulnerable or marginalized groups. Both Romania and Bulgaria face difficulties aligning educational outcomes with labor market demands, resulting in gaps that hinder the integration of young people into the workforce and compromise their safety and personal development.

The overall objective of the project is to bridge this gap by modernizing educational infrastructure, equipping training centers with state-of-the-art tools, and fostering cross-border collaboration to develop joint training programs. The expected change is an improvement in youth employability and safety, with educational programs more closely aligned with the real-world demands of employers and personal development needs. This will lead to better-prepared young people entering the workforce with relevant skills, enhanced safety, and more inclusive opportunities for those from marginalized backgrounds.

Key outputs include the modernization of the sports hall at the Dolj County Police Inspectorate, procurement of specialized equipment such as driving simulators and physical training devices, and routine upgrades at the Academy of Economics in Svishtov. Additionally, joint workshops and training sessions will produce a comprehensive Guide for Youth Safety and Conduct. These outputs will benefit students and young adults, by providing modern training environments, relevant skills development, and a standardized approach to youth safety.

The cross-border approach is critical, as the challenges of youth safety, inclusion, and employability transcend national borders. Joint training sessions and workshops will foster cooperation between Romania and Bulgaria, allowing both countries to share best practices, standardize training programs, and create a unified response to common challenges. This approach leverages combined resources and expertise, ensuring a stronger and more cohesive impact.

What is original about the project is its holistic approach to addressing youth safety and employability by integrating modern technology, infrastructure improvements, and collaborative cross-border efforts.
