The introduction of innovative training tools and joint programs that combine personal finance, green economy, self-defense, and safe driving creates a multifaceted learning environment that is both practical and forward-looking. 
LP non-eligible expenditures : 68,057.88 Euro/340,970 RON.

titleEn: Go Out and Learn
summaryEn:
The project aims at developing new ways of improving cooperation, social interaction and lifestyle, through simple but out-of-the box concepts. Lifelong learning is the keyword, but this will not represent just a cliché - but a concept for training outside classroom, in most areas Arts can comprise.
The common challenge facing both young musicians, but also elder person from the Bulgaria-Romania border region is related to the territorial distance from the capitals of both countries and the lack of artistic events - concerts, master classes, workshops, etc. in which musicians but also common people above 50 years, who are almost retired and live in small cities with no opportunities to learn new things, to relax and perform arts. For young performers, another problem is the lack of professional experience in an international environment, insufficient communication skills with specific musical terminology in English.
Using the territorial proximity of the two regions - Ruse and Giurgiu, we aim at setting up the framework for joint work of young musicians from Bulgaria and Romania in an international environment, through their participation in master classes and concerts. Under the project, we will furnish a chamber music training room with a grand piano and sound equipment, music tablets, desks and chairs, necessary for outdoor and indoor chamber concerts. In this way, conditions will be created for young musicians to participate in various concerts on both banks of the Danube.
On the other hand, elder persons (mostly women) both in Bulgaria in Romania, living in small cities, have little space to cultivate their own passions and interests, and are mostly busy with family lives, household and agricultural activities. The project offers the hopefully start for new ideas to jointly take part in classes aiming at developing new skills for performing art – dancing, calligraphy, painting. Thus, Art will be taught as an universal language, no matter geography, nationality or other social distancing facts.

Thus, the Project Objective is to set up the framework for training and lifelong learning in different types of arts – music, dancing, painting and calligraphy for people on both sides of the border. Thus, the Project Objective is to set up the framework for training and lifelong learning in different types of arts – music, dancing, painting and calligraphy for people on both sides of the border. Following the project implementation, persons at vulnerable ages (young artists and elder people) from both sides of the border will gather new skills and will speak a new language – Art. The project defined objective is fully in line with the Programme’s specific objective, since it will support to improving equal access to inclusive and quality services in training and lifelong learning. Main outputs envisaged:
-	80 people trained in painting
-	80 people trained in calligraphy
-	40 people trained in dancing
-	40 people trained in music
-	16 young people attending a piano mastercourse
-	A big final event, organized in the premises of the Opera in Ruse.
The approach envisaged is rather simple. A specialized communication Contractor will closely cooperate with the Project Management Team from both sides of the border, in order to identify participants for in all trainings. Then, the structure of the courses will be designed by specialized contractors in each of the envisaged fields, including exact dates and locations and organizing the logistics for the participation of trainees from both countries. The content of each course will be uploaded on the e-learning platform, so that it becomes accessible for every interested person.
The final event will be designed in such a way that it will sum up a significant part of the training results – comprising a concert, some exhibitions and a dance show. Amongst the spectators we consider to have as guests also project key actors from both countries – MA, Joint Secretariat, local and regional public authorities.

The idea of the project itself is original. It brings together people from both sides of the border through joint learning events, but not in a standard topics or in the classroom. Training in arts for amateurs is a rather rare form of training; moreover, when participants come from small cities or rural areas, this is rather unusual, nevertheless it promotes inclusion and, as already described above, it supports people speak the same language – arts. As a conclusion - Art is the expression of souls. Training in Arts - brought by the project - will be helping people (who otherwise would have low chances to it, given the geographic context) to learn how to express themselves.

titleEn: Joint training schemes in tourism and long-life learning in the cross-border region of Dobrich-Constanta
summaryEn:
The project covers the cross-border area of Dobrich district and Constanta county and aims at implementing common measures for common challenges by the project partners European Institute for cultural tourism EUREKA (PL) and Ovidius University of Constanta (P2). 
Main goal of the project is to contribute to Improving equal access to inclusive and quality services in training and long-life learning through developing, promoting and implementing joint innovative complex training schemes in tourism and stakeholders networking in the cross-border region Dobrich-Constanta. 
The project contains three specific objectives that correspond to the three work packages.
Specific objective 1: Developing joint innovative complex approach for training and LLL in tourism through research and stakeholders networking in the cross-border region Dobrich-Constanta; implementing joint measures for improving the link between the labor market and the education and training system in tourism. 
Specific objective 2: Creating joint complex training scheme in tourism designed for long life learning, incl. digitized learning tools, for the professions: "Administrator in Hospitality ", “Chambermaid in Hospitality”, “Waiter-bartender”. Promoting the benefits of the training schemes to the tourism business of the cross-border region Dobrich-Constanta
Specific objective 3: Improving equal access to inclusive and quality services in training and long-life learning through implementing joint innovative complex training schemes in tourism and face-to-face vocational trainings of different target groups, including vulnerable, marginalized groups and people from remote villages/areas in the cross-border region of Dobrich-Constanta. Promoting market orientation and improving quality aspect of training and education in tourism through stakeholders networking and training. Creating conditions for promotion, multiplication and sustainability of project results.
The project is aimed at solving the identified common challenges of the labor market. For years, imbalances in the labor market have been observed in the cross-border region of Dobrich-Constanța. Tourism businesses advertise vacancies, but they remain unfilled, which is why companies resort to importing staff. At the same time, the number of compact groups of people who are long-term unemployed, young people who do not study and do not work, minorities in social isolation, remote rural areas where forms of lifelong learning are not offered are growing. 
The project aims to contribute to solving these challenges by creating joint training schemes and innovative training tools for three professions in tourism, for which there is the greatest demand from the tourism business: "Administrator in Hospitality", "Chambermaid in Hospitality", "Waiter-bartender". Innovative training tools such as video films, a Digital tool for building key competences and a platform for learning Romanian/Bulgarian language will be complemented by internship abroad. 120 representatives of the target groups from the cross-border region Dobrich-Constanta will be trained within six training courses. Furthermore, the training materials can be used for self-study by people from the target groups. A special emphasis in the training content will be placed on building green skills.
Another target group represent educational and training institutions, which prepare personnel for tourism. The project will contribute to increasing the capacity of the training institutions through a joint workshop (WP1) and a “Train the Trainer” workshop (WP3) with a total of 30 participants and will create conditions for partnerships and networking with the tourism business in order to maintain feedback and update the educational content according to the market needs.
The project aims to achieve sustainability of results by creating and publishing video films and video clips for all main activities and achieved results: video films about the six training courses in three professions; two promotional events for the tourism business; two workshops for training institutions, information campaign with publication of press releases and press conferences.
The project builds on the results of a previous joint project, implemented under the INTERREG V-A Program Romania-Bulgaria, namely project ROBG-158 with Acronym “LAB mobile”. Within the framework of LAB mobile project, Ovidius University created and equipped a Center for lifelong learning. This activity is now being upgraded with additional equipment and expansion of the capacity оf the center. The partners will also promote and use the language platform Romanian/Bulgarian language, created under the LAB mobile project and maintained by the LP- EICT EUREKA NPO. Achieving the set goals will be possible thanks to the equipment, which will be used to provide the trainings and the promotional campaign. The project will be managed by a highly qualified joint staff.

titleEn: Cross-Border Initiative for Religious Communities’ Learning and Engagement
summaryEn:
CIRCLE tackles the common challenge of the Programme for poor mobility and adresses low educational attainment especially in rural/remote CB regions of the target groups. By creating a Joint Distance Learning Centre and interactive inclusive e-learning platform in 3-languages (that will operate for at least 5 years after the project end) CIRCLE will offer training programs to equip target groups with professional skills in project management and fundraising. These endeveors together with organized 5 cross-border mobilities that will be held in partners' languages and along with 2 training sessions will equip learners with competencies to offer or seek employment, provide social services for marganilized communties in their church dioceses and support income-generating activities. 
The overall project objective is to imporve equal access of the chosen target groups in the cross-border region to education, training and lifelong learning by establishing a pioneering Cross-Border Distance Learning Center and organization of 5 in-person mobilities, combined with distance online trainings,2 pilot training sessions and 1 interactive e-learning tool, involving 3 partners & 160 people in the joint-learning schemes by the end of the project and 500 end-users 5 years beyond the project. The expected change that CIRCLE will make to the current situation is that through in-person and distance mobilities, and online training sessions it fosters a culture of lifelong learning, allowing participants to adapt to the evolving needs of their communities. Additionally, the joint-learning schemes will strengthen relationships among participants from Bulgaria and Romania, facilitating ongoing support and collaboration. Engaging 160 participants with a goal of reaching 500 end-users of e-learning interactive tools, post-project ensures lasting benefits for the church dioceses providing opportunitiy for lifelong learning of chosen groups with low skills from remote cross-border area. This collective effort will empower church workers and NGOs, creating a more resilient and engaged community that can better address social and economic challenges. 
The main outputs of the project are: Established Cross-Border Joint Distance Learning Centre; Developed 3 training programmes integrating 3 interactive courses; Developed e-learning interactive tools (e-platform integrating 3 learning modules with 30 video lessons); Organized 2 training seminars to pilot testing of the e-platform and the e-lessons; Organized five in-person and distance learning mobilities in Project Management, Online Fundrasing and Good social practices, and EU funding opportunities. Target groups who will benefit from the outputs are church communities and dioceses (such as church workers, priests, church members, and administrative staff within churches), theologians and theology students, NGOs that focus on church/community development tailored to vulnerable people, and the general public.
CIRCLE adopts a cross-border approach by establishing a Joint Distance Learning Center, interractive e-platform that provides joint training programs and lessons in Bulgarian, Romanian, and English for churches, NGOs, and theology students from both Bulgarian and Romanian cross-border region facing joint challenges. Thus it addresses significant barriers to training access, by offering a hybrid educational model integrating on-site and distance learning. Located in Vidin and Craiova, it facilitates the exchange of best practices and training delivery, enhancing collaboration between organizations and empowering community leaders to tackle social and economic disparities effectively.
The original character of the project is the creation of a pioneering Joint Distance Learning Center and interactive e-platform based on an LMS plug-in that will provide customized multilingual online training programs and distance learning opportunities specifically for churches, NGOs, and theology students in remote urban and rural areas. This initiative uniquely addresses significant barriers to training access—such as high costs, territorial challenges, and language issues—by offering free, tailored programs through a hybrid model of in-person and online learning.
Located in Vidin and Craiova, the center will facilitate best practice exchanges and deliver essential training in topics covered by CIRCLE. The robust online platform will feature interactive e-lessons and user-friendly design, enhancing learning with engaging assessments and certification options.Innovative solutions, including portable training resources and digital engagement tools, will reach target groups with limited access to traditional educational facilities.Thus CIRCLE fosters lifelong learning, increase the opporutnities for employability and community participation while addressing economic disparities & social exclusion.

titleEn: Enhancing Quality and Universal Access to Learning and Inclusive Training for Youth
summaryEn:
Education is necessary for a society's inclusive and long-term growth.Egalitarian and high quality education helps promote marginalized groups' participation in the development process as a whole,hence minimizing socioeconomic unfairness.Education can exacerbate existing social inequities if equitable access and learning opportunities are not prioritized.
Despite improvements,challenges remain in ensuring access to quality and inclusive education,according to the latest Country Reports for both Romania & Bulgaria,issued by the European Commission.
In Romania,educational attainment is one of the lowest in EU and educational outcomes are greatly impacted by socio-economic factors,the vocational education and training not being sufficiently attuned to the labour market.Participation in early childhood education is low,the enrolment rate for children between 3 years and the starting age of compulsory primary education being one of the lowest in the EU (

78.2% in Romania and 80,1% in Bulgaria compared with EU average of 93%).Participation rates are generally worse for disadvantaged groups,Roma and rural areas.Moreover,the rural-urban gap and the situation of Roma in education remains critical in both countries:in Romania 79% and in Bulgaria 75% of Roma children aged 0-17 are at risk of poverty,leading to educational disadvantage due to socio-economic and minority status.
EQUALITY arrised based on the previous mentioned issues pattern,specifically lack of connection between education and labour market (1),disadvantaged marginalised groups (2),ethnic groups particularly Roma & Turks (3),rural areas (4)–all of these issues being deeply rooted in the partner locations-every single one of the project`s activities targeting to overcome such barriers.
All children have the right to evolve to the best of their abilities,and to attain their full intellectual potential,but not all benefit from an ideal educational model that fulfills their individual demands while also balancing them with the larger community.Education is a critical aspect in human society's evolution,being the most powerful tool for shaping the future.Project`s partnership,as representatives of the public administration and public school system,having the integrated image of children`s day to day reality and aspirations,are commited to reach project`s overall objective as to invest in the children`s education and their personal development,every aspect of EQUALITY`s project advocating as a vector of change by expanding chances for social inclusion and labor market integration for both present and future generations.
EQUALITY project will ensure the achievement of all 3 output indicators for Programme`s PA3,through:
-RCO87-the partnership between two organisations from neighboring regions, namely Baneasa commune from Constanta county (Romania) and "Hristo Smirnenski" Primary School from General Toshevo municipality,Dobrich district (Bulgaria) and the Associate Baneasa Theoretical Highscholl,cooperating across the ROBG border,during project`s implementation and after its completion,
-RCO85–396 pupils from Faurei Secondary School no. 1 and "Hristo Smirnenski" Primary School,will participate in joint training schemes within the project activity “Thematic Trainings” targeting the topics requested by the school community:vocational counselling,lifecoaching training,self-esteem counselling,and 32 teachers from both project schools will participate to the joint training on the topic of non-formal education and anti-bullying.
-PSO4–both partners will develop investments in education such as,for Baneasa commune the “Baneasa Creative Education Club for children and youth“ (1)and for "Hristo Smirnenski" Primary School the "Outdoor Multifunctional Sports Area" and Non-Formal Educational Ateliers (2).
Project consortium`s approach is a multilevel one,targeting in the same time and measure-pupils and teachers (1), parents (2),and the larger community.Any society's cornerstone,no matter the physical borders,is its educational system,having significant responsibility for the overall social,political,and economic advancement of communities.EQUALITY focuses on the transboundary character of the education,both engaging and challenging the cross border communities in increasing the inclusion of marginalised youth and encourging their personal development.
Project`s originality resides in its (a) participatory configuration by beginning at the community level and involving schoolchildren,parents and teachers in local educational planning and decision-making hence increasing levels of ownership and understanding of the value of education,(b) flexible and context adapted learning by engaging marginalised communities and addressing relevant non-formal learning topics suited to their realities and cultural practices,and (c) secure learning environments that place a high priority on childrens` physical and social-emotional safety as a necessary condition for inclusive education

titleEn: Cross-border Multidisciplinary Telemedicine Education Collaboration
summaryEn:
MITEC joins the efforts of the Medical University - Pleven, the University of Medicine and Pharmacy in Craiova, the "Open Hand" Foundation and ARoTT Romania to address the challenges in the field of medical education and healthcare in the program area.
The Romania-Bulgaria cross-border area faces the following challenges:
- shortage of medical specialists;
- limited access to high-quality educational resources and technologies;
- lack of access to modern training methods and technologies for medical professionals.
The two medical universities are the only ones in the cross-border area and they know very well the challenges in medical education, they know their strengths and weaknesses and for these reasons they join their efforts to obtain synergy in education and in medical care.
Pleven Medical University is strong in neurosurgery and ENT specialties, Craiova University of Medicine and Pharmacy is strong in gastroenterology. It is in these three specialties that the two universities join their efforts to achieve positive change in the cross-border area through a cross-border approach.
The main objective of MITEC is to improve the quality of medical education and training of students and trainees in the fields of neurosurgery, gastroenterology and ENT through the implementation of modern imaging and telemedicine technologies.
To achieve this goal, the following activities will be carried out:


1. Creation of a telemedicine classroom


2. Development of learning materials and programs


3. Training and development of personnel
The implementation of the main objective of the project will lead to the following changes in the program area: Improving the qualification and skills of medical specialists; Expanding access to high-quality learning resources; Improving the quality of medical services in remote areas.
The change will be achieved by using the main results of medical students, medical professionals and patients: A telemedicine room created and equipped with modern technology; Developed and accessible multimedia resources for neurosurgery, ENT and gastroenterology; Conducted pilot training with 20 students (10 from Bulgaria and 10 from Romania); Organized events for the exchange of experience and knowledge between specialists and students.
Medical students will improve their knowledge and skills through access to modern infrastructure and teaching materials. Medical professionals will have the opportunity for professional development and training with the help of new technologies. Patients will have access to better quality medical services thanks to better trained professionals.
The approaches that will be used in the implementation of the project are infrastructure construction, development of training resources, training and development.
The need to use the cross-border approach is due to the following reasons:
- Sharing of resources and knowledge: Cooperation between project partners will allow sharing of expertise and resources.
- Synergy in education: Joining the efforts of universities will increase the quality of education and create better conditions for students.
- Better patient care: Cross-border cooperation will lead to better medical care throughout the region.
The integration of resources and knowledge between the two universities is an innovative approach that will increase the effectiveness of training and the quality of healthcare. The two medical universities will collaborate for the first time in their history.
Implementation of modern telemedicine technology for training purposes is also a novelty for the region.
And last but not least, the creation of interactive training materials that combine video lessons, animations and virtual simulations is also an innovative approach in medical education at these universities.
In conclusion, MITEC aims to improve medical education and healthcare in the cross-border region by establishing a telemedicine classroom and developing online learning resources. Through cross-border cooperation between universities and partners, the project will create better conditions for training and professional development of medical professionals, which will lead to higher quality medical services and better patient care.

titleEn: Joint cross-border education and training schemes with an emphasis on lifelong learning activities between the Municipality of Vetovo and the Municipality of Giurgiu
summaryEn:
The "LEARN BRIDGE" project, is a collaborative initiative between the Municipality of Vetovo in Bulgaria and the Municipality of Giurgiu in Romania. This project aims to address common challenges faced by these cross-border regions, including high rates of early school leaving, youth unemployment, digital divides, economic disparities, and social exclusion. By fostering cross-border cooperation, the project seeks to create sustainable, inclusive educational and economic opportunities with a strong focus on lifelong learning and digital literacy.

Both Vetovo and Giurgiu are rural, less developed areas facing several socio-economic challenges. The high rates of early school leaving are a significant concern, with rates in these regions being substantially above the EU average, especially in rural settings. Youth unemployment is another major issue, with a considerable percentage of young people categorized as NEETs (Not in Education, Employment, or Training). Additionally, there is a pronounced digital divide, limiting access to technology and modern educational tools, which impedes both educational and economic participation in the digital economy. Economic disparities are prevalent, as these areas lack the economic opportunities found in urban centers. Social exclusion is also a problem, particularly for vulnerable groups who face marginalization due to inadequate access to quality education and economic opportunities.

The overall objective of the "LEARN BRIDGE" project is to enhance social inclusion, stimulate local economic development, and improve cross-border cooperation by providing digital education and training programs tailored to the specific needs of the communities. The project seeks to improve educational outcomes by reducing early school leaving rates through engaging and practical education methods. It aims to enhance employability by equipping young people and adults with essential digital and entrepreneurial skills. The project also focuses on reducing social exclusion by creating inclusive learning environments that accommodate all, including marginalized groups. Furthermore, it seeks to promote economic development by supporting entrepreneurship and the adoption of digital tools to improve local businesses. The expected change from the project is the creation of a more educated, skilled, and inclusive community in both municipalities, contributing to a sustainable environment for economic growth and social cohesion.

The project will deliver several key outputs. These include joint training programs in digital literacy and entrepreneurship for 30 youth participants, 15 from each country. It will also provide workshops for 30 educators on digital tools and innovative teaching methods aimed at reducing early school leaving. A new Center for Lifelong Learning will be established, offering ongoing education and training for all age groups and equipped with modern digital tools. Additionally, the project will feature specialized training programs for local entrepreneurs, agricultural producers, and craftspeople to enhance their digital and business skills. The primary beneficiaries of these initiatives include young people, educators, local entrepreneurs, marginalized groups, and the broader community in Vetovo and Giurgiu.

The approach of the "LEARN BRIDGE" project is based on the necessity of a cross-border strategy, given the similar challenges faced by Vetovo and Giurgiu. This collaborative effort enables both municipalities to develop sustainable solutions more effectively by combining their resources, expertise, and knowledge. The cross-border cooperation facilitates intercultural understanding, the sharing of best practices, and the strengthening of regional ties. The partnership has been formalized through a Memorandum of Cooperation, emphasizing a joint commitment to alternative education and lifelong learning.

The project introduces several innovative elements. It integrates digital education by focusing on digital literacy and entrepreneurial skills that are tailored to the community's specific needs, addressing both educational gaps and economic challenges. The cross-border collaboration itself is an innovative approach to tackling rural and socio-economic challenges through shared solutions. Additionally, the project will establish a sustainable Center for Lifelong Learning, equipped with the latest technology to provide continuous education, which is particularly innovative in rural contexts where access to digital tools is often limited.

In summary, the "LEARN BRIDGE" project presents a novel approach to addressing shared socio-economic challenges through a combination of digital education, cross-border collaboration, and inclusive training programs. This project is designed to achieve a long-term positive impact on the communities of Vetovo and Giurgiu.

titleEn: Connect through performance, education and values
summaryEn: The Connect through performance, education and values ​​project aims to ensure quality academic training for students from Romania and Bulgaria through joint learning, exchange of best practices, knowledge of common history and ensuring sustainable development through the development of the skills needed on the labor market. the project will develop the educational infrastructure of two universities (the University of Craiova and the University of Veliko Tarnovo), 200 students will be trained and a network of NGOs, public institutions and training providers will be created in order to promote learning throughout life and sustainable development.

titleEn: "Mountain School Without Borders"
summaryEn:
The level of development of a society can be judged by how it treats and cares for people with disabilities and how those in a disadvantaged position are accepted. The common challenge of the cross-border area that the partners of this project want to tackle is to jointly raise the level of equal access to inclusive and quality services in education, training and lifelong learning by developing accessible infrastructure, including by promoting sustainability for distance and online education and training. For this, the Special Technological High School "Beethoven" - Craiova, the Municipality of Berkovica and the District Council, Dolj joined forces and developed their ideas into a project proposal for a Mountain School without Borders. High school teachers daily face the challenge of educating children with special needs and, in their concern and love, not only teach them basic knowledge, but also make them full citizens of society and qualitatively prepare them for the job market. In the municipality of Berkovitsa, there are four centers for the accommodation of family-type children with graduates of different age groups and some of them with SEN. Rarely, children deprived of parental care and those with special needs, also Roma and disadvantaged, have access to winter sports (skiing, snowboarding, sledding, etc.), as well as the opportunity to be trained in them. At the same time, motor activity at lower temperatures for children with mental disabilities has a beneficial effect on their development. Although it is difficult but not impossible for children and adults with physical disabilities to practice winter sports, it requires the right environment, equipment and competent coaches and assistants. By assessing these challenges and needs, the partners determined general goal of the project: Ensuring equal access to inclusive and quality services in ski training, mountain sports and learning in a natural natural environment, by developing accessible infrastructure adapted physically for people with SEN in a disadvantaged position, etc. in support of this goal, more specific goals were formulated
-Creating an accessible, inclusive and quality environment for learning and practicing mountain winter and summer sports and outdoor sports, as a condition and basis for achieving the goal.
-Building a joint Romanian-Bulgarian teaching capacity for teaching winter and summer mountain sports, including working with people with special needs, including training volunteers to be assistants in the practice of these sports, included by the disadvantaged.
- Development and joint implementation of educational courses in skiing and winter sports, mountain climbing and orienteering, combined with training in natural sciences in nature (natural science, biology, astronomy, geography, etc.) and acquisition of digital skills in an outsourced educational process.
The expected change that this project will make in the current situation is to improve the access of students with SEN to mountain winter and summer spots and outdoor ones, to attract and motivate young people at risk of dropping out of education and employment by training them as assistants and enabled short-term mobility and increased the qualifications of teachers, thus creating a potential of ski and mountain teachers in the cross-border region.
As a result, we expect to build a Mountain School without borders that will provide all the possibilities (adapted physical environment for skiing and climbing, specialized equipment for skiing by people with physical disabilities and human resources ski teachers, mountain teachers and assistants so that all children can feel equal and in their access to inclusive and quality services in education and training, teachers to find new opportunities in the spirit of lifelong learning and striving to achieve better opportunities for all children cannot be hindered, neither by the river - a border, nor by language difficulties, nor by the stigmas in society.

titleEn: Cross-border cooperation to ensure an attractive educational environment
summaryEn:
The proposed project seeks to stimulate the development of existing educational activities in the target region by improving the quality and applying innovative approaches through the introduction of distance and online learning in a region with negative socio-economic indicators and the presence of minority groups and disadvantaged youth in the districts of Pleven, Bulgaria and Dolj, Romania.
The overall goal of the project is to create a modern and attractive educational environment in the two partner schools from Bulgaria and Romania with the support of experts from the Romanian partner 3, introducing distance and online complementary learning for equal access to inclusive and quality educational services. 
Specific project objectives:


1. Collaborative actions in the development of training materials and curricula, trainings, appropriate equipment and digitized tools, and outdoor learning spaces to create the conditions for inclusive and equitable quality education.


2. Establish a joint learning network for complementary extra-curricular learning, promoting cohesion and positive impact among young people in the cross-border region. 
Two thematic work packages will be used to implement the project, corresponding to the defined specific objectives. WP 1: "Development of training materials for students and trainers and equipment of training venues", WP 2: "Establishment of a joint training network and implementation of 6 joint extra-curricular training activities in interest clubs".
The project will contribute to improving the motivation of all participants in training, educational, motivational and other similar approaches that ultimately contribute to improving the quality of education and training services and increasing employment opportunities. This improves general socialisation and stimulates the provision of educational and training services by the relevant educational structures, as well as stimulating the interest of learners (including members of minority groups, young people in socially disadvantaged situations and/or those at risk of social exclusion). 
The partners start from the notion that the introduction of innovative educational and motivational approaches will stimulate the general interest of learners in specific areas of their general and complementary education and will form in them a more sustainable interest in the advantages of distance and online learning. Since, in terms of general indicators, both the Bulgarian and the Romanian target region are lagging behind some European indicators and those registered in the national statistics of both countries, the project partners are of the opinion that the implementation of the measures envisaged by the project can be beneficial for the recipients of these measures and, through the exchange of synergistic experiences and adaptation, can create useful common approaches. To summarise, a cross-border approach is appropriate in this case, as with similar problems in the two neighbouring regions, it is necessary to compare the effectiveness of the concerted impact measures and assess how and to what extent they have a positive and sustainable effect.
If we take into account the massive use by young people of modern computer and Internet possibilities for entertainment and leisure, the partners are of the opinion that the transition to more significant distance and online learning improves both their general educational background and their overall personal development. Broadly speaking, these main lines of influence include both the improvement of currently existing educational and training services and the gradual incorporation of new forms contained in information technology for personal development, motivation and socialisation. 
The outputs of the project implementation contribute to the achievement of the output indicators of Priority 3, SO 

4.2 of the programme, namely RCO85 Participation in joint training schemes - 2 trainings (teachers and students); RCO87 Cross-border cooperation between organisations - 3 organisations will implement cross-border cooperation (1 from Bulgaria and 2 from Romania); RCO4 Investment in education, training and lifelong learning services - two investments in education (one in Bulgaria and one in Romania). Teachers, students and the local community will benefit from the outputs of the project during its implementation and after its formal closure.

titleEn: Innovative educational services in the cross-border region of Vidin - Montana - Dolj
summaryEn:
The project aims to increase the key competencies and facilitate the integration into the labor market and the digital society of the population in rural areas and representatives of vulnerable groups in the cross-border Vidin-Montana-Dolj region. This will be achieved by developing innovative educational services, providing online resources for self-learning and organizing trainings on key competencies.

The project addresses the general challenge facing the cross-border region of Vidin - Montana - Dolj, related to the insufficient preparation of the population in rural areas and representatives of vulnerable groups for adaptation to the modern labor market and digital society. In the conditions of rapidly developing technologies and new requirements for workers, this region is faced with the need to increase key competences, which is essential for the social and economic integration of the population.

The main objective of the project is to improve the level of key competences among the population in the cross-border region by providing innovative educational services that will meet the identified needs. The expected change includes better preparation of people for the labor market, increasing their digital literacy and creating conditions for more successful social and economic integration. This project will increase the region's competitiveness by providing its residents with the necessary skills to successfully integrate into modern society.

The project will lead to the following main results:
- Development of an online educational platform: The platform will be an essential tool for providing training and resources accessible to all residents of the region. It will be used by adults, youth and vulnerable groups who need to increase their competences.
- Creation of training programs and materials: These programs will focus on key areas such as digital skills, entrepreneurship and foreign language learning. The training materials will be available both online and through mobile training centers that will serve remote and underdeveloped areas.
- Conducting pilot trainings: The pilot trainings will include representatives of the target groups from Bulgaria and Romania and provide them with practical skills to help them better integrate into the labor market and the digital society. A total of 600 residents of the cross-border region (300 from Bulgaria and 300 from Romania) will be included in the trainings - 200 people (100 from Bulgaria and 100 from Romania) on digital competences, 200 people (100 from Bulgaria and 100 from Romania) on entrepreneurship and 200 people (100 from Bulgaria and 100 from Romania) on foreign language skills (Bulgarian and Romanian). The foreign language training will be conducted online, through the platform, where the self-training materials necessary for the learners will be provided (including video lessons), as well as support from qualified teachers. 

Beneficiaries of these results will be the population in rural areas in the cross-border region of Vidin - Montana - Dolj, the Youth Not in Education, Employment, or Training (NEET's), and representatives of vulnerable groups who need to improve their skills for better social integration.

The project will use a cross-border approach, which is essential to address common challenges facing the region. Through cooperation between the partners from Bulgaria and Romania, resources, experience and good practices will be shared, which will contribute to the development of more effective solutions. The cross-border approach will allow the project to reach a wider audience and create sustainable results that will be applicable in other regions.
The project is new and original in that it combines traditional educational methods with innovative digital solutions and mobile services. The creation of an online platform that provides access to training for various target groups, as well as the use of mobile training services, is an innovative approach for the region. This project will not only provide new learning opportunities, but also create a sustainable development model that can be applied to other cross-border regions.

The project will create sustainable learning mechanisms that will continue to function after its completion. The online platform will remain active and the project partners will continue to organize trainings and maintain the developed resources. In addition, the project will promote equal access to education and support the social inclusion of vulnerable groups in the region. In addition, through the implementation of various communication activities, the awareness among the population in rural areas will be increased regarding the importance of lifelong learning.
The project ensures sustainability by developing tools and methodologies that can be used and adapted after its completion.

titleEn: PROMoting IncluSivE and Quality Education through Technology, Leadership and Sport - Hard
summaryEn:
The project "PROMoting IncluSivE and Quality Education through Technology, Leadership and Sport - Hard" will be implemented in partnership by two accredited Universities, University of Craiova (Romania) and D.A. Tsenov Academy of Economics (Bulgaria), and a Romanian NGO, Engage in Education Association. 

The project aims to increase the graduates' competences and skills making them more atractive on the Labour Market and implicitly to improve their employability in the RO-BG cross-border region. 

Complex infrastrutures for education will be carried out:


1. an infrastructure at DATsenovAE that includes equipment and renovation for 4 classrooms: (a) for independent practical work and exercises, (b) for creative and project work, (c) a videoconferencing and synchronous learning room, (d) classroom for theoretical training and asynchronous training and equipment for a gym space.


2. an infrastructure at UCV that includes: (a) an unconventional space that will allow students working individual or in teams, (b) an indoor sports field and (c) equipment for a lab focused on innovative technologies in optics (d) equipment for a lab focused on air quality sensors (e) equipment for communication.

All 3 partners will collaborate in organising 6 joint summer schools (5 in RO, 1 in BG) in English language, aiming to develop competencies in communication, innovative and green technologies, programming, IoT, working with data, artificial intelligence which are required by employers; will encourage students to develop sustainable and environmentally friendly economic bussinesses (optics, urban horticulture, restauration in art and culture) in the RO-BG cross-border area. Students will also learn how to be more adaptable and flexible, how to work in an international environemnt, how to reduce stress, and to have a healthy lifestyle.

All three partners will collaborate in organising together 5 joint courses (3 in RO, 2 in BG) in English language in the framework of this project. The courses will be fucused on communication in English (that will help the communication between students, academics, entrepreneurs, employers, stakeholders, public institutions), circular and green economy, EU policies, sustainable development and corporate social responsibility, social entrepreneurship and innovation, urban horticulture (green spaces to reduce the effect of air pollution in the RO-BG cross-border area).

ENGAGE (Partner 3 in the project) will collaborate with UCV and DATsenovAE in developing a network of partnerships between NGOs, companies, firms, local public authorities and stakeholders in the localities located along the Danube, both in Romania and in Bulgaria. This network of partnerships will be established to make a bridge between graduates and employers, and preserve the quality of the environment and promote green sustainable development in cross-border area. All 3 partners will collaborate to organise 2 job fairs (1 in RO, 1 in BG), with employers from both sides of Danube, 3 workshops and 2 conferences on hot topics in the cross-border area (employability, competencies required by Labor Market, adaptation at climate change, the importance of a clean environment and sport for human health).

The general objective of the project: Increasing the quality of professional training for 220 students and graduates from Romania and Bulgaria through relevant training activities (5 courses, 6 summer schools), exchange of good practices and investments in educational infrastructure (2)

Expected change: A better connection between graduates and employers and a greater openness of graduates to entrepreneurship in green and innovative technologies.

The main results: 2 infrastructures in education, 40 certificates with ECTS, 180 diplomas and certificates in the framework of this project, 2 job fairs, 6 summer schools for students, 4 courses for graduates, 2 job fairs, 3 workshops and 2 conferences.

What is new/original: Joint courses and summer schools in English in two universities from both sides of Danube is something new, a change of paradigm in the RO-BG cross-border area. Another new element is than an NGO collaborates with two universities bringing its experience in non formal education and the relation with employers, entrepreneurs and NGOs from the cross-border area. It is a formal and non formal synergy in education for students', academics', employers' for the communities' benefit. The Erasmus+ programme allows EU mobilities but they are isolated in the cross-border area (only a few academics had mobilities for teaching or training, none student's mobility).

LP: the non eligible expenditures will not be higher than 50,000 euro (to be revised during implementation).

titleEn: Cross-Border Academy for Smart Industry Competence and Future Excellence
summaryEn:
Our SkillsBridge project proposal addresses critical challenges faced by the Romanian-Bulgarian CBr region, including low participation in LLL, digital skills gaps, and educational discrepancies. Both Romania and Bulgaria experience significant issues such as adult education participation rates around 1% in both countries, well below the EU average of 

9.2%, there is an urgent need for accessible and engaging lifelong learning opportunities. There are substantial gaps in educational outcomes between these regions and the EU average, particularly in advanced technological skills. This is reflected in low tertiary education completion rates and high NEET rates, which are significantly above the EU average. The current educational and training systems do not adequately meet the demands of modern industries, especially in fields critical for economic growth such as automation, robotics, and digital technologies.

The overall objective of the SkillsBridge project is to enhance access to inclusive and quality education and training services across the Romanian-Bulgarian border, focusing on Industry 

4.0 skills development. The latter is meant to be achieved via targeted investments in state-of-the-art training facilities and creating a comprehensive digital learning platform. In addition the project aims to:

1) Significantly improve access to education for adults, students, and vulnerable groups in both countries, directly addressing the low participation rates in lifelong learning.
2) Offer advanced training in automation, robotics, and digital skills, the project to help bridge the skills gap between the educational system and labor market needs, improving employability and regional economic development.
3) Enhance cooperation between Romanian and Bulgarian institutions, aligning training programs and resources to support a more integrated workforce and reduce regional educational disparities.

 Main Outputs and Beneficiaries are as follows:

1) Cross-Border Smart Industry Academy: A state-of-the-art training facilities in Romania and Bulgaria, equipped with advanced technology for hands-on learning in automation, robotics, and digital skills.
2) SkillsBridge Online Training Tool: A digital platform offering interactive training modules, virtual workshops, and remote learning resources accessible to all project participants.
3) Skill Booster Accelerator Program: A comprehensive training programs developed collaboratively, covering critical Industry 

4.0 technologies and aligned with market demands. The program is synergetically complemented by an Experience Multiplicator Program - a cross-border mobility programs allowing participants to gain practical experience in different industry settings across Romania and Bulgaria.

Beneficiaries:

1) Students and NEETs will benefit from increased access to high-quality training and educational resources, improving their skills and employability.
2) Employees and unemployed individuals will receive upskilling and reskilling opportunities aligned with current industry needs, enhancing their job prospects.
3) Vulnerable Groups including people with mobile disabilities, those from remote or rural areas, and minorities, will gain access to inclusive and accessible training resources.
4) SMEs will benefit from a more skilled workforce capable of meeting modern industry demands, contributing to regional economic growth.
5) Educational Institutions will utilize advanced training facilities and digital tools, improving their educational offerings and aligning with industry standards.

The SkillsBridge project will use a comprehensive approach that integrates physical and digital training resources. The development of a cross-border academy, combined with a robust digital learning platform, will provide accessible and high-quality education across both countries. Joint curriculum development and cross-border training initiatives will ensure that all participants receive consistent and relevant education.

The SkillsBridge project is innovative and original in several ways:

1) We are combining physical training facilities with a comprehensive digital platform as a novel approach that addresses both on-site and remote learning needs.
2) We are focusing on joint curriculum development and shared training resources between Romania and Bulgaria, which is unique, fosters regional cooperation and creates a unified approach to skills development.
3) The emphasis on advanced technologies such as automation and robotics ensures that the training is aligned with the latest industry trends and labour market needs and will help prepare participants for future job markets.
4) The SkillsBridge lab equipment is meant to be mobile and will facilitate effective experiential training 
5) The training of vulnerable and underrepresented groups ensures that educational opportunities are equitable and inclusive, setting a new standard for accessibility in cross-border education initiatives.

titleEn: Regional Network for Inclusive Education
summaryEn: The project addresses the needs identified in the Programme documents to improve cooperation in the cross-border region in inclusive education. There are no joint Bulgarian-Romanian initiatives in this direction, with very few exceptions. The project therefore aims to make a progress by fulfilling two interrelated objectives: to build a sustainable and collaborative cross-border network of inclusive education professionals – Community of Practice (CoP); to improve the methodical capacity of these professionals to implement inclusive education policies, through mutual learning and exchange of best practices. The project operates in all 15 eligible NUTS3 regions. Its strategy is built in the following logical sequence: research, analysis and assessment of needs - development of resources and means of improvement - intervention (capacity building activities) - reporting of results, analysis and sustainability measures. The corresponding work packages and activities are arranged in a similar way. The WP1, envisages a large-scale study of the current state of inclusive education across the border region, its needs and challenges. Based on the research report, an international meeting of experts and stakeholders will decide the curricula of training schemes for educators. There will be two kind of such schemes: 6 thematic exchange of experience workshops in the field of inclusive education and 8 joint training seminars in the same direction. WP2 refers to the consolidation of the professional community of specialists working in the field of inclusive education from both countries through the use of the concept of Community of Practice - CoP (more precisely virtual CoP - VCoP) - this is part of the innovative contribution of the project . To this end, online tools, including a resource site and others, will be developed to provide this community with access to methodological resources and the possibility of remote communication. The project ends with a closing event - a conference to evaluate the achievements, disseminate the results and plan the future collaboration and development of the network. The main results are related to the continued cooperation after the end of the project, as well as to increase the capacity to carry out inclusive education in the target region. At least 150 specialists from both countries are expected to directly benefit from the project, and through them - many more students. The cross-border nature of the project is determined by the European approach to the development of education, which is based on the exchange of best practices and resources between member countries, rather than common legislation and regulations.

titleEn: Ensuring equal access to inclusive and quality education services, including by creating a sustainable joint pilot model for distance and on-line education and training in Byala-Giurgiu-Silistra
summaryEn:
Byala, Giurgiu and Silistra as well as the rest of the cross-border region faces several common territorial challenges in the sphere of inclusive education for children with SEN: limit access to quality education, including specialized services for children with SEN, lack of resources, training, and support, inadequate educational infrastructure, especially in rural and isolated areas, limited or lacking access to assistive technologies and adaptive learning tools hinders the educational progress of students with SEN. There is shortage of specialized educational services, such as sensory therapy, speech therapy, occupational therapy, and psychological support, which are essential for children with SEN. According to the existing data (highlighted in the Territorial Analysis) both countries face challenges related to the training and availability of educators who are prepared to work with SEN children and lack of digital/online educational tools and resources. There is a need for digital resources, allowing children with SEN to participate in distance learning. 

The overall objective of the EQUAL project is ensuring equal access to inclusive and quality education services, including by creating a sustainable pilot model for distance and on-line education and training in Byala-Giurgiu-Silistra.
The main outputs of the EQUAL project are:
- Investments in ensuring proper endowment for SEN joint learning facilities - renovation of specialised therapy rooms, delivery of sensory and occupational equipment and electric car for children with SEN. This equipment for Sensory-Integrative Therapy facilitates a supportive environment where children can better manage their sensory input, allowing them to focus and thrive in educational settings.
- Development of joint innovative cross-border education and training platform for ensuring equal access to inclusive and quality education services. 
- Collaborative cross-border network for supporting the education of children with SEN.

The EQUAL platform for cross-border online education and training for children with special educational needs (SEN) is an innovative practice that will be used by experts, parents and other stakeholders as follows: 


1.	Collaborative Network: online community where teachers, parents, and students will receive support, share resources, strategies and best practices. Based on the EQUAL platform, a partner network of experts and other stakeholders will be developed, and in addition, a "virtual resource center" with methodological materials for each of the target groups will be created for the needs of the "network". Each expert or parent of a child with SEN will be able to use the specially developed assessment tools, respectively the appropriate training materials, with ability to discuss the development of the case with a selected expert from the network. In this way, the platform will provide an opportunity for distance online learning, and individual support and assistance to parents and children with special educational needs (SEN).


2.	Teacher training: Providing educators with the necessary training to effectively teach and support children with SEN in an online environment.


3.	Creating personalized learning plans to meet the individual needs of each child with SEN.


4. Online SEN learning resources.


5.	Use of accessible technologies ensuring that the platform is accessible to children with different disabilities.


6.	Parent involvement: Involving parents and guardians in the educational process to provide additional support and ensure continuity of learning at home.


7.	Good practices: EQUAL platform will be a place for the exchange of good training practices for children with special educational needs (SEN).
This useful tool is a new approach through which experts, parents and other stakeholders from the cross-border region and beyond will be able to find useful tools for learning, work and cooperate, as well as share the experience and resources to provide more effective and better-quality services for children with special educational needs (SEN).
Thе innovative functionalities of the EQUAL platform ensures that this tool will be used long-term by the target groups.

titleEn: EDUCATION FOR INCLUSION - A CROSS-BORDER APPROACH
summaryEn:
Education in a safe and inclusive environment is a must in any community and the Romanian and Bulgarian communities have understood the importance of tackling joint challenges together as the work force mobility is always evolving on both sides of the Danube. According to recent European studies, bullying has become an increasing phenomenon in Europe, especially in schools, and it should be jointly addressed by finding common solutions to a common challenge. Therefore, on both sides of the Danube counties joint solutions should address it. In order for education activities to thrive and produce results, all hindering elements, such as bullying, should be removed or at least reduced. Dolj County Council in partnership with Dolj County Center for Educational Resources and Assistance, Belogradchik, Vratsa and Vidin Municipalities intends to tackle this important issue through common activities with Bulgarian and Romanian associated school partners. Then, they will take educational endeavors to the next step, by identifying professional aptitudes of students by means of exchange practices on the basis of an online certified career orientation platform, as an element of novelty approach, whose findings will be made available to all stakeholders in the target cross-border area as an element of novelty in approaching this raised social issue.
The overall objective of the project is the improvement of educational facilities, instruments and learning spaces as support for anti-bullying and inclusion initiatives followed by aptitude tests development for career orientation. The partners intend to implement a set of new methods able to tackle the challenges faced by the educational environments of most European countries: bullying among students. The specific objectives of the project include increasing the level of knowledge on bullying in schools both in Dolj County and in Bulgarian neighboring counties, Vidin and Vratsa, increasing the skills of professionals to manage bullying situations; encouraging the development of positive relationships with students and building a favorable climate in classrooms; improving strategies for effective intervention in bullying situations; reduce bullying by involving the most important actors correctly, professional orientation of students through certified methods.
There will be several approaches to be implemented by the partners:
The activities of the project approach this common challenge and provide the professionals with the means of handling bullying in schools. The common methods and tools used within the project activities will be replicable and may be used in other educational institutions as well.
The first approach would be to set up common resources and arrange a resource room for specialists from partner institutions in order to carry out joint activities to prevent bullying and increase the level of awareness of professionals about the harsh consequences of bullying. The aim would be to provide a safe and friendly environment for all children attending school, to promote positive relationships among children regardless of cultural background.
The second approach will consist of exchanges of experience between specialists in order to establish long-term collaborative relationships. The main purpose of these exchanges is to set up the common methods to tackle bullying in all target schools.
The third approach will consist of creating an online platform with multimedia content made by specialists in the field, useful in educating and counselling on bullying and cyber-bullying situations among school children and adults around them: parents, teachers, school counselors. The aptitude tests included in the online platform identify the ways in which students orient themselves in choosing their career.
The forth approach is carrying out a set of joint activities on the topic of anti-bullying, by approaching the relevant resolution methods and contribute to the feeling of being included for children involved in such activities. These activities will be performed once the set of common methods will be established after the exchanges between experts in the partner regions.
 The fifth approach is organizing a creative and educational camp for children and several arts and sports events in the partner regions. By the cross-border approach, Romanian children will acquire a sense of belonging to the European space, will have a clear understanding that their problems are also the problems of Bulgarian children and their common resolution is a strong message that unity is a better approach for all issues addressed by the project.
The project results will consist in an increased number of specialists on both sides of the Danube whose capacity of tackling bullying in schools is enhanced. Also, the number of students who can better handle bullying will increase and the number of students with a clearer future perspective is improved in the targeted cross- border area.

titleEn: Bridging Education Across the Danube
summaryEn:
The "BEAD—Bridging Education Across the Danube" project addresses significant and pressing challenges faced by the CB regions of Silistra (Bulgaria) and Calarasi (Romania). Both areas have low educational attainment, high illiteracy rates, limited access to practical and digital skills, and high unemployment rates, as cited by the INTERREG Programme description. The two regions are also isolated from well-developed areas in both countries due to poor infrastructure and connectivity. These factors have fueled depopulation, internal migration, and a widening socio-economic gap. The lack of practical skills relevant to the labour market, insufficient digital infrastructure, and cross-border communication barriers further increase the region’s developmental struggles. 
On the other hand, Silistra is cited for having reached 100% broadband coverage which provides potential for substantial improvement in connectivity via digital infrastructure to facilitate inclusivity and the cross-border aspect in education.

Overall Objective and Expected Change: Improve the quality, inclusiveness, and cross-border scope of educational services in the region Silistra-Ruse, BG—Calarasi, RO, through developing advanced educational infrastructure that supports hybrid learning environments and lifelong learning opportunities for all.
By introducing new educational resources, cross-border curricula, digital tools, and exchange programmes, the project aims to reach out to rural and less connected communities to curb educational gaps, enhance basic digital, green and language skills and support the workforce to meet employers’ needs. 
The expected change is the creation of a more integrated, practical, and inclusive education and training framework accessible to all, including those in remote areas. By the end of the project, learners in the region will have gained critical skills and knowledge that will foster cross-border collaboration, improve their employability, and promote sustainable economic development.

Main Outputs and Beneficiaries: 
Integrated Collaborative Learning Labs: Two upgraded labs, one in Silistra and one in Calarasi, equipped with modern digital tools like interactive displays and communication platforms. These labs will serve as hubs for cross-border collaboration, enabling joint projects, research, and real-time engagement between learners and educators from both sides.
Joint Cross-border Education and Training Scheme (CETS): A new curriculum to develop soft skills, digital literacy, and green competencies. This joint scheme will offer onsite and online learning options, ensuring inclusivity for students in remote areas or with physical limitations.
Hybrid Learning Solutions: Integrating hybrid learning models, combining in-person and online courses to make education more accessible, particularly for those facing geographical and socio-economic barriers.
Digital Toolkit: A freely available digital resource on green, digital, innovative and sustainable practices in the rural areas, designed to support students and local businesses in the long-term.

The project's primary beneficiaries include secondary school and vocational high school students, as well as university students and graduates from Silistra and Calarasi. Local businesses, educators, and community members will also be involved in LLL. 

Cross-border Approach: This is essential to the BEAD project because the challenges in Silistra and Calarasi are shared, yet there needs to be more cooperation between the two regions. Therefore, the project promotes intercultural exchange, collaboration and mobility by connecting learners, educators, and businesses across the Danube. 

What’s New/Original About the Project: Building on the previous lighthouse projects ‘Career Paths to Youth Labor Mobility’, ROBG-156 and VISA (ROBG-147), the BEAD project introduces several innovative elements:
Integrated Learning Labs: The interconnected learning labs in Silistra and Calarasi will provide students with real-time access to joint courses and collaborative projects, fostering practical and transferable skills. 
Joint Curriculum: The development of a unified, cross-border education and training scheme is a first in the region. The curriculum focuses on much-needed transversal skills often overlooked in traditional education systems, particularly in rural and disadvantaged areas.
Hybrid Learning Models: The project will introduce hybrid learning approaches, combining onsite and online learning - an emerging but underutilised model in the region. 
Focus on Green and Digital Skills: Creating a digital toolkit on green, digital, and sustainable practices aligns with evolving EU priorities, but it is an original addition in this specific cross-border context. 
Cross-border Engagement: The project strongly emphasises building long-term partnerships between students, educators, and businesses across the Danube, encouraging the free flow of knowledge and skills.

titleEn: “Implementation of cooperation business model for energy efficiency in cross border region by Agrovin Ltd and SARANTA Ltd - EnEfVin”
Introducing low-carbon tourism in the CBC area of Bulgaria and Turkiye
summaryEn:
Project aims to address several common territorial challenges in the Programme area, while also leveraging opportunities to promote sustainable and inclusive development. These challenges create opportunities for the project to contribute to the development of the cross-border region and promote territorial cohesion. Instead of merely overcoming impediments, the project seeks to strengthen and expand low-carbon tourism practices as a model solution for sustainable development and increased competitiveness in the region. Among the challenges addressed is the underdeveloped year-round tourist infrastructure where limitations are faced and this hinders the full potential of the CBC area as a tourist destination. Sustainable tourism practices such as the low-carbon tourism are needed to protect the region's environment and natural heritage. The project's efforts to strengthen the competitiveness of the local economy, especially through the tourism sector, contribute to economic diversification. 
The overall objective of project "Introducing low-carbon tourism in the CBC area of Bulgaria and Turkiye" - Low-carbon CBC is developing and implementing integrated solutions for low-carbon tourism in the cross-border region of Kirklareli Province, Harmanli and Svilengrad municipalities, along with applying joint efforts of the partners for reduction of the carbon footprint of the tourism sector in the area.
Low carbon tourism, also known as sustainable or eco-friendly tourism, is a concept that aims to minimize the negative environmental impact of tourism activities. It focuses on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, conserving natural resources, and promoting local communities' well-being. The goal of low carbon tourism is to create a sustainable tourism industry that benefits both the environment and local economies. Key aspects and practices are transportation, accommodation, waste management, conservation and biodiversity, community engagement, education and awareness. By adopting low carbon tourism practices, destinations and stakeholders can reduce their environmental impact, conserve resources, protect natural and cultural heritage, and create more sustainable and resilient tourism industries. Within the current project PPs are joining their efforts by starting the development of a Low-Carbon CBC tourism route. This is envisaged through marking main points on the route where is a visible tourism potential but a sufficient popularity is not always acquired. The route is almost 260 km long with main points Haskovo - Harmanli – Svilengrad – Edirne – Kirklareli – Demirkoy – Igneada. Along with the utilization of the available natural and cultural assets PPs emphasize on construction of low-carbon tourism infrastructure and equipment, and on adding cultural assets for diversification of the existing attractions. Outputs targeted are: pilot actions for introduction of low-carbon tourism in the area through the development of the integrated tourism route and needed infrastructure and equipment for it (charging stations for electrical vehicles, supply of electrical bicycles and electrical scooters) in Kirklareli, Demirkoy and Harmanli, elaboration of an action plan for further introduction of the low-carbon tourism concept in the CBC area of Bulgaria and Turkiye in order the solution to be taken up (RCO84; RCO116; RCR104); construction of dedicated cycling infrastructure supported in Svilengrad – 

1.2 km bicycle lane as attraction and opportunity for low-carbon transport for tourism (RCO58; RCR64; RCO74); 1 cultural and tourism site (Historical museum Harmanli) supported through Conservation, restoration and exposure of movable archaeological asset - an early-medieval pottery furnace (RCO58; RCR64; RCO74); carrying out 1 training and 1 joint seminar, organized by KCCI for the tourism business sector and organizations that can take up or upscale the developed solution. PPs plan to fully uptake the integrated and multi-sectoral approach, along with the “environmental sustainability by design” approach. Cross-border approach is a n integral part of the current project proposal as it recognizes the interconnectedness of neighboring regions and seeks to leverage this connectivity for mutual benefit and shared prosperity. By working together, PPs address the complex challenges more effectively, promote regional development, and foster peaceful and cooperative relationships where at the same time exchange good practices and experience. The project is new and original due to the essence of its partnership – wider, multi-sectoral, including regional and local authorities, cultural institutions and organizations representing the business for intoxication and application of a concept that is extremely accurate to the present time.  Low-carbon tourism is important for the sector as much as the tourism sector itself is important for the economic development of the area with focus on overcoming environmental challenges.

titleEn: Together We Reveal the Greatness of Nature for Sustainable Tourism Between Two Seas
summaryEn:
The main objective of the project is to upgrade and promote the CB tourist (pedestrian and bicycle) route"Between Two Seas", which will gain international importance,to stimulate the development of tourism and the uniqueness of the services and products provided,to stimulate economic development in the CB region by popularizing the natural and cultural historical heritage in a wide territorial scope.

Our ambitions are aimed at developing sustainable tourism that minimizes the impact on the biological environment and shapes the views of tourists before and during their trip, as well as to inspire environmentally friendly tourism practices. Tourism is a major economic industry in the CBregion and we want to contribute to the development of its various forms - alternative,rural,ecological,adventure,etc.

The implementation of measures for the development of the tourism industry in places slightly affected by man must simultaneously contribute to the protection of nature and the well-being of the local population. The CBregion is rich in natural features with great biodiversity, in which nature has impressive dimensions, national parks and local communities that have preserved their traditions. Offering a set of similar tourism practices dominated by communication with nature and active participation with a certain physical commitment for tourists (walking, cycling, riding, etc.) is our first important emphasis. Our second important emphasis is the promotion of rural and agritourism. These varieties of alternative tourism are an important potential for the development of the CBregion. Attracting visitors to the region of the created route will stimulate the initiative of farmers in the field of tourism,retention of the population in rural areas and their revival will be achieved. The possibility to provide a stay in a rural environment (house or other accommodation),contact with the hosts, access to the farm is a service that tourists expect. These activities are usually complemented by various types of cultural tourism (visiting monasteries, museums, archaeological and other sights, crafts school). In general, a profitable tourism product should be a mixture of all these. The combination of different types of tourism is an important element for the sustainable development of various services in the CBregion.

Achieving sustainable economic growth in the CBregion is real when analyzing the evolution in the tourism sector, which is aligned on the one hand with the interests of the hosts and on the other the visitors. All services in the territory must be tailored to the needs of tourists, their security and safety, and protection of natural resources and features.

The project proposal sets the following specific objectives:
- Getting to know and fostering a responsible attitude towards nature and its protection;
- Stimulating the motor activity of the younger generation, the practice of walking and cycling sports, outdoor sports;
- Expanding the potential of the developed cycle route "Tоur Strandzha" from the Black Sea to the Aegean Sea and connecting it with the existing European routes 6 and 13, which pass through the CBarea;
- Stimulating the development of alternative forms of tourism in the CBregion.
