In implementation of the Territorial Strategy of the Program, the implementation of the project idea affects the following types of interventions - application of ecosystem practices in the management of natural assets with tourism potential, development of sustainable tourism, through the development and marking of a tourist route from the BlackSea to the AegeanSea, digitalization, by creating an opportunity for digital tracking of the route and all the sights around it, competitiveness and business environment, by organizing the exchange of experience between business representatives in the cross-border region and presenting the "The Good Example".

The main activities of the project described in two WPs:
- Repair, rehabilitation and socialization of tourist infrastructure of a suburban park in the town of Elhovo
- Construction and socialization of tourist infrastructure of Ecological Park in Dokuzdere Region-Keshan
- A Concept development and marking of a cross-border tourist route "Between two seas"
- Joint development of marketing and advertising materials to promote the tourist potential of the cross-border region
- Organization and conduct of Eco Training"The Greatness of Nature"
- Exchange of experience "The Good Example"/network event with the participation of representatives of the tourism sector in the CB region/
- Organizing and conducting a bicycle tour "Between two seas"
With the implementation of the project idea, a joint integrated tourist product will be built, through:
- actions for the development of natural assets with tourism potential
- strengthening the ties between natural and cultural sites on both sides of the border
- stimulating the development of services in the field of tourism.

titleEn: Cross-Border Innovation for Sustainability in the Circular Economy in Textile and Meat Processing
summaryEn:
The "Cross-Border Innovation for Sustainability in the Circular Economy in Textile and Meat Processing" (CBISTEMP) project aims to foster sustainability and promote circular economy practices in the textile and meat processing industries across the Bulgaria-Türkiye cross-border region. Through innovative technologies, collaborative approaches, and knowledge exchange, the project seeks to address the pressing environmental challenges and economic opportunities within these sectors. Project partners - KAPITONE OOD from Bulgaria and "Mustafa Deniz and Partners" from Turkey - represent these sectors.
For the Textile Sector (KAPITONE OOD): The proposal includes the acquisition and implementation of a computerized multi-needle quilting machine and an ultrasonic quilting machine. These machines are designed to enhance production efficiency, reduce waste, and support the development of high-quality, sustainable textile products.
For the Meat Processing Sector ("Mustafa Deniz and Partners"): The plan involves the introduction of a "-40" degree shock chamber, a meat grinder that pulls out the tendons, and a Modified Atmosphere Packaging (MAP) machine. This equipment aims to improve product shelf life, reduce waste, and ensure the sustainable processing of meat products.
The programme area faces significant environmental challenges due to industrial waste, resource inefficiency, and pollution, particularly within the textile and meat processing sectors. These industries are crucial for the local economies but often operate within linear economic models that contribute to environmental degradation. The common challenge is to transition these sectors towards more sustainable, circular practices that reduce waste, enhance resource efficiency, and minimize environmental impacts while supporting economic growth.
The overall objective of the CBISTEMP project is to implement circular economy solutions in the textile and meat processing industries, thereby reducing environmental impacts, improving resource efficiency, and fostering sustainable economic growth. The expected change is a significant reduction in industrial waste and pollution, alongside the creation of new business opportunities and jobs within circular economy frameworks. This shift will not only improve environmental outcomes but also enhance the competitiveness and resilience of the local industries.
Main Outputs:
Development and implementation of new technologies and processes for waste reduction and resource efficiency in textile and meat processing.
Compilation of best practices and standards for circular economy implementation in the targeted industries.
Training and educational materials for industry stakeholders on circular economy principles and practices.
Forums, and campaigns to engage the broader community and stakeholders in circular economy initiatives.
The project adopts a cross-border approach to leverage the shared experiences, challenges, and opportunities within the Bulgaria-Türkiye region such as: Pooling Resources and Expertise: Combining resources, knowledge, and technological expertise from both countries to develop more effective and innovative solutions. Jointly tackling transboundary environmental issues that affect the region as a whole, necessitating coordinated action. Fostering economic ties and creating a stronger, more integrated market for sustainable products and practices across the border.
What sets the CBISTEMP project apart is its focus on integrating circular economy principles specifically within the textile and meat processing sectors through a cross-border collaboration framework. This targeted approach, combined with the development of industry-specific technologies and practices, offers a novel pathway to sustainability that is directly tailored to the unique economic and environmental contexts of the Bulgaria-Türkiye region. Furthermore, the project's emphasis on stakeholder engagement and capacity building aims to create a lasting impact by embedding circular economy principles into the fabric of local industries and communities.
The cross-border collaboration between Bulgaria and Türkiye is vital for pooling resources, sharing knowledge, and jointly addressing the shared environmental challenges facing both nations. This cooperation enhances the project's ability to develop tailored, innovative solutions that can be applied across the region, fostering economic integration and environmental sustainability.
The originality of CBISTEMP lies in its targeted approach to integrating circular economy principles into the textile and meat processing sectors, facilitated by specific, cutting-edge equipment and comprehensive stakeholder engagement. This project sets a precedent for sustainable industrial innovation in the Bulgaria-Türkiye cross-border region, offering scalable models for broader regional and global application.

titleEn: CB technological Eco-Sustainable Union through circular and resource efficient investments
summaryEn:
The common territorial challenges addressed by the project include significant waste generation, particularly e-waste, energy consumption, and reliance on primary raw materials in both the metal processing industry in Bulgaria and the IT industry in Turkey. Both the metal processing industry in Bulgaria and the IT industry in Turkey contribute to substantial waste generation, including e-waste, which poses environmental and health risks if not managed properly. Energy-intensive processes in both industries lead to high energy consumption, contributing to carbon emissions and environmental degradation. Both industries heavily rely on primary raw materials, leading to resource depletion and increasing pressure on natural ecosystems. These challenges hinder the establishment of circular production processes and models, ultimately affecting the competitiveness of enterprises on both sides of the border.
The overall objective of the project is significant reduction in waste generation, incl. e-waste, energy consumption and primary raw materials in the metal processing industry in Bulgaria and the IT industry in Türkiye, promoting the establishment of circular production processes and models, increasing the competitiveness of enterprises on both sides of the border through a near-zero waste business model.
Specific project objective 1: Management, implementation and reporting of pilot actions in both Bulgaria and Türkiye to demonstrate the effectiveness of circular production processes and near-zero-waste business models.
Specific project objective 2: Implementation of circular and resource-efficient solutions in the production process of the 2 enterprises through investments in equipment.
. By focusing on waste reduction, energy efficiency, and circular design principles, the project aims to mitigate environmental impacts, enhance resource efficiency, and foster sustainable practices in both industries. Additionally, the project's emphasis on near-zero waste business models and the adoption of energy and resource-saving approaches aligns with the overarching objectives of the INTERREG VI-A IPA Bulgaria - Türkiye Programme, which seeks to promote cross-border cooperation and sustainable development in the region. Therefore, the project's relevance lies in its capacity to address common challenges, capitalize on shared opportunities, and contribute to the overall goals of the programme area.
The main outputs of the project: 
Output "Pilot Circular Economy Initiatives Implemented in Collaboration with Stakeholders" - executing pilot initiatives according to established plans, mobilizing resources, coordinating activities, and monitoring progress to ensure successful implementation. The output entails the successful development and implementation of pilot circular economy initiatives in collaboration with relevant stakeholders in BG&TR. The initiatives aim to demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of circular economy practices and resource-efficient behaviours within specific sectors or industries.
Output “Implemened circular and resource-efficient solutions” - Exploring, creating, and trailing novel approaches to address circular economy challenges involves integrating various new and established methods. These undertakings promote sustainable and equitable economic advancement within the cross-border region, facilitating the shift towards a circular and resource-efficient economy. Activities aim to transition businesses from linear to circular models, thereby curbing resource consumption and fostering inclusive growth.
The target groups, which will benefit from the project outputs are: 2 Local public authorities; Infrastructure and (public) service providers; Interest groups including NGOs; SME; Business support organisation; General public. 
Cross-border cooperation is essential to achieving the project's objectives and results for several reasons. The established collaboration between the partners from different regions of the two bordering countries allows for access to specialized resources, expertise, and technologies that may not be available locally. For example, the project will benefit from advanced manufacturing techniques or innovative IT solutions that are more readily available in one region than the other. By bringing together partners with diverse backgrounds and experiences, the project will leverage a wealth of knowledge and expertise. This collaborative approach enables the exchange of best practices, lessons learned, and innovative ideas, leading to more effective and sustainable solutions. 
The project represents a pioneering initiative in cross-border collaboration between Bulgaria and Türkiye to address common challenges in the metal processing and IT industries. By fostering knowledge exchange and cooperation, the project goes beyond existing practices and uses synergies between the two countries.

titleEn: Driving Cross-Border Circular Pilot in Printed Circuit Board Production and Glass Processing
summaryEn:
Programme area common challenge the project tackles is the need for improving sustainability and resource efficiency within the realm of 2 industries in Bulgaria-Türkiye CB region - manufacture of loaded electronic boards and glass processing. Environmental and resource-related challenges that need to be addressed are: 
Manufacture of loaded electronic boards - printed circuit boards (PCBs) requires significant amounts of raw materials, incl. metals (copper, gold, silver), plastics, chemical additives and involves multiple energy-intensive stages (material extraction, fabrication, assembly, testing). PCB manufacturing generates significant amounts of waste, including trimmings, offcuts, and rejected boards. The disposal of obsolete or end-of-life PCBs contributes to e-waste accumulation, which is a challenge for recycling and proper disposal. Disposal of PCBs, either through landfilling or incineration releases hazardous substances into the environment. Addressing these challenges requires integrated environmental approach as adopting cleaner production technologies, promoting resource efficiency and recycling, fostering collaboration across the industry to drive innovation and best practices.
Glass processing, incl. cutting, shaping, and finishing, also has several environmental and resource-related challenges. It requires significant energy inputs during heating and shaping stages, which contributes to greenhouse gas emissions and climate change. Glass processing techniques as cutting and polishing require water for cooling and lubrication, which may strain local water resources and contribute to water pollution if not properly managed and treated. Glass processing methods involve the use of chemicals for cleaning, etching, coating and improper handling and disposal of these chemicals leads to soil and water contamination, posing risks to human health and ecosystems. Glass processing generates various types of waste, including offcuts, trimmings, scrap glass, which may end up in landfills if not recycled or reused, contributing to the depletion of landfill space and environmental pollution. Addressing these challenges requires technological innovations and industry best practices as improving energy efficiency, optimizing water usage, implementing pollution prevention measures, promoting recycling and circular economy principles, and adopting cleaner production technologies.
To address these challenges, Hedy Computers EOOD and AÇIKGÖZ CAM ve PENCERE SİSTEMLERİ developed the project “HEAC Pilot” which overall objective is to implement innovative circular economy practices in the production processes of printed circuit boards (PCBs) and glass processing within the CB context. This involves developing and piloting sustainable, resource-efficient and circular approaches that minimize waste generation, promote material reuse and recycling, and enhance the environmental sustainability of these industries across borders. Through collaborative efforts and knowledge exchange between the partners, the project aims to demonstrate the feasibility and benefits of circular economy principles in PCB production and glass processing, ultimately contributing to the transition towards more sustainable and resilient manufacturing practices.
The proposed technological investments in the 2 enterprises in the CB region will optimize resource use, minimize environmental impact, facilitate the implementation of sustainable production practices. LP1 will develop and launch a production line for PCBs including recycling, PP2 will develop and launch an automated glass processing line connected to the cutting process. 
Main project outputs: 1) supported main economic activities of 2 enterprises in the CB region by investing in resource-efficient production technologies; 2) Re-shaped first stage of glass processing to reduce waste generated and increase the life of the final product through increased capacity - 120 pieces of tempered finished mixed glass production per hour from the initial production quantity of 25 pieces/hour); 3) replaced virgin material with "secondary raw material" - PCBs production using materials from old PCBs); 4) prolonged life of PCBs that otherwise will be disposed - repair of PCBs; 5) waste reduction - old PCBs will not be discharged as waste, they will be used in new production. 
The key components of project collaborative approach are: CB Collaboration between the 2 companies from BG and TR to leverage expertise, share resources, foster synergies for achieving common sustainability goals; open dialogue and collaboration to accelerate the adoption of sustainable technologies and practices across the region; pilot actions to showcase best practices for enhancing product durability and resource efficiency. CB approach will address environmental challenges across the border more effectively and promote coordinated action to achieve common sustainability goals based on partners’ strengths and resources.

titleEn: Green Renewable Energy & Efficiency Network of Sustainable Textile and Hospitality Environmental Practices
summaryEn:
Lead Partner: DELENA DD EOOD
Partner: Şapçı Akaryakıt- Yer Karoları ve Turizm İşletmeleri Sanayi ve Ticaret Ltd
The "GREENSTEP" project aims to foster cross-border collaboration between DELENA DD EOOD, a Bulgarian textile company, and Şapçı Akaryakıt- Yer Karoları ve Turizm İşletmeleri Sanayi ve Ticaret Ltd, a Turkish hotel operator. The project focuses on implementing sustainable practices in the textile and hospitality industries to promote energy efficiency and reduce environmental impact.
GREENSTEP Objectives:
-	To implement energy-efficient measures and renewable energy solutions in the textile and hospitality sectors.
-	To enhance the competitiveness of DELENA DD EOOD and Şapçı Akaryakıt through technological modernization and sustainable practices.
-	To contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and promote environmental sustainability in the cross-border region.
Key GREENSTEP Activities:
-	Supply and installation of energy-efficient equipment in DELENA DD EOOD's textile production facilities, including knitting machines, ironing equipment, and steam generators.
-	Renovation of Şapçı Akaryakıt's hotel building to improve energy efficiency, including the replacement of sheathing insulation and windows.
-	Knowledge exchange and capacity building activities to promote best practices in sustainable textile production and hospitality management.
-	Cross-border collaboration and coordination to ensure effective implementation of project activities and exchange of experiences between Bulgarian and Turkish partners.
Expected GREENSTEP Outcomes: 
-	Increased energy efficiency and reduced carbon footprint in the textile and hospitality sectors.
-	Enhanced competitiveness of DELENA DD EOOD and Şapçı Akaryakıt through improved production processes and reduced operational costs.
-	Strengthened cross-border partnerships and knowledge sharing networks for sustainable development in the region.
-	Contribution to the achievement of environmental objectives under the INTERREG VI-A IPA Bulgaria Türkiye Programme.
The "GREENSTEP" project represents a strategic collaboration between DELENA DD EOOD and Şapçı Akaryakıt- Yer Karoları ve Turizm İşletmeleri Sanayi ve Ticaret Ltd to promote sustainable practices and energy efficiency in the textile and hospitality industries. Through joint efforts and cross-border cooperation, the project aims to achieve tangible environmental and economic benefits while fostering innovation and competitiveness in the participating companies.

titleEn: Ecological Leap for Circular Wood Processing Industry
summaryEn:
Project CIRCULAR2GETHER is developed in full correspondence to the strategic and thematic scope of the INTERREG VI-A IPA PROGRAMME BULGARIA- TÜRKIYE as it targeted at strengthening the territorial cohesion taking
into account sectoral disparities in the CB area and the need for more cross-border coordinated actions in the energy and environmental fields. Thus, the project brings together local private project partners from Harmanli (BG) and Kesan (TR) who complement each other with their different perspectives and share the overall mission to develop sustainable solutions for integrating circular and green economy approaches in wood processing industry and boost cross-border coordinated actions for ensuring environmentally friendly CB region. The concept of adapting the circular business models through resource efficiency and waste reduction derives from covering the needs of modern society in the long run without jeopardizing quality of life of future generations. 
CIRCULAR2GETHER activities include mandatory combination of investment and soft type of actions that are in close synergy and involve introducing and promoting business models and tools, which will aim to bring about change in the wood processing industry and foster circular manufacturing practices. By promoting the principles of sustainability, resource efficiency and waste reduction, the project will reshape the way products are designed and processed, while avoiding >10% of virgin materials, generating by 15% less waste and prolongation of the products' life. Furthermore, an industrial symbioses is achieved as the waste material will be re-used in another wood production processes.
By driving the transition towards circular construction, the partnering companies will achieve a lasting impact and contribute to a greener, more sustainable future in full accordance with the European and national environmental legislation, horizontal principles and Healthy environment, waste treatment and recycling initiatives.
Furthermore, as the Green Deal emphasizes, the combination of practice and learning is the core of the policy for sustainable transition to a circular economy. In this response, CIRCULAR2GETHER will provide solutions and bring partners' accumulated knowledge and experience in managerial, economic, environmental aspect to all interested parties how to keep its production in a technical cycle free of waste.
The project's solutions will provide guidance to wood processing professionals, other production sectors, policymakers and stakeholders, enabling them to implement circular practices at various levels, from local to regional.

titleEn: Maritsa Timeless Journey
summaryEn: The main challenge addressed by the project with acronym Times the seasonality and lack of year-round tourism in the cross-border area of Bulgaria and Turkey. Both countries experience significant fluctuations in tourist arrivals, with peak visitation during specific periods, particularly centered around the summer months. This creates economic dependency on these specific periods, leading to financial challenges for tourism-related businesses and reduced employment opportunities during the off-peak seasons. Additionally, the concentration of tourists during peak seasons strains local infrastructure, impacts the visitor experience, and puts pressure on cultural sites and natural areas. The overall objective of the “Maritsa Timeless Journey” project is to unlock the region's year-round tourism potential, drive sustainable economic growth, and improve regional competitiveness, supporting digital tourism transformation. The project aims to achieve this by developing and implementing a pilot year-round tourism product named “Maritsa Timeless Journey”. This tourism product will be based on the common historical heritage of Bulgaria and Turkey, focusing on the Maritsa River Trade Route and the cultural diversity of the cross-border region. By creating an all-season tourism product, the project seeks to reduce the dependency on peak seasons, enhance the region's attractiveness to tourists throughout the year, and generate sustainable economic benefits for local communities. The project will produce several key outputs: Current repair, renovation, and revitalization of the History Museum "Prof. Alexander Fol" in Malko Tarnovo, providing an enriched cultural attraction for visitors; Establishment of a "City Archive" digital center in Edirne, serving as a scientific tourism and educational hub; Restoration and conservation of "Izvora na Belonogata"/"Gerganina chesma" in Harmanli, preserving a significant natural heritage site; Development of a joint solution for boosting year-round cross-border tourism, encouraging collaborative efforts between Bulgaria and Turkey; Pilot development of the year-round labeled tourism product "Maritsa Timeless Journey," serving as a model for integrated all-season tourism; Production of a promotional film "Maritsa Timeless Journey," raising awareness and promoting the region as a year-round destination. The beneficiaries of the project outputs include local communities, tourists, cultural institutions, educational institutions, and tourism-related businesses in the cross-border area. The cross-border approach is essential for the success of the project because it aims to address the common challenge of seasonality and year-round tourism in the region. By collaborating between Bulgaria and Turkey, the project partners will pool their resources, expertise, and cultural heritage to develop a joint solution for integrated tourism development – a common methodology for standrardization of year-round tourism labeling. The cross-border approach facilitates the sharing of best practices, the exchange of knowledge, and the promotion of cultural diversity, resulting in a more comprehensive and impactful year-round tourism product. The uniqueness of the "Maritsa Timeless Journey" project lies in its focus on turning the region's diverse cultural heritage and history into a valuable asset. Instead of trying to overcome the differences between Bulgaria and Turkey, the project capitalizes on these differences and creates a joint tourism product based on the shared history and the Maritsa River Trade Route. This approach ensures the preservation and promotion of the unique cultural heritage of the region while fostering sustainable tourism development. The project's emphasis on a year-round labeled tourism product is also innovative, as it seeks to move away from seasonality and create a more stable and thriving tourism economy in the cross-border area.

titleEn: CrossBorder MetalSustain Connect - ZKI - VOLTA & Armosan Initiative
summaryEn:
The challenges to the industrial sector from the CB area in the context of double transition objectives are significant, given the unsatisfactory starting points (low levels of digitalization and resource productivity, very high levels of carbon intensity). The project aims to address several common territorial challenges within the programme area: limited sustainable development initiatives, resource-intensive intensity in the CB region, environmental degradation, disparities in economic development and cross-border cooperation. Many areas in the CB region still rely heavily on traditional industries that are resource-intensive and environmentally harmful. Shifting towards more sustainable and innovative practices is crucial for reducing environmental impact and increasing economic resilience. The transformation of the companies' production suitable for a climate-neutral, resource-efficient economy and reduce waste throughout the product lifecycle is the main goal of the project. The project fosters collaboration and knowledge exchange between Bulgaria and Türkiye, contributing to improved cross-border cooperation and alignment of policies and strategies for sustainable development.
The project overall objective, within the framework of developing circular bio-based business models, solutions, and products, is to catalyze the transition to a circular and resource-efficient economy in the Bulgaria-Türkiye cross-border region and to transform the companies' production suitable for a climate-neutral economy and reduce waste across the entire product lifecycle. The initiative aims to foster the adoption of circular economy principles among 2 enterprises and stakeholders in the region. By promoting practices such as resource optimization, waste reduction, and product lifecycle management, the initiative seeks to shift towards more sustainable and resilient economic models. Through pilot actions and investments in equipment and technology, the initiative will facilitate the implementation of sustainable production practices among participating enterprises. This includes the adoption of eco-friendly technologies, energy-efficient processes, and waste-free production methods. By promoting circular and resource-efficient business models, solutions, and products, the initiative aims to reduce the environmental impact of economic activities in the region. This includes minimizing resource consumption, greenhouse gas emissions, pollution, and waste generation throughout the product lifecycle.
The main outputs within the project are related to embracement, development and testing new solutions to tackle with issues of circular economy - combination of several new solutions and existing practices developed, adopted, and implemented, which support the sustainable and inclusive economic growth of the CB region and related to transition to a circular and resource efficient economy by activities for transformation of businesses from linear to circular economy and reducing the resource consumption. The project's focus on sustainable development and circular economy principles will support local governments in achieving their environmental and economic objectives, infrastructure and service providers through improved efficiency, reduced costs, and enhanced service quality and interest groups including by gaining access to valuable information, resources, and networks related to sustainable development and environmental conservation. SMEs will benefit from the project outputs through increased access to sustainable technologies, practices, and markets. 
The integrated new approaches adopted in the project combine investments, transfer of know-how, management and development of circular bio-based business models, resource-efficient solutions and products. The Cross-border cooperation between the two project partners is necessary for the achievement of the project’s objectives and results for reasons related to the need for: shared resources and assets, complementary circular and resource-efficient business models, shared management and communication strategies, cross-border cooperation and knowledge exchange. By taking a cross-border approach, the CBMSC-ZVA Initiative will increase the effect of these shared resources more effectively, combining the strengths and unique characteristics of each side. This cross-border approach amplifies the impact of efforts and increases the region's competitiveness.
The combination of approaches, methods and collaborations between the partners with the aim of reducing waste and achieving resource efficiency in the new within the project. The implementation of zero-waste production bio technology in Bulgaria, combined with resource efficiency in Türkiye, builds on the existing business models of traditional circular characteristics, adding the availability of resource efficiency and reducing the footprint of both enterprises on the environment.

titleEn: Cooperation for reloading tourism generation skills in the border areas of Yambol and Kirklareli
summaryEn:
The project aims to drive tourism growth, foster sustainable practices, and promote economic development in Yambol and Kirklareli. It seeks to position these regions as attractive destinations by improving tourism infrastructure and enhancing the skills of the workforce. The project includes renovating and establishing tourism and cultural centers, promoting collaboration between businesses and educational institutions, and providing training programs for unemployed people and existing staff engaged in the tourism industry.
Tourism is the common sector of the CB area covered by the territorial strategy, which is giving opportunities for cooperation and working in the direction of achieving sustainable and inclusive economic and social growth.
The common challenges of the tourism ecosystem and its economic actors in its most part are relating to the recovery of the post - COVID 19 on both sides and adaptation of the economic operators to the new tendencies. 
The main challenges faced by the tourism sector in the target areas include business closures and job losses, changing travel preferences and behaviors due to the pandemic, limited local market for tourism services, and language barriers and digital promotion issues for local operators. 
The PPs are aware that there is a need to increase the number of professional tourism experts in the region and make the tourism sector more attractive to young people.
Their main goal of the project is to increase the adaptability of the labor market in the tourism sector, focusing on reskilling and upskilling existing staff and attracting more young people to the sector. 
The solutions proposed by the partners include developing a joint plan to increase tourism attractiveness, establishing infrastructure for training and skills development, improving tourism promotion capabilities, facilitating exchange programs between Turkish and Bulgarian operators, and diversifying tourism offerings based on regional potentials. These solutions aim to meet the specific needs of the target areas, such as the limited availability of specialized education and training in tourism and the lack of channels for specific training in event, festival, cultural, and shopping tourism. 
The project builds upon previous initiatives and aims to enhance the skills of those already employed in the industry, improve the competitiveness of employers, and contribute to the growth of local tourism. It also addresses the training needs of individuals involved in community center activities and seeks to unlock the full potential of festival tourism through professional training.
The main outputs of the project are:
- Joint 5-year plan for increasing tourism attractiveness: The project will develop and implement a comprehensive plan targeting the recruitment of young people, particularly NEETs, in the tourism sector.
- Infrastructure for reskilling and upskilling: The project will establish the necessary infrastructure to provide training opportunities for the existing staff engaged in the tourism sector.
- The project will enhance the capacity of tourism operators by providing training in digital tools and IT marketing technologies. 
- SkıllsInTourism will facilitate exchange programs and cooperation between Turkish and Bulgarian tourism and business actors, fostering knowledge sharing and collaboration in the industry.
- The project will focus on promoting and developing cultural and festival tourism in the Yambol region and urban and shopping tourism in the Kirklareli province. 
The project presents a new and innovative approach to addressing the challenges and opportunities in the tourism sector in the target areas of Yambol and Kirklareli. It brings together a diverse partnership of businesses, educational institutions, cultural organizations, and local policy makers, creating a collaborative and multidimensional approach to tourism development. By promoting CBC and leveraging the unique cultural and urban tourism assets of Yambol and Kirklareli, the project aims to attract more visitors, generate greater economic impact, and establish the regions as prominent destinations in the broader tourism market. One of the unique aspects of the project is its focus on skills development and capacity building. 
Also, it emphasizes the importance of CBC and knowledge exchange. It aims to diversify tourism offerings and promote the sustainable development of rural, eco, and cultural tourism, as well as urban-leisure and shopping tourism.

titleEn: Joint responsibility and sustainable development for future in CBC region
summaryEn:
The jointly developed project idea is based on a common approach to determine the role of the specific business, its degree of impact, possible risks and ways to actively participate in decision-making related to climate change; realizes a common goal, through the application of measures, management tools and specific activities for mitigation and adaptation; covers joint activities between partners in the cross-border region; partners demonstrate readiness for common action – changing the business model and taking an active civil role.
The opportunity to work together to implement the recommended measures from the performed audits of both enterprises is an opportunity to achieve jointly set goals in this project proposal. The main goal of the project is the joint implementation of urgent measures for energy efficiency in production enterprises in the CB region, through the implementation of technological equipment and the introduction of a system for monitoring, control and management of energy consumption. The relevance of the project is indisputable because it will lead to a saving of energy resources of over 40%. The implementation of project activities and the communication of enterprises for the implementation of joint initiatives will contribute to the territorial convergence of businesses and will open new opportunities for cooperation in their common economic activity. The two production enterprises join efforts to overcome the common challenges of the modern world, through the implementation of this joint project, which will certainly contribute to achieving energy efficiency and reducing the amount of energy consumed, respectively will lead to a reduction in the amount of greenhouse gases generated by their activity. The established partnership and the set goals, planned activities and expected results are tailored to support the sustainable development of enterprises and to contribute in their scale to achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement and the European Green Deal. The drive for the development of two ambitious companies in the person of their owners is the main reason for the search for the right solutions, modern technologies and cross-border cooperation in line with contemporary political and economic challenges. The planning of activities, goals and future development of enterprises is related to optimization and implementation of energy efficient solutions and technologies, as well as more effective management and reduction of energy consumption. Improving energy efficiency in enterprises will have a positive impact in terms of economic growth and the creation of new jobs, and saving energy will also lead to saving financial resources. At the same time, the partners will research, accumulate knowledge, look for solutions for the implementation of renewable energy sources. Effective solutions require proper planning, specific expertise and serious investment, which will lead to higher capital costs for businesses.

titleEn: Touch Your Cultural and Natural Heritage
summaryEn:
The focus of the Project proposal with acronym: “TOUCH” is over three of the five specific objectives of the Call, namely: Competitiveness and business environment; Tourism and Ecosystem practices and services in the management of natural assets with tourism potential.
Its overall objective is: To promote sustainable cross-border cooperation and cultural exchange between Project partners through the preservation of historical heritage, promotion of traditional crafts and the development of craft and tradition-based tourism, while also fostering environmental awareness and cooperation of public and business organizations. 
Project Specific Objectives as defined by the Partners are:
- To restore and install lighting on Sarachane bridge, a historical heritage in Edirne, Turkey, in order to preserve its cultural significance and enhance its attractiveness for tourists and locals alike.
- To reconstruct and repair park space of wide public importance in Dimitrovgrad, Bulgaria, incorporating elements inspired by the traditional craft of "saldzhiystvo," thus creating a public space that reflects the region's cultural heritage and promotes local crafts.
- To collaboratively develop a comprehensive strategy for craft and tradition-based tourism in the cross-border region, which will outline actionable steps and initiatives to leverage the area's cultural heritage and crafts for sustainable tourism development.
- To organize the "Journey of Crafts" event, which will involve a cultural exchange along the Maritza River, showcasing traditional crafts and practices from both regions, fostering cultural appreciation, and promoting cross-border tourism.
- To conduct an environmental cleaning event in Edirne, Turkey, with the active participation of various institutions and organizations from both regions, aiming to raise awareness about environmental cleanliness, conservation, and the importance of cross-border cooperation for environmental protection.
The Project addresses several common challenges and opportunities which are in line with the defined needs and development potentials within the Strategy for Integrated Territorial Development of the CBC area. 
To strengthen territorial potentials and existing cross-border linkages, the project is focused on enhancing and leveraging the shared strengths and assets of both areas rather than merely trying to overcome obstacles. This approach involves building upon the existing positive aspects of the areas and fostering cooperation to create a mutually beneficial environment. For this reason, Project partners are going to make a thorough analysis of the cultural, historical, economic, and environmental aspects of both areas to identify commonalities and synergies. Highlighting these shared strengths will help develop their common strategy for Tourism development and create a foundation for collaboration and mutual growth.
The organization of the common event that starts in Dimitrovgrad and finishes in Edirne is a showcase the traditions, crafts, and heritage of both regions. 
The Project also aims to facilitate connections between businesses and entrepreneurs from both regions. Encouraging cross-border trade and collaboration can lead to economic growth and new opportunities for businesses on both sides.
Through the event in Dimitrovgrad and Edirne, the Project is expected to encourage the formation of cross-border partnerships and networks between local organizations, cultural institutions, tourism agencies, and environmental groups. 
Leveraging cultural heritage and traditional crafts to boost tourism in the region, attracting visitors interested in experiencing unique cultural aspects.
Tourism and increased economic activity resulting from the project will positively impact local businesses and create job opportunities.
The environmental cleaning event and collaborative efforts promote environmental consciousness will lead to more sustainable practices in both regions.
By restoring historical heritage and promoting traditional crafts, the project contributes to the preservation of cultural assets for future generations.
And last but not least – the Project Is expected to enhance diplomatic and friendly relations between the two regions, potentially leading to further cooperation in other areas.
Integrating green infrastructure elements in the park and considering eco-friendly lighting solutions for the bridge go beyond typical park and bridge development practices. These approaches prioritize environmental sustainability, storm water management, and biodiversity conservation, setting a precedent for greener public spaces.
Incorporating innovative storytelling methods, heritage interpretation techniques, and cultural installations elevates the park and bridge projects beyond their physical structures. It creates a deeper connection with the region's history, crafts, and traditions, offering visitors a richer and more immersive experience.

titleEn: "Business model for energy efficiency in cross border region of Chicken group Ltd and Aytach et Ltd - GREEN FOOD"
Tourism through culture - our common future
summaryEn:
The main objective of the project is to restore and preserve the cultural achievements of artists, creators and sculptors, to popularize the specific spiritual climate of the region, to cultivate a desire and high criteria for creative expression among young people, for sustainable development of cross-border tourism potential.

With the implementation of the project idea, the two cultural institutions set the following specific objectives:
- preservation of tangible and intangible cultural heritage;
- encouraging the development of lesser-known cultural heritage sites and practices in order to develop their potential and reduce pressure on well-known “hotspots”;
- support for the professional development of young artists;
- overcoming seasonality by supporting activities that stimulate the development of alternative forms of tourism and generate attendance in the inactive (low) season.
- promoting the development of joint strategies and strengthening cooperation between cultural institutions in the region.

In implementation of the Territorial Strategy of the Programme, the implementation of the project idea will have impact on the following types of interventions - application of ecosystem practices in stimulating creation, through activities that provoke creativity and engagement, to build new values and lifestyles (WP2 - activity 

2.2 - Organization and conduct of an plein air "Dialogues"), development of sustainable tourism, through establishing a Cultural-Educational Centre and Museum in the city of Burgas (WP1 - Activity 

1.1) and organizing a joint event - round table and a campaign, which demonstrate art and creativity as a potential for the development of "creative" tourism in the cross-border region to business representatives in the cross-border region and presenting the potential of young and established artists, digitization, through the application of new marketing technologies, elaboration of materials that will demonstrate our thematic destinations to provoke the imagination of potential tourists, to feel the atmosphere of the region, to feel our hospitality before even making a reservation and all the attractions around, competitiveness and business environment, through the realization of a round table and meeting between business representatives, artists and creators from the region to generate ideas for the development of thematic destinations that will provoke investment interest, their initiative and entrepreneurship on the part of businesses in order to improve and upgrade the services provided.

Main activities in the project idea separeted in two work paquages are:
- Repair and reconstruction of the building of the Graphic Base-Burgas to establish a "Cultural-Educational Centre and Museum"
- Joint development of a concept for thematic branding and promotion of the cross-border region and development of a sustainable tourist product "Tourism on the go"
- Organization and conduct of a networking event - a round table on the topic "Culture - our common future"
- Organization and conduct of a plein air "Dialogues"
- Organizing and conducting a joint promotional tour "Tourism on the go"

With the implementation of the project activities, we will reach the following target groups:
 - students and pupils, studying different fields of art;
- creators;
- representatives of the tourism industry (hoteliers, tour operators, non-governmental organizations, branch organizations working in the field of culture and tourism);
- municipalities (departments of culture and tourism) to provide information and materials about their territory in order to promote it.

The ultimate goal of the project idea is to develop a significant synergy between creativity, culture and tourism, to strengthen and preserve local traditions and cultural heritage, to create new approaches and practices for using cultural resources as a tool for economic development in order to expand the tourist season, increase the sustainability in the sector and expand the economic profile of cities by enhancing creative industries, encouraging cultural understanding and developing products and services to attract the interest of visitors and ensure sustainable economic growth.

With the implementation of the project idea, a joint integrated tourist product will be built, which unites:
 - actions to develop the creative potential of the cross-border region with tourist potential
- strengthening the ties between artists and cultural sites on both sides of the border
- stimulating the creativity of young people.

titleEn: To preserve biodiversity and nature for our future
summaryEn:
The project aims to enhance tourism attractiveness and promote sustainable practices in the cross-border region of Enez (Turkey) and Bakadjik (Bulgaria) by addressing the common challenge of limited infrastructure and environmental awareness.

Overall Objective:
The project's overall objective is to create a more sustainable and appealing cross-border region by developing and implementing new solutions. These solutions will include environmentally friendly food sales areas, solar energy systems, recycling points, and educational initiatives to raise awareness about environmental conservation.

Expected Change:
Through the implementation of the project, the region will experience an increase in the number of visitors, along with improved levels of satisfaction among tourists due to heightened environmental consciousness. The project will foster a sense of pride and identity in the cross-border community by preserving shared cultural heritage and promoting sustainable tourism practices.

Main Outputs and Beneficiaries:
The main outputs of the project include the establishment of environmentally friendly food sales areas, installation of solar energy systems, creation of recycling points, and the organization of educational events. The local communities, women's cooperatives, students, tourists, and environmental organizations will benefit from these outputs.

Cross-Border Approach:
The cross-border approach is essential to address the common challenges faced by both Enez and Bakadjik. Collaboration between municipalities, NGOs, educational institutions from both sides ensures a holistic and integrated implementation of sustainable solutions, leveraging the strengths and expertise of each partner.

New/Original Aspects:
The project's focus on environmentally friendly solutions, such as solar energy systems and recycling points, sets it apart from conventional tourism initiatives. The emphasis on joint activities, like the "Respect for Nature School" and the Green Team building event, fosters cross-border cooperation, cultural exchange, and environmental awareness among students and professionals. The comprehensive and sustainable approach of the project positions it as an innovative model for territorial development in the cross-border region.

titleEn: Empowerment & Governance for Action in the Cross-Border Region
summaryEn:
The overall objective of the Governance project is to support the Strategy Board in its tasks to govern the Territorial Strategy of the INTERREG VI-A IPA Bulgaria – Türkiye 2021—2027 Programme and thus ensure the achievement of Programme’s Specific Objective “Fostering the integrated and inclusive social, economic and environmental local development, culture, natural heritage, sustainable tourism and security, in areas other than urban areas” under Priority 2 “Integrated development of the cross-border region”.
Specific objectives of the project aim at building the capacity of stakeholders for the effective fulfilment of their tasks, enhancing the efficiency of decision-making processes, improving the collaboration between SB members for better outcomes, facilitating their active and inclusive participation in the implementation of the TS, developing mechanisms for accountability on decisions for their long-term impacts on social, economic, and environmental well-being of the CB region. 
In this connection, with its package of planned actions and activities, the current project proposal addresses the need of a more supportive approach with respect to the bodies burdened with the overall responsibility for the efficient implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the TS. In terms of critical tasks and functions it is expected to result in better endorsement of the TS, improved decision making and project selection process, more effective monitoring process of the TS.
Cumulatively the above-expected improvements should contribute to the achievement of the Programme specific objective and respectively lead to a more sustainable regional economic development in the border area between both countries. The aim at the end of the project is to obtain one self-sufficient, sustainable and pro-active SB that guarantees full engagement with the adopted TS objectives and its implementation for the benefit of the local integrated territorial development and in full respect of the public interest.

titleEn: Bridging Circular Economy in Cross-Border SMEs
summaryEn:
Our project, "Bridging Circular Economy in Cross-Border SMEs," is a collaborative effort between Eroglu Group and KAMA LTD, addressing the pressing challenge of environmental sustainability and production efficiency in the textile industry within the Bulgaria-Turkey program area. The common challenge that our project aims to tackle is the significant waste generation and resource inefficiency prevalent in the textile sector, a concern that transcends national boundaries and calls for a cooperative, cross-border solution.

The overall objective of this project is to foster a transition towards a more circular and resource-efficient economy in the textile industry. By implementing advanced cutting technologies and digital resource management systems, we aim to significantly reduce fabric waste and enhance production efficiency at both Eroglu Group and KAMA LTD. This shift is not only expected to lead to direct cost savings but also to a substantial reduction in the environmental impact, contributing to the sustainable development of the region.

The main outputs of our project include the installation of new textile machinery and the implementation of sophisticated digital systems for efficient resource management. These innovations are expected to serve as a model for similar SMEs in the region, demonstrating the tangible benefits of embracing sustainable practices. The beneficiaries of these outputs will primarily be the companies involved, but also it can serve as a model to the wider community, including other businesses in the textile sector.

The cross-border approach of this project is crucial, as it allows for the pooling of resources, expertise, and practices from two different countries, thereby creating a more comprehensive and impactful solution. This collaboration is essential to address the shared challenges in the textile industry effectively and to foster a collective shift towards sustainable manufacturing practices across the region.

What sets this project apart is its realistic approach towards improving sustainability in the textile sector. Rather than proposing a radical overhaul, the project focuses on integrating technological advancements with existing processes, making it particularly suitable for SMEs. This innovative blend of modern technology and circular economy principles in a cross-border collaborative framework positions our project as a pioneering initiative in the region's strive towards environmental sustainability and economic efficiency.

titleEn: Cross border business model in industry for energy efficiency implemented by Bimeks Tel Inc and BG Plast Ltd.
Cross border Cooperation of Furniture and Packaging Industries for Territorial Cohesion and Borderless Energy Efficiency
summaryEn:
The "Cross border Cooperation of Furniture and Packaging Industries for Territorial Cohesion and Borderless Energy Efficiency' project aims to address the common challenge of energy inefficiency and environmental impact in the border region shared by Türkiye and Bulgaria. The project seeks to enhance energy efficiency and reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the furniture and packaging industries, which are significant contributors to energy consumption and carbon emissions in the region. The project WoodEn aims to foster energy efficiency among companies operating in Bulgaria and Türkiye by promoting cross-border cooperation for benefiting from the European knowledge and practices for sustainable manufacturing processes and creating an efficient micro-climate in the production premises. 
Based on these analyses and facts the Project addresses the following common challenges of the local industries operating in the cross-border area of Bulgaria and Türkiye: 
-	Low opportunities of the Turkish and Bulgarian companies for acting in collaboration and supporting their joint competitiveness on the European and local markets. 
-	High initial cost of energy-efficient investments and the lack of financial incentives,
-	Insufficient access to technologies for energy efficiency and sustainable manufacturing processes, hindering progress towards European climate targets.
-	High costs of energy and resources, which not only affect the competitiveness of companies but also contribute to increased greenhouse gas emissions.
-	The need to create a more favorable work environment to improve productivity and employee satisfaction, aligning with the principles of sustainable development.
-	Limited opportunities for innovation and development due to the lack of access to modern technologies and knowledge, essential for achieving climate neutrality.
-	Lack of experience, especially of the Turkish companies in development and implementation of European Union funded projects, and lack of expertise of the local companies especially in development of cross-border cooperation projects with foreign companies. 
There is a certain need expressed by the local companies for cooperation and exchange of experience with other companies and organizations to address common challenges and achieve better results, in line with the collaborative efforts required to meet European climate goals.
The project tackles identified common challenges and opportunities through a multifaceted approach aimed at promoting energy efficiency, fostering cross-border cooperation, and implementing pilot energy -efficient solutions. 
Companies participating in the WoodEN project focus on optimizing their manufacturing processes and creating efficient production conditions in their building stocks. This involves adopting energy-efficient technologies and practices throughout their operations, such as upgrading machinery and implementation of energy efficiency measures of their production buildings. By optimizing the manufacturing workflow and ensuring needful production micro-climate, the partner companies will minimize energy waste and enhance their overall productivity, by contributing to the European, national and global climate neutrality strategies. 
WoodEN project has a strong cross-border cooperation feature - it provides a unique opportunity for countries to share knowledge, best practices, and technological advancements related to energy efficiency. 
The project is a certain measure for cooperation and complement of the both project partners from the each side of the border: the partners will demonstrate joint energy-efficiency measures, will exchange knowledge and combine their efforts for the energy efficiency with more than 60 % and reducing the GHG emissions with more than 18,5 tons per a year. Engaging in cross-border cooperation for sure will open up new market opportunities and economic prospects for project partners and target groups. The LP will benefit from the expertise and operations of the PP2 in production of recyclable carton packages and the PP2 will benefit from the new business opportunities. 
The project is a platform for sharing of trans-boundary knowledge in production of energy efficient furniture and carton packages, and utilization of the row material by the best possible way. The both companies will reduce their carbon footprint and contribute to a sustainable future, demonstrating their commitment to sustainability, attracting eco-conscious customers and employees. 
The project's emphasis on implementing energy-efficient practices and technologies in these industries demonstrates an innovative approach to addressing environmental challenges while promoting economic growth and regional cooperation.

titleEn: Trans-Border Cooperation and Technical Modernization for Energy Efficiency in BG-TR Wood Industry
summaryEn:
The TIMBREfFiciency cross-border cooperation project will be realized in the partnership of two companies from the border area of Bulgaria and Türkiye, operating in the wood processing sector. 
The project addresses a common challenge in the cross-border area shared by Bulgaria and Türkiye. Both countries face inefficiencies and outdated technologies in their wood processing industries, leading to increased energy consumption, environmental impact, and production waste. Recognizing the need for modernization and sustainability, the project aims to enhance energy efficiency and reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the timber production sector, contributing for the territorial cohesion and environmentally - friendly cross-border region. 
The overarching objective of TIMBREfFiciency CBC project is to transform and upgrade the wood processing activities in both Bulgarian and Turkish companies, that will ensure sustainable and green development of the region and contribute to the national, European and global aims in climate neutrality. By implementing energy-efficient measures, adopting cutting-edge technologies, and fostering cross-border collaboration, the project seeks to create a more environmentally friendly and sustainable cross-border region. The project aspires to bring about a significant change in the current wood processing landscape. Anticipated outcomes include a substantial reduction in energy consumption of the both companies, namely more than 85% efficiency, improved production efficiency, and a noteworthy decrease in greenhouse gas emissions with nearly 60 tons per a year. 
The project will deliver tangible outputs such as the introduction of modern machines for ensuring implementation of energy-efficient practices, and the establishment of sustainable production methods. LP - Gamitreid 2 is set to upgrade its timber sawing and small unused wooden parts crushing machinery, essential for pellet production. The existing sawmill, in operation for a decade and technologically outdated, will be replaced with a state-of-the-art sawmill line. This modernization aims for increased efficiency, productivity, and energy efficiency. Additionally, the new sawmill line will automate processes currently carried out manually by workers, eliminating the need for manual intervention in more than two other production stages. The modernization initiative aims to enhance efficiency, productivity, and energy efficiency. The new industrial wood chipper will enable 100% reuse of wooden waste by resizing the wood particles to the required sizes for pellet production. In contrast, the existing crusher is both highly depreciated and inefficient, leading to suboptimal reuse of the company's waste.
PP2 will introduce a new cross-cut saw with automatic diagnostics for assessing the quality and conditions of wood materials, as well as measuring and cross-cutting the material. This optical cross-cutting saw is designed to fully automate tasks that currently require the manual labor of six or more people, leading to more than 90% energy efficiency and a massive reduction in waste and GHG emission. Both partners in cross-border cooperation will realize public awareness and partnership events such as Networking event in Babaeski and Timber Energy event in Kameno with participation of Bulgarian and Turkish companies, wood sector operators and stakeholders. The project partners will conduct training for staff on sustainable production practices and take charge of project visualization and result dissemination. 
These outputs will directly benefit the partnering companies involved in wood processing, as well as the broader community by contributing to a cleaner environment.
The cross-border approach is crucial for addressing the shared challenges faced by Bulgaria and Turkey in the wood processing industry. By collaborating on the implementation of sustainable practices, the project leverages the strengths of both countries and fosters knowledge exchange, leading to a more impactful and regionally tailored solution.
What sets TIMBREfFiciency apart is its innovative approach to combining modern technologies, sustainable practices, and cross-border collaboration. The project introduces cutting-edge machinery, implements energy-efficient measures, and establishes a cooperation for sustainable wood processing. This innovative blend positions TIMBREfFiciency as a pioneering initiative in the region, offering a template for other cross-border projects aiming to enhance environmental sustainability and energy efficiency.

titleEn: We work together to support sustainable solutions
summaryEn:
The common challenges that unite the aspirations of the two partners are to overcome:
1/ the dependence and vulnerability of SMEs in the cross-border region from frequent extreme events and their consequences, which directly affect the production of products used in the services of tourist accommodation facilities.
2/ the need to build capacity in SMEs in the cross-border region to implement the right policy and implement appropriate mechanisms for adaptation to the changes that have occurred as a result of climate change.
3/ the need to set realistic goals for improving energy efficiency in response to the goals set by the EU until 

2030.
4/ an opportunity that brings us closer and unites us in an effort to be active and useful both for the business and for the users of our products and services.
The general goal of the project is aimed at optimized environmental management, through joint training to promote an environmentally responsible attitude in the field of accommodation services and the production of products for them. The support contributes to the implementation of an integrated approach for targeted and coordinated implementation of energy efficiency measures in all economic sectors.
In the process of joint implementation of the project, successful cooperation is planned to find approaches to improve the environmental standards of the manufactured products and the services provided with the environmental standards and product requirements applicable to them.
With the implementation of the project, the partners set goals that will lead to an improvement in the state of the environment and the climate, namely:


1. Improving the energy efficiency of enterprises in the cross-border region providing services and producing products with care for people


2. Cultivation of a responsible attitude and implementation of environmental protection policies and the action plan in the field of services and production of goods for people


3. Limiting the adverse effects of the activities of enterprises in the cross-border region on the environment and climate


4. Promotion of the environmental sustainability of SMEs in the cross-border region and the actions they should implement
From an economic point of view, the benefits of the approach are numerous – increasing resource efficiency, reducing material costs, stimulating innovation, disconnecting economic growth from resource consumption, developing the labor market, reducing waste and the costs of its disposal.
The partners in the project are companies operating in a region with a rich natural heritage - the unique Strandzha mountain and the richness of the Burgas and Pomorie lakes. The sustainability and development of the partners' activities is highly dependent on the state of natural resources and their conservation. This fact is a very sentimental prerequisite for cooperation, undertaking joint actions and measures, technology for transformation and creating the catch for convergence and development.
Achieving these results is of direct benefit to both enterprises, as the amount of energy used will be reduced and the sustainability of the enterprises will be improved.
The enterprises in the cross-border region will benefit from the achieved results of the project, through the published information about the planned project activities, about the implemented energy efficiency measures in the companies and the benefit of implementing the eco-labeling criteria.
The project partners, through the implemented activities, will become a good example and incentive for the companies in the cross-border region to implement energy efficient measures aimed at reducing the amount of energy used in the activity. The effect they will achieve will contribute to the achievement of the national goals of both countries, related to the implementation of a policy to increase energy efficiency, as well as to the promotion of the production and consumption of electricity from renewable sources.
The regional environmental inspections in Bulgaria and Turkey will benefit from the results of the project related to the results of the realized investments in the region and the effect of the reduced consumption of energy resources, the reduced amount of generated greenhouse gases and their impact on the surrounding environment. Results and reliability of reporting will be improved.

titleEn: Cross-Border Cooperation to Energy Efficiency in Tourism Sector and Environmentally-Friendly Bulgaria-Türkiye Region
summaryEn:
Tourism, as one of the largest economic global sectors, is one of the largest energy-consuming sectors. At the same time the hotel industry constitutes one of the most energy and resource intensive branches of the tourism industry. Heating, air-conditioning, ventilation and cooling systems typically account for a major and frequently the largest portion of the energy consumed in the hotels. Catering is the second largest portion in the energy consumed in the hotels. In fact, hotels and other types of accommodation account for 2% of the 5% global CO2 emitted by the tourism sector. A study by the World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) found that a 20% improvement in energy efficiency can lead to a 14% reduction in carbon dioxide emissions within the sector.
Project CARE-Tour aims to address the common challenge of promoting sustainable tourism practices and enhancing energy efficiency in the cross-border area of Bulgaria and Türkiye, by jointly tackling the common challenges such as the high energy consumption operations and technologies in the accommodation facilities of the two sides of the border and the need for certain joint measures of the tourism operators for supporting the European and national goals in Green Transition and climate change adaptation. 
The current project CARE-Tour is covering the cooperation of two companies operating in the tourism sector and located in Edirne and Yambol regions. The both companies combining their efforts and sources for ensuring smooth transition to more sustainable models, including measures to mitigate and adapt to climate change and ensure sustainable and responsible tourism. 
The overall objective of the project is to enhance environmental sustainability and energy efficiency in the Bulgaria-Türkiye cross-border area by cooperation of the tourism sector through joint solutions, innovative practices, and community engagement. The project aims to contribute for territorial cohesion and environmentally -friendly cross-border area fostering energy efficiency in the tourism sector and ensuring at least 42 % energy efficiency and decreasing of the GHG emissions in the CB area with more than 78 tones per year. 
This will be accomplished through the integration of cutting-edge technologies, such as A++ heating and cooling systems, and by promoting sustainable behaviors among staff and the hotel guests.
Main outputs of the project include development of joint energy efficiency solution plan between the partners and integration of modern and more efficient technologies in the both hotels with aim contributing to development of environmentally-friendly cross-border area. 
The partners will combine their existing technical, human and financial resources for implementation of the Responsible Visitor Campaign, distribution of informational materials among the tourism operators for their awareness about the European goals and measures for climate neutrality, organization knowledge exchange events and stimulation cross-border cooperation of tourism operators. These outputs will benefit local tourism operators, hotel guests, and the broader community by raising awareness, promoting sustainable practices, and reducing environmental impact.
The partners will apply certain cross-border cooperation approach for the achievement of all expected project results. 
The cross-border approach is crucial as it allows for the exchange of knowledge, resources, and best practices between Bulgarian and Turkish tourism operators. Collaboration across borders enhances the effectiveness of energy efficiency measures and ensures a more comprehensive approach to sustainable tourism. At the same time the cross-border cooperation will contribute for the achievement of the Programme's objective in straightening the territorial cohesion of the Bulgaria - Türkiye cross-border region. 
What sets this project apart is its focus on integrating energy efficiency measures into the tourism sector, its collaborative approach involving both Bulgarian and Turkish partners, and its emphasis on promoting responsible tourism practices among the tourism sector representatives, hotel staff members and visitors for long-term sustainability and clean cross-border area.

titleEn: Cross-Border Partnership for Advancing European Priorities and Energy Efficiency in the window-glass and Joinery Industry
summaryEn:
The main objective of the project WinTechENERGY is to contribute for the sustainable energy transition of the Bulgarian and Turkish companies from the border area by providing cross-border cooperation opportunities and financial support for reducing their energy consumption and increasing the technological performance of the border companies, leading to energy efficiency of more than 47 % and reducing of the GHG emissions with nearly 40 tons per a year, fostering collaboration and achieving measurable improvements in energy efficiency and sustainability.
The project combining efforts of two companies - Bulgarian company Europlast Engineering Group Ltd and Turkish SMEs - Aydogan AKINCI - AKINCI CAM operating in flat glass-working, glazing and window-Joinery production industry. 
Their collaborative efforts are aimed at addressing common territorial challenges, including the imperative to align with emerging trends and respond to the climate change mandates of national, European, and global regulatory bodies. The project is particularly focused on aligning with the EU's enhanced climate ambition under the European Green Deal, to reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions in this energy intensive sector. The project partners recognize two primary needs: firstly, the imperative to take significant steps to decrease their energy consumption through various means, and secondly, the necessities to produce high-performance products that directly enhance energy efficiency in other sectors and buildings.
However, there is an urgent need for technological investments and the replacement of outdated and energy-intensive machinery in the production operations of the both companies to minimize energy losses and ensure sustainable energy efficiency in the production operations and in their products.
Through the project, the partners anticipate a tangible improvement in energy efficiency practices, leading to a reduction of over 47% in energy consumption and nearly 40 tons of greenhouse gas emissions annually. This change will contribute to a more sustainable and environmentally friendly cross-border region.
The project will produce several key outputs, including a joint energy efficiency solution strategic plan, technological investments in production machinery, capacity building through training workshops, and the development of good practice guides for energy-efficient in the buildings. These outputs will benefit both project partners, employees of participating companies, local stakeholders, and the general public.
The partners will take a cross-border approach to address common energy efficiency challenges faced by both Bulgaria and Türkiye. By collaborating across borders, they will share knowledge, resources, and best practices to achieve greater impact and sustainability. The both companies are operating in the same field of industry and have many complementary elements. By collaborating across borders, the project partners will increase their cross-border cooperation capacity and share experiences and best practices, which for sure will lead to more effective solutions in the cross-border area. 
For the first time economic operators - companies from the both sides of the border will combine their knowledge, human, financial and technical sources and focus to the cross-border cooperation project covering implementing cutting-edge technologies and best practices in energy efficiency within the glass processing and window-joinery sectors. The LP will fully renovate its production line: will replace seven technologically outdated production machines with six automatized one including CNC machine, CAD included and cutting edge machines for operation with aluminum and PVC profiles. This initiative is projected to achieve over 63% energy efficiency and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by more than 

2.7 tons per year. The PP2 will implement sufficient energy efficiency measure for installation of a new flat glass tempering furnace in its premises in Edirne. This Glass tempering furnace is expected to increase production efficiency by more than two times, achieve over 32,58% energy efficiency, and
result in a reduction of more than 37 tons of GHG emissions per year.
By introducing new methodologies and approaches, the project partner aim to set a precedent for sustainable production practices in the region, leading to long-term environmental and economic benefits.

titleEn: Uniting Borders for Clean and Energy Efficient Metal Industry in the cross-border area of Bulgaria and Türkiye
summaryEn:
The SustainaMetal project aims to enhance territorial cohesion by fostering collaboration between companies in the iron-steel and metal industry in Bulgaria and Türkiye.
The metal industry ranks among the most energy-consuming sectors globally. Iron and steel production is very energy intensive, with energy and raw materials accounting for 60-80% of the costs, as those for energy are between 15-25%. The proportion of energy in production costs highlights its importance for the iron and steel sector.
The SustainaMetal project addresses the high energy intensity and elevated greenhouse gas emissions prevalent in the metal industry within the border areas of Bulgaria and Türkiye. Both countries' metal sectors face challenges such as outdated technologies, limited incentives for innovation, and fragmented cooperation, hindering progress towards energy efficiency and sustainability.
