The primary objective of the current project is to achieve a minimum 55% improvement in energy efficiency and reduce over 90 tons of greenhouse gas emissions per a year in the cross-border area. This will lead to a more sustainable and competitive metal industry, aligning with EU strategies for clean energy transitions and climate neutrality.
Key outputs of the project include investments in the building stock for energy efficiency, modernization of production technologies by replacement of the most energy consuming melting furnace unit and implementation of efficient microclimates. 
Both Lead Partner- Kirovci Ltd. and Partner PP2 - Vize Dokum, along with other metal industry companies in the Cross border region, will benefit from these outputs. Additionally, public awareness events and training activities will promote environmental sustainability in the region, benefiting local communities and stakeholders.
The project adopts a cross-border approach to leverage the complementary strengths and resources of companies from both sides of the border. By pooling knowledge, expertise, and finances, the project partners can collectively address common challenges and achieve greater impact. This approach is essential due to the interconnected nature of the metal industry and the shared environmental concerns that transcend national borders.
The SustainaMetal project introduces several innovative elements. It is the first initiative to foster cross-border cooperation specifically within the metal industry in the BG-TR border region.
By bringing together companies with similar challenges and objectives, the project creates a base for shared learning, collaboration, and sustainable development. 
Additionally, the project aligns with EU policies such as the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), contributing to broader efforts for environmental stewardship and economic resilience at regional and European level.

titleEn: Development of business and tourism potential in the cross-border region
summaryEn:
The goal of the proposal is to increase competitiveness of local economies in the cross-border region, through the development of the business and tourism potential of the territories of intervention. This will be achieved through the designation of three integrated exhibition centers to showcase and promote businesses and their products and services, as well as the regional and cultural heritage of the territory. The centers will provide exposure and education for the business and tourism sectors and will stimulate cross-border growth and collaboration.
During the development of the project proposal, the three organizations reached a mutual agreement on the idea that there is a need to stimulate local economies and tourism by providing a platform for businesses and locally produced products and services with the goal to promote them and help them develop beyond their traditional market and scope. The conclusion that was reached and the activities that were envisaged derive from the need to work towards a more inclusive, integrated cross-border economy that cherishes cultural diversity and allows businesses to improve and expand.
To tackle the identified common challenges, three spaces (one in each partner's territory) will be renovated and repurposed to integrated business and tourism exhibition centers. The exhibition centers will be used to showcase and promote local products, as well as the organization of thematic educational and promotional events focused towards business and tourism.
The realization of the project will allow the development of previously untapped potential of the cross-border region (specifically the regions under the scope of the project) and will provide an opportunity for sustainable development of the economical and tourist potential of the region. The innovative approach of an integrated central hub for business and tourism will provide a new method for development of the participating regions and will allow the exploration of new avenues that were previously unavailable to local businesses, institutions and service providers. Through cross-border collaboration, exchange of experience, culture and training - local capacity will be stimulated and regional identity will be preserved, making each territory of intervention more attractive. The results from the project could be reproduced in different places in the cross-border region and contribute to the further improvement of the quality of life of its people.

titleEn: Green Smiles: Development of sustainable tourism and green initiatives in the Municipalities of Topolovgrad (Bulgaria) and Büyükkarştıran (Turkey)
Karnobat and Kirklareli Invest in The Future
summaryEn: Karnobat Municipality, Bulgaria, and Kırklareli Municipality, Turkey, share rich cultural and historical heritage, as well as sites with unique biodiversity and distinctive local traditions whose tourist potential to a large extent has not been tapped. Stemming from this common challenge, the present project aims to unite the efforts of the two local governments to ensure better utilisation of available resources for cultural, eco and wine tourism, and to offer more diverse and higher quality tourist services. This aim will be achieved through investments in integrated measures in the tourist sector comprising of refurbishment of cultural and natural sites, combined with the development of a twinning strategy in tourism, and a wide promotional campaign to unleash local potentials, ensure cohesion and help upscaling project results and solutions. The main outputs will be preserved and upgraded tourist infrastructure, upskilled tourist personnel and enhanced cooperation among stakeholders leading to better economic perspectives and improved quality of life for the entire population in the two localities who will be the main beneficiary of the project results. The novelty of the project is in the integrated approach to combine hard investments with promotion and capacity building activities, and to apply cross-border cooperation and exchange of experience and best practices in order to ensure synergies and maximise the benefits of the undertaken activities.

titleEn: Gateway Through History: Mobility of Cross-Border Destination Exploring
summaryEn:
The MOBIGATE aims to create a sustainable joint tourist product that enables responsible travelers to embark on a cultural and natural heritage journey through the CB areas of Burgas and Kirklareli. The project is focusing on enhancing cultural and natural tourism infrastructure, sustainable mobility between specifically historical sites like Rusokastro and Petrova Niva, Kiyikoy and its natural areas, and nature park Kavaklımeşe Oak Grove. By promoting alternative mobility options and responsible tourism practices, it seeks to increase the quality of visitor experiences and strengthen the links between cultural and natural sites.
The CB region is identified as one with accumulated problems in various areas, generating a negative cumulative effect, which is crucial for deepening the more acute problems and has an overall negative impact in all areas of development. The common challenge faced by the program area is the underutilization and maintenance of historical and natural sites that are located in remote areas, making them difficult to access and manage. Also PPs are facing with the realization of the area's potential, which is directly dependent on the compliance of the implemented tourism policy priorities in a wider European context, including increasing the competitiveness of the sector and promoting the development of sustainable, responsible and high-quality tourism; improving the culture of cooperation between the public, business and non-profit sectors as an important condition for their successful development in a highly competitive environment. 
The PPs aim to address these challenges by collaboratively developing sustainable solutions that promote responsible tourism and improve infrastructure in these areas. 
With the implementation of the project, the partners strive to achieve a more inclusive, sustainable and integrated development of the target territory, a fair transition and territorial integration in Europe; ensure long-term profitability and competitiveness; maximize the contribution of tourism to the economic well-being of the territory and the profit share; increase the number and quality of local jobs in tourism, including the level of remuneration, conditions and opportunities for work, seeks a broad and fair distribution of economic and social benefits from tourism in the territory; maintain and improve the quality of life in local communities, including social structures and access to resources, amenities and support systems, avoiding any form of social degradation or exploitation.
The main outputs of the project will be the responsible tourism development plan, responsible tourism information campaigns, the development of a responsible tourist profile, and the planning of sustainable mobility forms. These outputs will be utilized by local businesses, tourism operators, and the general public, providing them with knowledge and resources to engage in responsible tourism practices. Additionally, the project will create eco-friendly travel guides and digital maps for responsible tourists, enhancing their experience and accessibility to the cross-border area's cultural and natural sites.
The main results that will be produced:
- Creation of new regional tourist products for the CB area, based on natural resources and cultural-historical heritage, improved tourist infrastructure and implementation of regional marketing and advertising;
- Realization of the potential of the CB area, including increasing the competitiveness of the sector and promoting the development of sustainable, responsible and high-quality tourism;
- Using the unused potential for the development of SMEs from the region in the tourism sector;
- Creating conditions for rediscovering and developing unpopular destinations and supporting local communities through the development of cycling routes in the region and promoting digital and physical sustainable mobility.
The approach taken by MOBIGATE involves a cross-border/transnational/inter-regional collaboration between four partners from the Burgas and Kirklareli districts. By pooling their expertise and resources, the partners aim to create unified and effective solutions for responsible tourism and infrastructure improvement. 
The innovativeness of the project is considered because:


1. It envisages the creation of an integrated tourist regional product on the territory.


2. It applies a balanced integrated approach, oriented to territorial needs as the key to achieving a general cumulative effect.


3. Introduces a new organizational method under INTERREG - IPA CBC BG-TR Program 2021-2027 - participation of a wide range of partners- in the overall process of preparation, discussion, adoption and implementation of the strategy according to the principle of partnership and the model of multi-level management


4. It envisages the development of alternative tourism models with an emphasis on the little-known ones in Bulgaria and Turkiye- sustainable and geotourism;

titleEn: Exploring the Past: Experimental Archaeology as a Catalyst for Tourism and Growth
summaryEn:
The EPACT project aims to achieve sustainable and inclusive growth in underdeveloped cross-border areas in Bulgaria and Turkiye by focusing on increased competitiveness of the local economy through digital and green transformation, and investing in tourism, cultural, social, and educational potential. The project involves four partners who will create an archaeological campus using three historical sites as a joint product to stimulate economic and social development, enhance employability, and improve competitiveness in the region.
EPACT addresses common challenges in the border area, including the seasonal nature of tourism, limited promotion to the younger generation, and the need for further investment in site socialization- development of attractive tour programmes in the target archaeological sites and infrastructural improvements. The project's main objective is to create a year-round and attractive tourism product that utilizes the region's rich archaeological potential to drive sustainable growth.
The project has a strong feature of integrated project: combine investment, development of sustainable tourism in the region for ensuring inclusive economic growth and stimulating competitiveness of the local economy, ensuring digital services for the tour operators, green and sustainable knowledge for the local people.
The restoration and socialization of three historical sites—Aquae Calidae, Rusokastro, and Aşağıpınar—are central to the project's goals. This involves implementing restoration works in Aquae Calidae and establishing campus area for the young people engaged in the experimental archaeology; creating solar systems for green energy, improving accessibility in Rusokastro, and reproduction of Neolithic village in 1/1 scale and establishing information centers for visitors in Aşağıpınar open air museum. The project's innovative aspect lies in establishing an archaeological camp for promotional and educational purposes, attracting a diverse range of visitors and enhancing the region's tourism appeal.
Capacity-building programs will empower local communities involved in tourism, ensuring they benefit from the sector's incomes. Additionally, investments in digital solutions and joint promotions will maximize the visibility and reach of the tourism product. 
The project will also strengthen connectivity on a regional level, aligning with national, regional, and local strategies.
EPACT seeks to transform the target areas into an active and attractive cross-border destination by combining historical sites, fostering sustainable tourism, and promoting economic and social development through an integrated approach: combining territorial historical, archaeological and tourism potential, capacity building for the locals and responding to the needs of the businesses. All of these will be done on cross-border level with a cross-border cooperation within public, local development and social partnership structure. 
Main outputs: 
- Realized crucial investments in the three important archaeological areas: Aquae Calidae, Rusokastro, and Aşağıpınar, all aiming their successfully utilization in the one joint Cross-border destination of Experimental archaeology, that will be promoted at regional, national and European level, especially among he young enthusiastic in archaeology and history lovers. 
- Established working and attractive tour programmes for visitors of the three destinations, by elaboration of Joint Work Plan of the CB destination, exchange of experience and implementation trainings for the local people for their benefiting by the tourism development and created incomes. 
- Ensured connectivity between the destination and the local tour companies, ensuring them rich tourism offering and digital solutions for their services and activities. 
- Respecting activities for climate neutrality and sustainable development, increasing the knowledge and adopting skills to the locals in green transformation. 
EPACT's commitment to promoting territorial cohesion and regional development by integrating the archaeological tourism product on a cross-border level and enhancing complementary attractions is a strategic approach to foster collaboration and create a more appealing tourism destination. It using cross-sectoral and cross-border cooperation approach to realize all its objectives.
The new and unique for the Cross-border area will be developed Archaeological Campus as part of the tourism offering: This campus will not only provide educational and research opportunities but also allow visitors to actively engage in experimental archaeology and gain hands-on experience with the region's rich cultural heritage. Empowering local communities and benefiting from the made investments in the target areas also is an unique approach for the project - the trained people will be an active part from the tourism programmes in these sites and joint destination, and promotion of their products in the visitors centers.

titleEn: Shared Shores&Stories: Discovering the Rich Cultural Heritage&Terroir of Pomorie-Kırklareli Tourist Area
summaryEn:
The overall objective of SHARE project is to strengthen tourism in the Pomorie-Kirklareli border region by capitalizing on its cultural heritage, natural beauty, gastronomy, and unique attractions. By creating a unified and appealing destination, the project aims to increase tourist flows, boost the local economy, and establish the region as a competitive and sustainable year-round tourist destination through tourism initiatives and digital connectivity. 
Specific objectives of the Project are: 

- To establish a cohesive and integrated tourist area that encompasses both Pomorie and Kirklareli, encouraging cooperation and synergy between the two regions.
- To build a positive and appealing image of the Pomorie-Kirklareli region through strategic planning and branding efforts as an attractive destination for cultural and culinary experiences.
- Remodel a municipal building to become a "Home of culture and traditions." The facility will serve as a cultural hub and co-working space, promoting the region's heritage and offering a space for collaboration. 
- Provide Virtual Reality Experience while the Community center in Pomorie will provide VR glasses to visitors, allowing them to experience the tours developed in Türkiye, showcasing the attractions of the cross-border region.
- Successfully organize two major events, "Pomorie Fest" and "Terroir&Traditions Festival" in Kirklareli, to celebrate the project's results and attract visitors.
- Implement targeted activities and marketing campaigns to enhance the image and visibility of the Pomorie-Kirklareli tourist area, thereby attracting more visitors and tourists to the region.
- Provide essential information to tourists and enhance their experience through the creation of a dedicated website and a smart app for the Pomorie - Kırklareli Terroir&Traditions Tourism Route will. 
- Introduce low-emission vehicles and charging stations to promote sustainable tourism and eco-friendly transportation within the region.
- Assist and guide tourists in the area through the various attractions and experiences available in the region by the installation of 25 route signs.
- Strengthen cross-border cooperation and foster mutual understanding between Bulgaria and Türkiye through joint planning, execution, and celebration of the project's achievements.
These specific objectives propose solutions to unleash and develop territorial potentials of the cross-border area to all five specific objectives of the Call as defined within the Territorial Strategy of the Programme, namely: Competitiveness and business environment; Digitalisation and climate neutrality of the local economy; Employability and labour market adaptability; Tourism; Ecosystem practices and services in the management of natural assets with tourism potential. This actually brings to the project the integrated and multi-sectoral approach to reach the defined overall objective.
During the project lifetime, several new solutions and existing solutions will be adopted and implemented to achieve the specific objectives and overall goal of developing the cross-border tourist area "Pomorie-Kirklareli". These solutions include:
- Develop a new cross-border tourist information system that integrates data from both Pomorie and Kirklareli. This system will provide comprehensive and up-to-date information about tourist attractions, events, accommodations, and transportation options in the region.
- Adopt smart tourism solutions, such as the mobile apps to enhance the visitor experience and provide real-time information on local points of interest, routes, and events.
- Introduce electric/hybrid vehicles (EVs) and establish EV charging stations in strategic locations within the tourist area. This move will promote sustainable transportation options and reduce the carbon footprint of tourists. 
- Implement measures to preserve and showcase the cultural heritage of both Pomorie and Kirklareli - the establishment of cultural centers, and the promotion of the routes within the region.
- Collaborate on joint marketing campaigns that target eco tourism market segments and highlight the unique selling points of the Pomorie-Kirklareli tourist area. 
- Through the social media establish feedback mechanisms to collect input from tourists about their experiences in the cross border area. This feedback will be used to continuously improve and tailor tourism offerings to meet visitor expectations. 
SHARE Project goes beyond existing practices in the tourism sector in the Bulgaria-Türkiye area because the project's approach emphasizes strong cross-border collaboration between Pomorie Municipality in Bulgaria and Trakya Development Agency in Kırklareli, Türkiye.

titleEn: THRACIA Alive: Partnership for experiential Cultural tourism from the Black Sea to Maritsa
summaryEn:
CULTHRA is a cross-border cooperation project that aims to address common challenges faced by the border regions of Bulgaria and Turkiye in utilizing their cultural values for tourism development. 
The project's overall objective is to establish a sustainable and attractive cross-border cultural destination that aligns with global tourism trends. To achieve this, the project will integrate ten cultural house-museums into one cultural destination and renovate two important cultural monuments in Sredec and Uzunkopru. Additionally, a new cultural center will be established in Kirklareli, and an ethnographical center will be revived in Elhovo. 
The project seeks to promote experiential cultural tourism and create a branded destination that can appeal to a diverse range of travelers by promoting the rich culture of these Thracian lands. 
The main outputs of the project are: 
- development and enhancement of cultural house-museums and cultural centers, the restoration of important cultural monuments and their activaiton as zones for promoting and demonstrating cultural skills and values, that the modern tourists are looking for. 
- promotion of traditional handcraft culture and traditions, by integrating them in the daily programmes of the cultural centers and involving the locals and tourists in the interactive events for achieving of these craft skills. 
- Elaboration and starting application by the partner institutions / organizations of a strong Marketing and Branding strategy of the new developed cross-border Thrace Cultural Destination as a source of Experiential Cultural Tourism in the CB area. 
- Stimulating the local people and especially NEETs to take a part in the training and skills development activities, by making the tourism sector and especially working in the event organization, tour promotional service sector attractive for them and increasing their competitiveness and employability. 
By transforming these cultural assets into interactive, creative, and inspiring spaces, the project aims to attract more tourists, including those interested in authentic cultural experiences. The revitalization of handcraft culture and traditions will be achieved through workshops, training programs, and marketing efforts, benefiting local artisans and preserving intangible cultural heritage.
A cross-border approach is a main tool for the achieving of the project results and deeply needed because the project seeks to leverage the cultural assets on both sides of the border. By collaborating and pooling resources, the partners will create a first cultural destination promoting Thracian joint culture, will be a platform for exchange of expertise and a leverage for joint inclusive economic growth and prosperity. The joint efforts of cultural institutions and tourism operators will ensure successful marketing and branding of the region, positioning it as a sustainable and highly competitive destination for experiential cultural tourism.
What sets the CULTHRA project apart is its focus on integrating cultural heritage and handcraft traditions into a cohesive tourism product. By revitalizing cultural monuments and promoting handcraft culture, the project not only preserves cultural heritage but also offers economic opportunities for local communities. The emphasis on sustainability and green practices aligns with global trends and ensures that the project's impact is long-lasting and environmentally responsible. Moreover, by integrating digital knowledge and marketing strategies, the project aims to overcome existing barriers and promote the existing cultural tourism potential to a wider audience. 
Through these innovative approaches, CULTHRA is poised to create a unique and attractive cross-border cultural destination that responds to the demands of modern tourists while preserving and promoting the rich heritage of the region.
In the frame of the project the PPs for the first time will give a life to the cultural house - museums in the border areas and will developed a new one working under the same philosophy: To be not only centers for watching of the historical objects, but an active, attractive, creative and inspiring cultural sites. The partners will benefit from the rich Thracian culture and will promote it worldwide by ensuring close cooperation of the public institutions, local policy makers, cultural organizations and the private sector actors. They will open their doors for the visitors and tourists that will benefit from these rich cultural values and will be a part from the creative activities of these house - museums - such as loom weaving, making of own souvenirs, pottery, making of kukers' masks benefiting from the rich Kukerlandiya culture, etc.
All these activities are the unique features of the project and the most original is the cross-sectoral structure and cross-regional partnership of the project, combining all partners under one destination: Thracia Experiential Cultural Tourism Destination.

titleEn: "ENPORT STRANDJA - an integrated approach to the development of sustainable tourism in the cross-border region"
summaryEn:
As a particularly remote and depopulated area, the CB region of Strandzha lacks basic production resources. The region has great potential for the development of tourism, but it is unused. THE MAIN CHALLENGE that the "ENPORT STRANDZHA" project has to deal with is the development of the tourist potential of the territory. The project aims to address the challenge of increasing competitiveness and improving the business environment; increasing digitalization and climate neutrality of the local economy; improving employability and labor market adaptability; development of ecosystem practices and services in the management of natural assets with tourism potential.
The MAIN OBJECTIVE of the project is to develop a consistent and purposeful tourism policy in the cross-border area of Strandzha region as an integrated response to local needs, based on a partnership between the public sector, institutions, the private sector and non-governmental organizations, which generates jobs, creates broad opportunities for the development of entrepreneurship, long-term economic and social benefits, increases tourism revenue, leading to sustainable and inclusive economic growth.
With the implementation of the project, the partners strive to: achieve more inclusive, sustainable and integrated development of the target territory, a fair transition and territorial integration in their own countries and in Europe; ensure long-term profitability and competitiveness; maximize the contribution of tourism to the economic well-being of the territory; development of attractive sites of natural and cultural heritage; formation and marketing of regional tourism products; increasing the capacity of lower level municipal centers to keep the free movement of people and to withstand the competition from big cities.
MEASURABLE RESULTS FROM THE PROJECT: 


1.	Pilot joint activity, - 1 item;


2.	 Jointly developed solutions - 4 items.;


3.	 Special bicycle infrastructure - 

2.5 km.;


4.	 Supported cultural and tourist sites - 4 items

 FINAL EFFECTS ON THE TARGET TERRITORY:
 1 Stimulating the development of local communities; 2 Compensating for the lack of economic potential and business activities in settlements that lack basic production resources; 3 Improving the sectoral employment of the population; 4 An opportunity to create a comprehensive identity of the territory in the marketing and advertising of Bulgarian destinations through sustainable tourism.
The sustainable tourism is an opportunity to emphasize on the uniqueness of the target territory for the development of new markets at the national and global level; 5 Shared values, experience, knowledge and effective interaction will have a beneficial effect on local communities, on partner relationships; 6 Through the created conditions for the exchange of experience on the project between experts in different fields, the development of innovative models in the field of tourism development in particular will be supported.
In long term, the FINAL BENEFICIARIES will have a number of additional benefits: population - improved quality of life; (inter)national visitors – innovative tourist product; travel companies and tour operators - increased income. All this will contribute to the economic revival of the region and will stop its depopulation.
The project logic envisages not just a combination of partners, but an application of a real BALANCED AND TERRITORIAL-ORIENTED CROSS-BORDER INTEGRATED APPROACH to achieve sustainable results, which include: Territorial approach - based on an area with sufficient coherence and critical mass in terms of human, financial and economic resources; "Bottom-up" approach - participation of local people in the decision-making for the future; Public-private partnership - participation in the project of representatives of the public, business and non-profit sectors.
The approach is necessary because it is the only way to overcome the common challenges and make the most of the unused growth potential.
The project is innovative because it includes: 

1. new ideas - development of a little-known in Bulgaria and Turkey form of tourism - sustainable; 

2. new joint products - integrated tourism regional product of the territory, "Internet-based virtual TOURIST CENTER "STRANDZA", joint Network "INN.Rete" - Innovation Network, local charter of the client; 

3. new services and activities - Construction of a Tourist "in situ" center with bike lanes, training for entrepreneurs and study visits. 

4. a new model of a cooperation project - a partnership project of DIFFERENT stakeholders: public bodies, private participants, NGOs. 

5. Innovative project strategy, with good definition and determination of goals and results. 

5. Introduces a new organizational method under the INTERREG 2021 -2027 Bulgaria Türkiye Program - participation of a wide range of partners in the overall process of preparation, discussion, acceptance and implementation of the project.

titleEn: Developing INnovative Alliances for Management, Innovation, and Collaboration in European BioEconomy
summaryEn:
The DINAMIC DANUBE project represents a strategic partnership of 13 organizations, combining academic expertise and business support capabilities to jointly address the complex socio-economic challenges facing rural areas in the Danube Region. The primary focus is on mitigating the depopulation trend that threatens the region's economic backbone – small family farms, which are the main target group of this proposal- by strenghtening their capacities through lifelong learning, mentorship and technology introduction. The contemporary challenges confronting small family farms, particularly in the Southeast Danube Region, underscore the pressing need for targeted interventions to strenghten their sustainability, competitiveness, and resilience. Key obstacles such as skilled workforce migration, an aging population, lack of modern technological adoption, and weak business support ecosystems pose significant barriers that DINAMIC DANUBE aims to overcome. The project will implement a holistic approach combining education, technological integration, and capacity-building initiatives, with a special emphasis on empowering female farmers. This methodology not only strengthens local economies but also contributes to the overall sustainable development of the region. DINAMIC DANUBE will directly engage 500 small family farms from the Danube area, providing them with lifelong learning opportunities, peer mentorship programs, and facilitating the implementation of innovative technologies in underdeveloped and marginalized areas. Moreover, the project will establish a strong Danube-wide network in the bioeconomy and precision farming sectors, comprising key stakeholders who will serve as stewards for disseminating project results to other business support institutions, thereby reaching a broader base of family farms within the program area. The project findings will be proposed as policy recommendations to national-level institutions, enabling them to witness the tangible outcomes of the implemented solutions. Furthermore, the consortium plans to sustain its efforts by following up on the developed joint study and action plan, paving the way for future initiatives over the next four years. With a specific objective (SO1) Capacity Building and Skills Upscaling project directly contributes with new curriculum and on the field training brings the skills and knowledge of small family farmers to a higher level. This will not only support acquired knowledge implementation but support their production and distribution on long term, reaching several programme outputs such as facilitating the work and cooperation of the organizations across borders (

Merging all these new innovations for small family farms in Southeast Europe will open dialogue to tackle large structural issues such as migrations, boosting agricultural economy and diversity preservation. Finally, DINAMIC DANUBE actively advocates for policy reforms aimed at refining existing frameworks and regulations, with a specific focus on improving educational systems across the participating countries. By fostering a culture of cooperation and continuous improvement, the project improves to the collective capacity of stakeholders to address challenges and seize opportunities for sustainable agricultural development within the Danube region producing 3 main results: Joint strategies and action plans taken up by organization, organizations with increased institutional capacities due to their participation in cooperation activities across the borders and finally solutions taken up by organizations.

titleEn: Artificial Intelligence Readiness in Education
summaryEn: Artificial intelligence represents not just a technological advancement, but a societal shift that will permanently alter various sectors, including education. AI enables teachers to work more efficiently by co-creating class content and automating tasks like test grading. It also has the potential to reduce administrative burdens, allowing teachers to focus on high-value tasks. Moreover, schools that embrace AI can provide students with a competitive edge in future job markets, where AI literacy will be essential. However, integrating AI into education faces challenges due to the conservative nature of the educational system and the lack of standards or recommendations from ministries. The main goal of our project is to address these challenges by helping educational institutions understand AI's transformative potential and incorporate it effectively into teaching process. Through lectures, workshops, conferences, working groups and dissemination, the main project aims to empower teachers, students, and administrators with practical knowledge of AI. Our ultimate aim is not merely widespread AI usage, but rather the enhancement of educational systems to better prepare students for the future economy by fostering core skills like critical thinking and creativity. This preparatory project will lay the groundwork by analyzing the current state of education systems, defining needs, developing educational curriculum, creating project plans, seeking partnerships and funding, and conducting additional activities to enhance the relevance of the main project.

titleEn: Improving Water Quality in the Danube River Basin: Nature-Based Solutions for Sustainable Wastewater and Stormwater Management in Small Settlements
summaryEn:
The D-CLEAN project aims to address the pressing issue of wastewater (WW) and stormwater (SW) pollution in the Danube River Basin (DRB) by rising awareness, building capacity, and identifying, testing and showcasing practical solutions. Our aim is to improve water quality within the DRB by promoting the use of sustainable WW and SW management practices resilient to climate change and providing stakeholders with the necessary tools.

The ambitious EU water policy (the revised Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive; the Water Framework Directive) will require significant investments in WW and SW infrastructure in the near future, taking WW and SW management to a higher level, while many countries in the DRB are still struggling to fulfil the requirements set out in the previous version of the Directive, especially in relation to small settlements, resulting in significant pollution of water bodies in the DRB.

Our approach focuses on creating a clear framework to enable and support WW and SW management in small settlements. We advocate the use of nature-based solutions (NBS) that are tailored to local needs and offer a sustainable approach with multiple environmental, social and economic benefits for the DRB. Our project emphasizes knowledge transfer, capacity-building, and a holistic approach to building the capacity of decision-makers and practitioners.

Given the common challenge of regenerative WW and SW management, the need for transnational cooperation is emphasised. By pooling expertise and resources, we aim to effectively tackle dispersed pollution and mainstream NBS solutions - an innovative approach that could solve the region’s problems. Transnational collaboration provides a platform for sharing experiences, learning, and showcasing and testing potential solutions, fostering a collective learning environment.

The project outputs will be based on pilot actions where solutions will be co-designed and tested in different geographical areas of the DRB - including the Sava River Basin; the Drava-Mura River Basin, the Tisza River Basin and the Lower Danube. As a result, a roadmap for WW and SW management in the Danube region and a transnational strategy for sustainable management will be developed. These outputs will provide practical guidance, recommendations and support to the responsible authorities and practitioners for the development of specific national strategies on WW and SW management in small settlements. Additionally, the project will provide trainings, establish training materials, launch a knowledge hub, and organize webinars to facilitate knowledge sharing and capacity-building. All this will be supported by a comprehensive and targeted communication and dissemination strategy to ensure real impact - also outside the project partnership and beyond the project lifetime. This will result in the uptake of designed solutions and strategies in will have direct impact on increased capacities of organizations on WW and SW management.

To summarize, our project aims to address the multi-layered challenges of WW and SW management in the DRB through a collaborative, innovative, and transnational approach to ultimately striving for improved water quality and a sustainable future for all stakeholders involved.

titleEn: Flexible disadvantage compensation trainings for early school leavers in vocational education
summaryEn:
The FLEXITRAIN project aims at integrating early school leavers into the labour market through developing, testing and rolling out novel, flexible disadvantage compensation training methods in the Danube Region. Early school leaving remains a substantial challenge for education policy makers in Europe. According to Eurostat, the average rate of early school leavers decreased steadily in the past 10 years from 13% in 2022 to 9,6% in 2022 with significant differences and performance among member states. Remarkably, the Danube Region includes countries with the highest and lowest dropout rates but not with the typical pattern seen in many other fields of economy and society. Starting from a transregional analysis and benchmarking, the partnership will identify underlying reasons for early school leaving. The transnational benchmarking will also help select vocational training tools/methods that can form the base for the FLEXITRAIN toolbox. This toolbox will be jointly developed, tested and introduced by the partnership. Partners will run pilots in each region with new and/or upgraded flexible vocations tools, methodologies. The project aims at rolling out its jointly developed solution through dissemination, through initiating changes in institutional settings and taking its results to vocational centres in partner regions. This will be faciliated by our Joint Strategy and Action Plan.
The expected change is tested, introduced and upscaled new and/or upgraded flexible learning paths in vocational training centres that contribute to reduced dropout rates in the Danube Region.
The FLEXITRAIN partnership is composed of 11 partners and 12 ASPs from 9 countries of the Danube Region. The coverage in terms of geography is strong and offers excellent opportunities to have analysis results and develop a joint solution that holds relevance overall in the Danube Region. The consortium includes 4 NGOS, 3 training centres, 1 national public authority, 1 chamber of commerce, 1 university and 1 employment centre, which is further enriched by our ASPs.

titleEn: Lakes and Reservoirs in the Danube River Basin - “Towards coordinated actions of lakes and reservoirs management to reduce flood risks in the Danube River Basin”
summaryEn:
Europe and the citizens of the EU have to face the risks and hazards of floods due to the effects of climate change. The main aim of the project is to focus on the roles of lakes and reservoirs, to observe their relevance in flood risk control and reduction and to create a useful tool that serves the targets of flood risk mitigation.
Over the past decades Danube countries have recognized that it is not enough to implement measures at national level to manage floods and reduce associated risks, nations have to conceive issues transnationally.Several international projects have already been launched to assess flood risk levels on river basin level.However,reservoirs and lakes have also major effect in flood risk reduction, with addition to fluvial systems,which has not been the subject of concerted studies and analyzes. The transnational effects of lakes and reservoirs are not precisely defined yet, and there is no coordination platform where the affected countries can make requests or exchange data for the use of reservoirs in other countries in emergency situations.
Although many large reservoirs have been constructed primarily to generate power, positive effects on flood control are also evident. Large alpine annual storage reservoirs, often built as dams and found in the mountainous parts of the Danube basin, can attenuate and translate flood waves.Downstream sections benefit more the greater the retention capacity of the reservoirs and the closer the distance to the reservoir.
The potential for active flood management is likely to be lower for reservoirs at run-of-river power plants. Due to the low retention capacity, weir gates are opened during floods. Flood relief measures thus often focus on the time before the event,where additional storage volumes can be created by targeted pondage draw-down. Particularly in the case of reservoirs (pondages) for hydroenergy, an intense draw-down could represent a considerable economic risk. Flood control measures are therefore subject to various tensions. To what extent storage reservoir facilities built on rivers contribute to the reduction of flood risks can not be appropriately assessed without sufficient, resilient and relevant case-specific data. LAREDAR is expected to provide new insights into the interrelationship between reservoirs and floods along transboundary river sections, based on investigations in the pilot regions. The aim is not only to investigate the existing impacts of reservoirs holistically and at the catchment level, but also to suggest additional good practices that will improve flood risk management.
With the help of the project it should be possible to quantify the potential impact of storage reservoirs on floods in order to derive measures for the reduction of flood risk in downstream river stretches.
The porject's main objective is to improve the transnational flood risk mitigation management of the Danube River Basin (DRB) with a specifically tailored newly developed platform which enhances sustainability in the frame of transnational cooperation under the ICPDR umbrella. Based on the No.2007/60/EC Directive on the assessment and management of flood (Floods Directive), first will explore the potential lakes and reservoirs in the entire Danube catchment having significant impact on flood risk management and the ICPDR DFRMP Annex - 2 and the Danube Strategy will be taken into account, as well. Analyzes will focus on flood routing on lakes and reservoirs, as well as the technical status of a hydrological and hazard assessment of incident caused, e.g. by a dike or levee failure.
Since a reservoir could be a significant facility of a catchment area, which could be suitable for flood peak reduction, it may be necessary to review the flood control practices and operational management (operation rules)of such reservoir.The purpose of the review is to reach the highest benefit on flood attenuation and/or propagation.Modelling of flood hazard situations will also be carried out and the results can also be used to create optimal operating water levels (elevations) for lakes and reservoirs, taking into account WFD ecological and biodiversity aspects, as well. The modelling will explore how reservoirs can be operated to achieve and increase cross-border benefits.
However, since no long-term plans or reconciliation/harmonization/cooperation structures are available, the outcome of the project will be a developed coordination platform, where each country could exchange data and information in the event of a major flood, and the higher risk countries will be able to formulate requests on modified reservoir operation towards upstream countries. Based on the surveyed and identified hazard and risk maps, a risk management guidance will be developed that will assist the countries in reviewing and modifying DRBMP and FRMP.The achievements of the new method in flood risk management will be checked and demonstrated with a flood preparedness exercise for DRB.

titleEn: Universities Revitalizing Growth and Empowerment in the Danube Region
summaryEn:
URGE main objective is to develop the multiannual and multilateral project that will provide a base for making a lasting impact through collaboration with scientific diaspora in participating countries. The common challenge jointly tackled in this project revolves around the phenomenon of brain drain and the potent role of diaspora in addressing it. As scholars, we recognize the profound impact of brain drain on Southeast Europe, where talented individuals often seek opportunities abroad, leading to a loss of human capital and expertise. We also face a severe lack of data on the scope and characteristics of scientific diaspora that might be engaged and contribute to home societies. Within this challenge lies an opportunity — the potential of our diaspora to become agents of change, to invest not only financially but also through the transfer of knowledge and networks.

At the heart of our ambition lies the recognition of the invaluable role of scientific diasporas. They are not just bridges between worlds; they are catalysts for innovation, for collaboration across borders. The project recognizes the vital role of scientific diasporas in fostering cooperation, innovation, and problem-solving in emerging economies. It emphasizes the importance of leveraging the expertise and networks of scientific diasporas to advise and support their countries of origin in addressing challenges such as brain drain. Lack of information on opportunities, lack of institutional networks able to make cooperation run more smoothly and lack of financial resources for first contact and early-stage project developments, are significant obstacles for a more systemic cooperation. The key novelty of this initiative that wants to bridge particular actions of different countries on diaspora engagement with the focus on scientific, highly-skilled diaspora that can bring positive impact in academic community of the region and enable both scientific and economic advancement and higher competitiveness. 

The URGE project main objective is to establish a joint scientific diaspora network that will enable institutional framework and mechanisms to mitigate the effects of brain drain within academic community and subsequently contribute to societal development with their expertise. In pursuing this objective, we aim to:



1.	Build a Joint Scientific e-Diaspora Platform: At the core of our initiative lies the establishment of a joint platform that unites the scientific diaspora within Southeast Europe. This platform will serve as a dynamic hub, mapping the diaspora and creating comprehensive expertise portfolios for each member. By utilizing the collective wisdom and diverse experiences of the diaspora, we aim to leverage their knowledge to fuel innovation and progress within the region. It will build on the individual short-lived attempts in participating countries to build a database of scientific diaspora, scaling up these efforts to joint action institutionalized within largest universities in the region.



2.	Support Scientific Circulation and Science Diplomacy for Academic and Societal Development. We are dedicated to facilitating the circulation of scientists between diaspora and home countries, by organizing virtual events featuring tailored breakrooms for focused discussions based on expertise and enabling shorter stays in the region for impactful collaboration. By cultivating a culture of collaborative learning with diaspora representatives and joint mentorship program for early career researchers, we aim to equip academic community members from our countries with the skills necessary to involve in a dynamic global research environment. Additionally, our programs include seed funding initiatives aimed at catalysing joint work among scientists for applying to competitive funding, further enhancing their ability to drive innovation and make meaningful contributions to their respective fields.



3.	Embed the e-Diaspora into the national scientific infrastructure: Drawing insights from the Montenegrin model, it's imperative to engage with stakeholders across country's scientific landscape to develop a comprehensive integration plan, ensuring alignment with existing infrastructure and regulatory frameworks for each country. This is a key action to ensure sustainability of the project outcomes. With targeted awareness campaigns and engagement initiatives among targeting groups, we will effectively provide durable tool for fostering collaboration and innovation, helping researchers to build new partnerships and opportunities.

The project will extend its outreach to associate partners and other universities in the region through the Danube Rectors Conference and Rectors’ Forum of Southeast Europe and Western Balkans. We cooperate and coordinate our efforts with Regional Cooperation Council making our action complementary to diaspora activities of RCC and bringing synergy by focusing on scientific diaspora as invaluable resource.

titleEn: Diversifying labour markets in industrial cities of the Danube Region via enhanced stakeholder cooperation & skills matchmaking to support local transitions & promote long-term sustainable development
summaryEn:
SteelCityZen is a collaborative endeavour of 11 partners from 9 countries (HU, RO, BA, ME, CZ, BG, RS, AT, SI) aimed at addressing the shared challenges faced by (mono)industrial cities across the Danube Programme Region (DPR).

CHALLENGE: When it comes to local labour markets, these cities – characterised by their strong reliance on single, often resource intensive industries – confront significant vulnerabilities conditioned by local skills path dependencies, volatile operation of major industrial enterprises, and increasing push for green and digital transitions. These vulnerabilities affect a big part of their local populations (incl. esp. citizens with lower education levels). While local branches of regional / national public labour market support organisations are dedicated to providing support to local citizens and businesses with regards to employment issues, they lack a connection to local place-based development processes, failing to stay attuned to new local labour market challenges presented by local (industrial and twin) transitions. Thus, there is a strong need for enhancing the mechanisms of labour market support and related capacity building for public authorities and labour market professionals.

OBJECTIVE & EXPECTED CHANGE: The project’s overarching objective is to empower Danube Region towns with strong (mono)industrial legacies in facilitating labour market diversification aligned with the priorities of their local economic restructuring (including green & digital transitions). This is to be achieved via strengthening local stakeholder cooperation and coordination (under the leadership of municipalities working closely with local employment support bodies) and enhancing local skills needs assessment & matchmaking mechanisms. By the end of this project, municipalities of the SteelCityZen partner cities and local labour market professionals will be better equipped for supporting local labour market diversification processes. 

APPROACH & ITS TRANSNATIONALITY: SteelCityZen presents a comprehensive approach to labour market diversification in (mono)industrial cities of the DPR. Stemming from the premise that such cities need to tackle multiple economic transitions when developing labour market interventions, the project offers an innovative framework to support municipal decision-making and support functions regarding local re-/upskilling, employment and job creation practices. 

Central to SteelCityZen's approach is the recognition of the need for a transnational perspective. The project was designed to address the baseline problem of creating solutions for cities undergoing difficult industrial transition periods; however, by fostering collaboration and knowledge exchange among cities across the Danube Region, the project seeks to leverage collective expertise and resources to ensure that project solutions can be adapted to any specific context. The main feature of the SteelCityZen methodology is its flexibility reflected in its ability to accommodate both commonalities and specificities of the labour market situations in 8 DPR SteelCityZen cities.

MAIN OUTPUTS & TARGET GROUPS

The main project outputs include: 
# 3 innovative solutions for supporting labour market diversification and relevant capacity building processes (O

2.2), validated via relevant pilot actions (O

2.1). These solutions include: 1) Online Platform for local labour market restructuring (skills needs assessment & matchmaking at the local level), 2) Community-driven spaces for local labour market diversification attuned to the local labour market challenges & vulnerabilities, 3) Long-term frameworks of cooperation between municipalities and local employers for developing local job placement & re-/upskilling aligned with local economic priorities. 
# Joint Strategy and Action Plans (O

3.1) jointly developed within the partnership for all 8 SteelCityZen cities to elaborate on the measures for increasing the adaptiveness of municipalities and local labour support organisations to the needs of local labour market diversification.

These outputs are geared towards empowering municipalities, businesses (including bigger enterprises and SMEs), and local communities to navigate the complexities of economic and labour market restructuring and embrace the changing role of municipalities in the process. The learnings from the project are meant for further use, replication, and capacity building among municipalities and labour market professionals across the Danube Region.
WHAT IS NEW & ORIGINAL ABOUT STEELCITYZEN: So far there has been no other project aimed at supporting municipalities in adopting a comprehensive approach for labour market diversification in (mono)industrial cities. Thus, SteelCityZen represents a bold and forward-thinking initiative that holds the potential to catalyse positive transformation across the Danube Region and beyond.

titleEn: Establishing a Danube training academy as measure against brain drain from rural and crisis regions
summaryEn:
Project territory and common challenge: TransAC's project territory comprises 7 regions: Carinthia in Austria, Zenica-Doboj Canton in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Karlovacka County in Croatia, Northern Bavaria in Germany, the West Region in Romania, Vojadina in Serbia, and the Kharkiv Region in Ukraine. The objective of TransAC is to tackle the issue of brain drain in these rural and crisis-stricken regions. According to Eurostat, rural regions are non-urban areas. Crisis regions are areas that have been cut off from the global flow of goods due to factors such as war. In the project area, limited job opportunities make life less attractive, prompting many young people to relocate. The population in the project area is ageing, which exacerbates the problem of brain drain and social stress. This is a common challenge.

Overall objective and expected change: The TransAC project aims to address the negative impacts of brain drain and social stress in rural and crisis regions. It will focus on young learners, who are most likely to migrate, as well as vulnerable learners, including the unemployed, early school leavers, women, older people, and workers in carbon-related industries, who are most affected by social stress. Both groups will receive training to improve their future prospects. The project focuses on training for additive manufacturing due to its economic potential for the project territory, as well as the high demand for trainees in this field. To fully realize the potential of the labor and training markets, relevant stakeholders, such as industry/SMEs, policymakers, and schools, will be involved in the development process and throughout the project. The expected change is to enhance the project territory as a good place for learning and living by providing opportunities for learners. We are also committed to look how TransAC can improve the situation of Roma people.
Main outputs and beneficiaries: There are 3 main outputs that reinforce each other. Output 

1.2 is the pilot training centre, which serves as TransAC's innovation space for developing training services. This includes the development of course content, laboratory equipment, co-teaching formats, FabLabs, and micro-credentials. Testing will be conducted in all seven project regions before the training services are transferred to the Training Academy. Output 

1.3 relates to the Training Academy, which aims to capitalize and commercialize the training services developed in the pilot training center. Stakeholders from industry, education, and policy will be involved to address labor and training market needs. Finally, Output 

2.1 focuses on the 572 learners directly reached by TransAC, including 192 school children, 228 university students, and 152 vulnerable individuals. Learners will provide input through interviews and questionnaires on entry points, training formats, content, and methodology. Special attention will be given to the correct handling of vulnerable learners with the assistance of interdisciplinary teams comprising teachers, technical researchers, and social workers.
The main beneficiaries of the outputs will be the learners and stakeholders, ultimately benefiting the project territory and the Danube region.
Approach: The TransAC approach employs a co-creation format using a triple-helix innovation method. The project unites educational institutions, industry, policy makers, and facilitators to establish an effective framework for education and training. It is suggested that this project should not be limited to a national basis, as it may attract the most talented individuals from other regions. A national project may improve one region, but at the expense of neighbouring regions and nations. If another region were to undertake a similar project, it could attract talent from the first region, resulting in a migration of talent within countries rather than continuous development for the benefit of all. To prevent unhealthy competition between already disadvantaged regions, the TransAC project has adopted a transnational approach.
Innovation: The approach employed by TransAC is innovative and unique. It uses a multidisciplinary approach to additive manufacturing training, integrating expertise in social work, education, and technical research. This approach facilitates the development of high-quality training services and provides learning opportunities for disadvantaged learners. The training academy utilises advanced educational methods, including virtual labs, remote labs, mobile labs, and FabLabs, to provide an interactive learning experience. At TransAC, the Coding School and FabLab are integrated with traditional educational methods to establish a mutually beneficial relationship. Learners have the freedom to set their own goals through models such as micro-credentials. The training academy helps learners improve their skills while managing their work and personal commitments through part-time or distance learning programmes.

titleEn: FUNCTIONAL DANUBE AREAS - Enhancing Institutional Capacities for Managing Functional Urban Areas in the Danube Region
summaryEn:
The Danube Region faces notable discrepancies in regional development policies, characterized by a deficiency in implementing integrated urban and regional development strategies due to inadequate local and civil participation. This gap is particularly pronounced in the development of functional urban areas (FUAs) based on genuine linkages and interdependencies among urban centers and smaller settlements. 

Functional Urban Areas (FUAs) are territories located around a city or urban centre and linked to this central area through economic, social and cultural links. These areas form a functional unit, as people living there share infrastructure, services and economic activities, while commuting to the city centre and sharing labour markets. Key documents defining the concept of functional urban areas include ESPON research reports and studies, such as the ESPON Database and the ESPON Territorial Reference Handbook, and the OECD report Functional Urban Areas (FUAs) - A New Approach to Metropolitan Areas, which details the OECD methodology for defining functional urban areas.
FUAs, as networks of cities or towns with functional relationships extending beyond individual cities, present significant management opportunities in urban planning and development. Effective management strategies for FUAs entail networked cooperation, joint strategic planning, collaborative projects, utilization of funding opportunities, and communication and partnership building among participating cities and regions.

The absence of a common governance methodology for FUAs in the Danube Region underscores the importance of exchanging best practices and experiences among countries to foster joint thinking and knowledge sharing. Although cross-border links within FUAs are prevalent, they rarely culminate in a unified administrative unit.
To address these challenges, the FUNDA project aim to consolidate FUA delimitation methodologies, integrate good practices, and establish a monitoring system/data platform for successful FUA delineation and management in the Danube Region as well as to establish a governance methodology, which will be elaborated in the transnational strategy as joint solution for policy makers and local and regional actors for FUA management. With the establishment of the FUA-NET network, the results of the project are expected to have a long-term impact, by joining committed cities, FUAs and stakeholders.

9 out of 14 countries in the Danube Region are participating in the FUNDA project, with 11 financing partners and 10 ASPs, allowing for knowledge sharing between partner countries with different experiences in the field of functional urban area management.

Transnational cooperation is pivotal in addressing common challenges transcending national borders. In preparing the project, the partners identified three such key challenges and three pilot activities to address these.
Pilot activities within the project explore themes such as integrating human public services, green infrastructure, and business infrastructure into FUA management, culminating in an unprecedented, complex, multi-perspective management model applicable to the Danube Region. 
Participatory planning -which will also play an important role in the pilot activities of the project- plays a crucial role in promoting social cohesion, conflict resolution, and democratic decision-making in FUAs by considering multiple perspectives and engaging various stakeholders.

Stakeholders at local, regional, national, and transnational levels stand to benefit from the project, with local authorities gaining insights into local challenges and opportunities, regional authorities broadening their understanding of FUA management, and national authorities enhancing their governance models. Sectoral agencies, infrastructure providers, and service providers can leverage project outcomes to improve their efficiency and collaboration. Furthermore, the involvement of interest groups, enterprises, business support organizations, and European Groupings of Territorial Cooperation (EGTCs) in participatory planning ensures diverse perspectives are considered, promoting sustainable and inclusive urban development in the Danube Region.

In conclusion, collaborative efforts and knowledge sharing are essential for effectively managing FUAs in the Danube Region, with transnational cooperation and participatory planning serving as vital tools in addressing complex urban challenges and fostering inclusive development. Through initiatives like the FUNDA project, stakeholders can work together to build resilient and prosperous urban-rural communities across borders.

titleEn: Personalized Approach to Territorial Life and Career Support
summaryEn:
The common challenges faced by the countries involved in the PATHS project are rooted in the lack of opportunities for informed career choices and the lack of services that are widely available (including for children of disadvantaged, rural areas and parents with low educational attainment). This highlights shortcomings in terms of equal and equity opportunities. Young people wishing to enter secondary and higher education currently only attend ad hoc, limited information-sharing career awareness sessions and events provided by educational institutions, which increases the risk of drop-out, both in secondary and higher, vocational and adult education. In addition, disadvantaged rural areas are characterised by the outward migration of young people and those with higher education, the ageing of the resident population and the depopulation of the countryside. This situation not only negatively impacted the well-being and living standards of young people (especially NEETs) but also posed threats to the social and economic sustainability of these areas.
A solution is therefore needed to help them (at local level) to stay in the area and to make informed, self-aware career choices.
The general objective of the project is to develop accessible, inclusive, high quality services at the municipal level, strengthening LLL and the retention capacity of rural areas, by developing and expanding the existing institutional and professional capacities.
The primary target groups:
o Young people (12-18) living in rural areas who would have access to career guidance presentations, information materials and online information only in an institutional framework, on a case-by-case basis, without a holistic approach. In many cases, this means an educational institution far from their place of residence, in the context of classroom lessons. The socio-economic status of the family does not allow them to access a market-based service at their own expense. Young people participate in the "I own the path!" camp and in LPs.
o Mentors who, as counsellors, trainers, coaches, teachers, parents, social workers, psychologists, etc., take part in mentor training and are then qualified to run the municipal LPSS, and as professionals from SMEs and large companies, take on the task of hosting young people for work placements, supervising their work and evaluating their performance. 
As a result of the project, a LPSS will be established at the municipal level, independent of the education and training institutions, which will provide young people living in rural areas with full access to innovative, self-awareness-based career guidance services in their localities, thus improving their labour market situation. Following an individual development process, these young people test their knowledge and skills in a workplace environment. The result is a jointly developed solution that will be tested by the partners (HU, SK, RO, BA, CZ, HR) in a LP project with 2 components.
The planned actions will help to prepare both mentors and young people participating in the PATHS programme for the LP. All actions will be accompanied by monitoring and social impact measurement tools.
A and SI do not benefit from most of the common challenges, but are rather good practice countries that ensure the professional quality of the project. They are also involved in joint development and implementation. 

The long-term sustainability of the solution will be ensured by: 
- The 2 comp. of the model tested in the LPs, jointly developed by the PPs, will remain operational in the LP municipalities, with the commitment of mentors beyond the project period.
- Development and establishment of the Strategy, AP and Network of the DR LPSS, with a continuous exchange of knowledge and experience, also after the project closure;
- Policy recommendation in the field of LL support: integrating the mentor training programme into the portfolio of the institutions concerned and into the legislative environment.
- In the framework of the DR LPSS Network, the following will continue to operate after the closure of the project: Career Guidance Expert, Coordination and Methodology Team (CG ECMT, national level), Intersectoral Working Groups (IWG, national level) as Sectoral Learning Dialogues (SLDs).
A priority focus area for the DR Strategy in 2024 is the creation of a more attractive and liveable settlement environment for young people, counteracting the brain drain, building on the resources of local community spaces. This common challenge requires a common solution, which the PATHS project model is an appropriate response to. 

The social innovation elements of the project are based on linking the settlement environment and career orientation, expanding the range of services available at the place of residence, generating and maintaining cross-sectoral cooperation, compensating for the lack of capacity and resources in the education and training institutions and in the settlements.

titleEn: Turning Danube Region into Competitive International Education Destination
summaryEn:
This project will develop all preparatory activities and will result in the development of a proposal for the main project which aims to make the Danube Region more competitive by making it more attractive in the international education and research market and reverse negative migration trends characterized by brain drain, and instead support positive brain circulation mechanisms across the region.

To develop such a project proposal, this seed money project will:
- Analyse current situation in Danube region countries regarding the internationalization of education and their strengths and weaknesses as destinations for international students
- Identify supporting mechanisms to improve the offer (such as for example specialized language trainings for teachers in order to increase number of courses available in English...)
- Identify joint collaboration opportunities that would increase the value proposition for international students and researchers, such as joint programmes, joint summer/winter schools, etc.
- Explore opportunities for joint promotion (Danube pavilion at EAIE, NAFSA and other international fairs, joint materials, websites, joint student recruitment agency/intermediary...)
- Do a report on brain circulation in the region, also including topics such as number of STEAM students, women resarchers, models for reintegration, etc.
- Organize stakeholders consultation to make sure that the proposed support measures to be included in the main project proposal will impact positively the stakeholders and create a sustainable and long-lasting change

The project will be implemented by experienced organizations, who are in charge of implementing international cooperation in higher education in their respective countries and who are in constant contact with the main beneficiaries and will significantly involve the stakeholders views and perspectives into the development of the support activities of the main project.

titleEn: Integrated Disaster Management Network in the Danube Region
summaryEn:
The consortium, through its concerted efforts, seeks to implement a transformative project that fundamentally enhances disaster management capabilities within the Danube Region. This endeavor is rooted in the recognition of escalating environmental challenges and the imperative for a coordinated, transnational response. Our primary objective is the establishment of a unified disaster management framework, tailored to the diverse and specific conditions prevalent across the Danube countries, thereby ensuring a cohesive and effective approach to disaster prevention, preparedness, and response.

Innovatively leveraging advanced technologies, the consortium aims to revolutionize early warning early action, facilitating swift and informed decision-making. The establishment of a secure, cross-border information-sharing platform will enable the seamless exchange of critical data, enhancing coordination and operational efficiency across national borders.

Recognizing the paramount importance of local community engagement, the project is committed to fostering grassroots involvement in disaster risk reduction. Through comprehensive awareness and educational programs, the consortium will empower communities, enhancing their resilience and capacity to actively participate in disaster management efforts.

By adopting and adapting successful practices from across the globe, alongside the development of new, innovative solutions, the consortium's approach transcends traditional disaster management methodologies. It emphasizes cross-border collaboration, standardization of procedures, and the integration of cutting-edge technology, setting a new benchmark for disaster management practices both within the Danube Region.

In conclusion, the consortium is dedicated to building a disaster-resilient Danube Region through this project. By addressing the immediate challenges of disaster management and laying the groundwork for sustainable, long-term resilience, the consortium's collaborative effort will safeguard the region's environment, economies, and communities against the adverse effects of climate change and natural disasters.

titleEn: Danube Region's Youth Leadership in Ensuring Resilience through a Proactive Approach in Water Sector
summaryEn:
The involvement of the Youth in building water secure resilient society effectively managing extreme events such as floods and droughts, ensuring water quality, mitigating of biodiversity loss, and trade-offs to waterborne transport -lags to what is needed in the Danube Region. Recognizing the importance of increasing societal preparedness for climate change-induced hazards in line with the EU Strategy for the Danube Region, it is very important to engage the youth in addressing these pressing issues. General knowledge and awareness and the skills for resilient management through water career choices are areas in which many young people in the Danube Region lack leadership skills and relevant backgrounds for informed, and self-driven action and activities. Multiple institutions on national level (Ministries, Research Institutes, Universities, NGOs) and transnational level (such as EUSDR, ICPDR, GWP) reflect this situation. They develop activities to raise awareness, engage, build capacities, support youth networks and knowledge exchange, drive youth – governance dialogue, including establishing Danube Youth Council. The experience and evidence collected by them show clearly – that urgent transformation is needed in key areas. 
1, Knowing the youth, their interests, needs, and knowledge on water management issues. 
2, Enhancing skills for resilience building in water and related sectors, and enable intergenerational cooperation. 
3, Creating platforms for meaningful youth participation, knowledge co-creation, and leadership
4, Channelling youth engagement, representation in decision-making and facilitating dialogue with young stakeholders
The proposal creates strategically aligned youth-targeted activities supporting the EUSDR Strategy Action Points of the Priority areas PA4 (Water Quality), PA5 (Environmental Risks), PA7 (Knowledge Society) in a mid-term, and through partners and Danube Youth Council Members is linked to PA 1A (Waterways Mobility) and PA9 (People & Skills). The approaches designed by joint forces of the partners and invited representatives of target groups in the seed money facility project will be fundable under open schemes as a standalone proposal - the main project. Activities will be adaptable to constitute working packages or tasks in other proposals, which will improve the fundability of the main project ideas. Each of three project outputs is supported by carefully selected preparatory activities. We map and analyse the state of the play and review the youth activities undertaken in the water sector in the Danube Region.
