The species is endangered by unsustainable human activities and climate change issues, such as extreme temperatures, shifts in precipitation patterns and fluctuating water tables throughout the year, by invasive pathogens (e.g. Hymenoscyphus fraxineus) and by a frequently observed loss of natural reproduction. Considering the lack of guidance on how to manage these forests, a significant decrease in abundance of narrow-leaved ash can be expected in near future with consequent economic losses, destabilization of stands and loss of alluvial forests biodiversity. Having this in mind, a coordinated international approach is needed to enhance the resilience of narrow-leaved ash forest resources and ecosystem services in the Danube region, with a strong emphasis on sustainable forest management and conservation of this species genetic resources.

Therefore, overall objective of SCAN-DANUBE is to counteract narrow-leaved ash forests decline in the Danube region by providing novel strategies and guidelines for forest management and conservation of this tree species in both commercially used and protected alluvial forests of the Danube area. The SCAN-DANUBE consortium consists of 6 project partners and 9 associated partners from Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Czech Republic, Serbia and Slovenia, geographically covering the largest part of the natural distribution of narrow-leaved ash in the Danube region, and is led by the Mendel University in Brno.

SCAN-DANUBE includes 3 thematic special objectives (SOs): 1) interpreting and advancing the knowledge regarding the narrow-leaved ash past and the present status in the Danube region, 2) enhancing management and conservation of this species across the thematic region, and 3) implementing novel monitoring system and breeding strategies to enhance the vitality and preservation of narrow-leaved ash in the partner’s countries.

To address these specific objectives, the SCAN-DANUBE focuses on the following goals: i) to overview the current and past status of narrow-leaved ash in the partner countries, as well as to contribute to the better understanding of drivers leading to the decline of narrow-leaved ash forests across the Danube region and their dependence on specific climate and habitat conditions and management history, ii) to develop the strategies and guidelines for sustainable management and conservation of narrow-leaved ash forest resources, including improvement of natural regeneration by enhancing seed production and addressing factors affecting fruiting patterns and germination, iii) to establish a monitoring network, based on novel Internet of Things (IoT) technology, able to automatically generate data of trees vitality in a near real-time, iv) to produce the guideline providing best practices for plant selection, propagation, and plantation establishment, v) to increase and share the science-based knowledge among state authorities, nature conservation officers, national park managers, forest companies and private forest owners, in order to increase decision security while managing and protecting narrow-leaved ash forests across the Danube region. The relevant stakeholders will contribute to the project by providing their practical experiences and expressing their interests, guiding, therefore, the development of strategies and sustainable action plans.

titleEn: Supporting the socio-economic integration of youth leaving child protection systems by developing their skills and capacities through more inclusive leaving care policies in the Danube region
summaryEn:
The countries in the Danube region still face many challenges in terms of social inclusion, equal opportunities and improving the quality of life, especially in terms of people from vulnerable or marginalized groups. Such a category is represented by young people leaving the special child protection system, a series of common challenges being identified in this sense. Among the problems underlying the difficult situation in which this social category finds itself in the countries of the Danube region, is the one related to education, considering two perspectives: on the one hand, insufficient training or the lack of effective training, and on the other hand, the incompatibility between education and the needs of the labour market. Associated with the lack of motivation and low self-esteem among young people coming from the child protection system, this problem results in the lack of skills and qualifications needed to find a job, which ultimately leads to unemployment. All these aspects create financial difficulties for young people who come out of the care system, in most of the countries in the Danube region problems have been reported regarding housing, access to the healthcare system and low quality of their lives. Therefore, the common challenges in the Danube region countries presented above will be jointly addressed in the project.
The project aims to improve leave care policies in the Danube region and develop an educational program for young people leaving the special child protection system that includes the development of personal skills required to be integrated in the labour market, including mentoring programs and opportunities to support employability. Social integration measures will include pilot activities to insert vulnerable young people into training programs, internships and specialized support for independent living. Therefore, the expected change the project will make to the current situation refers to increasing the employment chances of young people leaving the care system – and at the same time, the general improvement of their quality of life, by developing the necessary skills and creating opportunities in this regard.
The main outputs the project will produce are: Joint Pilot testing of Skills4Life Innovative Training Programme dedicated to young people leaving special child protection system; Co-designed Skills4Life Innovative Training Programme dedicated to young people leaving special child protection system, tested and validated; Pilot testing of Skills4Life Innovative Mentoring and Counseling Model for Youth; Jointly developed, tested Skills4Life Innovative Mentoring and Counseling Model for Vulnerable Youth Integration; Danube Skills4Life Strategy for disadvantaged youth; Danube Skills4Life Action plan for Strategy implementation; Pilot actions on youth integration to labour market; Jointly developed, tested S4L Support Methodology for successful and effective implementation of youth integration policies, based on the pilot actions implementation; Skills4Life Youth Empowerment Network for the Danube region. Among those who will benefit from these outputs are: young people coming from the institutionalized system; organisations that work with young people; education/training centers; companies in the project implementation areas; local, regional and national public authorities; society in general. 
The project builds consistent mechanisms that provide direct support for young people who no longer benefit from institutional care, such as: access to free training, counselling and mentoring services; connections to public authorities that can provide guidance and support; connections to potential employers. The field addressed in the project presents a series of particularities specific to the country of each partner. Similarly, know-how differs from one state to another, and cooperation exponentially increases the volume of available information, as well as the way of working with the target groups. Transnational cooperation is necessary to address the identified challenges as it enables shared learning, capacity building, coordinated action on cross-border challenges, policy alignment and harmonization, as well as networking and collaboration between stakeholders. By this approach, the project partners, target groups, project area, and DRP area can gain access to a wider range of resources, expertise, and opportunities, leading to more effective and sustainable outcomes.
The project's approach goes beyond existing practice by offering a comprehensive and tailored support system for young people leaving the special child protection system. Through innovative training programs, personalized mentoring and coaching, practical pilot actions, and collaborative networking opportunities, the project aims to empower young people with the skills, resources, and support they need to successfully transition to independent adulthood and integration into the labour market.

titleEn: Innovative Water Retention for Climate Change Mitigation, Sustainable Agriculture and Flood Protection
summaryEn:
Climate change results changing precipitation conditions, evapotranspiration and drier soil conditions which all contribute to a decrease in groundwater recharge. Given the current trends, his phenomenon will be most pronounced in the middle and lower sections of the Danube, threatening the water supply of millions of people. Groundwater is in direct interaction with nearby rivers, tributaries or irrigation channels: when the river level is high, the tributary recharges the groundwater, while when the river level is low, the tributary has a draining, tapping effect, creating a depression in the groundwater level. The presence of a tributary or paleochannel also affects the groundwater level: paleochannel crossings influence the stability of the dikes. 

The project aims to address several challenges such as water scarcity and declining water quality; flood protection challenges due to outdated infrastructure; coordination among different stakeholders in water management approaches; access to reliable data for decision-making; capacity development and awareness raising.

They are planned to be tackled as the following:


1. Tailored methodologies for managed aquifer recharge (MAR) technology;


2. Pre-feasibility studies and pilot actions in sample areas;


3. Establishment of monitoring systems;


4. Policy development and stakeholder engagement;


5. Environmental impact analysis and capacity building.

The main project objective is: establishment of an integrated and sustainable transnational water management approach in the Danube River Basin, through promotion of innovative water retention measures, as nature-based groundwater management solution, for the sake of mitigation of climate change impact, sustainable agriculture and flood protection.

The project has three specific objectives, including:


1.	Development of a joint methodology, through collection of archive data, delineation of sampling areas and development of pre-feasibility studies for the application of innovative water retention technologies.


2.	Establishment of a monitoring system for MAR technologies in the four cross-border pilot areas. It serves a twofold aim: investigation of the hydrodynamic connection between paleochannels and the Danube river and determination of dike stability in the selected sample areas.


3.	In order to establish an integrated and sustainable transnational water management approach in the Danube River Basin, for the application of innovative water retention measures, a joint action plan will be developed.

The project plans to have the following outputs:
-	Pilot feasibility studies elaborated for the four sample areas on application of MAR technologies: for the Upper/Upper-Middle section (Austria-Hungary), Middle (Hungary-Serbia), Lower Danube (Bulgaria-Romania) and the Sava river (Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia).
-	Development of a solution in form of a methodology handbook for application of MAR technology in the Danube river basin.
-	Establishment of pilot monitoring system for paleochannels and dike stability in the four pilot areas.
-	Testing of a monitoring system and dike stability solution in the pilot areas.
-	Elaboration of a joint action plan for improvement of dike stability.
-	Development of an action plan for the Danube area on application of MAR technology.
-	12 organisations cooperating in the project from 8 countries, thereof 5 is expected to have increased capacity, not being involved in MAR related projects before.

Main beneficiaries of the project are the partners, national and regional public authorities dealing with water management and flood protection, local public authorities located in the pilot and sample areas, sectoral agencies dealing with water management and research, infrastructure and public service providers. Given the project has a strong scientific and methodological background, higher education and research institutions are also key beneficiaries. SMEs, primarily in the agricultural sector also belong the target groups, as well as the general public, as water consumer.

As climate change is global and the Danube river is a transnational asset, transnational cooperation is essential. The collaborating partners represent different key players, including public national and regional water management bodies, universities, sectoral agencies and regional authorities, as well as private organisations with excellence experience in the project’s domain. As the Danube is a cross-border river in many places, the targeted pilot areas are all cross-border. The project methodology-wise heavily builds on the DEEPWATER-CE project, but focusing directly on areas located on alluvial and fluvial strata built up by the river itself, either directly at the Danube (Upper/Middle-Upper, Middle, Lower Danube) and at the Sava as tributary with very similar setup.

titleEn: Exploring the Roman Legacy: Creation of a theme region and cultural route along the Roman Danube Limes to empower the socio-economic development of shared European heritage
summaryEn:
The Roman Danube Limes, spanning over a length of 2400 kilometres from Germany to the Black Sea, is a prominent and outstanding example of a transnational heritage connecting multiple European countries in a macro-region. Its Western segment (Germany, Austria, Slovakia) has already been inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage in 2021; its Eastern part (Croatia, Serbia, Bulgaria, Romania) as well as the related Dacian Limes (Romania) are still on the Tentative List waiting for being incorporated in the huge transcontinental UNESCO World Heritage “Frontiers of the Roman Empire”. Thus, the Roman Danube Limes is a common European heritage that needs to be presented and promoted with joint efforts and following a common concept along its entire extent telling the story of the people that lived in the Danube Region 2000 years ago. It has not just been a border between the Roman Empire and the so-called Barbaricum, but also a pathway from West to the East and vice versa connecting the various Roman Danube provinces as well as the Germanic people and the Romans during peace times.
Several EU projects dealt with the Roman heritage in the Danube Region and its preservation and valorisation for a sustainable culture tourism in the past. Different tools and strategies for its promotion have been developed in this context and first steps towards a future European Cultural Route following the ancient pathway along the Danube have been laid out.
The present project brings together the relevant Interreg DTP projects (Living Danube Limes, Danube’s Archaeological eLandscapes, Iron-Age-Danube, ARCHEODANUBE, ISTER, Transdanube Travel Stories) as well as the networks built up around them, and capitalises their best-of outcomes with the overall aim to create a Cultural Route embedded in a wider Theme Region and submit it for certification in the last phase of the project aiming to become certified Cultural Route of the Council of Europe. Dealing with the Roman heritage within a larger Theme Region opens the possibility to, on the one hand, be able to expand the Cultural Route in the future, if required, and on the other hand to also tell the story of the remote hinterland which supplied the Limes line and therefore is an important factor of the Roman story-telling.
As a first and crucial step a network will be established providing a transnational platform for exchange and participation for all stakeholders dealing with the Roman heritage in the Danube Region (political stakeholders of various level, local/regional/national authorities, national UNESCO commissions, associations, archaeological sites and parks, museums, archaeologists and other researchers, tourism agencies and initiatives, cultural operators, other economical stakeholders etc.). A Scientific Board formed at the beginning of the project (partly already during its application phase) will accompany the process and support conceptualisation of the Cultural Route. 
A common interpretation and presentation framework for the whole Danube Region will be outlined and a joint branding strategy implemented to strengthen the coherence of the shared heritage. Existing information and tools will be gathered, and the gaps identified during this process will be closed. Various tools and formats for the presentation and promotion of Roman key sites along the route will be developed and installed (Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality (VR/AR) 3D models, Roman theme trails for hikers or bikers, visibility measures, Roman events, physical promotion material, mobile app, website, etc.).
All those actions taken, strategies outlined and tools implemented in the framework of the project aim at the overall target which is the creation of a Cultural Route along the Danube within a greater Theme Region and the submission of the same Route for certification to become a Cultural Route of the Council of Europe.

titleEn: Danube Ruralscapes - a Network of Professional Support for Self-organized Village Clusters Achieving Sustainable Heritage-based Ruralscapes
summaryEn:
Most of the Danube Region consists of rural landscapes with networks of rural villages having traditional architecture and land use that define its identity, but today a lack of planning and management capacities with respect to urban centers lead to the decay of these rural landscapes and their quality of living. Danube Ruralscapes aims to develop a common good practice model for rural town planning that can serve as a basis for national, regional and local-level public policies in the Danube Region area where national legislation and regional governance regulating heritage-based and sustainable rural planning are missing or not able to target village communities with limited resources and a lack of professional competences. The goal is to bring expertise and professional capacities in sustainable architecture, landscape planning, and heritage preservation to rural micro-regions, in village clusters with a potential for heritage-based, landscape-integrated, and climate-conscious construction. This initiative aims to boost regional attractiveness and the rural application of the sustainable development goals through unified and professionally supported development of the rural landscape by increasing institutional capacities through training, professional guidelines co-created with local stakeholders and a cooperation model between rural municipalities, stakeholders, and their civil society in micro-regions with united Ruralscapes. 
PSO1 aims for a model for developing sustainable Ruralscapes in the Danube Region, therefore creates a transnational Network of Knowledge for sustainable heritage-based rural architecture (O

1.1) where the best professional knowledge from these fields will unite in order to study and plan ruralscapes. Transnational cooperation including the involved regions, architecture and landscape professionals at an academic level, the civil society, NGOs and development agencies will highlight the good and bad practices in the region, and formulate together a model for Architecture and Rural Landscape Identity Guides for village communities in the Danube Region, a tool and policy basis that will be able to merge the most innovative planning and development knowledge with the local heritage-based challenges and potentials of village communities (O

1.2). 
The toolkit will build on available knowledge of the partners and will continue developing the policy tools of "Architectural Manuals'' available in AT, CZ, HU and RO, up to now mostly born in top-down approaches. Danube Ruralscapes will apply an inclusive bottom-up approach in order to develop more inclusive and usable toolkits to be diffused in most countries of the Danube Region Area. In order to achieve this, Danube Ruralscapes must define the ideal multi level governance structure to give control to village communities in alliance with regional and professional networks (PSO2), enabling rural micro-regions to manage such professional tools without long term assistance from the project. Action Plans will give a framework for collaboration and management from the level of the village and its stakeholders to the regional center (O

2.1), enabling the co-creation of the toolkit and policy recommendations. This process implemented and tested in 7 micro-regions will ultimately lead to policy-level recommendations for regional or national administrative and spatial planning authorities in each country (O

2.2). 
In order to arrive to such solutions, the innovative approach iles in the piloting of the model in 6 countries (O

3.2), enabling a bottom-up co-creation process, a continuous refinement based on real feedback, and 7 “Architecture and Rural Landscape Identity Guides” to be implemented in real life (O

3.1).These guidelines will not only focus on the built heritage but also highlight the visibility and development potential of regional identity, traditional building techniques and the most innovative sustainability driven material culture, public space development and landscape management. Their goal is to give a comprehensive tool to village communities for the sustainable development of more liveable and attractive rural landscapes where new generations will want to live and have pride in their sustainable and heritage-based Ruralscapes (PSO3). Professional partners will assist local and regional governments in creating easily understandable formats for the guidelines and will facilitate their testing in pilot projects, and provide expert support during interventions not typically accessible in those regions. Local mentoring of village municipalities and stakeholders who develop the built environment (enterprises, institutions, and the local private builders) will take place by academic and professional experts in sustainable architecture, heritage reconstruction, town and landscape planning, effectively increasing the capacities of stakeholders from the rural areas of the Danube Region.

titleEn: Inclusive and Accessible Rural Tourism Enhancement - Advancing Inclusivity and Accessibility in Less-Known Rural Tourism Heritage Sites
summaryEn:
The IARTE project is an innovative initiative aimed at transforming rural tourism in the Danube region by enhancing accessibility and inclusivity at less-known tourism and cultural sites for people with disabilities (PWDs). It brings together a consortium of partners - RARIS (Regional Development Agency Eastern Serbia), RCMS (Development Centre Murska Sobota), and ATP Vidin (Association for Tourism Promotion - Vidin) - to address the challenges PWDs face in accessing less known rural tourism and heritage sites.

Main Project aims to transform rural tourism by enhancing accessibility for visitors with disabilities to visit less-known cultural heritage sites in rural areas. This project seeks to bridge the gap between the potential of rural tourism and the accessibility challenges faced by individuals with disabilities. IARTE’s primary objective is to improve infrastructure, services, and staff training at less-known rural tourism and heritage sites, making them accessible and welcoming to all visitors, particularly PWDs.

By focusing on less-known sites, the project aims to diversify the tourism offering in the region and reduce over-tourism at popular sites. The project's findings and best practices will be widely disseminated to influence policy and encourage wider adoption of accessibility standards in rural tourism.

Focused on analyzing the needs and developing project activities for staff training, development of inclusive trails, adaptive adventure activities, and accessible site infrastructure, the project fosters inclusivity in rural and heritage tourism. It also leverages digital tools, creating a support kit for accessible tourism, ensuring heritage sites and rural attractions cater to all, bridging the gap in tourism inclusivity in the Danube region.

Key project activities are:


1. Needs Assessment: Assessing the state of the accessibility in less-known tourism and cultural rural sites, and assessing the needs of PWDs through workshops.


2. Gap Analysis and Recommendations: Identifying the gap between current accessibility and PWDs' needs, followed by comprehensive recommendations.


3. Detailed Activity Planning: Development of a work plan covering training programs, infrastructure development, and assistive technology deployment. This will include development of intervention logic, stakeholder engagement plan, allocation of responsibilities and resource planning


4. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Risk Management Framework: Establishing criteria and methodologies for project monitoring and evaluation and developing risk mitigation strategies.


5. Funding Possibilities Report: Identifying potential funding sources and developing a strategic approach for securing funding.

RARIS will lead the project coordination, ensuring effective internal communication and collaboration among partners. The project will include thematic groups and activity managers for specialized focus areas. Quality in the project will be ensured through regular evaluations, stakeholder feedback, and adherence to EU standards. The project will include periodic project evaluations to assess its impact and scope.

While IARTE is a stand-alone project, it is designed with the potential for future integration into larger projects or initiatives, promoting scalability and long-term impact.

titleEn: Implementation of new and advanced infrastructure screening technology for better cross-border cooperation and connectivity in the Danube Region
summaryEn:
The main transport issues in the Danube region revolve around the need for better connectivity, particularly for areas outside the TEN-T corridors, to ensure comprehensive and sustainable mobility. There is a strong necessity to improve public transport efficiency, enhance safety across transport networks and reduce the environmental impact of transportation. Efforts are required to integrate strategic management of transport services and infrastructure maintenance, including coordination across borders to eliminate bottlenecks and capitalise on the region’s mobility potential.
Resolving issues of transport infrastructure maintenance and especially maintenance costs, foremost when it comes to bridges and viaducts, which are technically and financially more demanding, requires a coordinated effort involving different stakeholders to prioritise maintenance needs, allocate sufficient funding and implement effective inspection and monitoring programmes. All stated challenges are even more present when it comes to the cross-border transport infrastructure which is for the most part old and not maintained as often as required.
This Project is built on the need for innovative solutions for preserving and enhancing transport infrastructure while improving the level of efficiency and safety inspection procedures, testing, rehabilitation and maintenance activities.
Periodic and thorough inspections of bridges are necessary to maintain safe bridge operation and prevent structural and functional failures. In addition, data on the condition and operation of bridges is necessary for road managers to make informed investment decisions as part of an asset management programme. Regular inspections and maintenance of cross-border bridges over Danube between the Republic of Croatia and Republic of Serbia revealed additional challenges that complicate their upkeep, efficiency, and safety.
New technologies and methods have significantly evolved, offering improved efficiency, safety and longevity of these critical infrastructures. Within the Project proof of concept will be tested for usage of georeferenced 3D photogrammetry in bridges and viaducts inspection and testing maintenance screening. Georeferenced photogrammetric recording uses drones for precise measurements which can be very useful in preparing condition reports for experts to assess structural conditions. This technology was first used by the Croatian Roads on the Pelješac bridge, the largest suspension bridge in Croatia, opened to traffic in July 

2022. The technology gave significant achievement in enhanced inspection accuracy, cost efficiency and risk reduction but it needs to be tested if the results and achievements would be the same when applied on old and nearly dilapidated infrastructure.
Newly developed Concept will compare results achieved through standard bridge inspection infrastructure screening and innovative inspection methods, together with reporting procedure technology in order to define the most efficient, effective and reliable method of transport infrastructure screening and inspection as precondition for adequate maintenance.
The Concept developed by Project’s expert working group will define which technology and common inspection procedures timeframe of usage allows best results in early detection of problems on bridges and viaducts, enabling less expensive, targeted maintenance, preventing minor issues from becoming major, expensive repairs.
New and widely applicable Concept of new technology usage in bridge and viaduct inspection, testing and maintenance will be promoted through the Danube Region as well as within the professional associations while be practically applied within the main project, for which the detailed workplan and screening of possible EU funding will be elaborated.
Project partners will join their experience and technical specific knowledge to implement tests on application of innovative technology on the 3 cross-border bridges on the Danube, between Croatia and Serbia, to test if new technology can be reliable in provision of accurate, real-time data on the condition of older bridges. After the testing phase, expert group will analyse the results of the test screening and develop a Concept for the usage of innovative technology in periodical infrastructure inspection. The Concept will compare results achieved through standard infrastructure screening procedures and innovative technology to define the most efficient, effective and reliable method of transport infrastructure screening and inspection as precondition for adequate maintenance. Although the 3 cross-border bridges are not directly linked to the TEN-T core and comprehensive network, the Project supports development of secondary road network and links to the TEN-T network in the Danube region thanks to the possibility of wide application of expected results. The Project will contribute to broader connectivity, accessibility and development goals in Danube region.

titleEn: Resilience driven enhancement of the social-economic upscaling of the Danube-Drava-Sava macro region
summaryEn:
The Danube macro-region, spanning across 14 countries, intertwines with regions sharing numerous border points. Unfortunately, a considerable portion of these border regions grapples with marginalization, facing significant challenges in socio-economic development. These peripheral areas often contend with issues such as low rates of civic engagement, limited capacity for resource absorption, and restricted access to essential expertise and exemplary models of progress. Despite the presence of dedicated Cross-Border Cooperation (CBC) programs within each border area aimed at fostering regional growth, they operate within silos, lacking interconnectedness. Consequently, the wealth of knowledge, successful initiatives, and best practices cultivated within one border area fail to transcend geographical boundaries, impeding the potential for collaborative advancement across neighbouring territories. There exists a crucial need to bridge these divides and establish robust channels for the exchange of insights and experiences, thereby unlocking the collective potential of the Danube macro-region for inclusive and sustainable development.

The objective of the preparatory project is to formulate a comprehensive master plan, i.e a joint transnational development program spanning from 2025 to 2035, comprising an action plan and a tailored training program, aimed at fostering the advancement of the peripheral border regions within the Danube macro-region. This endeavour seeks to boost participation in EU funding initiatives, enhance the absorption of resources, and cultivate competence among the target demographic groups residing in the lagging-behind areas. By strategically focusing on capacity building and competence development, the project aims to empower these communities to leverage available resources effectively and capitalize on opportunities for sustainable development. Through this concerted effort, the project aims to bridge existing disparities, catalyse socio-economic progress, increase the resilience of the communities and foster greater inclusivity within the Danube macro-region.

By conducting thorough assessments, implementing targeted capacity-building initiatives, and formulating strategic plans, the partnership aims to enhance the absorption capacity of the region and to increase the capacities and resilience of the population, thereby catalysing its development. Our overarching goal is to foster sustainable progress in border regions by actively engaging stakeholders, facilitating access to resources, and identifying diverse funding avenues. Embracing a cross-border approach, we prioritize collaborative efforts to ensure effective cooperation across borders, thereby amplifying the project's impact throughout the Danube macro-region.

titleEn: Humanoid Robotics Integration and Innovation in the Danube Region
summaryEn:
The Danube region is a mix of different places, stages of growth, and cultures, and it is at the edge of significant changes thanks to artificial intelligence. A new and exciting project is coming to life, merging AI's possibilities with the emerging field of working alongside humanoid robots. Sparked by the teamwork within the EUSDR PA8's Artificial Intelligence Working Group, this effort highlights AI's crucial role in transforming the economy. It specifically aims to introduce humanoid robots into vital areas such as agro-food, senior care, and manufacturing, seeking to enhance the region's health and wealth. These three key sectors are critical due to the ageing population, the added value to manufacturing, and the exploitation of natural resources. Furthermore, the significance of these sectors is underscored in an ongoing DRP project called BrAIn, where collaboration under the AI umbrella has already begun, spotlighting the need for more concrete projects involving humanoid robots.
Humanoid robots, a new but rapidly growing part of AI, blend high-tech features with the ability to act like humans. Designed to look and work like us, they open up possibilities once thought to exist only in sci-fi movies. However, deploying these robots in diverse areas like the DR is uncharted territory. There is tremendous potential for them to transform everyday jobs across numerous fields, but figuring out how to maximize this potential is still in its early stages. This challenge involves introducing cutting-edge technology into regions that vary greatly in their readiness for technology, the skills of their workers, and their openness to robots.
This submission is for a preparatory project, a crucial first step toward developing a larger-scale initiative dedicated to integrating humanoid robots in a way that is both effective and sensitive to the needs and values of the DR. Our goal is not just to overcome technical obstacles but to foster a deep understanding and acceptance of these technologies among the public.
These include increased operational efficiencies in key targeted sectors, improved quality of life through advanced care options, and the fostering of a tech-savvy workforce, so by that improving SMEs competitiveness. Drawing parallels with successful humanoid robot integrations in other regions, we anticipate a 20% improvement in operational efficiencies in targeted sectors, alongside a significant increase in STEM engagement across the community. The project focuses on ensuring that as these robots become part of daily life, everyone can benefit, regardless of the extent of technology integration in their community or their feelings about robots.
Looking ahead, the project commits to tailoring humanoid robot applications to meet the immediate needs of the DR and to laying the foundation for lasting impact and continuous innovation. 
Our vision extends beyond the project's timeframe, aiming to establish a sustainable ecosystem for AI and robotics integration that supports ongoing growth, scalability across sectors, and adaptability to future technological advancements .In sectors like agro-food, there is potential for precision agriculture and automated processing; in senior care, the promise of companionship and assistance; and in manufacturing, the efficiency of automated assembly lines and quality control. Each sector faces distinct challenges in accepting and adapting to humanoid robots, from operational integration to ethical considerations and dynamics of human-robot interaction.
In addressing these challenges, the initiative not only aims to facilitate the practical application of humanoid robots but also to foster a deeper understanding and acceptance of these technologies. Through education, hands-on demonstrations, and pilot projects, the project seeks to showcase the tangible benefits of humanoid robots, dispelling fears and building a foundation for future innovations. 
This project is designed as a foundational step towards crafting a comprehensive initiative that specifically addresses Priority Area 8 in the EUSDR, focusing on enhancing the Competitiveness of Enterprises. Four experienced partners, who have previously collaborated on related projects, are poised to undertake an in-depth examination of the challenges identified. They will develop a well-structured work plan and budget, underpinned by thorough background studies, to lay the foundation for a successful, future-oriented project.
To ensure the initiative's relevance and incorporate a broad range of perspectives, partners will conduct participatory workshops and organize an international event. These efforts aim to gather valuable insights and feedback from key stakeholders and actors in the field. Such a collaborative approach not only enriches the project's development process but also aligns with our commitment to fostering a dynamic and inclusive ecosystem for technological innovation and enterprise competitiveness in the DR.

titleEn: Building institutional capacity and cooperation to Develop Data Exchange ecosystem in Danube region with the aim of supporting and coordinate better absorption rate of EU funds and Invest EU.
summaryEn:
Building institutional capacity and cooperation to Develop Data Exchange ecosystem in Danube region with the aim of supporting and coordinate better absorption rate of EU funds and Invest EU. (DevelopDataExchange), we will reply to the Action Plan of EUSDR, Priority area (PA) 10: 
-	Action 3: To review bottlenecks relating to the low absorption rate of EU funds and Invest EU 
-	Action 4: To support better coordination of funding 
The project "DevelopDataExchange" is of paramount importance for the sustainable development and prosperity of the Danube Region. It addresses the pressing need for efficient absorption of EU funds, which presents a significant opportunity for the region to tackle challenges, drive innovation, and foster economic growth. However, achieving optimal absorption entails overcoming various barriers and ensuring that funds are utilized efficiently and effectively.
The project recognizes the importance of cooperation among stakeholders across sectors, including government agencies, local administrations, businesses, research institutions, and civil society organizations. By leveraging collective expertise and resources, the project aims to tackle complex regional challenges such as infrastructure development, environmental sustainability, and social inclusion.
Key challenges identified include limited participation in European and international calls for funding, as well as a lack of collaboration among various sectors in the Danube Region. These challenges hinder the region's ability to address issues holistically and leverage innovative solutions.
The project's main goal is to establish collaboration among stakeholders and identify potential consortia to participate in various European funding calls related in Data Exchange. The sectors within Data Exchange used, will be choosed during SO1 and SO4 of DevelopDataExchange. Expected results include the formation of consortia for regional, national, and European funds, thus increasing participation in calls for proposals.
Several challenges hinder the efficient absorption of EU funds within the Danube Region. Limited participation in European and international calls, lack of cooperation among sectors, and historical fragmentation are among the key challenges addressed by the project. The lack of clear rules, legislation, and technological readiness further complicates the exchange of data without losing connectivity between states.
To overcome these challenges, the project advocates for prioritizing one of four key areas and channeling efforts towards it. This necessitates collective discussion among the Danube region states to address gaps and work together on major European projects. Additionally, establishing mechanisms for communication and coordination among stakeholders is crucial for maximizing the impact of EU-funded projects and driving sustainable development.
In terms of relevance to wider strategies and policies, the project aligns with Priority Area 10 (PA10) of the EU Danube Strategy, which focuses on institutional capacity and cooperation. By strengthening institutional capacities, enhancing coordination, and fostering collaboration, the project contributes to achieving the objectives outlined in PA10 and other relevant EU policies and strategies. Collaboration with the EuroAccess MacroRegion initiative further enhances participation from the Danube region in European and international challenges.
Furthermore, the project aligns with the European Strategy for Data, which aims to create a single market for data to ensure Europe's global competitiveness and data sovereignty. By promoting data exchange and collaboration, the project contributes to the implementation of the European Data Strategy and Digital Decade goals.
The geographical scope of the project includes the Danube Region, with potential partners ranging from infrastructure and service providers to interest groups, business support organizations, and higher education and research institutions. The involvement of diverse stakeholders is essential for maximizing the impact of EU-funded initiatives and fostering sustainable regional development.
Through collaboration and building institutional capacities, the project aims to create a conducive environment for enhanced participation, collaboration, and innovation within the Danube region in the topic of Data Exchange (Potential sectors will be choosed by collective brainstorming SO4 and activities in SO1). By addressing barriers to funding absorption and facilitating transnational project implementation in several sectorial Data Exchange, the project seeks to propel the region towards sustainable growth and development while maximizing the impact of EU funds and Invest EU resources.

The activities will be realised in Danube region.
Mobility sector and related sectors to mobility in this project (DevelopDataExchange) will not be choosed, because the mobility and related sectors are in other proposal of SMF.

titleEn: Activation 4 All
summaryEn: Project Activation 4 All aims to create a main project whose goal is establishing a unique interdepartmental and multidisciplinary mechanism for empowering and providing support to vulnerable groups and persons at risk of social exclusion, established with the aim of recognizing and encouraging the fulfillment of the full potential of users, their social inclusion, participation in the local community, teaching and retraining and ultimately their work activation and thereby enabling economic independence. The goal of the project Activation 4 All will be achieved through 4 outputs: creation of a report on the situation on the field related to the topic of the main project; creation of the work plan of the main project; creation of an analysis and report on the possibilities of financing the main project; consultative meetings and a round table with relevant stakeholders.

titleEn: AI based Cluster Cooperation in the Danube Region
summaryEn:
At European level, clusters are recognised as drivers of twin transition in SMEs for a resilient value chain development across the 14 industrial ecosystems. Despite existing initiatives in the field of transnational cluster/SME cooperation, there is a lack of an efficient and structured approach to translate the successful cooperation between cluster networks into efficient commercial, technological, or project-based cooperation between member SMEs on one hand and, respectively, to scale-up punctual successful partnerships between 2 companies to the level of entire cluster networks. It is thus difficult to measure the impact of clusters and SMEs collaboration on the development of green, digital, and resilient value chains in the Danube Region and beyond. Furthermore, relevant information about economic performances of SMEs is difficult to gather, requiring immense effort and time, not being able to provide “real-time” inputs in support of industrial policy measures. 
The matter is even more relevant for the Danube Region which is characterised by large competitiveness gaps between the old, the new Member States and the non-EU countries. There is a need for strengthening the synergies and cross-relationships between quadruple innovation stakeholders in order to facilitate the uptake of innovative technologies across the region, considering that digitalisation is a main driver for competitiveness.
Against this background, the 5 Danubian National Cluster Associations (Romanian, Hungarian, Czech, Slovak and Ukrainian) have taken on developing an AI empowered cluster cooperation platform aiming at 1) enhancing C2C, C2B, B2C, B2B cooperation between cluster stakeholders in the Danube Region from several points of view: commercial, technology transfer and innovation, participation to international RDI projects; 2) providing useful “real-time” information on economic competitiveness of Danubian clusters and SMEs; 3)allowing exchange of best practices and fostering individual and institutional learning processes with a particular focus on twin transition processes; 4) strengthening the resilience of Danubian value chains. 
While the development of the AI empowered cluster cooperation platform will be the scope of the main project, under the current Seed Money Facility, the partners aim:
-	To better understand the current state of play in terms of the use of AI in international cooperation processes.
-	To define the functionalities of the AI cooperation platform encompassing all relevant aspects.
-	To identify potential funding opportunities for the implementation of the main project.
a) Analysis of the current challenges and needs; b) development of the main project’s workplan and establishment of a road map towards a successful project submission under pre-identified financing sources (such as Horizon Europe or Digital Europe) represent the main activities of the project. In addition to this, a wide consultation of national stakeholders will lead to the establishment of a multidisciplinary Expert Group which will support the definition of the platform functionalities. A general event and a project generation seminar in Budapest will be organised in support of a successful main project definition. 
The results will support several categories of relevant stakeholders in the Danube Region and beyond: it will enhance cooperation between cluster and SMEs by better positioning them on transnational resilient value chains; it will enhance twin transition process at company level and raise their innovation and internationalisation capacities; it will support regional, national, Danubian policy actors in better defining S3 and competitiveness policies.

titleEn: Education Digital Gateway in the Danube Region
summaryEn:
The EDIGI-Bridge project іs an innovative initiative tо support the growth оf start-ups with the focus оn digitalization in the partner countries оf the Danube Region and beyond. It aims to prepare a project proposal, which will focus on developing a comprehensive set оf educational programs and consultancy services, specifically tailored to support digitally focused start-ups. The project will provide them with targeted support to develop knowledge, skills, and insights, which are necessary to succeed in the digital economy.

The EDGI-Bridge project will focus on the preparation of the project proposal, which will be aimed at creating a supportive framework, that will not only focus on critical digital competencies but will also foster an environment conducive to innovation and entrepreneurial success. EDIGI-Bridge project is committed to preparing a proposal, that will develop an array оf services, including a specialized digital platform, training modules, workshops, and one-to-one consultancy designed to address the unique challenges and opportunities for start-ups generated by the digital transformation оf current societies.

The focus оn start-ups that are at the forefront оf digital innovation will allow for a significant impact оf start-up companies оn the economic landscape оf the Danube Region/Europe and drive forward technological advancement and competitiveness. The main project will focus on creating an ecosystem оf digitally empowered businesses, and, іn that capacity, tо contribute to the sustainable development of the European economy and to enhancing its position іn the global market. The main project will allow start-ups tо gain the tools and the confidence to navigate the complexities оf the digital age.

The main project proposal will be based on the sound need analysis, which will involve the analysis оf secondary and the collection оf primary data as well as the analysis of relevant policy documents. Also, a comprehensive study оf potential funding sources and grant schemes will be carried out tо allow for an informed submission оf the main project proposal for funding tо maximize the chances for award оf the grant and tо progress to the implementation of the main project.

titleEn: Enhancing the development of Centres of Vocational Excellence in the Danube Region by fostering competence and skill development, business-education cooperation and transnational networking
summaryEn:
Thematic focus:

Our main project is a comprehensive initiative aimed at enhancing the development of Centres of Vocational Excellence (CoVEs) in the Danube Region (DR). CoVEs are pivotal institutions that provide high-quality vocational education and training (VET) programs tailored to meet the specific needs of industries or sectors, thereby playing a crucial role in equipping individuals with the skills, knowledge, and competencies required to excel in their chosen fields and contribute effectively to the labour market.


Challenges tackled:

-	Regional imbalances and negative trends e.g. out migration deriving from the lack of effective structures and models in peripheral regions to develop their human capital,
-	Growing tendency of early leavers from education especially in the eastern regions, which usually contain rural areas with a high share of disadvantaged population,
-	The rigidity of educational infrastructure and services not being able to give prompt responses to labour market needs,
-	Low level of skills and competences,
-	Non-harmonised demand and supply concerning VET.

The project addresses these multifaceted challenges faced in VET, focusing on two key areas: i) Teaching and learning, and ii) Cooperation and partnerships:

i)	 In the area of “Teaching and learning”, the project aims to anticipate future skill needs and equip individuals with relevant skills and competences. This involves developing innovative solutions for curricula-based competence development, implementing lifelong learning approaches and providing personalized career guidance services. Moreover, the project emphasizes the importance of green skills development to facilitate the transition to a sustainable economy, addressing areas such as renewable energy, resource efficiency, sustainable agriculture, circular economy and climate change adaptation. Additionally, the project focuses on enhancing the quality and efficiency of VET systems by modernizing education systems and strengthening work-based learning opportunities.

ii)	In the area of “Cooperation and partnerships”, the project seeks to establish long-term partnerships between educational institutions, businesses, and other stakeholders to promote innovation, skills forecasting, work-based learning, and the retraining of unemployed and inactive individuals. By fostering collaboration with universities, research organizations and international networks, the project aims to facilitate knowledge exchange, promote entrepreneurship and enhance the competitiveness of key industries. Furthermore, the project emphasizes the importance of creating inclusive and quality employment opportunities by empowering disadvantaged groups to access education and employment opportunities.


Main objective and expected result:

The main objective of the project is to strengthen VET systems in the DR, transforming them into Centres of Vocational Excellence. Through innovative approaches, strategic partnerships, and sustainable financing models, the project endeavours to create a more responsive, inclusive, and high-quality VET system that meets the needs of individuals, businesses, and society. By investing in people, promoting human capital development, and fostering collaboration between stakeholders, the project contributes to building a skilled workforce, promoting social inclusion, and fostering sustainable development.

The expected result of the project is the establishment of a sustainable network of CoVEs that contribute to the overall development and prosperity of the DR. By strengthening the capacity and competitiveness of VET institutions, the project aims to enhance the employability of individuals, combat brain drain, drive economic growth and promote social inclusion. Ultimately, the project seeks to build a skilled workforce, stimulate entrepreneurship, and create opportunities for individuals and communities across the DR to thrive.


Contribution to EUSDR:

The SMF DANUBE COVES project supports the preparation of a complex strategic transnational project that will contribute to EUSDR PA9 (People and skills). The objective of our proposal is to enhance vocational education and training in the DR by fostering:

-	competence and skill development in VETs (with a special focus on green skills and learning competences),
-	business-education cooperation,
-	transnational networking for mobility and transfer of good practices.

This initiation deals with both focus topics (I. Labour Market and Social Policies, II. Education and Training) of PA

9. Actions as “Intensify Cooperation in Labour Market Policies (action 1)”, “Quality and Efficiency of Education and Training Systems” (action 5), “Relevant and High-Quality Knowledge, Skills and Competences” (action 6) and “Inclusive Education, Equity, Common Values and Sustainable Development” (action 8) are included in the EUSDR Action Plan. Our project is in line with all above actions.

titleEn: Talented Education for Socially Less Advantaged
summaryEn:
The TESLA – Talent Education for Socially Less Advantaged – project, with a partnership entailing 4 countries - Hungary, Serbia, Austria, and Romania - leverages a wide range of competencies, expertise in various fields, and its broad network to develop its program package with the main objective of preventing school dropout among young people ages between 15-19 by the PPs: 

LP: Hungarian Association for Talent Support Organizations (MATEHETSZ) (HU)
PP2: Network for Regional Development Foundation (HÁRFA) (HU)
PP3: Talent Support Council of Vojvodina (VATT) (RS) 
ASP1: Amőba Foundation (RO)
ASP2: CREFOP Foundation (RO)
ASP3: Primera – Centre for Continuous Professional Development of Teachers (AT)
ASP4: CONCORDIA Social Projects (AT)

In the main project, we plan to develop a new methodology for the complex talent-focused development of the young age group (15-19 years), particularly those in disadvantaged situations. Additionally, we aim to design and implement development activities aimed at preventing early school leaving, facilitating the attainment of degrees, and the successful integration into the labour market on a pilot basis across partner countries, which capitalisation shall contribute to the development of the Danube Region. There will be further development of previously applied skill and competence measurement and evaluation methodologies tailored to the specific needs of target groups. 
Identifying talent in everyone and, based on individuals' strengths, accompanying mentorship, leading the youth through individual or group programs aimed at developing talent areas for the prevention of early school leaving. The main project aim is to achieve a mindset shift and expand entrenched institutional practices: instead of focusing solely on remedying weaknesses, seeking to introduce a new approach methodology – bridging disadvantages through nurturing talents. To this end, in the SMF project, we prepare the program package as follows.

SO1: Report on the state of play in the field of talent focused development of young people at risk of dropping out: The project partners will conduct a transnational needs assessment, identify of needs and challenges and evaluate the institutional capabilities in the field of talent development among young people (aged 15-19) at risk of dropping out of education.

The output focuses on investigating existing methodologies for reaching out to the target group and measuring their competencies and skills, as well as assessing best practices in development frameworks tailored to individual needs for success in the labour market and addressing contemporary challenges. The report will also explore barriers faced by educational institutions, youth workers, social workers, and civil organizations in preventing dropouts. Additionally, previous projects related to talent identification and development will be reviewed to identify synergies and overlaps.

SO2: Main project work plan: Elaboration of main project work plan regarding the predefined main activities of the project, like: reaching out the students at risk of dropping out, awareness raising programs; improvement of competence and skill measuring tools related to the target groups; competence measurement of the selected target group – involving control groups; assessment of motivation and strengths and weaknesses of the target group; evaluation of the survey results and development of individual improvement plans; implementation of the improvement plan; tutoring programs; small scale interventions in collaborating countries; project result assessments and policy recommendations; dissemination processes; project management. The main project work plan consists of activities, the logical structure of activities, as well as the specification of relevant outputs and results of the activities. The document will also aim to outline potential international partnership, as well as indicative project budget.

SO3 Report on funding possibilities: Suitable funding sources will be identified from EU programmes, national funds and private contributions, aimed at creating positive societal impacts, particularly among youth, to prevent early disengagement from education. Additionally, a roadmap will be created for transitioning from the seed money project to the main project, detailing milestones, funding activities, and partnership agreements.

SO4 Additional outputs and activities: Additional preparatory efforts will enhance transnational participatory planning and preparatory concepts and methodologies involving the target groups. Workshops will facilitate networking and the exchange of knowledge and best practises in talent-focused development among young people at risk of dropping out. Awareness raising activities and motivation mapping will be prepared and tested and in addition a detailed project implementation frameworks (concept papers) will be prepared to intensify the readiness of the main project for an immediate launch.

titleEn: Navigating University Autonomy: Academic Policy Center for Better Higher Education
summaryEn:
The long-term goal of the project is to establish an Academic Policy Centre (APC) which will develop policy-relevant research within the regions of Central Eastern (CEE) and Southeastern Europe (SEE) focusing on the universities and university-relevant public policy. The project will create a synergy between the stakeholders invested in research and higher education in Belgrade (Serbia), Rijeka (Croatia), and Budapest (Hungary) and will focus on the creation of an architecture of clusters of experts from across the region. APC would serve as a hub for fostering stronger collaboration on joint project development and mobility schemes between the partners. The primary focus of the first phase will be on the analysis of the specificities of the university policies in the partner countries with the main aim of amending the existing disparities in the tertiary level of education within the Danube Region, finding common strategic ways to improve the existing policies in each of the countries that suffer from the wider tendency of “corporate governance” of the universities. The final goal of the main project is to create a strong policy hub that will address all the problems the universities are facing with respect to the local and regional legislations, the division and not collaboration between public and private sectors, and finally, the brain drain of staff as well as students all three countries are facing. 

The need for establishing such a jointly coordinated policy hub arises from what is currently regularly the subject of policy debate as the „crisis of the universities“ in various parts of the world, including Europe as a whole. There are several facets of this perceived crisis, one of which is the above-mentioned rise of corporate governance of the universities, growing issues between the logic, methodology and interests of university administrations, which increasingly consist of managers, and not of academics, as has traditionally been the case, on the one hand, and the academic staff, on the other. Universities face a situation where, based entirely on corporate-style criteria, whole areas of studies that have traditionally been considered fundamental for overall education are being reduced to the margins of academic programmes or abolished altogether. This is particularly the case with social sciences and humanities. Over the past several years universities in the Danube Region have been the subject of many crises with either actual or threatened academic staff layoffs due to the staff’s specialization in areas that university administrations consider problematic either economically (they do not attract many students) or politically (they focus on social critique). This policy has strongly affected the brain drain of some of the leading scholars and academics from the region and consequently had an impact on the overall level of the quality of staff at the respective universities. In addition, in many universities and academic communities, the relationship between teaching and research as staff activities, and more acutely, between the teaching staff and the research staff, continue to be unresolved, with problematic differences in terms of salaries, ability to work additionally in different institutions, and particularly the inter-institutional mobility within the region.

The relationship between universities and governments is fraught, with governments exerting direct control over academic life through ministries. University autonomy, initially meant to protect against ideological influence, has been stretched to include broad decision-making powers for both institutions and individual staff. However, governments have countered this by introducing specific laws and policies that regulate nearly every aspect of university life. Additionally, informal control mechanisms, such as political influence over student unions and parliaments, further diminish university autonomy. This trend, observed notably in Serbia and Hungary, disrupts the balance of decision-making bodies within universities, impacting matters like curriculum and leadership appointments.

In sum, there is a clear need for an overarching policy that would remedy these issues of value conflict and generate creative and productive relationships between universities and policymakers in redefining the clouded boundaries between the university, and the public administration, and reinvigorating the spirit of learning and scholarship that has been in decline due to the numerous unresolved policy dilemmas about the universities, their role in the economy, the value of learning vs. employment, excellence vs. income, etc.

titleEn: Danube Ventures: Empowering Young Entrepreneurs
summaryEn:
Danube Ventures is a transformative initiative aimed at empowering young entrepreneurs in the Danube region to catalyze socioeconomic development and contribute to the EU Strategy for the Danube Region. With a strategic focus on Slovakia and neighboring countries, this project seeks to leverage transnational collaboration and funding sources to support the growth and sustainability of entrepreneurship ecosystems in the region.
The project will commence with a comprehensive analysis of the current state of entrepreneurship in the Danube region, with a specific emphasis on Slovakia and EUSDR countries. This report will provide insights into past and present activities in the field, identify existing challenges and gaps, and assess complementary projects implemented in the region. By understanding the contextual landscape, the project aims to develop targeted interventions to address critical needs and opportunities for young entrepreneurs.
Building upon the insights gained from the initial report, Danube Ventures will develop a robust work plan outlining activities, outputs, and expected results of the main project. This plan will encompass a diverse range of initiatives, including entrepreneurship workshops, mentorship programs, networking events, and research endeavors. The project will foster collaboration among stakeholders and leverage transnational partnerships to create a supportive ecosystem for startup growth and innovation. An indicative budget plan will guide resource allocation, ensuring effective implementation of project activities.
In parallel, the project will conduct a thorough analysis of funding possibilities available in the Danube region to sustain the main project beyond the initial seed funding. This report will explore a variety of funding sources, including grants, sponsorships, and public-private partnerships, tailored to the needs and priorities of youth entrepreneurship supporting initiatives. A strategic roadmap will outline steps to secure additional funding and ensure the long-term impact and sustainability of the project, aligning with the objectives of the EU Strategy for the Danube Region.
We plan to organise variouse networking events, workshops and seminars. The lead parner and its partner have extensive knowledge and experiences in organising these kind of events on an international level. For a better publicity, we will use our platforms, websites and podcast to reach the main target groups. 
Through these strategic outputs and activities, Danube Ventures aims to create a conducive environment for entrepreneurship, empower young talents with the necessary skills and resources, and drive inclusive growth and prosperity across the Danube region. By leveraging transnational collaboration and funding sources, the project seeks to maximize its impact and contribute to the overarching goals of the EU Strategy for the Danube Region.

titleEn: SMF CONSPIRO - Breathing Together for Cleaner Air
summaryEn:
Aim of this SMF proposal is to prepare strategic international project tackling the problem of air pollution from home heating systems and other residential combustion.
Central point of the main project is comprehensive informational/awareness raising campaign using all the tools of public communication and targeting full spectra of citizens and stakeholders. Specific focus will be given to educational, lawmaking, multi-level governance and best-practice-sharing activities, where especially impacts of the pollution on human health would be taken into account.
To activate public interest and to collect large amount of data from the areas where air pollution data are missing (smaller settlements up to 50 thous. inhabitants), massive use of low-cost monitors (network measurements with citizens´ participation and providing of the data via web and mobile apps) will be tested and implemented. The data generated by the measurements will be combined with satellite data (Sentinel 5) to provide smart air pollution forecast with alert for citizens; this will help to decrease direct people exposition to the pollutants. The data will also be used for correlations with regional health statistics to illustrate the impact of the pollution on human health (such correlations are missing now because of the lack of air quality data for small settlements).
Further goals of the project – besides shifting of public opinion and providing relevant inputs for multi-level governance – are also formalization of the low-cost measurements in small settlements (supplementary to official/state monitoring network) and international harmonization of air quality legislative and social-economical corrective tools.
The proposal exactly fits into the PA6, topic 2 objectives. Moreover, it will help to develop general EU political priorities on Air Quality issue by proving the importance of the pollution from residential heating in smaller settlements (impacts on citizens´health).

titleEn: Integrated Danube Environmental Assessment and Monitoring for Nature Based Solutions
summaryEn:
The focus of the project considers collection and evaluation of a broad spectrum of datadata sources for the enhancement of blue infrastructure through nature-based solutions (NBS) within the Danube catchment area. The project aims to integrate in-situ monitoring (not part of the project), remote sensing, and modeling data into a decision-support tool IDEAM NBS. This tool is intended to facilitate the identification, planning, and implementation of natural water retention and improvement measures across the Danube region, including the integration of EU and national The project's core objective is to gather and assess a wide array of data sources to bolster blue infrastructure via nature-based solutions (NBS) within the Danube catchment area. It seeks to integrate in-situ monitoring data (outside the project's scope), remote sensing, national-level reports from various governmental and non-governmental bodies, and modeling data into the IDEAM NBS decision-support tool. This tool, functioning as an online GIS platform, is designed to streamline the identification, planning, and execution of natural water retention and enhancement measures throughout the Danube region, incorporating both EU and national datasets. Special attention is given to the distinct hydrological features characteristic of the various Danube regions, aiming to leverage their uniqueness for environmental improvement.
The project's ambit includes partnering with state environmental agencies to access national data, striving for the standardization/harmonization of data formats as feasible, and scrutinizing policy-specific datasets. It aims to utilize outputs from European research projects alongside remote sensing data to examine the state of both former and active floodplain areas of Danube river and its tributaries. Furthermore, the initiative will pinpoint potential sites for NBS implementation and appraise the capacity of nature-based solutions to address a spectrum of challenges. These include flood prevention, drought issues in agricultural landscapes, and water quality enhancement.
As part of the project, a consortium will foster collaboration with designated state institutions capable of providing pertinent data. The specific institutions across the participating countries will be identified in the forthcoming stages. Specifically, in individual countries, these institutions are:
- Czech Republic - Water Management Research Institute VUV TGM, Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Povodí Moravy, s.p., Czech Hydrometeorological Institute
- Slovenia - Slovenian water agency, Slovenian environment agency (data owners and beneficiaries), Institute for water of the Republic of Slovenia; problem owners (Association of municipalities and towns of Slovenia) 
- Montenegro - Ministry of agriculture, forestry and water management (directorate for water and agriculture), Water Administration, Institute for Hydrometeorology and Seismology, Environmental Protection Agency, Ministry of tourism, environment, sustainable development and northern region development (directorate for nature protection and its climate change sector, directorate for environment and its waste waters sector), Association of local authorities and municipalities, Energy Company of Montenegro (EPCG) 
- Bosnia and Herzegovina - Sava river basin Water Agency (Federation of BIH and Republika Srpska); Ministries of the environment (entities or state coordination Ministry); (if spatial layers needed and lidar - Federal Administration for Geodetic and Property Legal Affairs), Public Utility Company 'Vode Srpske' Bijeljina, Republic Hydrometeorological Institute RS, Federal Hydrometeorological Institute 
- Serbia - Jaroslav Černi Water Institute University of Belgrade
- International - IUCN, GWP, ICPDR, UNECE, Sava and Danube Commissions

Furthermore, other groups of stakeholders will be identified, with whom the project proposal will be addressed with regard to their specific interests and requirements. Examples can be energy companies operating facilities directly in the watershed, agricultural unions and groups that directly affect the inability of the landscape to retain water, etc.

titleEn: Innovative underwater robotics for monitoring and protection of Danube river pollution
summaryEn:
ROBORIVER addresses following COMMON TERRITORIAL CHALLENGES: 
(1) The Danube environment is facing major impacts from pollution. The Danube environment represents a challenging framework for exploitation of innovative cutting-edge techniques and technologies related to automatic control as it constitutes important resource for food, employment, and economic revenue. This requires development of new methods and solutions for exploration, as well as setting up strong cooperative links among universities, research institutes, local public authorities, SMEs and stakeholders across programme area towards this goal. For these reasons, there is recognized actual derived interest in the development of new skills and competences to support the exploration, observation, sampling, intervention and persistent monitoring of the Danube river quality and protection of environment.
(2) Needs for enhancing implementation of activities addressing research, investments and competitiveness of stakeholders up taking innovative technologies of underwater robotics and gaining new skills. Currently, there is no standard method used to sample microplastics from riverine systems. Most microplastic research focuses on quantity, in particular on particle numbers, and composition of microplastics. The complexity of microplastics and the lack of harmonization in sampling methodology make it difficult to compare different studies cited in Innovation technologies and methods of scanning, sampling and monitoring – underwater robotics are addressed to be developed to bear high relevance for the future economic development of programme area and its economic resilience. Better innovation capacities should be crucial to adapt this area to the growing importance of the tertiary, services-oriented sector. As programme area do not equally benefit from research and innovation, knowledge and technology transfer thus remain a critical need. Tackling innovation-related challenges will help to reduce territorial disparities between project’s areas that might otherwise lead to unequal opportunities.
(3) Special emphasis is on competitiveness and innovative approaches with deployment and uptake of new technologies of underwater robotics for detecting and sampling microplastics in various Danube riparian environment.
(4) Insufficient related human skills development, weak involvement of stakeholders and interrelation of business and the public sector incite clear need for project in field of innovative underwater robotics technologies development and deployment.

Within the thematic field of the main project, relevance of the challenges described to the EUSDR action plan: PRIORITY AREA 4: Water quality and PRIORITY AREA 9: People and skills.

MAIN OBJECTIVE planned is development of 3 outputs for main project aiming to develop/create of innovation underwater robotics for monitoring and protection of Danube river pollution: Output 

1. Report on the state of play of innovative pollution monitoring and protection of Danube River, Output 

2. Main project work plan and Output 

3. Report on funding possibilities.

Planned expected results of main project: 

1. Build/created and deployed innovative underwater robotics, 

2. Newly developed training programme for specific innovative skills.

Macro-regional dimension of the project and transboundary impact of its results are the underlining aim of the project and shall be ensured by the composition of the partnership covering all Danube riparian countries and by the transnational character of project outputs, guaranteeing their transferability and adoption in the entire Danube region and beyond, to the entire inland navigation sector, given topic addressed: need for future-looking competences in inland navigation.
