titleEn: Decision Support System for Global Water Balance
summaryEn:
Agriculture is a major consumer of water resources, and the major cause of water consumption in agriculture is irrigation. Irrigated land represents 20% of the cultivated land worldwide but 40% of the food production. Farming activities account for almost 70 % of global water withdrawals, reaching as much as 95% in some developing countries. Therefore, this action aims to develop a simulation model with an adaptive real time control and agent-base modelling components to overcome the problem of soil infiltration temporal and spatial variability, which will support increase water use efficiency of 10% leading to large water savings, introduce a considerable potential for sizeable reductions in non-beneficially consumed water (54–76%) and significant increases in crop water productivity (9–15%) through transitions from surface to sprinkler or drip systems, by 

2050.

In this regard, the action will have three major work packages (WP): 
-WP1- Integrating activities comprising, (a) integrated database activities, which will be developing a new data set of the global distribution of irrigation systems, for each grid cell and crop functional types (CFT), together with country-level shares of irrigation systems with a series of socioeconomic and biophysical factors adopting national statistics from AQUASTAT; (b) congress/workshop organisation activities which will promote integration and the spreading of excellence as well as to spread knowledge on both existing and new tools and models. 
-WP2- Capacity development activities comprising, (a) an offline formal training courses (FTCs) organisation activities, which will be based on outputs of the workshops explained in the previous activity for spreading excellence for irrigation efficiency as part of the program on “Irrigation-Related Agent-Based Modelling tool for Sustainable Water/Irrigation Management”; (b) an online agent-based modelling education programme (ABMEP) activities featuring higher technology irrigation systems which have manifold co-benefits, e.g., improved crop quality, conserving nitrate groundwater concentration, reducing water logging, saving energy, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. 
-WP3- Simulation and modelling activities comprising (a) surface irrigation spatiotemporal simulation activities presenting for the first time spatially and temporally explicit estimates of global irrigation system performances for the world’s major crop types, based on process-based simulation of underlying local biophysical conditions for target regions of the action; (b) irrigation-related agent-based modelling activities building options for interactions among farmers will be a way to increase the benefit of the downstream farmers and even the whole system in the model, allowing for the consideration of irrigation decisions on crop choice, irrigation forecast, and water allocation.

Along these lines, target groups of the action will be following: 1- various stakeholders, farmers, and local professionals, at individual level. 2- A wide range of organisations involved in irrigation such as water user organisations, at organisational level. 3- Research groups, government extension agencies, private companies that share common objectives such as improved livelihoods at a farming level or improved water management or increased agricultural productivity, at a national level. 

In this respect, expected results of the action will be: 1- A new decision support system for global water balance (Dss-GwB) composed of two components that will serve as a coupled model for extending its scope by considering more irrigation-related factors or adding different crops to optimize water allocation strategies and crop yields to simulate farmers’ decision making. 2- Built capacity among, (a) farmers to improve their understanding and appreciation of irrigation management as the main factor that affect crop yields and water use by making crop development independent from rainfall, and of increasing water usage efficiency (WUE) to decrease the amount of water used in attaining expected yields, through an Agent-Based Modelling Education Programme (ABMEP); (b) senior professionals for developing their capacity to include good organisations and strong institutional structures within which individuals can work effectively, and an enabling environment that encourages successful irrigation development, through implementation of Formal Training Courses (FTC).

titleEn: Protecting the Black Sea Ecosystem by raising public and sectoral awareness and reducing microplastic pollution
summaryEn:
Microplastics, as an emerging problem, cause harm to organisms in the Black Sea. Further, unstandardized methodological applications for microplastic detection from water and substrate samples make the problem even bigger. Thus, new approaches are urgently needed to diminish the microplastic influence in the Black Sea and minimize the contribution of the microplastic sources. For this purpose, this project will gather 5 partners from Türkiye, Romania, Bulgaria, Ukraine, and Georgia to enhance awareness-based neighborhood cooperation and cross-border information exchange using scientific and innovative awareness methods. Country-specific raising awareness strategies will be developed to meet the cultural differences. The main purpose of the current project is to contribute to reducing microplastic pollution among the specific target groups by using the scientific knowledge collected by applying standardized methods during the project implementation and increasing the awareness level. To do so, “bottom-up” and “top-down” approaches will be utilized together to inform stakeholders about the status of microplastic pollution in the Black Sea, the level of contribution to microplastic pollution by various sectors (maritime, fisheries, aquaculture, and tourism), and potential precautions and methods to contribute to mitigating the influence of these pollutants. Target groups will include citizens, tourists, students at all education levels, sectoral workers, sector representatives, local and national authorities, and decision-makers. Various sector-specific activities and information based on the target groups will be used such as field trips and works, in-situ training, visual materials, scientific information, and other materials. The adverse effects of microplastics on marine ecosystems will be shown via various tools and activities including meetings, workshops, toys, play cards, TV programs, etc., and finally during a family day organization. Further, potential approaches to contribute to reducing microplastic input by several sectors will be tested. Finally, a family day organization will be organized and all kinds of litter and specifically microplastics will be collected from a chosen beach to introduce the potential influence of those pollutant to the kindergarten and elementary school students and families. This project aims to reach approximately 7000- 8000 stakeholders directly and more than 2.000.000 beneficiaries indirectly. 
A transnational cooperation approach will be needed to implement this project because microplastic is a common issue for the whole Black Sea region due to their mobility and therefore this issue could be handled only by applying a harmonized and standardized methodology. The project will identify four common potential sources of microplastic pollution in the Black Sea, test some precautions that could be useful to diminish the sectoral microplastic input, and contribute to the microplastic awareness of the all stakeholders.

titleEn:
Sustaining BSB Biodiversity through Traditional 
Knowledge and Innovation
summaryEn:
The Black Sea basin is home to a diverse range of ecosystems including grasslands, forests,
wetlands, coastal areas, etc. It is characterized by a high number of species concentration as well as
a richness of endemic and relict plant species. For example, Georgia is home to more than 200
endemic species, Bulgaria to 270, Greece to 760, Romania to 228 etc. Although the Black Sea
countries implement substantial measures for the safeguarding of biodiversity, traditional
ecosystems still face significant losses. It is also significant that traditional ecological knowledge
(TEK), which accumulated and tested the relationships between people and the natural environment
over the centuries like many practices across other domains of intangible cultural heritage are
declining due to industrialization, urbanization and other global development processes.
BIOSUSTAIN unites these two important challenges and aims to respond to the common problem of
the deterioration of traditional ecosystems and the reduction of indigenous species faced by the
Black Sea Countries based on the innovative application of traditional knowledge of nature. The
project seeks to develop and test a complex TEK-based approach, which stimulates innovation
through the synthesis of traditional and scientific knowledge. For the viability of the results, the
action strengthens cross-sectoral cooperation and supports generation of economic benefits from
the sustainable use of the local biodiversity for local communities. The central issue is also
emphasizing the role of local communities and strengthening their capacity as stewards of their
natural environment.
The project incorporates 4 main groups of activities, which are interconnected and build the logical
chain of intervention to achieve irreversible positive changes. (a) Conduction of -identification studies on TEK preserved by indigenous and local communities in specific locations; 
(b) Stimulation of innovation and fostering the development of new applications of local species through experimentoriums; (c) Capacity-building of local communities, empowering them to maintain
traditional ecosystems and derive sustainable benefits from the harmonious relationship between
economic growth and the conservation of biological diversity. (d) Promotion and awareness raising
about TEK in various target groups, aiming to strengthen understanding of its crucial role in
safeguarding biodiversity.
Project main results include:


1. Methodology and pilot studies of TEK in one region per partner country


2. Developed innovative methods of application of indigenous species in merging industries


3. Built Capacity local indigenous communities to effectively safeguard traditional ecosystems,
local landscapes, and the associated sustainable knowledge. By equipping these communities with
the necessary knowledge and skills, the project empowers them to protect their cultural and
economic interests while maintaining a harmonious relationship with their everyday landscape.


4. Raised awareness on the importance of TEK and local communities’ role in safeguarding
landscapes, ecosystems, and biodiversity, among the general public and relevant stakeholders.
BIOSUSTAIN targets to involve a broad spectrum of stakeholders, each benefiting from the project's
activities. Local communities form the most significant target group, as they gain increased
recognition, skills, and new models on safeguarding related landscapes and productive systems. For
local and regional governments and sectoral agencies, BIOSUSTAIN provides TEK know-how for
further reflection in relevant policies and action plans. This empowers decision-makers to
incorporate the insights gained from the project into their strategic frameworks, thereby ensuring the
conservation and sustainable management of biodiversity at a larger scale. Educational institutions,
of various academic backgrounds, will also benefit from the original research and results from the
experimentoriums serving as a foundation for further research and improvement of educational
programs. By engaging youth from both local communities and educational fields, the project actively
promotes research skills development and facilitates intergenerational knowledge transfer.
Furthermore, SME and business-supporting organizations in various merging sectors will gain access
to traditional species, allowing them to green their value chains. Given the complexity of
the goals, the project relies on strong international cooperation. By testing and validating the
intervention methodology in diverse natural, economic, and social environments, the project will not
only adapt its approach but will also benefit from international experiences and accumulated
knowledge, enriching the project team's expertise.

titleEn: Cooperation through Tech-Based Practices to Struggle Invasive Species and Climate Change for a Sustainable and Resilient Agriculture(AGRICOOP)
summaryEn:
Invasive alien species-IAS are becoming widespread worldwide and pose a threat to the agricultural sector. Within the project, it is aimed to determine the IAS that are widespread in the project partner(PP) countries and to develop methods of combating these IAS. The lack of awareness of people and institutions interested in agricultural activities in the fight against IAS leads to the inability to effectively combat and to a decrease in productivity in the agricultural sector. With the Climate & Pest Detection Station(CPDS) to be placed in the pilot regions to be determined in each PP country, climate data in the pilot region will be obtained and the IAS that are dense in the region will be determined and the methods of combating these species will be customized.The activities to be carried out will raise awareness among the target audience in partner countries about combating IAS and adaptation to climate change. The outputs obtained at the end of the project will reveal guiding practices as a pilot study against the possible spread of IAS in different countries as well as the PP countries. With the trainings to be given to farmers, raising awareness about IAS will contribute to increasing the yield of agricultural products.
The main challenge that the project aims to address is to identify IAS in the region and develop methods to struggle IAS, which pose a significant threat to agricultural production and climate resilience.According to the Global Invasive Species Program, "climate change and IAS pose two of the greatest threats to biodiversity and the provision of valuable ecosystem services. Worldwide, the estimated damage from IAS is more than US$

1.4 trillion annually - 5% of the global economy - and their impacts span a wide range of sectors including agriculture, forestry, aquaculture, transportation, trade, energy production and recreation."
The overall objective is to foster sustainable resilient agriculture, to enhance agricultural product quality and productivity by detecting IAS and developing struggle methods, to develop joint solutions and pilot actions for different types of environmental hazards in affected and exposed regions in the BSB, to facilitate knowledge exchange among stakeholders, to integrate advanced technological systems to the target groups’ use which will also provide awareness and adaptation on climate change
The Project will address the lack of transnational collaborations and technology-based agricultural practices to share good practices and know-how on the use of innovative technological advances in the areas of climate change resilience and adaptation, in particular the joint struggling IAS, taking into account ecosystem-based approaches in the context of clean and green zone. In this context, the Project will develop a mobile pest detection application (MAPPEST).
The main outputs of the project; a study report on the IAS that currently exist in the region of the PP countries and have the potential/risk of entering the region in the near future and the characteristics of these IAS, a report on the measures that can be taken against IAS jointly created by all PPs, MAPPEST developed for farmers, density and migration map of IAS, applied control methods activities, capacity and awareness raising training modules, seminars and International Forum on the ımpact of climate change on agricultural pests and control methods. The beneficiaries of the project are the PPs, all actors of the agricultural ecosystem, farmers, farmer cooperatives, chambers of agriculture, agriculture and forestry directorates, national/regional/local development agencies, HEIs and research institutions, stock exchanges, chambers etc.
Although the way agriculture is practiced in each country is different, climate change and the problems posed by IAS pose a common challenge. Because when IAS infect a region or country, their populations tend to increase when new ecological living conditions are favorable. In the fight against IAS, it is extremely important that all PPs and the target groups act together in the areas where the pest is transmitted and present. More effective results are achieved when neighboring countries with pest problems work together. The fight against the IAS is easier and faster when the pest can be prevented from spreading to new areas. This situation brings the need for countries to integrate technology-based practices into the agricultural sector for sustainable and climate change compatible agricultural policies and to share the results of good practices.Therefore, transnational cooperation is needed to share the results in the form of good practices and to create international impact. Within the AGRICOOP Project, PPs from border neighbouring countries Türkiye, Bulgaria and Georgia came together with the need for transnational cooperation and having common interests in improving product quality and productivity in agriculture by identifying IAS and developing methods to struggle.

titleEn: Healing Environmental by Reef Options in the Black Sea
summaryEn:
The Black Sea region is currently experiencing severe environmental degradation, including pollution, eutrophication and marine litter. To address these challenges and improve the ecological state of the marine ecosystems in the Black Sea, the HERO project has been formulated. The project employs various solutions, including clean-up operations to remove litter, data collection and analysis to gain a better understanding of the issue and habitat restoration through the use of artificial reefs. Additionally, the project focuses on raising awareness and promoting responsible waste management practices.

What sets the HERO project apart is its innovative approach, which incorporates biotechnological water quality management techniques and integrates multiple objectives such as ecosystem health, litter management, habitat restoration, biodiversity preservation and awareness-raising. By collaborating across borders, the project facilitates shared responsibility, knowledge sharing, comprehensive approaches, enhanced data collection and analysis and improved public awareness and behavior change.

The project's outputs will be beneficial to various stakeholders, including local and national public authorities, interest groups and NGOs, higher education and research organizations, business support organizations and the general public. These stakeholders will gain access to research findings, data, methodologies and resources that supports decision-making, advocacy efforts, academic programs, research initiatives and business development. The general public will be actively engaged through awareness-raising campaigns aimed at promoting responsible waste disposal practices and fostering a culture of environmental responsibility. Leveraging the expertise and experiences of its partner institutions, the HERO project is a collaborative effort involving four key partners: UABSC, IPA, ShU and BSU. Each partner brings specific expertise and contributions that are crucial for the successful implementation of the project and its objectives.

The composition of the partnership ensures that the partners' competencies and contributions are complementary. PP2's expertise in coastal cleaning and waste management complements Universities’ scientific knowledge. UABSC adds an economic perspective to the project, while BSU’s and SHU's research activities contribute to the scientific understanding of the Black Sea region. By combining these different areas of expertise, the partnership creates a comprehensive approach to address sea pollution, improve waste management, restore habitats and promote sustainable development in the Black Sea region.

UABSC, as the lead partner, concentrates on the development of the blue economy. They have specialized expertise in promoting sustainable economic activities and understanding the economic potential of coastal and marine resources. UABSC ensures that the project's initiatives align with sustainable development objectives and contribute to the blue economy. They provide economic perspectives, knowledge and opportunities for sustainable economic development. 

The HERO project involves several key activities and outcomes. Clean-up operations involve divers, boats and sea sweepers to remove litter from the seabed while collecting data on litter types, quantities and sources. Marine surface and coastal litter reports are prepared monthly to analyze litter patterns and trends. Litter investigation analysis helps identify potential or heavily damaged habitats, considering various factors. An interactive digital map is developed, integrating inventory data to visually represent litter distribution. Artificial reefs are installed in different marine habitats to enhance biodiversity and a joint monitoring protocol and reports track the impacts of the reefs on water quality, biodiversity and community life. Intermediate results are shared through conferences, promoting knowledge exchange and creating a know-how database. An "Be a HERO" Awareness-Raising Campaign is conducted to raise public awareness about the negative impacts of litter and promote responsible waste disposal. Underwater photography and video exhibitions are held to celebrate the significance of artificial reefs.

The project's outcomes include improved marine ecosystem health, enhanced understanding of litter patterns and trends, identification and protection of damaged habitats, increased knowledge and collaboration in coastal management, improved decision-making through data visualization, biodiversity enhancement and sustainable tourism, enhanced monitoring and adaptive management, increased awareness and responsible waste management practices and community engagement and empowerment. These outcomes collectively contribute to the overall improvement of the ecological state of marine ecosystems in the Black Sea region.

titleEn: easyPEST: EstAblishing long-term monitoring SYstem for plant PESTs around the Black Sea
summaryEn:
The common challenge: easyPEST endeavors to address hazards induced by invasive alien species (IAS), particularly invasive alien insect pests of trees (IAIPT), a prevalent issue in the Black Sea Basin (BSB) exacerbated by climate change, which carries environmental, economic, and sociological ramifications. easyPEST is structured to pioneer an "early IAIPT warning system" based on an artificial intelligence (AI) platform. This entails conducting pilot studies that involves active participation from trained citizens in data collection processes for addressed pests. The ultimate goal is to expand and upscale this initiative to neighboring countries in BSB, and additional pest species, thereby enhancing regional pest management efforts.

The intertwining factors of global trade and climate change have introduced new pest challenges in BSB. Through our observations in the region, it has become evident that “citizens are profoundly troubled by IAS issues”. Their distress often stems from pervasive misinformation, leading to psychological pessimism. In response, some are contemplating changing the tree species in their orchards, a drastic measure driven by concerns over the impact of IAS. Remarkably, even for pests like the Asian chestnut gall wasp, for which long-term solutions are available, such reactions persist. This scenario not only jeopardizes the well-being of the local population but also poses a significant threat to the tree-dominated ecosystems across the region.

The overall objective: easyPEST aims to develop and implement a platform which “facilitates cross-border communication of plant and biodiversity protection organizations and researchers” for focusing on the common pest problems. By doing so, the project seeks to enhance understanding of the potential invasion routes of future pests, and thus to “establish a monitoring approach for an early warning system”. The project aims to “raise awareness and empower individuals to handle pest issues more effectively” by actively involving citizens in the project. easyPEST aims to provide researchers with a groundbreaking opportunity to collaborate using a “cross-border dataset on population ranges, fluctuation patterns, and life cycles of pests”. This dataset will enable the prediction of climate change-related risks and the development and implementation of control methods. The project will promote climate change adaptation and prevention measures against invasive pest species, utilizing an ecosystem-based approach to enhance resilience. Engaging citizens in this process will not only improve the project's effectiveness but also enhance public mental well-being.

Outputs:
Output 1: Implementing Jointly Developed Pilot Tests of the easyPEST AI Platform for Pest Identification and Early Warning (related indicator: RCO84)
Output 2: Cross-Border Organisations on the Pathway of Pests in Georgia, Greece, and Turkiye Collaborate for the Common Pest Problems (RCO87)
Output 3: Public Trainings and Workshop Organized Across Borders for Raising Awareness Related to Invasive Pests and Climate Change and for Educating Citizen Scientists (CSs) (RCO115)
Output 4: The easyPEST AI Platform Connecting CSs to Scientists for Monitoring and Early Warning of the Pest Invasions (RCO116)

Results: Data regarding presence and distribution of 15 pest species across the region will be collected with cooperation of four organisitions. Throughout the project duration, national PPOs will be engaged through workshops and pilot actions designed to integrate and test the easyPEST platform. Active participation from PPOs will be encouraged also after the project completion to enhance the platform's effectiveness and ensure its relevance to regional pest management strategies through a cooperation agreement among partner organisations (related indicator: RCR84). The project includes a structured protocol where the HU BIYOSFER Museum, which includes experts also to be consulted during the project, in collaboration with HAO and ISU, will take responsibility for system improvements. This will expand the geographical scope of the easyPEST platform and incorporate additional tree pests and diseases (RCR104).

Need for transnational cooperation: There exists a “deficiency in consistent pest monitoring and an efficient data collection and data repository system in the southern BSB”, which serves as a pathway for pest organisms. Pests transit from Greece to Georgia or vice versa through Turkiye, yet “communication challenges persist among transnational forestry and agricultural departments”. This communication gap allows pests to swiftly invade the entire region, often without detection. However, possessing prior knowledge about range-expanding pests can facilitate prompt preparations, including psychological readiness, implementation of quarantine measures, procurement of chemical supplies, and deployment of trapping methods, consequently enhancing damage mitigation efforts more effectively.

titleEn: Protection of virgin forests as a green solution for the Black Sea
Restoration of green infrastructure. Rethinking the green idea
summaryEn:
The border region covered by the project is characterised by its diverse natural features and high biodiversity. 
Despite the efforts of the municipalities of Sapareva Banya and Gevgelija, park areas in the cities are not in the necessary condition to provide adequate recreational facilities for the local population. An important challenge for partners is to consider urban parks as a source of various ecosystem services and to manage them accordingly. Particularly important for nature conservation and biodiversity conservation is to renovate parks in a sustainable way. Adding educational functions to urban parks is an opportunity to reconnect people and nature.
Local authorities on both sides of the border are tasked with developing and implementing various plans and strategies, including those related to EU climate policies. At the same time, small municipalities in the cross-border region, such as the project partners, lack their own capacity for high quality planning, including the integration of European climate objectives that relate to biodiversity and nature conservation. 
A constraint to the implementation of local policies is that the nature of climate policies for sustainable development and the benefits of ecosystem services are not known among communities in the cross-border region. Public acceptance of local climate policies is insufficient for their consensual adoption. Raising awareness among local communities about the benefits of ecosystem services will not only stimulate citizen participation in the policy process, but also contribute to bringing communities in the cross-border region closer together through common shared values.
The overall objective of the project is to contribute to the conservation of nature and biodiversity in the cross-border region of Sapareva Banya - Gevgelija through the construction and renovation of urban parks, increasing the capacity of local authorities to plan and implement policies in accordance to the EU environmental policies and improving the understanding of the benefits of ecosystem services by local communities.
The main project outputs and their users are:
- Renovated urban parks of Sapareva Banya and Gevgelija, which will benefit the population of these towns.
- Jjoint strategic plan for biodiversity conservation and valuation of ecosystem services in the cross-border region developed. The plan will benefit the administrations of the two partner municipalities and other local stakeholders.
- Developed guidelines for the implementation of local environmental policies, project identification and green procurement. The guidelines will benefit the partner municipalities. 
- Conducted trainings for municipal officials and stakeholders in the Sapareva Banya and Gevgelija region.
The present project includes creation of guidelines and tools for municipalities to improve their capacity to plan and implement local policies, as well as to identify investment projects in the field of climate policies and in particular biodiversity and green infrastructure. After its implementation, guidelines for mainstreaming climate policies in local governance, model terms of reference and specifications for green procurement will be available in several activities that are relevant to the project's theme. Novelty is the application of an interdisciplinary approach that involves the use of landscape architecture and the design of the parks to be renovated under the project in a way that represents urban ecosystem services and their benefits.
Strengthening interlinkages and synergies in the cross-border region, as well as identifying barriers to cooperation, is vital to achieving the objectives of the European Green Pact and its overall and cross-sectoral ambition. An integrated approach is also needed to move beyond treating local policies simply as an aspect of cohesion and for regional development in the supranational territory.

titleEn: A journey without borders - from rich history to technological future
summaryEn:
In the cross-border region between the Republic of Bulgaria and the Republic of North Macedonia lies a treasure trove of rich cultural heritage waiting to be unveiled and celebrated. Our project, "A journey without borders - from rich history to technological future," takes on the common challenge of preserving and promoting this diverse cultural heritage, transcending boundaries with a digital solution within the cross-border approach.

Our overall objective is to create an immersive and attractive all-season tourism product that seamlessly integrates modern digital solutions with the region's rich history and cultural assets. Through the delivery of a cutting-edge GIS digital platform and specialized equipment, we aim to digitally map and showcase 20 tourist sites, 100 artifacts, and 20 cultural and historical objects. The project seeks to ignite curiosity and foster a deeper connection with cultural treasures by presenting them through interactive exhibitions, virtual tours, and captivating content. The main outputs of our project will include the GIS platform, digital tours, and models, long-term museum strategies, and skills analysis for young talents. These outputs will benefit museums, cultural workers, artists, youth, and tourists, creating a more inclusive and engaging experience for all stakeholders.

Our approach embraces inclusivity and cross-border collaboration, drawing from the shared history and interwoven narratives between Bulgaria and North Macedonia. By partnering with diverse organizations, including museums, research centers, and creative industries, we harness a wide range of expertise, resources, and perspectives to address the needs of different target groups and sectors. What sets our project apart is the seamless fusion of tradition and innovation. By embracing digital transformation, we breathe new life into ancient artifacts and historical sites, presenting them in ways that resonate with modern audiences. The use of GIS technology, augmented reality, and 3D modeling allows us to showcase the region's cultural heritage in immersive and interactive ways, marking a new chapter in preserving and celebrating our shared past.

On the other hand, the activity "Digital Renaissance: Reviving Museums in the Digital Age" envisions a future where technology and culture intertwine, empowering the next generation to be the torchbearers of their heritage. Through cross-border collaboration and innovative approaches, our project strives to create lasting change, ensuring that the rich cultural treasures of the region continue to inspire and captivate generations to come. Together, we embark on this extraordinary journey to spark curiosity, unveil hidden treasures, and ignite a new passion for cultural heritage in the digital era.

titleEn: Sustainable tourism in the experience economy
summaryEn:
The overall objective of the project is to contribute to the economic development in CB region by creating conditions for an all-season tourism and sustainable use of cultural and natural resources in the covered area. 
The project idea is aimed at the application of modern digital tools for the promotion of tourist attractions and marketing of destination. The focus of the project is to involve visitors in the creation of the tourism product by the concept of "experience economy".
Adapting existing tourism development policies to the current expectations of tourists and visitors is an important prerequisite for successful sustainable tourism development. The development and implementation of a joint tourism marketing strategy is an appropriate response to these expectations. 
The application of innovative tools for the visualisation and presentation of tourist attractions undoubtedly contributes to the attractiveness of the destination and to linking natural resources and cultural heritage, local legends, historical context and contemporary events.
Importantly, the project concept contributes to the introduction of the principles of the "circular economy" in the tourism industry by providing for the reuse and adaptation of buildings and facilities for tourism purposes. Each of the buildings to be renovated under the project has lost its previous functions and will be revitalised physically but also conceptually.
Creating a competitive identity for tourist destinations on both sides of the border is a complex process. The reason is that the tourism product is the result of the interaction of multiple entities involved in tourism development. The desired destination image is the result of overlaying these brands, which is ideally achieved through the active participation of all stakeholders, with the main objective of increasing tourism revenues in the cross-border region and stimulating economic development. In regions with highly developed tourism, it is the corporate and large business structures that create their own brand, making the most of the destination's competitive advantages. They are also the main entities that communicate most actively with each other in order to build a competitive identity for the region. In regions with underdeveloped tourism, as is the case here, there are generally no major players, which are replaced by municipalities in marketing activities. 
After the implementation of the project the main outputs will be produced:
The municipalities of Sapareva Banya, Kratovo and Rankovce will improve their capacity to implement local tourism policy and promote economic development through joint destination marketing and upgraded infrastructure and new tourist information services.
Tourism and cultural entrepreneurs in the targeted territory will be trained in the applying the concept of "Еxperience Еconomy". Their competitiveness will be increased due to the availability of innovative presentation tools and new tourist attractions.
The project activities will contribute for the development of better competitive environment for SMEs, raise the attractiveness of the tourist destinations and improve the quality of the tourist services.

titleEn: Inclusive Coastal Resilience in the Euro-Med
summaryEn:
INCORE-MED brings citizens back into the heart of coastal planning. In Italy, Spain, Portugal, and Croatia, the project tests two advanced participation tools to improve coastal and marine policies: SWAP and Democracy Labs.
The SWAP tool (Scenario Workshops + Adaptation Pathways) helps local actors co-design realistic climate adaptation plans by blending community visions with expert climate projections, using scenario mapping and multicriteria analysis. As for Democracy Labs, it creates discussion spaces where citizens and authorities co-develop new rules and formats for public engagement in marine planning.
These tools are deployed to: 1) create and update participatory cartographies and climate risk perception maps; 2) integrate nature-based solutions in local action plans; 3) disseminate the methodology to new territories through methodological insights and online courses.

titleEn: Holistic EnvironmenTAl and Social Adaptation Framework for Extreme heat
summaryEn:
Cities often become much hotter during heatwaves because of concrete surfaces, lack of green spaces, and city design. Some communities are especially at risk, particularly in poorer neighborhoods where people may already face health and social challenges.

To tackle this, HEATSAFE is taking action in Spain, Italy, Albania, Bulgaria, and Greece. The project is helping cities create clear plans to prepare for and respond to heatwaves. It supports local governments in making smart decisions using practical tools, while also involving local people to make sure solutions match the needs of each area.

In each location, HEATSAFE is testing real-life improvements like cool areas for public use, better emergency responses, and education campaigns to raise awareness. The results will be shared widely so that other cities across the Mediterranean can use the same methods.

By combining science, urban planning, public health, and community input, HEATSAFE aims to build safer, healthier, and more climate-ready cities for everyone.

titleEn: Eco-nautical sea routes
summaryEn:
As the world's largest tourist destination, Mediterranean ports are under intense tourist pressure. This makes their protected areas more vulnerable to overtourism.
The ECO-SEAROUTES project aims to create an eco-nautical route linking ports committed to: 1) respect a common sustainability standard in a transnational approach; 2) redistribute tourism flows to neighbouring coastal and inland areas. 
To achieve this, the project encourages local decision-makers to create and develop new local tourist routes to less crowded areas and their cultural heritage. It will use a bottom-up and participatory approach, ready to be shared and replicated.

titleEn: Development of Sustainable Astrotourism in Euro-MED Regions
summaryEn:
Astrotourism is a new type of tourism in nature areas that focuses on the observation of celestial objects. Specifically, it consists of hiking and astronomy tours, observation of the nocturnal fauna, off-grid hotels, tourist services offered by astronomical observatories...

The MedSkyTour project has two main objectives: to develop this type of tourism and to implement actions aimed at reducing light pollution. In this way, the eight regions involved are not only creating new growth opportunities for sustainable tourism but are also generating real benefits for nocturnal biodiversity.

titleEn: Promoting a Circular Economy with Low Plastic Zones on Mediterranean Islands
summaryEn:
LooP Zone takes on one of the Mediterranean’s most visible challenges: the plastic waste crisis on tourist islands. With over 200 million visitors each year, and single-use plastics (SUPs) products, making up more than 60% of marine litter, island territories like Formentera, Salina, Skiathos, Vis, and Gozo face growing pressure—especially as most local waste management systems can’t keep up.

LooP Zone creates “low plastic zones” where municipalities, tourism businesses, and local innovators act together to prevent and phase out SUPs. Hotels, beach bars and restaurants receive tools to assess their plastic footprint and adopt sustainable and reusable alternatives; new value chains for SUP-free products are supported through innovation labs; and local policies are strengthened to align with national bans.

The model, built on a 3-pillar approach—policy, business support, and innovation—is tested locally, transferred and accessible via a digital platform, and scaled through a regional island network. The goal: transform the tourism sector from a take-make-waste model to a circular economy that works for both people and the sea.

titleEn: Resilience ENhancing to adapt FORests to Climate change Effects and to prevent biotic and abiotic hazard
summaryEn:
In Mediterranean regions hit by wildfires and windstorms, RENFORCE shifts forest management from reaction to prevention. In other words, the project develops practical tools to cut risks before disaster strikes.
It sets up participatory prevention plans in pilot zones, combining local knowledge with forestry science. On the ground, this means mapping high-risk areas, managing vegetation to act as natural firebreaks, and applying storm-resistant planting strategies.
RENFORCE also builds common protocols across borders to anticipate damage. It delivers decision-making tools for public authorities, training programmes for landowners, and a shared strategy to embed risk reduction into forest planning.

titleEn: Creative craft for industrial symbiosis in blue-economy sectors - RECONNECT
summaryEn: RECONNECT aims to boost the circular economy in the Mediterranean by reusing waste from fisheries and aquaculture to create valuable bio-based products. It promotes collaboration between industries, craft-based businesses, and communities using innovative technology and sustainable business models. The project highlights the role of crafts in driving creative and social approaches to circularity. It supports cooperation between sectors that rarely interact, benefiting both large industries and small firms. RECONNECT will test its tools with 130 SMEs and create networks and resources to ensure long-term impact in sustainable blue economy practices.

titleEn: Strategic Harmonization and Resource Enhancement in the MEDiterranean: Advancing Water Management and Innovation through Non-Conventional Resources.
summaryEn:
SHARE.MedWATER delivers scalable solutions to reuse rainwater, greywater, and treated wastewater in rural and island regions across seven Mediterranean countries. 

It sets up community-level pilots where rainwater is harvested to irrigate crops, greywater from homes is reused for toilet flushing, and treated wastewater supports green spaces. At district level, two large-scale demos coordinate water reuse across agriculture, tourism, and urban services.

Inspired by energy-sharing models, SHARE.MedWATER builds a framework for managing and distributing non-conventional water sources collectively. A decision-support tool helps authorities weigh costs, environmental impact, and user needs. Through transnational cooperation, it aims to reduce dependence on freshwater, strengthen climate resilience, and support EU and regional water strategies.

titleEn: Transferring Tourism Carrying Capacity Tool TO CARE about Sustainability of MED ecotourism strategies, plans, products and services.
summaryEn:
The Tourism Carrying Capacity Limit (TCCL) tool developed in the ALTERECO project addresses the risk of overtourism and its impact on the natural and cultural heritage of Mediterranean destinations.
The TO CARE MED project will extend the TCCL tool to other coastal, island, rural and protected natural tourist destinations, focusing on two aspects. First, the TCCL tool will be adapted to each destination. Then, it will be transferred using a 'cascade training model'. This will bring methodologies from the transnational level to local learning and implementation.

titleEn: Systemic circular bioeconomy solutions to support start-up and social driven innovation in rural areas
summaryEn: BIOSTARS supports rural communities in the Mediterranean by helping them build stronger local economies through sustainable, bio-based businesses. The project brings together startups, investors, and communities to create jobs, reduce environmental impact, and promote social innovation. Using a special toolbox developed from earlier projects, BIOSTARS will guide regions in setting up bioeconomy startup villages. It offers practical and social solutions, training, and support to boost green skills, encourage entrepreneurship, and connect local players in a shared effort to grow circular, resource-efficient rural economies.

titleEn: Biodegradable aquaculture nets
summaryEn:
AquaBioNets is a project supporting sustainable aquaculture in six Mediterranean countries. It brings together key groups like governments, businesses, researchers, and communities to promote eco-friendly practices, especially the use of biodegradable nets.
The project strengthens skills, supports innovation, and helps create local policies through a collaborative approach called the Living Lab. It addresses issues like pollution, tough global competition, and unclear regulations. All results, including training materials and policy guides, will be shared publicly to help spread sustainable aquaculture across the region.

titleEn: Enhancing Communities and Organizations for Climate Change Transition
summaryEn:
The project addresses the common and growing challenge of climate change impacts in the Romania-Bulgaria cross-border region, particularly extreme weather events, fluctuating water levels along the Danube River, soil erosion, and biodiversity loss. These issues threaten infrastructure, local economies, and the safety of communities, exacerbated by fragmented environmental data collection and limited institutional cooperation. Both countries face these challenges, but their responses often lack coordination, making a cross-border approach essential for effective adaptation measures. The project seeks to overcome these obstacles by establishing a collaborative framework for gathering and analyzing environmental data, developing climate adaptation strategies, and engaging local communities in sustainable practices.

The overall objective is to enhance the region’s capacity to adapt to climate change through institutional collaboration, sustainable environmental interventions, and public engagement. By integrating real-time data collection with community-driven adaptation measures, the project aims to transform climate resilience from a fragmented effort into a coordinated and evidence-based process. The expected change is the creation of a long-term, sustainable mechanism for collecting and analyzing environmental data to inform decisions, enabling timely responses to climate risks. This will reduce vulnerability, improve ecosystem stability, and equip institutions and communities with the knowledge and tools needed to address climate challenges.

The project will produce several key outputs to achieve these goals. The Băilești Center for Climate Adaptation Collaboration in Romania and the Oryahovo Center for Climate Change Adaptation in Bulgaria will be established as central hubs for collecting, analyzing, and sharing environmental data. These centers will support local authorities, law enforcement agencies, and environmental organizations in coordinating climate adaptation measures. A 10-hectare afforestation initiative in the State Forestry "Oryahovo" will improve flood protection, enhance water retention, and stabilize ecosystems, directly benefiting residents in nearby communities. The Best Practice Guide for Preparing Vulnerable Groups for Climate Change Adaptation will provide practical methodologies to help local authorities and communities protect their most vulnerable members. By project completion, at least one organization is expected to formally adopt the guide, ensuring long-term scalability and impact. The beneficiaries include public authorities, local communities, and environmental experts, who will gain access to practical tools and improved institutional capacity to mitigate and adapt to climate risks.

The project’s approach is comprehensive and grounded in cross-border collaboration. It leverages the strengths of both Romanian and Bulgarian institutions, ensuring the collection and application of environmental data are harmonized across the region. The strategic involvement of IPJ Dolj in Romania is vital, as the police force operates continuously and has extensive territorial coverage. With its officers in the field 24/7, IPJ Dolj can collect real-time observations on environmental changes, such as water levels, vegetation shifts, and infrastructure vulnerabilities. This data, systematically centralized at the Băilești Center, will be shared with decision-makers for informed, proactive responses. This collaboration between law enforcement and climate adaptation is a key innovation, creating a real-time data flow unmatched by traditional monitoring systems. The cross-border approach ensures that Romanian and Bulgarian stakeholders jointly analyze environmental risks and coordinate climate adaptation measures, which is critical given the shared reliance on the Danube River and its flood-prone ecosystem.

The project introduces several original elements. The integration of IPJ Dolj’s field forces into environmental monitoring represents a novel and effective way to collect accurate, real-time data and enhance decision-making. The combination of institutional collaboration and law enforcement-driven data collection is innovative and scalable, serving as a model for other regions. The creation of two dedicated climate adaptation centers, equipped with modern technology, allows for sustained cooperation, while the afforestation initiative provides tangible, nature-based flood protection. The Best Practice Guide is designed to be practical and replicable, ensuring that local authorities in both countries can adopt effective strategies for climate resilience. Through these innovative solutions, the project not only addresses immediate climate risks but also lays the foundation for long-term cross-border collaboration and sustainable development.

titleEn: Green Infrastructure Initiatives and Forest Restoration for Climate Adaptation in Zimnicеа and Svishtov areas
summaryEn:
The project addresses the common environmental challenge in the Romania-Bulgaria cross-border region, where flood risks, rising groundwater levels, and soil erosion pose significant threats to local communities, infrastructure, and biodiversity. Both Zimnicea (Romania) and Svishtov (Bulgaria) are located along the Danube River, making them highly vulnerable to seasonal flooding, uncontrolled surface runoff, and environmental degradation. Without intervention, the increasing frequency of extreme weather events will continue to weaken natural flood defenses, erode soil, and reduce climate resilience in both municipalities.

The overall objective of the project is to strengthen natural flood protection mechanisms through ecologization and afforestation, reducing the negative impact of floods, improving soil stability, and enhancing the adaptive capacity of the region to climate change. By implementing nature-based solutions, the project will increase water retention, limit erosion, and restore green infrastructure, creating a sustainable ecological barrier to protect urban, peri-urban, and rural communities. The expected change is a significant reduction in flood risks, improved soil quality, and a healthier environment, benefiting local populations, municipal administrations, and regional ecosystems.

The project will deliver several key outputs, including the ecologization and afforestation of 4.268 hectares in Zimnicea and 5.798 hectares in Svishtov. These actions will strengthen flood resilience, prevent land degradation, and increase biodiversity. The investment also includes the purchase of specialized equipment (tipper truck, tractor, shredder, disc harrow, fan sprayer/watering tank, plow, auger, fertilizer spreader, and rotary tiller) to ensure the long-term maintenance and sustainability of the afforested areas. The project will also benefit local communities, public authorities, and cross-border stakeholders by creating a best-practice model for flood prevention through afforestation. An awareness campaign, reaching at least 400 people, including local authorities and school children, will promote the importance of forest conservation and climate adaptation.

The project requires a cross-border approach because flooding and environmental risks do not stop at national borders. As both Zimnicea and Svishtov face similar climate challenges, a joint intervention ensures that measures taken on one side of the border do not negatively affect the other. By working together, the two municipalities can exchange best practices, share expertise on afforestation and ecological restoration, and develop a coordinated response to climate change. The integration of afforestation efforts in both regions will create a continuous green infrastructure, improving the region’s overall flood resilience and enhancing cooperation between Romania and Bulgaria.

The project is innovative because it combines afforestation, ecologization, and modern maintenance methods into a single, integrated approach to flood protection. Unlike traditional flood prevention strategies that rely on costly gray infrastructure (dikes and drainage systems), this project promotes nature-based solutions that are self-sustaining, environmentally friendly, and cost-effective. Additionally, the pilot investment in Cadastral Plot 22262 (Zimnicea's archaeological site) introduces a new approach to ecological restoration, demonstrating how natural grass coverage can serve as a protective flood barrier against erosion without disrupting historical sites.

By investing in green infrastructure, strengthening flood protection mechanisms, and enhancing cross-border cooperation, the project creates a replicable, sustainable model for climate change adaptation in the Romania-Bulgaria programme area.

titleEn: Adapting viticulture to climate change by implementing ecosystem-based measures to maintain economic viability
summaryEn:
The project aims to build climate-resilient viticulture practices and infrastructure in the cross-border regions of SW Romania and NW Bulgaria. It collectively focuses on enhancing vineyard resilience against climate change through innovative solutions such as precision viticulture, smart water management, green systems, and cross-border cooperation. By integrating digital technologies, creating a collaborative network, and developing sustainable infrastructure, these projects strive to safeguard viticulture and ensure its long-term viability.

Challenge Addressed:
The common challenge tackled by the activities is the severe impact of climate change on vineyards in Romania and Bulgaria. Climate change, including rising temperatures, extreme weather events, droughts, soil erosion, pests, and diseases, threatens grape quality and yield. These challenges undermine the economic sustainability of the viticulture sector, requiring innovative and region-specific solutions for climate adaptation.

Objective & Expected Change:
The overarching objective is to enhance vineyard resilience and sustainability by integrating advanced technologies, developing climate-adapted practices, and fostering cross-border cooperation. The project aims to create adaptive strategies that help grapevines thrive under changing climatic conditions. The expected change is a more sustainable, efficient, and resilient viticulture sector that reduces environmental impacts, lowers carbon emissions, and improves water management while ensuring long-term agricultural viability.

Main Outputs & Beneficiaries:
-Digital system for climate monitoring and early warnings, benefiting vineyard managers and farmers.
-Climate-resistant grapevine varieties, benefiting grapevine breeders and growers.
-Research articles and guides to disseminate findings, benefiting farmers, researchers, and policymakers.
-Cross-border hub for knowledge exchange and best practices, benefiting viticulturists, entrepreneurs, and experts.
-Multilingual interactive platform with resources and AI assistance, benefiting viticulturists and winemakers.
-Documentary videos and training programs, providing knowledge to a wider audience of viticulture professionals.
-Green buffer zones for vineyard protection, providing a new practice that benefits viticulturists by reducing the impact of extreme weather.
-Photovoltaic-powered irrigation systems, providing a scalable example of cost reduction and green energy use, benefitting cross-border viticulturists.
-Reports and newsletters to disseminate project results, benefiting the broader viticulture community.

Approach & Need for Cross-Border Collaboration:
The project utilizes a cross-border approach, crucial for addressing shared challenges in viticulture across SW Romania and NW Bulgaria. By pooling expertise, resources, and innovative solutions, the projects ensure that both countries benefit from shared knowledge and region-specific practices. This collaboration facilitates the development of scalable solutions for climate adaptation that can be applied across borders and enhances the long-term sustainability of the viticulture sector.

Innovation & Originality:
The innovative aspects of this project include:
-The integration of digital technologies like precision viticulture, drone monitoring, and AI-powered assistance to support climate adaptation.
-The creation of green buffer zones to protect vineyards and promote biodiversity, along with smart water management powered by renewable energy.
-The development of a cross-border collaborative network that shares knowledge, best practices, and resources, enhancing the region’s ability to respond to climate change.
-The use of interactive digital hubs, AI-driven support, and documentary videos to provide accessible, real-time assistance and disseminate research findings.

These combined efforts will significantly contribute to the long-term resilience of viticulture in Romania and Bulgaria, ensuring that the sector adapts to the ongoing challenges posed by climate changes and pressures. By implementing innovative solutions and fostering cross-border collaboration, the project aims to build a viticulture sector that is more sustainable, resource-efficient, and resilient to extreme climate changes. This holistic approach will safeguard the livelihoods of viticulturists, promote biodiversity, and secure the future of grape production, benefiting not only local communities but also preserving the region’s rich viticultural heritage for future generations.

titleEn: A green region along the blue Danube
summaryEn:
The project "A green region along the Blue Danube" will be implemented in partnership by two accredited Universities - University of Craiova (Romania) and D.A. TSENOV University (Bulgaria) and a Romanian NGO - Engage in Education.
The project aims to increase the quality of life of the inhabitants along the two banks of the Danube by increasing the quality of the environmental conditions. Complex actions will be carried out:
-the green arrangement of some spaces in both countries: a University Botanical Garden in Romania and the green arrangement of the campus of the D.A.Tsenov University. 
 - monitoring the quality of the environment in order to prevent harmful effects; the quality of the Danube waters will be monitored from Drobeta Turnu Severin to Constanta; The collected data will be sent to a data processing center that will be established by the Partner University in Bulgaria. This University will produce periodic and weekly environmental data analysis bulletins that will be sent to local public authorities and NGOs in the cities in Romania and Bulgaria located along the Danube
Also, a network of sensors will be created in the cities on the Bulgarian and Romanian side of the Danube; the data will be transmitted and processed by the Shvistov Computing Center (Partner University 1 in the project)
The Engage in Education Association (Partner 3 in the project) will coordinate the creation of a network of partnerships between NGOs and local public authorities with headquarters in the localities located along the Danube, both in Romania and in Bulgaria. This network of partnerships will be established in order to preserve the quality of the environment and promote green development.
The common challenge:
Along the Danube, on the Romanian-Bulgarian border, there are numerous towns, businesses, nuclear power plants (Kozlodui and Cernavoda) and implicitly there are risks of pollution that are currently not monitored.
The general objective of the project and the expected change:
Improving the protection and conservation of nature along the Danube, in the Romanian-Bulgarian cross-border area through complex actions: increasing green areas, creating a common system for monitoring air, water and soil quality and by establishing a network of NGOs to promote sustainable development and biodiversity
The main results:
- The establishment of a university botanical garden by the University of Craiova
- The green arrangement of the campus of the partner university in Bulgaria-
- Establishing a complex monitoring network of air, water and soil quality
Why a cross-border approach is needed:
The Danube is a river common to both countries and a unified approach is needed to protect it
What is new/original
The establishment of a complex air, water and soil quality monitoring network by the university; creating a system that allows the collection and processing of data in real time on the quality of river waters.
Non-eligible expenditures for LP: Quality audit services 3,260.48 euro+13 sensors 3,000.00 euro=6,260.48 euro
University of Craiova will purchase 1 sensor for monitoring of radiation, 10 sensors type A3 and 2 sensors for monitoring of water for proper implementation of the project activities, achievement of the indicators and results

titleEn: Black Sea Basin Sustainable Logistics and Cooperation Network
summaryEn:
BSB- LOGINET Project is related to the 3rd priority of the Black Sea Cross-Border Cooperation program, Building up mutual trust, in particular by encouraging people-to-people actions. It was prepared in partnership with the Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Samsun (lead partner) from Turkey, Ajara from Georgia and Varna from Bulgaria to combat various challenges faced by the logistics sector, which is closely related to commercial cooperation in the region. The general objective of the project is to increase cross-border trade and cooperation in the Black Sea Basin by strengthening cooperation between institutions and encouraging mutual trust and people-to-people interactions. Our specific objective is to establish a new cooperation network in the logistics sector among the chambers of commerce and industry in the cities of Samsun, Varna and Ajara to strengthen regional trade.. The challenges addressed in the selected region are as follows; 1- Institutional cooperation networks are not sufficiently developed in the region. There is a lack of consistent inter-institutional cooperation and mutual trust among various stakeholders in the region. Public and private sector organizations often operate separately, leading to fragmented efforts to address common challenges. 2- There is a significant need for advanced digital platforms and data-sharing systems for monitoring, management and communication within the logistics chain. 3- Complicated and time-consuming customs procedures hinder trade. 4- As logistics activities intensify, environmental impacts grow, including increased greenhouse gas emissions and greater pressure on natural resources. The adoption of green and blue economy principles is still in its early stages. The target audience of the project is public authorities, logistics-related organizations, local governments, business NGOs, youth and women in the 3 regions. Our project focuses on common challenges in the selected region that can be intervened in this project dimension, in terms of capacity building, knowledge sharing, increasing digital skills and increasing stakeholder participation. A needs analysis and roadmap study will be conducted on the status of the logistics sector in the selected region. According to the content determined by the lead partner, each partner will prepare their own region's report, and then these reports will be combined and presented to local and regional institutions. As part of the capacity-building activities, 50 young people, 50% of whom are women, will receive logistics operations management training in Samsun and Ajara. 2 workshops will be organized in each region on increasing digital skills in the sector and environmental sustainability.
A hackathon with 24 young participants on Creating Sustainable and Efficient Solutions in Cross-Border Logistics will be organized in Samsun. Young people will present digital solutions in the sector in a competitive environment. Varna and Ajara will each provide the participation of a group of young people in this event. The Cross-Border Logistics Information Exchange Portal will be another innovation of our project. It will be an online portal that facilitates information sharing, joint planning and synchronized activities. At the same time, with the artificial intelligence chatboot integration, all information and data regarding trade and logistics between the countries in the region will be accessible and complex questions will be answered. A sustainability agreement will be made between Ajara CCI and Samsun CCI after the project is completed, and this innovation will be used continuously by the partners.
There are centers in the EU countries that have internalized and successfully implemented the blue and green economy in the logistics sector. A study visit will be made to these centers. Each partner will visit a separate center (port, logistics center, international fairs etc.) as a delegation, after the visit, they will share their impressions of the visit in online meetings and at the logistics summit. Since the target audience of each partner is different, the number of delegations that will participate in the visit will vary. A total of 30 organizations will participate in the study visit and observe good practices.
The Black Sea Logistics Summit will be an important event where all activities of our project will be reviewed, and issues such as the status of the logistics sector in the region and the established cooperation network will be discussed. The logistics summit will be organized in Samsun, and the partner institutions will attend the summit with delegations of 10 people.

titleEn: Bringing Regional actors Into (G)lobal community – driven actions Toward climate adaptation and resilient ecosystems in the Black Sea region
summaryEn:
Public authorities play a pivotal role in the achievement of the EU’s energy and climate targets for 2050 and beyond by setting the path through multi-level governance policies and integrated planning tools addressing the sectors like most significant energy-saving potential, aimed to increase environmental, social and economic sustainability, and by showing the way at a regional and local level to influence choices and behaviour patterns of the main actors and the general public. The variety of countries' specific policies and EU accession practices presupposes the significant barriers and challenges related with these endeavours:
-lack of multidisciplinary skills in public authorities at all levels;
- insufficient vertical coordination at a territorial level and horizontal coordination among different departments within local authorities for the production of multi-sector planning tools (plans, programmes, etc.) allowing the achievement of simplification, synergies and economies of scale;
- difficulty in engaging stakeholders and main actors in the policy and plans development;
- difficulty in accessing best practices and tested cross-sector solutions due to language barriers or poor knowledge of sources of information;
- difficulty in implementing measures envisaged in the planning documents especially in energy and climate plans due to hindrances in financing solutions for the actions or in mediation with stakeholders and the public
-economic discrepancies between the various countries resulting from the energy prices, climate change, etc.
- differences between regions especially large cities and other areas, including rural areas as well as the level of integration into the EU policy implementation. 
In order to respond to these challenges, the overall objective of BRIGHT project is to empower public authorities in four participating countries: Bulgaria, Moldova, Georgia and Türkiye with the necessary skills and capacities to better planning, implementing and monitoring sustainable energy and climate policies through optimization of geographical and technical synergies and complementarity.
Strengthening the institutional capacities will lead to improvements in addressing various problems of social and economic development, foster human resource uptake for public management, finance operation, share experience thus building a mutual trust and encouraging people to people actions for achieving resilient BS region.
The work plan focuses on capacity building and development of policies and plans based on extensive work with public authorities, involving stakeholders and acting for further exploitation and replication of the actions. A unified approach is proposed to establish a solid background enabling the easy access to legislative pre-conditions which will support raising skills of municipal officers and further uptake of measures in cooperation with their communities. Technical expertise is offered by the partner teams to facilitate the local planning of energy and climate documents, realization of actions and their multiplication. Local forums and workshops are envisaged in the partner territories to enhance cooperation and inclusion.
24 rural municipalities will be targeted by the four partner organizations (six per each), four of them will experience the practical planning and execution process.
The expected outputs and results of BRIGHT are: an Established Methodology for uptake energy and climate actors in the joint planning and programming at (g)local level; created Expert Partner teams as digital twins for experience exchange; set up of Partners cooperation for local energy and climate policy development and implementation.
BRIGHT is a partnership initiative of four partners representing four Black Sea countries: the Union of Bulgarian Black Sea Local Authorities as a lead partner, within an EU member state, the Agency for cross border cooperation and European integration (Moldova), the National Association of Local Authorities (Georgia) and the Eastern Black Sea Development Agency (Türkiye), three of them representing EU candidate countries.
The partners' previous experience in EU and national pilot projects will be capitalized to test the active participation of selected pilot municipalities, their represented stakeholders and community actors. New tools will be proposed on an open platform for benchmarking and knowledge sharing (emission inventories evaluation & monitoring, best practices, guidelines & training materials for partner expert and municipal staff ). A successful methodology for collaboration with the civil society by an integrative stakeholder approach for sustainable policies promotion and interactive initiatives will be applied.
The involvement of countries and areas with different levels of tradition in mutli-sector planning and capitalization of previous EU-funded initiatives are among the project's guiding principles and brings the added value at a cross border level.

titleEn: Enhancing innovation capacities and uptake of advanced technologies towards sustainable fisheries and eco-friendly aquaculture in Black Sea
summaryEn:
The project TIMMOD-NEXT aims to contribute to tackling one of the main challenges of the Black Sea area - the BLUE ECONOMY, underlined as “the connecting element for sustainable use of Black Sea resources” in the NEXT Black Sea Basin Programme. A key pillar in the Blue economy is fisheries and aquaculture (F&A) sector, as highlighted also in Common Maritime Agenda which contains concrete priorities and actions for the development of a sustainable blue economy. The Strategic Research and Innovation Agenda for the Black Sea, highlights the need of research and innovation actions in this area. EU Common Fisheries Policy (CFP) underlines that “Research and innovation efforts are needed to implement the CFP and acquire more food from the seas and oceans in a sustainable way”. 
At the same time the BSB Programme underlines that “The countries in the Black Sea Basin area have low levels of innovation infrastructure and investment”. The F&A sectors continue to grow but still need to be modernised by establishing a sustainable technical capacity through digitalization, uptake of innovation and advanced technologies, and increased environmental sustainability.

TIMMOD-NEXT addresses the above challenges bringing together 6 organisations from 5 countries within PO1/SO1 Field of Action 3, aiming at strengthening an existing innovation cooperation network, and uptake of research & innovation results obtained in a project successfully implemented in the framework of the Black Sea programme in the period 2020-2022 (the project TIMMOD).
The overall objective of TIMMOD-NEXT is to boost research and innovation capacities and facilitate the uptake of advanced technologies in Black Sea fisheries & aquaculture, by connecting research and business sectors, delivering joint solutions towards sustainable use of fish resources and growth of eco-friendly aquaculture, in line with the objectives of the Blue economy. The expected change will be achieved by delivering of a unique transnational solution – the Black Sea Innovation Network of Open-Air Labs for sustainable fisheries and aquaculture. This Innovation Network will act as a creative space where researchers and involved stakeholders with different expertise can collaborate in new ways to scale-up innovation. Adequate testing / training / demonstration equipment and software will be purchased and installed in 5 Open-Air Labs in 5 Black Sea countries connected in a network to secure co-creation/brainstorming, and scaling-up innovative tools & methods. The Network will play a central role in bringing the supply side of technological and digital solutions closer to the demand side (productive sector). This will create a win-win situation for all players within this ecosystem. 

The project will develop 5 main outputs, linking 5 research organisations cooperating in joint projects, and 6 organisations cooperating across border, jointly organising 3 public events across borders, carrying out a joint pilot action for development and implementation of the main project output the jointly developed solution – the Innovation Network, implemented by the participating organisations. This Innovation Network is expected to overcome barriers hindering the establishing a sustainable technical capacity of fisheries and aquaculture sector through digitalization, uptake of innovation and advanced technologies 
The main beneficiaries are research institutions, small-scale fisheries, aquaculture developers, SMEs providing services to fisheries and aquaculture, but also state fishery executive agencies, relevant authorities and decision makers, who shall provide policy support of the expected change. At the end of the day, it will influence people in coastal communities, providing new jobs, better environmental conditions, and improved wellbeing.

To achieve the above objectives, the work-plan of the project envisages to conduct an updated baseline study and inventory of advanced technologies in F&A, followed by a serious methodological, design and engineering works to establish the 5 Open-Air Labs in 5 countries, which will be further connected within the joint pilot action for testing and implementation of the Innovation Network, and show cased by the Web-portal provide information about sustainable aquaculture and fishery innovations and technology.
The implementation of TIMMOD-NEXT joint actions will bring the added value to transnational cooperation, needed to promote advancements on fisheries and aquaculture in the Black Sea, to maximize the economic benefits and to ensure the sustainable development of the sector. 
Aiming to support the cross-border cooperation between research and productive sector, and involving at transnational level also policy makers, service providers and business, the project TIMMOD-NEXT will demonstrate the efficiency of transnational cooperation for tackling the important challenges of sustainable fisheries and eco-friendly aquaculture in the Black Sea region.

titleEn: Cooperation for Wildfires Prevention and Nature Preservation in Protected Areas of the Black Sea Basin
summaryEn:
The Co-NatureGuard project addresses a critical common challenge in the Black Sea region: the prevention and management of wildfires, particularly in protected natural areas and national parks. The region's diverse ecosystems are increasingly threatened by the frequency and intensity of wildfires, exacerbated by climate change.
